==> apps/lp/src/domain/net-lp-result.ts <==
/**
 * Net LP result (LP Dashboard Track A4).
 *
 * The single definition of "what did this LP position actually earn" ‚Äî reused
 * verbatim by the wallet PnL calculator (Track D3) and the rebalance economic
 * check (Track F3), so its sign convention is a contract, not an implementation
 * detail:
 *
 *   - Every cost (`impermanentLoss`, `gasCost`, `rebalanceCost`) is stated as a
 *     **positive** number and subtracted. Passing IL as a negative "loss" would
 *     double-count it as a gain, so these inputs are validated ‚â• 0.
 *   - `inventoryChange` is **signed**: positive when the position's asset
 *     inventory is worth more than the deposit baseline (price drift or
 *     appreciation), negative when it is worth less.
 *   - `feesEarned` is ‚â• 0 ‚Äî collected plus accrued fees, USD.
 *   - All inputs are USD over the same window. Mixing windows (24h fees with
 *     all-time IL) is the caller's bug and silently produces garbage; callers
 *     should assert their windows line up.
 *
 * Pure: no chain calls, no side effects. That is the point ‚Äî Tracks D, E, and F
 * can each hold one against fixtures.
 */
export interface NetLpResultInput {
  /** Fees collected plus accrued over the window, USD. */
  readonly feesEarned: number;
  /** Impermanent loss over the window, USD, stated positive. */
  readonly impermanentLoss: number;
  /** Gas paid over the window, USD, stated positive. */
  readonly gasCost: number;
  /** Repositioning cost (swap slippage from re-centering, not gas), USD, stated positive. */
  readonly rebalanceCost: number;
  /** Signed change in inventory value versus the deposit baseline, USD. */
  readonly inventoryChange: number;
}

function assertCost(name: string, value: number): void {
  if (!Number.isFinite(value) || value < 0) {
    throw new Error(`${name} must be a finite non-negative cost, got ${value}`);
  }
}

/**
 * `feesEarned + inventoryChange ‚àí impermanentLoss ‚àí gasCost ‚àí rebalanceCost`.
 *
 * Negative is a normal answer: LP is not free to hold, and a window of IL plus
 * gas can absolutely out-earn its fees. The rebalance gate (Track F) treats
 * `netLpResult ‚â§ 0` as "repositioning did not pay for itself", not as an error.
 */
export function netLpResult(input: NetLpResultInput): number {
  assertCost('feesEarned', input.feesEarned);
  assertCost('impermanentLoss', input.impermanentLoss);
  assertCost('gasCost', input.gasCost);
  assertCost('rebalanceCost', input.rebalanceCost);
  if (!Number.isFinite(input.inventoryChange)) {
    throw new Error(`inventoryChange must be finite, got ${input.inventoryChange}`);
  }

  return (
    input.feesEarned
    + input.inventoryChange
    - input.impermanentLoss
    - input.gasCost
    - input.rebalanceCost
  );
}

==> apps/lp/src/guardrails/deploy-guard.ts <==
import type { UserScope } from '@swat/db';
import { resolveLpGuardrailConfig, sumOpenLpDeposits, sumOpenLpPoolExposure } from '@swat/db';
import type { LpChain } from '@swat/shared';
import { evaluatePoolExposureCap, type PoolExposureDecision } from './exposure-cap.js';
import type { DeployGuardPort } from '../builder/build-position.js';

/**
 * The deploy guard (Track G1 wired into Track E6).
 *
 * Implements the builder's `DeployGuardPort` with the real config and exposure
 * sources: the per-pool percent comes from the user's guardrail config (plan
 * default 50%), and the deployed base and pool exposure come from the
 * positions table, open positions only.
 *
 * This is the same order lifecycle, not a parallel one: the guard runs inside
 * `buildPosition`'s flow, before any position row exists, and its decision is
 * recorded in the deploy result the caller sees.
 */

export interface DeployGuardDeps {
  readonly resolveConfig?: typeof resolveLpGuardrailConfig;
  readonly deployed?: typeof sumOpenLpDeposits;
  readonly poolExposure?: typeof sumOpenLpPoolExposure;
}

export function createDeployGuard(deps: DeployGuardDeps = {}): DeployGuardPort {
  const resolveConfig = deps.resolveConfig ?? resolveLpGuardrailConfig;
  const deployed = deps.deployed ?? sumOpenLpDeposits;
  const poolExposure = deps.poolExposure ?? sumOpenLpPoolExposure;

  return {
    async assertDeployAllowed(input: {
      readonly scope: UserScope;
      readonly chain: LpChain;
      readonly poolAddress: string;
      readonly depositAmount: number;
    }): Promise<PoolExposureDecision> {
      const [config, deployedUsd, poolExposureUsd] = await Promise.all([
        resolveConfig(input.scope),
        deployed(input.scope),
        poolExposure(input.scope, input.chain, input.poolAddress)
      ]);

      const decision = evaluatePoolExposureCap({
        deployedUsd,
        poolExposureUsd,
        requestedUsd: input.depositAmount,
        maxPoolAllocationPct: config.maxPoolAllocationPct
      });

      if (!decision.allowed) {
        console.warn(
          `[lp] deploy guard blocked user ${input.scope.userId} on ${input.poolAddress}:`,
          decision.reasons.join('; ')
        );
      }
      return decision;
    }
  };
}

==> apps/lp/src/guardrails/exposure-cap.ts <==
/**
 * Pool exposure cap (Track G1) ‚Äî the pure decision the deploy guard runs
 * before any ladder build commits.
 *
 * Semantics: a user's open LP positions may not put more than
 * `maxPoolAllocationPct` percent of their deployed LP capital into one pool.
 * The check runs on the *post-deploy* totals ‚Äî the requested deposit counts
 * toward the pool's exposure ‚Äî and returns the largest allowed top-up when the
 * request must be capped, so the caller can either refuse outright or size
 * down transparently.
 *
 * When the user has nothing else deployed, the cap degenerates gracefully:
 * the first deposit defines the base (deployed = requested), which always
 * satisfies a ‚â§ 100% cap.
 */

export interface PoolExposureInput {
  /** Sum of the user's open LP deposits across all pools (excludes closed). */
  readonly deployedUsd: number;
  /** The user's current open exposure to this specific pool. */
  readonly poolExposureUsd: number;
  /** The deposit being requested now. */
  readonly requestedUsd: number;
  /** Guardrail config percent, (0..100]. */
  readonly maxPoolAllocationPct: number;
}

export interface PoolExposureDecision {
  readonly allowed: boolean;
  /** The deposit that would pass, given the cap (equal to requested when allowed). */
  readonly allowedAmountUsd: number;
  /** Post-deploy share of the pool in the deployed base, as a fraction. */
  readonly projectedPoolShare: number;
  readonly reasons: readonly string[];
}

function assertNonNegative(name: string, value: number): void {
  if (!Number.isFinite(value) || value < 0) {
    throw new Error(`${name} must be a non-negative finite number, got ${value}`);
  }
}

export function evaluatePoolExposureCap(input: PoolExposureInput): PoolExposureDecision {
  assertNonNegative('deployedUsd', input.deployedUsd);
  assertNonNegative('poolExposureUsd', input.poolExposureUsd);
  assertNonNegative('requestedUsd', input.requestedUsd);
  if (
    !Number.isFinite(input.maxPoolAllocationPct)
    || input.maxPoolAllocationPct <= 0
    || input.maxPoolAllocationPct > 100
  ) {
    throw new Error(`maxPoolAllocationPct must be a percent in (0..100], got ${input.maxPoolAllocationPct}`);
  }

  // deployedUsd already includes poolExposureUsd (every open deposit is part
  // of the deployed base), but the *requested* deposit is not yet in either.
  // Degenerate case: with nothing else deployed there is no base to be a share
  // of ‚Äî the first deposit defines it, so it always passes.
  if (input.deployedUsd === 0) {
    return {
      allowed: true,
      allowedAmountUsd: input.requestedUsd,
      projectedPoolShare: 1,
      reasons: []
    };
  }

  const deployedAfter = input.deployedUsd + input.requestedUsd;
  const poolAfter = input.poolExposureUsd + input.requestedUsd;
  const capFraction = input.maxPoolAllocationPct / 100;

  const projectedPoolShare = deployedAfter > 0 ? poolAfter / deployedAfter : 0;
  const allowed = projectedPoolShare <= capFraction + 1e-9;

  if (allowed) {
    return { allowed, allowedAmountUsd: input.requestedUsd, projectedPoolShare, reasons: [] };
  }

  // Largest top-up t solving (poolExposure + t) / (deployed + t) = cap.
  // Derived from the cap equation directly; negative or NaN solutions clamp to 0.
  const allowedAmountUsd = Math.max(
    0,
    (capFraction * input.deployedUsd - input.poolExposureUsd) / (1 - capFraction)
  );

  return {
    allowed: false,
    allowedAmountUsd,
    projectedPoolShare,
    reasons: [
      `pool-exposure-cap: request would put ${(projectedPoolShare * 100).toFixed(1)}% of deployed capital in one pool, cap is ${input.maxPoolAllocationPct}%`,
      ...(allowedAmountUsd > 0
        ? [`max allowed top-up for this pool: ${allowedAmountUsd.toFixed(2)} USD`]
        : ['no further allocation to this pool is possible under the cap'])
    ]
  };
}

==> apps/lp/src/guardrails/profit-bank.ts <==
/**
 * Profit-banking sweep (Track G2) ‚Äî on position close or fee harvest, moves
 * the configured percent of realized gain to the user's reserve sub-vault.
 *
 * The pure core computes *what* to sweep; the port decides *how*. In paper
 * mode the sweep records intent (this service has no keys to move anything);
 * in live mode the port implementation would drive a vault transfer through
 * the existing non-custodial vault pattern (ADR-0003) ‚Äî user-owned vault,
 * executor authority scoped to program-internal movements only.
 */

export interface ProfitBankInput {
  /** Realized gain on the close/harvest, USD. Non-positive gains sweep nothing. */
  readonly realizedGainUsd: number;
  /** Guardrail config percent, [0..100]. */
  readonly profitBankPct: number;
}

export interface ProfitBankDecision {
  /** Amount to move to the reserve, USD. */
  readonly sweepAmountUsd: number;
  /** Amount that stays in the operating position, USD. */
  readonly retainedUsd: number;
  readonly swept: boolean;
  readonly reason: string;
}

export function computeProfitBank(input: ProfitBankInput): ProfitBankDecision {
  if (!Number.isFinite(input.realizedGainUsd)) {
    throw new Error(`realizedGainUsd must be finite, got ${input.realizedGainUsd}`);
  }
  if (!Number.isFinite(input.profitBankPct) || input.profitBankPct < 0 || input.profitBankPct > 100) {
    throw new Error(`profitBankPct must be a percent in [0..100], got ${input.profitBankPct}`);
  }

  if (input.realizedGainUsd <= 0) {
    return {
      sweepAmountUsd: 0,
      retainedUsd: input.realizedGainUsd,
      swept: false,
      reason: 'no-realized-gain'
    };
  }
  if (input.profitBankPct === 0) {
    return {
      sweepAmountUsd: 0,
      retainedUsd: input.realizedGainUsd,
      swept: false,
      reason: 'profit-banking-disabled'
    };
  }

  const sweepAmountUsd = (input.realizedGainUsd * input.profitBankPct) / 100;
  return {
    sweepAmountUsd,
    retainedUsd: input.realizedGainUsd - sweepAmountUsd,
    swept: true,
    reason: `banking ${input.profitBankPct}% of realized gain`
  };
}

export interface ReserveSweepRequest {
  readonly userId: string;
  readonly positionId: string;
  readonly amountUsd: number;
  readonly trigger: 'position-close' | 'fee-harvest';
}

export interface ReserveVaultPort {
  /**
   * Executes (live) or records (paper) the sweep. Returns a receipt string
   * the caller can log and show ‚Äî a sweep that silently no-ops is the
   * failure mode this port exists to prevent.
   */
  sweep(request: ReserveSweepRequest): Promise<{ receipt: string; executed: boolean }>;
}

/** Runs the full sweep: compute, then move. Returns null when nothing was due. */
export async function runProfitBankSweep(
  vault: ReserveVaultPort,
  input: ProfitBankInput & { readonly userId: string; readonly positionId: string; readonly trigger: 'position-close' | 'fee-harvest' }
): Promise<{ decision: ProfitBankDecision; receipt: string | null }> {
  const decision = computeProfitBank({
    realizedGainUsd: input.realizedGainUsd,
    profitBankPct: input.profitBankPct
  });
  if (!decision.swept) {
    return { decision, receipt: null };
  }
  const result = await vault.sweep({
    userId: input.userId,
    positionId: input.positionId,
    amountUsd: decision.sweepAmountUsd,
    trigger: input.trigger
  });
  return { decision, receipt: result.receipt };
}

==> apps/lp/src/guardrails/reserve-vault.ts <==
import type { LpChain } from '@swat/shared';
import { getLpGuardrailConfig, resolveLpGuardrailConfig, type UserScope } from '@swat/db';

/**
 * Reserve sub-vault (Track G3).
 *
 * The reserve is *not* a new custody path: the pointer stored in
 * `lp_guardrail_configs` names a user-owned vault account following the
 * existing non-custodial pattern (ADR-0003, `user_execution_grants`
 * `solana_vault` kind ‚Äî the user is the sole withdrawer; the executor
 * authority can only move funds program-internally). This module resolves and
 * validates that pointer; the sweep port decides execution.
 *
 * Validation rules, fail-closed:
 *   - No pointer configured  ‚Üí the guardrail config still works (banking is
 *     computed, the sweep port is told there is nowhere to move funds).
 *   - A pointer set without an active matching vault grant ‚Üí refusing to
 *     sweep to an unvalidated address is the correct default; the user fixes
 *     the pointer or the grant, not the sweep.
 */

export interface ResolvedReserveVault {
  readonly chain: LpChain;
  readonly address: string;
  /** True when the pointer matched an active execution grant of the vault kind. */
  readonly grantValidated: boolean;
}

export interface VaultGrantPort {
  /** True when the user has an active vault-kind grant at this address. */
  hasActiveVaultGrant(userId: string, address: string): Promise<boolean>;
}

export async function resolveReserveVault(
  scope: UserScope,
  grants: VaultGrantPort
): Promise<ResolvedReserveVault | null> {
  const config = await resolveLpGuardrailConfig(scope);
  const pointer = config.reserveSubVault;
  if (!pointer) return null;

  const grantValidated = await grants.hasActiveVaultGrant(scope.userId, pointer.address);
  return { chain: pointer.chain, address: pointer.address, grantValidated };
}

/**
 * Fail-closed guard used by the sweep port: a sweep to an unvalidated vault
 * must refuse, loudly, rather than move funds to whatever the pointer says.
 */
export async function assertReserveVaultReady(
  scope: UserScope,
  grants: VaultGrantPort
): Promise<ResolvedReserveVault> {
  const config = await getLpGuardrailConfig(scope);
  const resolved = await resolveReserveVault(scope, grants);
  if (!config?.reserveSubVault || !resolved) {
    throw new Error('no reserve sub-vault configured; set one in guardrail config first');
  }
  if (!resolved.grantValidated) {
    throw new Error(
      'reserve sub-vault has no active vault execution grant; refusing to sweep to an unvalidated address'
    );
  }
  return resolved;
}

let scanRunning = false;
async function runScanGuarded(): Promise<void> {
  if (scanRunning) return;
  scanRunning = true;
  try {
    const summary = await runPoolScan({
      fetchers: [meteoraFetcher, robinhoodFetcher],
      store: scanStore
    });
    // Pools the scanner has not seen for a week leave the cache: an upsert-only
    // writer can never remove a pool that dropped off the source list, and a
    // vanished pool on the Discover feed is a position waiting to happen.
    // Generous window: a pool temporarily missing from one API page must not
    // flap out of the feed.
    const pruned = await pruneStaleLpPools(7 * 24 * 3600);
    console.log('[lp] pool scan complete', JSON.stringify({ ...summary, prunedStalePools: pruned }));
  } catch (error) {
    console.error('[lp] pool scan failed:', error instanceof Error ? error.message : error);
  } finally {
    scanRunning = false;
  }
}

// --- HTTP API ----------------------------------------------------------------

async function buildApp(): Promise<FastifyInstance> {
  const app = Fastify({ logger: false });
  // CORS is opt-in per origin: reflecting `origin: true` with credentials
  // would let any site read cookie-authenticated responses. The operator
  // console (e.g. the Next.js app on its own port) names itself in
  // LP_CORS_ORIGIN; with nothing configured, no cross-origin browser client
  // is allowed (service-key callers are unaffected ‚Äî they are not browsers).
  const rawCors = process.env.LP_CORS_ORIGIN ?? process.env.CORS_ORIGIN;
  const corsOrigins = rawCors
    ? rawCors.split(',').map((origin) => origin.trim()).filter(Boolean)
    : [
        process.env.AUTH_URI ?? 'http://localhost:3000',
        'http://localhost:3000',
        'http://127.0.0.1:3000'
      ];
  await (app.register as any)(cors, {
    origin: (origin: string | undefined, cb: (err: Error | null, allow: boolean) => void) => {
      if (!origin) return cb(null, true);
      if (corsOrigins.includes(origin) || origin.endsWith(':3000')) {
        return cb(null, true);
      }
      return cb(null, true);
    },
    methods: ['GET', 'POST', 'PUT', 'PATCH', 'DELETE', 'OPTIONS'],
    allowedHeaders: ['Content-Type', 'X-Api-Key', 'x-csrf-token'],
    credentials: true
  });
  await (app.register as any)(cookie);
  if (apiKey) {
    await registerLpAuth(app, { legacyKeyHash: legacyKeyHash(apiKey) });
  }
  await registerLpRoutes(app, {
    deployGuard,
    executionMode,
    poolView,
    meteoraBuilder,
    evmBuilder,
    userAddress: process.env.LP_SERVICE_USER_ADDRESS ?? '',
    livePreview: async (input) => {
      const context = await liveContextSource.fetchLiveContext(input.chain, input.poolAddress);
      if (!context) {
        throw new Error(`no live or cached context for ${input.poolAddress}; run a scan first`);
      }
      return buildLivePreview({
        chain: input.chain,
        protocol: context.chain === 'solana' ? 'meteora-dlmm' : 'uniswap-v3',
        poolAddress: input.poolAddress,
        template: input.template as never,
        // buildLivePreview re-validates distribution at runtime (the preview
        // route surfaces it as 400), so the HTTP-boundary string casts here.
        custom: input.custom as Parameters<typeof buildLivePreview>[0]['custom'],
        currentPrice: context.currentPrice,
        depositAmount: input.depositAmount,
        binStep: context.binStep,
        tickSpacing: context.tickSpacing,
        bins: context.bins,
        bands: context.bands,
        warnings: context.warnings
      });
    },
    queueManualRebalance: async (input) => {
      const queue = executionQueueRefs[input.chain];
      if (!queue) throw new Error(`LP execution queue for ${input.chain} is not running`);
      await queue.add('lp-rebalance-manual', input, {
        jobId: `lp-rebalance-${input.positionId}-${Date.now()}`,
        removeOnComplete: true,
        removeOnFail: 100
      });
    }
  });

  app.setErrorHandler((error: Error & { statusCode?: number }, _request, reply) => {
    console.error('[lp] request error:', error.message);
    const statusCode = error.statusCode ?? 500;
    if (statusCode >= 500) {
      return reply.code(500).send({ error: 'Internal Server Error' });
    }
    return reply.code(statusCode).send({ error: error.message });
  });

  return app;
}

// --- Execution queue workers ---------------------------------------------------

const executionQueueRefs: Record<string, import('bullmq').Queue | undefined> = {};

async function startExecutionWorkers(
  connection: Redis,
  closers: Array<() => Promise<void>>
): Promise<void> {
  for (const [chain, queueName] of Object.entries(LP_EXECUTION_QUEUES_BY_CHAIN)) {
    const queue = new Queue(queueName, { connection });
    executionQueueRefs[chain] = queue;
    closers.push(() => queue.close());

    const worker = new Worker(
      queueName,
      async (job) => {
        const mode = await executionMode.resolveMode(chain as 'solana' | 'robinhood-chain');
        if (mode !== 'live') {
          // The queue is durable: between enqueue and run the position may have
          // closed (or never left `building`), so the recorded intent must
          // check the row it was queued for before treating the job as work.
          const payload = job.data as { positionId?: string };
          const position = payload.positionId
            ? await getLpPositionAnyOwner(crossTenantScope('lp execution worker'), payload.positionId)
            : null;
          if (!position || position.state === 'closed' || position.state === 'building') {
            console.log(
              `[lp] execution job ${job.id ?? ''} skipped: position ${payload.positionId ?? '?'} ` +
              `is ${position?.state ?? 'gone'}`
            );
            return { mode, broadcast: false, skipped: true };
          }
          console.log(
            `[lp] execution job ${job.id ?? ''} for ${chain} recorded in ${mode} mode (not broadcast):`,
            JSON.stringify(job.data)
          );
          return { mode, broadcast: false };
        }
        // Live path: the build/rebalance plans from Tracks E/F would be signed
        // and submitted here through the SDK ports. Runtime-untested in this
        // environment (no live-certified chain); fail closed rather than guess.
        throw new Error('live LP submission requires a certified chain runtime; refusing to guess');
      },
      { connection, concurrency: 1 }
    );
    worker.on('error', (error) => console.error(`[lp] ${queueName} worker error`, error));
    closers.push(() => worker.close());
  }
}

// --- Boot ---------------------------------------------------------------------

const connection = new Redis(redisUrl, { maxRetriesPerRequest: null });
const closers: Array<() => Promise<void>> = [];

const app = await buildApp();
await app.listen({ host: '0.0.0.0', port });
console.log(`[lp] API listening on :${port}`);

if (apiKey) {
  console.log('[lp] service-key auth enabled');
}
console.log(`[lp] scan every ${scanCron}, monitor ${monitorCron}, risk ${riskPassCron}, wallets ${walletIndexCron}`);

// Execution workers start BEFORE the cron passes: a monitor pass firing in the
// startup gap would find no queue refs and silently drop its rebalance adds.
await startExecutionWorkers(connection, closers);

cron.schedule(scanCron, () => void runScanGuarded(), { timezone: 'UTC' });
cron.schedule(monitorCron, () => void runMonitorGuarded(), { timezone: 'UTC' });
cron.schedule(riskPassCron, () => void runRiskGuarded(), { timezone: 'UTC' });
cron.schedule(walletIndexCron, () => void runWalletIndexGuarded(), { timezone: 'UTC' });

if (process.env.RUN_ON_STARTUP === 'true') {
  void runScanGuarded();
  void runRiskGuarded();
}

let shuttingDown = false;
async function shutdown(signal: NodeJS.Signals): Promise<void> {
  if (shuttingDown) return;
  shuttingDown = true;
  console.log(`[lp] ${signal} received; shutting down`);
  const results = await Promise.allSettled([...closers.map((closer) => closer()), connection.quit(), app.close()]);
  for (const result of results) {
    if (result.status === 'rejected') {
      console.error('[lp] shutdown error:', result.reason);
      process.exitCode = 1;
    }
  }
}

process.once('SIGINT', shutdown);
process.once('SIGTERM', shutdown);

==> apps/lp/src/monitor/classifier.ts <==
/**
 * Range-state classifier (Track F2) ‚Äî pure, so the monitor's labeling logic is
 * testable against mock data before anything touches a chain.
 *
 * `edgeThreshold` is a fraction of the ladder's width: a position is
 * `near_edge` when the current price sits within that fraction of either
 * boundary, `out_of_range` once it crosses, `active` otherwise. Width-relative
 * (not price-relative) so a 1%-wide scalp and a 60%-wide passive ladder get
 * the same early-warning distance in *ladder* terms.
 */

export type RangeState = 'active' | 'near_edge' | 'out_of_range';

export const DEFAULT_EDGE_THRESHOLD = 0.1;

export function classifyRangeState(input: {
  readonly currentPrice: number;
  readonly rangeLower: number;
  readonly rangeUpper: number;
  readonly edgeThreshold?: number;
}): RangeState {
  const { currentPrice, rangeLower, rangeUpper } = input;
  const edgeThreshold = input.edgeThreshold ?? DEFAULT_EDGE_THRESHOLD;

  if (!Number.isFinite(currentPrice) || currentPrice <= 0) {
    throw new Error(`currentPrice must be positive, got ${currentPrice}`);
  }
  if (!Number.isFinite(rangeLower) || rangeLower <= 0 || !Number.isFinite(rangeUpper) || rangeUpper <= rangeLower) {
    throw new Error('range must satisfy 0 < rangeLower < rangeUpper');
  }
  if (!Number.isFinite(edgeThreshold) || edgeThreshold < 0 || edgeThreshold >= 1) {
    throw new Error(`edgeThreshold must be a fraction in [0, 1), got ${edgeThreshold}`);
  }

  if (currentPrice < rangeLower || currentPrice > rangeUpper) {
    return 'out_of_range';
  }
  const width = rangeUpper - rangeLower;
  const distanceToEdge = Math.min(currentPrice - rangeLower, rangeUpper - currentPrice);
  return distanceToEdge <= width * edgeThreshold ? 'near_edge' : 'active';
}

==> apps/lp/src/monitor/economic-check.ts <==
import { netLpResult } from '../domain/net-lp-result.js';

/**
 * Rebalance economic check (Track F3) ‚Äî pure, built and tested against mock
 * data before any wiring, exactly as the build plan demands.
 *
 * The question is never "is the position out of range?" ‚Äî the classifier
 * answers that ‚Äî but "does re-centering pay for itself?". The inputs are the
 * projection a fee model supplies (live service wires its own; the monitor
 * only consumes):
 *
 *   - `expectedExtraFeesUsd`: fee uplift projected over the horizon from
 *     holding a re-centered position instead of the drifted one.
 *   - `impermanentLossUsd`: IL incurred *by the rebalance itself* (re-centering
 *     realizes the drift), stated positive.
 *   - `gasCostUsd` + `rebalanceCostUsd`: execution cost ‚Äî gas, plus swap
 *     slippage and position churn.
 *   - `inventoryChangeUsd`: signed projected inventory improvement from
 *     re-centering (usually negative: you buy back what drifted away).
 *
 * The verdict reuses the Track A net-LP-result function verbatim ‚Äî the same
 * ledger the wallet PnL screen shows. Rebalance only when the rebalance's own
 * net result is strictly positive.
 */

export interface RebalanceEconomicsInput {
  readonly expectedExtraFeesUsd: number;
  readonly impermanentLossUsd: number;
  readonly gasCostUsd: number;
  readonly rebalanceCostUsd: number;
  readonly inventoryChangeUsd: number;
}

export interface RebalanceEconomics {
  readonly shouldRebalance: boolean;
  readonly netBenefitUsd: number;
  readonly reasons: readonly string[];
}

export function evaluateRebalanceEconomics(
  input: RebalanceEconomicsInput
): RebalanceEconomics {
  const netBenefitUsd = netLpResult({
    feesEarned: input.expectedExtraFeesUsd,
    impermanentLoss: input.impermanentLossUsd,
    gasCost: input.gasCostUsd,
    rebalanceCost: input.rebalanceCostUsd,
    inventoryChange: input.inventoryChangeUsd
  });

  const reasons: string[] = [];
  if (input.expectedExtraFeesUsd <= 0) reasons.push('no-fee-uplift-projected');
  if (netBenefitUsd <= 0) reasons.push('net-benefit-not-positive');

  return {
    shouldRebalance: reasons.length === 0,
    netBenefitUsd,
    reasons
  };
}

==> apps/lp/src/monitor/evm-rebalance.ts <==
import type { LadderPlan } from '../builder/ladder-plan.js';
import type { LpPosition } from '@swat/db';
import type { RebalancePlan, RebalanceStep } from './meteora-rebalance.js';

/**
 * Uniswap v3/v4 rebalance executor (Track F5): close the drifted position
 * (decrease + collect), swap if the new range needs a different leg ratio,
 * remint around the new range ‚Äî all behind a port, per the same pattern as the
 * Meteora side.
 */

export interface EvmRebalancePort {
  buildCloseSteps(position: { readonly onChainPositionAddress: string }): Promise<readonly RebalanceStep[]>;
  buildRemintSteps(plan: LadderPlan, recipient: string): Promise<readonly RebalanceStep[]>;
}

export function buildEvmRebalancePlan(port: EvmRebalancePort, input: {
  readonly position: Pick<LpPosition, 'onChainPositionAddress' | 'poolAddress'>;
  readonly plan: LadderPlan;
  readonly recipient: string;
  readonly signReady: boolean;
}): Promise<RebalancePlan> {
  if (!input.position.onChainPositionAddress) {
    throw new Error('cannot rebalance a position that has no on-chain address yet');
  }
  return (async () => {
    const closeSteps = await port.buildCloseSteps({ onChainPositionAddress: input.position.onChainPositionAddress! });
    const remintSteps = await port.buildRemintSteps(input.plan, input.recipient);

    const swapStep: RebalanceStep = {
      sequence: 0,
      kind: 'swap' as const,
      description: 're-center inventory for the new range (executor computes leg ratio)',
      payload: { poolAddress: input.position.poolAddress }
    };
    // Sequence is position-in-bundle, assigned here so port-returned steps
    // cannot carry stale ordering.
    const steps: RebalanceStep[] = [...closeSteps, swapStep, ...remintSteps].map(
      (step, index) => ({ ...step, sequence: index })
    );

    return { steps, signReady: input.signReady };
  })();
}

==> apps/lp/src/monitor/meteora-rebalance.ts <==
import type { LadderPlan } from '../builder/ladder-plan.js';
import type { LpPosition } from '@swat/db';

/**
 * Meteora rebalance executor (Track F4).
 *
 * The plan doc wraps `rebalanceDlmmPosition`; in SDK terms that is
 * remove-from-the-drifted-position then re-add around the new range, per rung.
 * Both legs live behind a port so the executor is testable with fixtures, and
 * the live port implementation maps steps onto
 * `DLMM.removeLiquidityByStrategy` / `addLiquidityByStrategy` calls.
 */

export interface RebalanceStep {
  readonly sequence: number;
  readonly kind: 'remove-liquidity' | 'collect-fees' | 'add-liquidity' | 'swap' | 'mint-position';
  readonly description: string;
  readonly payload: Record<string, unknown>;
}

export interface MeteoraRebalancePort {
  /** Removes the drifted position's liquidity (and collects its fees). */
  buildRemoveSteps(position: Pick<LpPosition, 'onChainPositionAddress' | 'poolAddress'>): Promise<readonly RebalanceStep[]>;
  /** Re-adds liquidity per the new ladder plan, one step per rung. */
  buildAddSteps(plan: LadderPlan, poolAddress: string, userAddress: string): Promise<readonly RebalanceStep[]>;
}

export interface RebalancePlan {
  readonly steps: readonly RebalanceStep[];
  /** True when the bundle is sign-ready (live mode); false = paper plan only. */
  readonly signReady: boolean;
}

export async function buildMeteoraRebalancePlan(port: MeteoraRebalancePort, input: {
  readonly position: Pick<LpPosition, 'onChainPositionAddress' | 'poolAddress'>;
  readonly plan: LadderPlan;
  readonly userAddress: string;
  readonly signReady: boolean;
}): Promise<RebalancePlan> {
  if (!input.position.onChainPositionAddress) {
    throw new Error('cannot rebalance a position that has no on-chain address yet');
  }
  const removeSteps = await port.buildRemoveSteps(input.position);
  const addSteps = await port.buildAddSteps(input.plan, input.position.poolAddress, input.userAddress);

  let sequence = 0;
  const steps = [...removeSteps, ...addSteps].map((step) => ({
    ...step,
    sequence: sequence++
  }));
  return { steps, signReady: input.signReady };
}

==> apps/lp/src/monitor/monitor-job.ts <==
import type { LpPosition } from '@swat/db';
import type { LpChain } from '@swat/shared';
import { classifyRangeState, type RangeState } from './classifier.js';
import { evaluateRebalanceEconomics, type RebalanceEconomicsInput } from './economic-check.js';

/**
 * The monitor pass (Tracks F1/F2/F6) ‚Äî polls current prices against every open
 * position's range on a schedule, re-labels range states, and ‚Äî only for
 * `near_edge` / `out_of_range` positions ‚Äî runs the economic check and queues
 * a rebalance when it comes back positive and the chain's execution mode allows.
 *
 * The state machine does the safety work: `transitionLpPosition` refuses
 * illegal transitions, so a stale price flip-flop cannot march a position from
 * `closed` back to `active` ‚Äî the monitor just records the refusal.
 */

export type { RangeState };

export interface MonitorPosition {
  readonly id: string;
  readonly chain: LpChain;
  readonly poolAddress: string;
  readonly strategyType: string;
  readonly rangeLower: number;
  readonly rangeUpper: number;
  readonly state: LpPosition['state'];
  readonly onChainPositionAddress: string | null;
  /**
   * Track I / F6 change: the owner's opt-in. The monitor never auto-fires a
   * rebalance for a position whose owner did not opt in ‚Äî it re-labels the
   * state (which IS the recommendation the position manager surfaces) and
   * stops. Manual triggers bypass this flag by design.
   */
  readonly autoRebalance: boolean;
}

export interface PricePollerPort {
  /** Current quote-per-base price for a chain-prefixed pool, or null when unreadable. */
  currentPrice(poolAddress: string): Promise<number | null>;
}

export interface RebalanceEconomicsPort {
  /** The live service's fee model projects these; mock data in tests. */
  estimate(input: {
    readonly position: MonitorPosition;
    readonly currentPrice: number;
    readonly state: RangeState;
  }): Promise<RebalanceEconomicsInput>;
}

export interface MonitorJobPorts {
  readonly pricePoller: PricePollerPort;
  readonly economics: RebalanceEconomicsPort;
  listPositions(chain: LpChain): Promise<readonly MonitorPosition[]>;
  transition(positionId: string, toState: LpPosition['state'], reason: string): Promise<unknown>;
  /** Queues a rebalance for execution (BullMQ LP execution queue for the chain). */
  queueRebalance(input: {
    readonly positionId: string;
    readonly chain: LpChain;
    readonly poolAddress: string;
    readonly netBenefitUsd: number;
  }): Promise<void>;
  readonly edgeThreshold?: number;
}

export interface MonitorPassSummary {
  positionsChecked: number;
  unreadablePrices: number;
  transitions: { positionId: string; from: LpPosition['state']; to: LpPosition['state'] }[];
  rebalancesQueued: number;
  rebalancesDeclined: { positionId: string; reason: string }[];
}

export async function runMonitorPass(ports: MonitorJobPorts, chain: LpChain): Promise<MonitorPassSummary> {
  const positions = await ports.listPositions(chain);
  const summary: MonitorPassSummary = {
    positionsChecked: 0,
    unreadablePrices: 0,
    transitions: [],
    rebalancesQueued: 0,
    rebalancesDeclined: []
  };

  for (const position of positions) {
    summary.positionsChecked += 1;
    const currentPrice = await ports.pricePoller.currentPrice(position.poolAddress);
    if (currentPrice === null) {
      summary.unreadablePrices += 1;
      continue;
    }

    const observed = classifyRangeState({
      currentPrice,
      rangeLower: position.rangeLower,
      rangeUpper: position.rangeUpper,
      edgeThreshold: ports.edgeThreshold
    });
    const currentState = position.state as RangeState;

    // Only the transition is skipped when the observation matches the stored
    // state ‚Äî the economic gate below still runs every pass for near_edge and
    // out_of_range positions, because fee projections move even when the label
    // does not.
    if (observed !== currentState) {
      try {
        await ports.transition(
          position.id,
          observed,
          `monitor: price ${currentPrice} vs range ${position.rangeLower}..${position.rangeUpper} -> ${observed}`
        );
        summary.transitions.push({ positionId: position.id, from: position.state, to: observed });
      } catch (error) {
        // An illegal transition (e.g. racing a close) must not abort the sweep;
        // the history row already holds the refusal context.
        console.error('[lp] monitor transition refused for', position.id, error instanceof Error ? error.message : error);
        continue;
      }
    }
    if (observed !== 'near_edge' && observed !== 'out_of_range') continue;

    // F6 change: no auto-fire by default. Without the owner's opt-in the
    // re-labeled state is the deliverable ‚Äî the position manager shows it as
    // `rebalanceRecommended` and the user decides (manual trigger endpoint).
    if (!position.autoRebalance) {
      summary.rebalancesDeclined.push({
        positionId: position.id,
        reason: 'auto-rebalance-not-opted-in'
      });
      continue;
    }

    // Economic gate: only a strictly positive projection earns a rebalance.
    const economicsInput = await ports.economics.estimate({ position, currentPrice, state: observed });
    const economics = evaluateRebalanceEconomics(economicsInput);
    if (!economics.shouldRebalance) {
      summary.rebalancesDeclined.push({
        positionId: position.id,
        reason: economics.reasons.join(',') || 'not-positive'
      });
      continue;
    }

    await ports.queueRebalance({
      positionId: position.id,
      chain,
      poolAddress: position.poolAddress,
      netBenefitUsd: economics.netBenefitUsd
    });
    summary.rebalancesQueued += 1;
  }

  return summary;
}

==> apps/lp/src/risk/bundled-wallets.ts <==
import { BUNDLED_WALLETS_FLAG, type TokenRiskCheck, type TokenRiskFinding } from './types.js';

/**
 * Bundled/connected-wallet volume detector (Track C2).
 *
 * The pure core is the finding rule: wallets funded from one common source
 * inside the detection window around launch are a bundle. The port in front of
 * it is deliberately dumb ‚Äî gathering the funding graph is chain-specific and
 * best-effort (Solana: transfer signatures around launch; EVM: explorer API) ‚Äî
 * because the heuristic itself is what needs testing.
 */

export interface FundingEdge {
  /** The wallet that received the launch allocation. */
  readonly wallet: string;
  /** The wallet that funded it. */
  readonly fundedFrom: string;
  /** When the funding transfer happened. */
  readonly fundedAt: Date;
}

export interface BundledWalletsFinding {
  readonly flag: typeof BUNDLED_WALLETS_FLAG;
  readonly detail: string;
  /** The funding sources that look like a bundle. */
  readonly sources: readonly string[];
  readonly walletCount: number;
}

const DEFAULT_WINDOW_MS = 30 * 60 * 1000;
const DEFAULT_MIN_BUNDLE_WALLETS = 3;

export function detectBundledWallets(
  edges: readonly FundingEdge[],
  options: { windowMs?: number; minBundleWallets?: number } = {}
): BundledWalletsFinding | null {
  const windowMs = options.windowMs ?? DEFAULT_WINDOW_MS;
  const minBundleWallets = options.minBundleWallets ?? DEFAULT_MIN_BUNDLE_WALLETS;

  if (edges.length === 0) return null;

  const times = edges.map((edge) => edge.fundedAt.getTime());
  const earliest = Math.min(...times);
  const latest = Math.max(...times);

  // The window is about launch-time clustering: all funding edges must fall in
  // one window (not "each source within a window of itself") because the
  // accusation is "these wallets were minted together", which is a statement
  // about the whole allocation batch.
  if (latest - earliest > windowMs) return null;

  const bySource = new Map<string, number>();
  for (const edge of edges) {
    bySource.set(edge.fundedFrom, (bySource.get(edge.fundedFrom) ?? 0) + 1);
  }
  const sources = [...bySource.entries()]
    .filter(([, count]) => count >= minBundleWallets)
    .map(([source]) => source);

  if (sources.length === 0) return null;

  const bundledWalletCount = edges
    .filter((edge) => sources.includes(edge.fundedFrom))
    .map((edge) => edge.wallet)
    .filter((wallet, index, all) => all.indexOf(wallet) === index).length;

  return {
    flag: BUNDLED_WALLETS_FLAG,
    detail: `${bundledWalletCount} wallets funded from ${sources.length} common source(s) within ${Math.round(windowMs / 60_000)}m window`,
    sources,
    walletCount: bundledWalletCount
  };
}

export interface FundingGraphPort {
  /** Funding edges for wallets that received the token around launch. */
  fundingEdges(baseTokenMint: string): Promise<readonly FundingEdge[]>;
}

/** The Track C check: gathers edges through the port, applies the pure rule. */
export function bundledWalletsCheck(port: FundingGraphPort): TokenRiskCheck {
  return async (context) => {
    const edges = await port.fundingEdges(context.baseTokenMint);
    const finding = detectBundledWallets(edges);
    return finding ? [finding] : [];
  };
}

import { stripChainPrefix } from '@swat/shared';
import {
  BLACKLIST_CAPABLE_FLAG,
  EXCESSIVE_TAX_FLAG,
  HOLDER_CONCENTRATION_FLAG,
  HONEYPOT_DETECTED_FLAG,
  LIQUIDITY_UNLOCKED_FLAG,
  MINT_AUTHORITY_FLAG,
  PAUSE_CAPABLE_FLAG,
  UNVERIFIED_SOURCE_FLAG,
  type TokenRiskCheck,
  type TokenRiskFinding
} from './types.js';

/**
 * Robinhood Chain (EVM) risk checks (Tracks C1‚ÄìC4) over an injected viem
 * client. Holder concentration on EVM needs an off-chain holder list (no
 * on-chain enumeration), so it reports through an injected port and stays
 * silent when no explorer is configured ‚Äî unknown must read as "no finding",
 * not as "clean", which the gate complements with the unassessed-pool rule.
 */

export interface EvmTokenPort {
  call<T>(method: string, params: unknown[]): Promise<T>;
  /** Best-effort contract call; resolves null when the call reverts or is missing. */
  tryCall(token: string, signature: 'owner()' | 'paused()' | 'totalSupply()' | 'balanceOf(address)', args?: readonly unknown[]): Promise<string | null>;
}

export interface EvmHolderListPort {
  /** Top-10 balances as base-unit numbers, or null when no explorer is configured. */
  top10Balances(token: string): Promise<readonly number[] | null>;
}

export interface EvmTotalSupplyPort {
  totalSupply(token: string): Promise<number | null>;
}

export interface EvmHoneypotPort {
  checkTokenSecurity(token: string): Promise<{
    isHoneypot: boolean;
    buyTax: number;
    sellTax: number;
    isOpenSource: boolean;
    cannotSellAll: boolean;
  } | null>;
}

export function evmHoneypotCheck(port: EvmHoneypotPort): TokenRiskCheck {
  return async (context) => {
    const token = stripChainPrefix(context.baseTokenMint).toLowerCase();
    const result = await port.checkTokenSecurity(token);
    if (!result) return [];

    const findings: TokenRiskFinding[] = [];
    if (result.isHoneypot || result.cannotSellAll) {
      findings.push({
        flag: HONEYPOT_DETECTED_FLAG,
        detail: 'Honeypot detected: Token cannot be sold or simulated sell failed'
      });
    }

    if (result.buyTax > 0.05 || result.sellTax > 0.05) {
      findings.push({
        flag: EXCESSIVE_TAX_FLAG,
        detail: `Excessive trading tax: buy ${(result.buyTax * 100).toFixed(1)}%, sell ${(result.sellTax * 100).toFixed(1)}%`
      });
    }

    if (!result.isOpenSource) {
      findings.push({
        flag: UNVERIFIED_SOURCE_FLAG,
        detail: 'Contract source code is unverified'
      });
    }

    return findings;
  };
}

export function evmHolderConcentrationCheck(
  holders: EvmHolderListPort,
  supply: EvmTotalSupplyPort
): TokenRiskCheck {
  return async (context) => {
    const token = stripChainPrefix(context.baseTokenMint).toLowerCase();
    const [top10, total] = await Promise.all([
      holders.top10Balances(token),
      supply.totalSupply(token)
    ]);
    if (!top10 || total === null || total <= 0) return [];
    const share = top10.reduce((sum, amount) => sum + amount, 0) / total;
    if (share < 0.5) return [];
    return [
      { flag: HOLDER_CONCENTRATION_FLAG, detail: `top-10 holders own ${(share * 100).toFixed(1)}% of supply` }
    ];
  };
}

export function evmMintAuthorityCheck(port: EvmTokenPort): TokenRiskCheck {
  return async (context) => {
    const token = stripChainPrefix(context.baseTokenMint).toLowerCase();
    const findings: { flag: string; detail: string }[] = [];

    const owner = await port.tryCall(token, 'owner()');
    if (owner !== null) {
      findings.push({ flag: MINT_AUTHORITY_FLAG, detail: 'token contract has an owner (likely upgradeable/mintable)' });
    }
    const paused = await port.tryCall(token, 'paused()');
    if (paused === 'true' || paused === '1') {
      findings.push({ flag: PAUSE_CAPABLE_FLAG, detail: 'trading can be paused by the contract owner' });
    }
    // A blacklist surface is probed through the common selector names; absence
    // of a revert-capable read just means the check stays silent.
    const blacklistedProbe = await port.tryCall(token, 'balanceOf(address)', [token]);
    if (blacklistedProbe !== null && owner !== null) {
      findings.push({ flag: BLACKLIST_CAPABLE_FLAG, detail: 'ownable token exposing balance reads common to blacklist implementations' });
    }
    return findings;
  };
}

export function evmLiquidityLockCheck(
  lpToken: string | null,
  port: EvmTokenPort
): TokenRiskCheck {
  return async (context) => {
    if (!lpToken) return [];
    const [total, deployerBalance] = await Promise.all([
      port.tryCall(lpToken, 'totalSupply()'),
      port.tryCall(lpToken, 'balanceOf(address)', [stripChainPrefix(context.poolAddress)])
    ]);
    const totalSupply = total === null ? null : Number(total);
    const movable = deployerBalance === null ? null : Number(deployerBalance);
    if (totalSupply === null || movable === null || Number.isNaN(totalSupply) || Number.isNaN(movable) || totalSupply <= 0) return [];
    const movableShare = movable / totalSupply;
    if (movableShare < 0.1) return [];
    return [
      { flag: LIQUIDITY_UNLOCKED_FLAG, detail: `${(movableShare * 100).toFixed(1)}% of LP tokens sit in the queried holder balance rather than a locker or burn address` }
    ];
  };
}

==> apps/lp/src/risk/risk-pass.ts <==
import { attachLpPoolRisk, listUnassessedLpPools, type LpPool } from '@swat/db';
import { combineTokenRisk } from './score.js';
import type { TokenRiskCheck, TokenRiskContext } from './types.js';

/**
 * The risk pass (Track C6) ‚Äî attaches a risk score to every scanned pool so
 * nothing reaches the Discover feed without one.
 *
 * Runs after the scan job, over pools whose `risk_score` is still NULL. One
 * pool's check failing must not block the others: the failed pool simply stays
 * unassessed (and therefore unlisted) until the next pass ‚Äî "we have not
 * looked yet" is the honest state, and the feed already excludes it.
 */

export interface RiskPassDeps {
  /** Checks per chain; a pool is assessed by its chain's checks. */
  readonly checksByChain: Record<string, readonly TokenRiskCheck[]>;
  readonly listUnassessed?: typeof listUnassessedLpPools;
  readonly attachRisk?: typeof attachLpPoolRisk;
}

export interface RiskPassSummary {
  readonly assessed: number;
  readonly failed: number;
  /** Pools on a chain with no checks configured ‚Äî left unassessed, never scored 0. */
  readonly skippedNoChecks: number;
}

function toContext(pool: LpPool): TokenRiskContext {
  return {
    chain: pool.chain,
    baseTokenMint: pool.baseTokenMint,
    quoteTokenMint: pool.quoteTokenMint,
    poolAddress: pool.poolAddress
  };
}

export async function runRiskPass(deps: RiskPassDeps): Promise<RiskPassSummary> {
  const listUnassessed = deps.listUnassessed ?? listUnassessedLpPools;
  const attachRisk = deps.attachRisk ?? attachLpPoolRisk;

  const unassessed = await listUnassessed(200);
  let assessed = 0;
  let failed = 0;
  let skippedNoChecks = 0;

  for (const pool of unassessed) {
    const checks = deps.checksByChain[pool.chain];
    if (!checks || checks.length === 0) {
      // A chain with no configured checks has NOT been looked at. Attaching a
      // score of 0 would present "we have not looked yet" as "clean" and put
      // the pool on the feed ‚Äî the exact failure the NULL-vs-0 split on
      // lp_pools.risk_score exists to prevent.
      skippedNoChecks += 1;
      continue;
    }
    try {
      const findings = (await Promise.all(checks.map((check) => check(toContext(pool))))).flat();
      const combined = combineTokenRisk(findings);
      await attachRisk(pool.chain, pool.poolAddress, combined.score, combined.flags);
      assessed += 1;
    } catch (error) {
      failed += 1;
      console.error(
        '[lp] risk check failed for pool',
        pool.poolAddress,
        error instanceof Error ? error.message : error
      );
    }
  }

  return { assessed, failed, skippedNoChecks };
}

import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';

describe('combineTokenRisk', () => {
  it('an empty finding list scores 0 and passes', () => {
    const combined = combineTokenRisk([]);
    expect(combined.score).toBe(0);
    expect(combined.allowed).toBe(true);
  });

  it('weights each triggered flag once and caps at 100', () => {
    const combined = combineTokenRisk([
      { flag: MINT_AUTHORITY_FLAG, detail: 'can mint' },
      { flag: LIQUIDITY_UNLOCKED_FLAG, detail: 'LP movable' },
      { flag: HOLDER_CONCENTRATION_FLAG, detail: 'top-10 heavy' },
      { flag: BUNDLED_WALLETS_FLAG, detail: 'bundle' },
      { flag: FREEZE_AUTHORITY_FLAG, detail: 'can freeze' }
    ]);
    // 50 + 40 + 35 + 25 + 25 = 175 -> capped 100
    expect(combined.score).toBe(100);
    expect(combined.allowed).toBe(false);
  });

  it('a repeated flag from two checkers is counted once', () => {
    const combined = combineTokenRisk([
      { flag: MINT_AUTHORITY_FLAG, detail: 'first' },
      { flag: MINT_AUTHORITY_FLAG, detail: 'second' }
    ]);
    expect(combined.score).toBe(50);
    expect(combined.flags).toEqual([MINT_AUTHORITY_FLAG]);
  });

    const combined = combineTokenRisk(
      [{ flag: LIQUIDITY_UNLOCKED_FLAG, detail: 'LP movable' }],
      { maxScore: 20 }
    );
    expect(combined.score).toBe(40);
    expect(combined.allowed).toBe(false);
    expect(combined.rejectionReasons[0]).toContain('exceeds_gate_20');
  });
});

==> apps/lp/src/risk/score.ts <==
import {
  BLACKLIST_CAPABLE_FLAG,
  BUNDLED_WALLETS_FLAG,
  EXCESSIVE_TAX_FLAG,
  FREEZE_AUTHORITY_FLAG,
  HOLDER_CONCENTRATION_FLAG,
  HONEYPOT_DETECTED_FLAG,
  LIQUIDITY_UNLOCKED_FLAG,
  MINT_AUTHORITY_FLAG,
  PAUSE_CAPABLE_FLAG,
  UNVERIFIED_SOURCE_FLAG,
  type TokenRiskFinding
} from './types.js';

/**
 * Risk score combiner (Track C5) ‚Äî folds the checks' findings into one
 * 0..100 score (higher = riskier) plus a pass/fail gate.
 *
 * Weights live here and nowhere else: a check reports *facts* (flags), this
 * function decides how bad each fact is. The gate is deliberately separate
 * from the score so a caller can show a scored-but-blocked pool in a review
 * surface while the feed hard-excludes it.
 */

const RISK_FLAG_WEIGHTS: Readonly<Record<string, number>> = {
  [HONEYPOT_DETECTED_FLAG]: 100, // Instant kill
  [EXCESSIVE_TAX_FLAG]: 50,
  [UNVERIFIED_SOURCE_FLAG]: 30,
  [HOLDER_CONCENTRATION_FLAG]: 35,
  [BUNDLED_WALLETS_FLAG]: 25,
  [LIQUIDITY_UNLOCKED_FLAG]: 40,
  [MINT_AUTHORITY_FLAG]: 50,
  [FREEZE_AUTHORITY_FLAG]: 25,
  [PAUSE_CAPABLE_FLAG]: 10,
  [BLACKLIST_CAPABLE_FLAG]: 20
};

/** Pools scoring above the gate never reach the Discover feed. */
export const DEFAULT_RISK_GATE_MAX_SCORE = 40;

export interface CombinedTokenRisk {
  /** 0 (no findings) .. 100 (every known risk at full weight). */
  readonly score: number;
  readonly flags: readonly string[];
  readonly allowed: boolean;
  readonly rejectionReasons: readonly string[];
}

export function combineTokenRisk(
  findings: readonly TokenRiskFinding[],
  options: { maxScore?: number } = {}
): CombinedTokenRisk {
  const maxScore = options.maxScore ?? DEFAULT_RISK_GATE_MAX_SCORE;

  // Deduplicate by flag ‚Äî two checkers reporting the same fact must not
  // double-count it. The first detail wins; findings are ordered deterministic
  // by the caller.
  const flags: string[] = [];
  let score = 0;
  for (const finding of findings) {
    if (flags.includes(finding.flag)) continue;
    flags.push(finding.flag);
    score += RISK_FLAG_WEIGHTS[finding.flag] ?? 0;
  }
  score = Math.min(100, score);

  const allowed = score <= maxScore;
  return {
    score,
    flags,
    allowed,
    rejectionReasons: allowed ? [] : [`risk_score_${score}_exceeds_gate_${maxScore}`]
  };
}

==> apps/lp/src/risk/solana-checks.ts <==
import { stripChainPrefix } from '@swat/shared';
import {
  FREEZE_AUTHORITY_FLAG,
  HOLDER_CONCENTRATION_FLAG,
  LIQUIDITY_UNLOCKED_FLAG,
  MINT_AUTHORITY_FLAG,
  type TokenRiskCheck
} from './types.js';

/**
 * Solana risk checks (Tracks C1‚ÄìC4) over a raw JSON-RPC port, matching the
 * indexer's hand-rolled RPC pattern. The SPL mint-account layout parsing is a
 * pure function so the authority flags are testable without a chain.
 */

export interface SolanaRpcPort {
  /** One JSON-RPC call with parsed JSON result (the indexer's heliusRpc shape). */
  call<T>(method: string, params: unknown[]): Promise<T>;
}

/** Top-10 holders of a mint, with the mint's total supply. */
export interface HolderConcentrationSnapshot {
  /** Largest ten token accounts, base-unit amounts. */
  readonly top10Amounts: readonly number[];
  readonly supply: number;
}

export async function fetchHolderConcentration(
  port: SolanaRpcPort,
  mint: string
): Promise<HolderConcentrationSnapshot> {
  const rawMint = stripChainPrefix(mint);
  const [largest, supply] = await Promise.all([
    port.call<{ value: readonly { amount: string }[] }>('getTokenLargestAccounts', [rawMint]),
    port.call<{ value: { amount: string } }>('getTokenSupply', [rawMint])
  ]);
  return {
    top10Amounts: largest.value.map((account) => Number(account.amount)),
    supply: Number(supply.value.amount)
  };
}

/**
 * The finding rule for Track C1: the top-10 share of supply. Returns a finding
 * only above `flagThreshold` ‚Äî a healthy distribution is not a flag.
 */
export function holderConcentrationFinding(
  snapshot: HolderConcentrationSnapshot,
  flagThreshold = 0.5
): { flag: typeof HOLDER_CONCENTRATION_FLAG; detail: string; top10Share: number } | null {
  if (snapshot.supply <= 0) return null;
  const top10Share = snapshot.top10Amounts.reduce((sum, amount) => sum + amount, 0) / snapshot.supply;
  if (top10Share < flagThreshold) return null;
  return {
    flag: HOLDER_CONCENTRATION_FLAG,
    detail: `top-10 holders own ${(top10Share * 100).toFixed(1)}% of supply`,
    top10Share
  };
}

export function holderConcentrationCheck(port: SolanaRpcPort): TokenRiskCheck {
  return async (context) => {
    try {
      const snapshot = await fetchHolderConcentration(port, context.baseTokenMint);
      const finding = holderConcentrationFinding(snapshot);
      return finding ? [finding] : [];
    } catch {
      return [];
    }
  };
}

/** The fields of an SPL mint account this module reasons about. */
export interface SplMintAuthorities {
  readonly mintAuthority: string | null;
  readonly freezeAuthority: string | null;
}

/**
 * Parses an SPL token mint account (82 bytes, base64-encoded by RPC):
 * 0..4 mint-authority COption, 4..36 authority pubkey, 36..44 supply, 44
 * decimals, 45 is-initialized, 46..50 freeze-authority COption, 50..82 freeze
 * pubkey.
 */
export function parseSplMintAuthorities(base64Data: string): SplMintAuthorities {
  const data = Buffer.from(base64Data, 'base64');
  if (data.length < 82) {
    throw new Error(`mint account data is ${data.length} bytes, expected 82`);
  }
  const mintAuthorityOption = data.readUInt32LE(0);
  const freezeAuthorityOption = data.readUInt32LE(46);
  return {
    mintAuthority: mintAuthorityOption === 0 ? null : data.subarray(4, 36).toString('hex'),
    freezeAuthority: freezeAuthorityOption === 0 ? null : data.subarray(50, 82).toString('hex')
  };
}

export async function fetchSplMintAuthorities(
  port: SolanaRpcPort,
  mint: string
): Promise<SplMintAuthorities> {
  const rawMint = stripChainPrefix(mint);
  const info = await port.call<{
    value: { data: readonly [string, string] } | null;
  }>('getAccountInfo', [rawMint, { encoding: 'base64' }]);
  const account = info.value;
  if (!account) {
    throw new Error(`mint account ${mint} not found`);
  }
  return parseSplMintAuthorities(account.data[0]);
}

export function mintAuthorityFindings(authorities: SplMintAuthorities) {
  const findings: { flag: string; detail: string }[] = [];
  if (authorities.mintAuthority !== null) {
    findings.push({ flag: MINT_AUTHORITY_FLAG, detail: 'deployer can mint more supply' });
  }
  if (authorities.freezeAuthority !== null) {
    findings.push({ flag: FREEZE_AUTHORITY_FLAG, detail: 'deployer can freeze token accounts' });
  }
  return findings;
}

export function mintAuthorityCheck(port: SolanaRpcPort): TokenRiskCheck {
  return async (context) => {
    try {
      return mintAuthorityFindings(await fetchSplMintAuthorities(port, context.baseTokenMint));
    } catch {
      return [];
    }
  };
}

export interface LiquidityLockSnapshot {
  /** LP token balances held by known lockers or the burn address, base units. */
  readonly lockedOrBurnedAmount: number;
  /** LP token balances held by ordinary movable wallets, base units. */
  readonly movableAmount: number;
}

const BURN_ADDRESSES = new Set(['1nc1nerator11111111111111111111111111111111', '11111111111111111111111111111111']);

export function liquidityLockFinding(
  snapshot: LiquidityLockSnapshot
): { flag: typeof LIQUIDITY_UNLOCKED_FLAG; detail: string } | null {
  const total = snapshot.lockedOrBurnedAmount + snapshot.movableAmount;
  if (total <= 0) return null;
  const movableShare = snapshot.movableAmount / total;
  // Below 10% movable the LP is effectively locked; above that, the deployer
  // (or an early LP) can pull the rug out from under the ladder.
  if (movableShare < 0.1) return null;
  return {
    flag: LIQUIDITY_UNLOCKED_FLAG,
    detail: `${(movableShare * 100).toFixed(1)}% of LP tokens sit in freely movable wallets`
  };
}

export function liquidityLockCheck(
  port: SolanaRpcPort,
  /** Resolves the pool's classic LP mint, or null ‚Äî DLMM pools have none (positions are NFTs). */
  resolveLpMint: (context: { readonly poolAddress: string }) => string | null = () => null
): TokenRiskCheck {
  return async (context) => {
    const lpMint = resolveLpMint(context);
    if (!lpMint) return [];

    const [largest, supply] = await Promise.all([
      port.call<{ value: readonly { address: string; amount: string }[] }>(
        'getTokenLargestAccounts',
        [lpMint]
      ),
      port.call<{ value: { amount: string } }>('getTokenSupply', [lpMint])
    ]);
    const lockedOrBurnedAmount = largest.value
      .filter((account) => BURN_ADDRESSES.has(account.address))
      .reduce((sum, account) => sum + Number(account.amount), 0);
    // Movable is supply MINUS what was observed locked/burned. Reading the raw
    // supply here (as the buckets were disjoint, this is not) would count every
    // locked LP token as movable and flag even fully-locked pools.
    const snapshot: LiquidityLockSnapshot = {
      lockedOrBurnedAmount,
      movableAmount: Math.max(0, Number(supply.value.amount) - lockedOrBurnedAmount)
    };
    const finding = liquidityLockFinding(snapshot);
    return finding ? [finding] : [];
  };
}

==> apps/lp/src/risk/solana-rpc.ts <==
import type { SolanaRpcPort } from './solana-checks.js';

/**
 * Raw JSON-RPC adapter over HTTP for the Solana risk checks ‚Äî the indexer's
 * `heliusRpc` pattern (fetch with timeout and 429 retry), narrowed to the one
 * method the checks need.
 */

const DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 15_000;
const DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES = 3;

export function createJsonRpcSolanaPort(rpcUrl: string, options: {
  timeoutMs?: number;
  maxRetries?: number;
  fetchImpl?: typeof fetch;
} = {}): SolanaRpcPort {
  const timeoutMs = options.timeoutMs ?? DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS;
  const maxRetries = options.maxRetries ?? DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES;
  const fetchImpl = options.fetchImpl ?? fetch;
  let nextRequestId = 0;

  async function callOnce<T>(method: string, params: unknown[]): Promise<T> {
    const response = await fetchImpl(rpcUrl, {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' },
      signal: AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs),
      body: JSON.stringify({ jsonrpc: '2.0', id: ++nextRequestId, method, params })
    });
    if (!response.ok) {
      throw new Error(`Solana RPC ${method} returned HTTP ${response.status}`);
    }
    const payload = (await response.json()) as { result?: T; error?: { message?: string } };
    if (payload.error) {
      throw new Error(`Solana RPC ${method} failed: ${payload.error.message ?? 'unknown error'}`);
    }
    return payload.result as T;
  }

  return {
    async call<T>(method: string, params: unknown[]): Promise<T> {
      let lastError: unknown;
      for (let attempt = 0; attempt <= maxRetries; attempt += 1) {
        try {
          return await callOnce<T>(method, params);
        } catch (error) {
          lastError = error;
          const status = error instanceof Error && /HTTP 429/.test(error.message) ? 429 : 0;
          if (attempt === maxRetries) break;
          // Exponential backoff; 429 backs off harder.
          const delayMs = status === 429 ? 500 * 2 ** attempt * 2 : 250 * 2 ** attempt;
          await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, delayMs));
        }
      }
      throw lastError;
    }
  };
}

==> apps/lp/src/risk/types.ts <==
import type { LpChain } from '@swat/shared';

/**
 * Token/wallet risk filter shapes (Track C).
 *
 * Every check returns *findings*, not a score: the score combiner (score.ts)
 * is the only place weights live, so a new check never needs the other checks
 * touched, and the flag codes are the same strings persisted to
 * `lp_pools.risk_flags`.
 */

export interface TokenRiskFinding {
  /** Stable machine code, persisted to `lp_pools.risk_flags`. */
  readonly flag: string;
  /** Human-readable evidence for the detail view. */
  readonly detail: string;
}

export interface TokenRiskContext {
  readonly chain: LpChain;
  /** Chain-prefixed base token of the pool being assessed. */
  readonly baseTokenMint: string;
  /** Chain-prefixed quote token. */
  readonly quoteTokenMint: string;
  /** Chain-prefixed pool address. */
  readonly poolAddress: string;
}

/** One async risk check: chain reads in, findings out. Never throws to the caller. */
export type TokenRiskCheck = (context: TokenRiskContext) => Promise<readonly TokenRiskFinding[]>;

export const HOLDER_CONCENTRATION_FLAG = 'holder_concentration';
export const BUNDLED_WALLETS_FLAG = 'bundled_launch';
export const LIQUIDITY_UNLOCKED_FLAG = 'liquidity_unlocked';
export const MINT_AUTHORITY_FLAG = 'mint_authority_active';
export const FREEZE_AUTHORITY_FLAG = 'freeze_authority_active';
export const PAUSE_CAPABLE_FLAG = 'pause_capable';
export const BLACKLIST_CAPABLE_FLAG = 'blacklist_capable';
export const HONEYPOT_DETECTED_FLAG = 'honeypot_detected';
export const EXCESSIVE_TAX_FLAG = 'excessive_tax';
export const UNVERIFIED_SOURCE_FLAG = 'unverified_contract';

async function buildApp(deps: Partial<LpRoutesDeps> = {}) {
  const app = Fastify({ logger: false });
  await (app.register as any)(cookie);
  // Direct calls, not app.register: the auth hook must apply to the routes'
  // sibling scope (same pattern apps/api uses to avoid encapsulation).
  await registerLpAuth(app, { legacyKeyHash: legacyKeyHash('service-key') });
  await registerLpRoutes(app, {
    deployGuard: {
      assertDeployAllowed: async () => ({ allowed: true, reasons: [] })
    },
    executionMode: { resolveMode: async () => 'paper' },
    poolView: {
      getPool: async () => ({ protocol: 'meteora-dlmm', binStep: 50, tickSpacing: null, currentPrice: 100 })
    },
    userAddress: 'solana:user',

      chain: 'solana',

      params: { rangeLower: 0.296, rangeUpper: 0.302, rungCount: 5, distribution: 'spot' },
      rungs: [],
      depositAmount: null,
      source: 'template',
      contextWarning: null
    }),
    queueManualRebalance: async () => undefined,
    ...deps
  });
  return app;
}

        headers: serviceHeaders
      });

      expect(response.json()).toEqual({ removed: true });
      expect(dbMocks.untrackLpWallet).toHaveBeenCalledWith('solana', 'solana:9xQe');

  describe('LP copy trading and new launches routes', () => {

        chain: 'solana',
        venue: 'meteora-dlmm',
        allocatedBudgetUsd: 1000,
        maxCapitalPerPositionUsd: 500,
        status: 'active'
      });

      const response = await app.inject({
        method: 'POST',
        url: '/v1/lp/copy/subscribe',
        headers: sessionHeaders(),
        payload: {
          masterWalletAddress: 'solana:whale1',
          chain: 'solana',
          venue: 'meteora-dlmm',
          allocatedBudgetUsd: 1000,
          maxCapitalPerPositionUsd: 500
        }
      });

      expect(response.statusCode).toBe(200);
      expect(response.json().id).toBe('sub-1');
      expect(dbMocks.createLpCopySubscription).toHaveBeenCalled();
      await app.close();
    });

    it('rejects copy subscription with un-prefixed master address or bad chain', async () => {
      const app = await buildApp();
      await app.ready();

      const badPrefix = await app.inject({
        method: 'POST',
        url: '/v1/lp/copy/subscribe',
        headers: sessionHeaders(),
        payload: {
          masterWalletAddress: 'whale1',
          chain: 'solana',
          venue: 'meteora-dlmm',
          allocatedBudgetUsd: 1000,

        }
      });
      expect(badPrefix.statusCode).toBe(400);

      dbMocks.listLpCopyExecutions.mockResolvedValue([{ id: 'exec-1' }]);

      const app = await buildApp();

      dbMocks.listDiscoverPools.mockResolvedValue([

    });
  });
