    // Defaulting to "open" on a failed lookup would turn every Gamma outage
    // into permission to trade blind.
    const fetchImpl = vi.fn(async () => jsonResponse({ error: 'nope' }, 503)) as typeof fetch;

    await expect(fetchPolymarketMarketState(CONDITION_ID, fetchImpl))
      .rejects.toBeInstanceOf(PolymarketMarketClosedError);
  });

  it('rejects a response for a different condition', async () => {
    const fetchImpl = vi.fn(async () => jsonResponse([
      gammaMarket({ conditionId: `0x${'b'.repeat(64)}` })
    ])) as typeof fetch;

    await expect(fetchPolymarketMarketState(CONDITION_ID, fetchImpl))
      .rejects.toThrow('for requested');
  });

    const derived = parsePolymarketMarketState(
      { conditionId: CONDITION_ID, active: true, closed: true, endDate: FUTURE },
      CONDITION_ID
    );

    expect(derived.acceptingOrders).toBe(false);
    // A closed market with no explicit UMA status is 'unknown', not 'unresolved'.
    expect(derived.resolutionStatus).toBe('unknown');
    expect(() => assertPolymarketMarketTradable(derived)).toThrow('is closed');
  });

  it('refuses a market missing or carrying an invalid end date', () => {
    expect(() => parsePolymarketMarketState(
      { conditionId: CONDITION_ID, active: true, closed: false },
      CONDITION_ID
    )).toThrow('missing its end date');

    expect(() => parsePolymarketMarketState(
      { conditionId: CONDITION_ID, active: true, closed: false, endDate: 'soon' },
      CONDITION_ID
    )).toThrow('invalid end date');
  });

  it('queries the condition and passes an open market through', async () => {
    const fetchImpl = vi.fn(async () => jsonResponse([gammaMarket()])) as unknown as
      typeof fetch & { mock: { calls: unknown[][] } };

    const resolved = await assertPolymarketMarketOpenForSubmission({
      conditionId: CONDITION_ID.toUpperCase(),
      fetchImpl
    });

    expect(resolved.acceptingOrders).toBe(true);

  it('falls back to endDateIso when endDate is absent', () => {

    // and not the other. Reading only `endDate` would report a market with a
    // perfectly good `endDateIso` as untradable.
    const parsed = parsePolymarketMarketState(

  it('reports secondsDelay as null when absent or nonsensical, never as zero', () => {
    // Zero is a positive claim that orders match immediately. Null says we do not
    // know, which is what the S4-M18 staleness rule needs in order to stay honest
    // about how much latency it has actually accounted for.
    const absent = parsePolymarketMarketState(
      { conditionId: CONDITION_ID, active: true, closed: false, endDate: FUTURE },

      CONDITION_ID
    );

    const configured = parsePolymarketMarketState(
      gammaMarket({ secondsDelay: 30 }),
      CONDITION_ID
    );
    expect(configured.secondsDelay).toBe(30);
  });

  it('blocks a submission into a market that stopped accepting orders', async () => {
    // The window this gate exists for: healthy book, market paused between the
    // signal and its execution.
    const fetchImpl = vi.fn(async () => jsonResponse([
      gammaMarket({ acceptingOrders: false })
    ])) as typeof fetch;

    await expect(assertPolymarketMarketOpenForSubmission({
      conditionId: CONDITION_ID,
      fetchImpl
    })).rejects.toThrow('paused for orders');
  });
});

==> apps/trade-executor/src/polymarket-market-state.ts <==
/**
 * Live market-state gate applied immediately before a Polymarket submission.
 *
 * The order book tells you about liquidity; it says nothing about whether the
 * market is still accepting orders, has closed, or has gone to resolution. A
 * depth walk can therefore look perfectly healthy on a market that will reject
 * the order ‚Äî or, worse, on one that is resolving, where an entry is simply a
 * donation.
 *
 * The stored `polymarket_markets` context cannot answer this either: it is
 * written by the indexer's backfill and is exactly as old as the last time that
 * ran. "Not accepting orders" is a state that flips between a signal and its
 * execution, which is precisely the window this gate covers, so the state is
 * re-read live and as close to submission as possible.
 *
 * The CLOB SDK has no market-state call keyed by condition (`fetchMarketInfo`
 * returns fees and tokens only), so this reads the same Gamma endpoint the
 * indexer uses to build market context.
 */

export type PolymarketMarketState = {
  conditionId: string;
  active: boolean;
  closed: boolean;
  acceptingOrders: boolean;
  resolutionStatus: string;
  /**
   * When the market becomes eligible for resolution ‚Äî per `/concepts/resolution`
   * that is what an end date *means*, which is why `polymarket-staleness.ts`
   * (`S4-M18`) uses it as the denominator for time-to-resolution rather than as
   * a display value.
   */
  endDate: Date;
  /**
   * The market's configured matching delay in seconds, or null when it reports
   * none. `/market-data/market-details` ‚Üí *Market Timing* documents
   * `secondsDelay` as the "delay, in seconds, before a newly placed marketable
   * order can match", and `/trading/place-orders` returns an order status of
   * `delayed` for exactly that case.
   *
   * Read here rather than inferred because it is latency *we* incur between
   * submission and any fill, so `S4-M18` charges it against the staleness
   * budget. Typed nullable to match the documented `integer | null`.
   */
  secondsDelay: number | null;
};

export class PolymarketMarketClosedError extends Error {}

const GAMMA_BASE_URL = 'https://gamma-api.polymarket.com';

function normalizeConditionId(value: string): string {
  const normalized = value.trim().toLowerCase();
  if (!/^0x[0-9a-f]{64}$/.test(normalized)) {
    throw new PolymarketMarketClosedError(`Invalid Polymarket condition ID: ${value}`);
  }
  return normalized;
}

/**
 * Parse only the fields this gate decides on. A market whose state cannot be
 * read is treated as untradable rather than assumed open.
 */
export function parsePolymarketMarketState(
  value: unknown,
  expectedConditionId: string
): PolymarketMarketState {
  const conditionId = normalizeConditionId(expectedConditionId);
  if (!value || typeof value !== 'object') {
    throw new PolymarketMarketClosedError(
      `Polymarket market state is unavailable for ${conditionId}`
    );
  }
  const raw = value as Record<string, unknown>;
  const returnedConditionId = raw.conditionId ?? raw.condition_id;
  if (typeof returnedConditionId === 'string'
    && normalizeConditionId(returnedConditionId) !== conditionId) {
    throw new PolymarketMarketClosedError(
      `Polymarket returned market ${returnedConditionId} for requested ${conditionId}`
    );
  }

  const active = raw.active === true;
  const closed = raw.closed === true;
  // Same derivation the indexer uses: an explicit flag wins, otherwise a market
  // is accepting orders only while it is active and not closed.
  const acceptingOrders = typeof raw.acceptingOrders === 'boolean'
    ? raw.acceptingOrders
    : active && !closed;
  const resolutionStatus = typeof raw.umaResolutionStatus === 'string' && raw.umaResolutionStatus.trim()
    ? raw.umaResolutionStatus.trim().toLowerCase()
    : closed ? 'unknown' : 'unresolved';

  // Gamma's market schema carries BOTH `endDate` (`string<date-time> | null`) and
  // `endDateIso` (`string | null`) ‚Äî verified in
  // `/api-reference/markets/get-market-by-id`. Both are nullable, so reading only
  // one can miss a market that populated the other. All four spellings are tried
  // and a market that carries none is still refused: the gate below and the
  // `S4-M18` staleness rule both need this timestamp, and neither may guess it.
  const endDateValue = raw.endDate
    ?? raw.end_date
    ?? raw.endDateIso
    ?? raw.end_date_iso;
  if (typeof endDateValue !== 'string' || !endDateValue.trim()) {
    throw new PolymarketMarketClosedError(
      `Polymarket market ${conditionId} is missing its end date`
    );
  }
  const endDate = new Date(endDateValue);
  if (Number.isNaN(endDate.getTime())) {
    throw new PolymarketMarketClosedError(
      `Polymarket market ${conditionId} returned an invalid end date: ${endDateValue}`
    );
  }

  // A delay that is absent, negative, or not a number is reported as null rather
  // than as zero. Zero is a positive claim that orders match immediately; null
  // says we do not know, which is what `S4-M18` needs to see to stay honest.
  const rawSecondsDelay = raw.secondsDelay ?? raw.seconds_delay;
  const parsedSecondsDelay = typeof rawSecondsDelay === 'number'
    ? rawSecondsDelay
    : typeof rawSecondsDelay === 'string' && rawSecondsDelay.trim()
      ? Number(rawSecondsDelay)
      : Number.NaN;
  const secondsDelay = Number.isFinite(parsedSecondsDelay) && parsedSecondsDelay >= 0
    ? parsedSecondsDelay
    : null;

  return {
    conditionId,
    active,
    closed,
    acceptingOrders,
    resolutionStatus,
    endDate,
    secondsDelay
  };
}

/**
 * Throw unless the market is open for a new order right now.
 *
 * Applied to sells as well as buys: submitting into a market that has stopped
 * accepting orders produces a rejected or ambiguous execution either way, and a
 * resolving market is redeemed rather than sold.
 */
export function assertPolymarketMarketTradable(
  state: PolymarketMarketState,
  now = Date.now()
): void {
  if (state.closed) {
    throw new PolymarketMarketClosedError(
      `Polymarket Protection: market ${state.conditionId} is closed`
    );
  }
  if (!state.active) {
    throw new PolymarketMarketClosedError(
      `Polymarket Protection: market ${state.conditionId} is not active`
    );
  }
  if (!state.acceptingOrders) {
    throw new PolymarketMarketClosedError(
      `Polymarket Protection: market ${state.conditionId} is paused for orders`
    );
  }
  if (state.resolutionStatus !== 'unresolved') {
    throw new PolymarketMarketClosedError(
      `Polymarket Protection: market ${state.conditionId} is resolving (${state.resolutionStatus})`
    );
  }
  if (state.endDate.getTime() <= now) {
    throw new PolymarketMarketClosedError(
      `Polymarket Protection: market ${state.conditionId} ended at ${state.endDate.toISOString()}`
    );
  }
}

/**
 * Read the current market state for a condition. Any transport or shape failure
 * raises ‚Äî an unreadable market is not a tradable one.
 */
export async function fetchPolymarketMarketState(
  conditionId: string,
  fetchImpl: typeof fetch = fetch
): Promise<PolymarketMarketState> {
  const normalized = normalizeConditionId(conditionId);
  const baseUrl = process.env.POLYMARKET_GAMMA_URL ?? GAMMA_BASE_URL;
  const response = await fetchImpl(
    `${baseUrl}/markets?condition_id=${encodeURIComponent(normalized)}`
  );
  if (!response.ok) {
    throw new PolymarketMarketClosedError(
      `Polymarket market state lookup failed with status ${response.status}`
    );
  }
  const payload = await response.json() as unknown;
  const market = Array.isArray(payload) ? payload[0] : payload;
  return parsePolymarketMarketState(market, normalized);
}

/** Fetch and gate in one step, for use immediately before a submission. */
export async function assertPolymarketMarketOpenForSubmission(params: {
  conditionId: string;
  fetchImpl?: typeof fetch;
  now?: number;
}): Promise<PolymarketMarketState> {
  const state = await fetchPolymarketMarketState(params.conditionId, params.fetchImpl);
  assertPolymarketMarketTradable(state, params.now);
  return state;
}

==> apps/trade-executor/src/polymarket-mirror-bound.test.ts <==
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import {
  POLYMARKET_MIRROR_DEFAULT_TOLERANCE_BPS,
  ceilToPolymarketTick,
  floorToPolymarketTick,
  planPolymarketMirrorBound,
  resolvePolymarketMirrorToleranceBps
} from './polymarket-mirror-bound.js';

/**
 * `S4-M16` ‚Äî the mirror's price bound comes from the master's fill.
 *
 * Every case here is a branch that changes what gets submitted, or refuses to
 * submit. None restates the arithmetic: the happy-path assertions are about the
 * *direction* of the grid move and the relationship between the bound and the
 * book, which is where a regression would actually hurt.
 */

const BASE = {
  direction: 'buy' as const,
  masterFillPrice: 0.4,
  bookLimitPrice: 0.4,
  tickSize: 0.01,
  shares: 50,
  minimumShares: 5
};

describe('polymarket mirror price bound', () => {
  it('bounds a buy at the master fill plus tolerance, not at the book level', () => {
    // The book says 0.40 is available. The bound is deliberately *looser* than
    // that so a tick of adverse movement between the walk and the submission
    // still fills ‚Äî but it is anchored on the master's fill, so it can never
    // chase beyond the tolerance.
    const decision = planPolymarketMirrorBound({ ...BASE, toleranceBps: 500 });
    expect(decision.kind).toBe('submit');
    if (decision.kind !== 'submit') return;
    expect(decision.boundPrice).toBe(0.42); // floor(0.40 √ó 1.05 = 0.42) on a 0.01 grid
    expect(decision.boundPrice).toBeGreaterThan(BASE.bookLimitPrice);
    expect(Math.round(decision.trackingBps)).toBe(500);
  });

  it('bounds a sell at the master fill minus tolerance, below the book bid', () => {
    const decision = planPolymarketMirrorBound({
      ...BASE,
      direction: 'sell',
      masterFillPrice: 0.6,
      bookLimitPrice: 0.6,
      toleranceBps: 500
    });
    expect(decision.kind).toBe('submit');
    if (decision.kind !== 'submit') return;
    expect(decision.boundPrice).toBe(0.57); // ceil(0.60 √ó 0.95 = 0.57)
    expect(decision.boundPrice).toBeLessThan(0.6);
  });

  it('floors a buy bound to the grid so the tolerance can only tighten', () => {
    // 0.40 √ó 1.015 = 0.406. Rounding up to 0.41 would pay more than the user's
    // stated tolerance allows, so the grid move goes the other way.
    const decision = planPolymarketMirrorBound({ ...BASE, toleranceBps: 150 });
    expect(decision.kind).toBe('submit');
    if (decision.kind !== 'submit') return;
    expect(decision.boundPrice).toBe(0.4);
    expect(decision.trackingBps).toBeLessThanOrEqual(150);
  });

  it('raises a sell bound to the grid so the tolerance can only tighten', () => {
    // 0.60 √ó 0.985 = 0.591. Rounding down to 0.59 would accept less than the
    // tolerance allows.
    const decision = planPolymarketMirrorBound({
      ...BASE,
      direction: 'sell',
      masterFillPrice: 0.6,
      bookLimitPrice: 0.6,
      toleranceBps: 150
    });
    expect(decision.kind).toBe('submit');
    if (decision.kind !== 'submit') return;
    expect(decision.boundPrice).toBe(0.6);
  });

  it('skips rather than chasing when the book has moved past the master fill', () => {
    // The master bought at 0.40; the cheapest ask is now 0.71. A resting order
    // would "solve" this by waiting, which is the failure FAK exists to avoid.
    const decision = planPolymarketMirrorBound({ ...BASE, bookLimitPrice: 0.71 });
    expect(decision).toMatchObject({ kind: 'skip', code: 'book-moved-past-master-fill' });
    if (decision.kind !== 'skip') return;
    expect(decision.reason).toContain('0.71');
    expect(decision.reason).toContain('0.4');
  });

  it('skips a sell when the bid has fallen below the master fill tolerance', () => {
    const decision = planPolymarketMirrorBound({
      ...BASE,
      direction: 'sell',
      masterFillPrice: 0.6,
      bookLimitPrice: 0.3
    });
    expect(decision).toMatchObject({ kind: 'skip', code: 'book-moved-past-master-fill' });
  });

  it('fails closed when the master fill price was never recorded', () => {
    // The mirror path must not silently fall back to a book-derived bound: that
    // is the un-sanctioned price this item exists to remove.
    for (const masterFillPrice of [null, undefined]) {
      expect(planPolymarketMirrorBound({ ...BASE, masterFillPrice })).toMatchObject({
        kind: 'skip',
        code: 'master-fill-price-unavailable'
      });
    }
  });

  it.each([0, 1, 1.4, -0.2, Number.NaN])(
    'fails closed on a master fill price of %s, which is not an outcome price',
    (masterFillPrice) => {
      expect(planPolymarketMirrorBound({ ...BASE, masterFillPrice })).toMatchObject({
        kind: 'skip',
        code: 'master-fill-price-invalid'
      });
    }
  );

  it('skips a sub-minimum order with a reason instead of rounding it up', () => {
    const decision = planPolymarketMirrorBound({ ...BASE, shares: 4.99, minimumShares: 5 });
    expect(decision).toMatchObject({ kind: 'skip', code: 'below-venue-minimum-order-size' });
    if (decision.kind !== 'skip') return;
    // Actionable, per S4-M24: it names the shortfall and what would fix it.
    expect(decision.reason).toContain('4.99');
    expect(decision.reason).toContain('5-share minimum');
  });

  it('accepts a share count exactly at the venue minimum', () => {
    expect(planPolymarketMirrorBound({ ...BASE, shares: 5, minimumShares: 5 }).kind).toBe('submit');
  });

  it('skips when the tolerance window contains no tick, rather than rounding to one', () => {
    // A master fill of 0.005 on a 0.01-tick market: the whole tolerance window
    // sits between 0 and the first grid line. Rounding up to 0.01 would double
    // the price the user pays.
    const decision = planPolymarketMirrorBound({
      ...BASE,
      masterFillPrice: 0.005,
      bookLimitPrice: 0.01,
      toleranceBps: 100
    });
    expect(decision).toMatchObject({ kind: 'skip', code: 'no-tick-inside-mirror-tolerance' });
  });

  it('skips a sell whose tolerance window rounds up past a valid outcome price', () => {
    // The master sold at 0.99 on a finer grid; this market's grid is 0.1, so the
    // conservative SELL floor ceilings to 1.0 ‚Äî not an outcome price. Reported as
    // a grid problem rather than a book problem, because widening the tolerance is
    // the operator's only lever here.
    const decision = planPolymarketMirrorBound({
      ...BASE,
      direction: 'sell',
      masterFillPrice: 0.99,
      bookLimitPrice: 0.9,
      tickSize: 0.1,
      toleranceBps: 1
    });
    expect(decision).toMatchObject({ kind: 'skip', code: 'no-tick-inside-mirror-tolerance' });
  });

  it('refuses a book level that is off the tick grid rather than bounding against it', () => {
    // Caller-contract violation: the book walk rejects off-grid levels, so this
    // can only mean the bound was derived from something that is not a validated
    // walk. Raising keeps the grid arithmetic below it honest.
    expect(() => planPolymarketMirrorBound({ ...BASE, bookLimitPrice: 0.4237 })).toThrow(
      /off the 0.01 tick grid/
    );
  });

  it('never submits a buy bound below the level the order has to reach', () => {
    // A bound under the book level cannot fill, so submitting it would burn the
    // signal's one-shot claim for nothing. Exhaustive over the documented grid.
    for (const tickSize of [0.1, 0.01, 0.005, 0.0025, 0.001, 0.0001]) {
      for (const masterFillPrice of [0.03, 0.17, 0.4237, 0.5, 0.8891]) {
        for (const toleranceBps of [0, 1, 25, 150, 500]) {
          const bookLimitPrice = floorToPolymarketTick(masterFillPrice, tickSize);
          if (bookLimitPrice <= 0) continue;
          const decision = planPolymarketMirrorBound({
            ...BASE,
            masterFillPrice,
            bookLimitPrice,
            tickSize,
            toleranceBps
          });
          if (decision.kind !== 'submit') continue;
          expect(
            decision.boundPrice,
            `tick ${tickSize} master ${masterFillPrice} tolerance ${toleranceBps}`
          ).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(bookLimitPrice);
          expect(decision.boundPrice).toBeLessThanOrEqual(
            masterFillPrice * (1 + toleranceBps / 10_000) + 1e-9
          );
        }
      }
    }
  });

  it('raises on a misconfigured tolerance instead of silently skipping every trade', () => {
    // A skip here would disable mirroring platform-wide with no operator signal.
    for (const toleranceBps of [-1, 5_001, 1.5, Number.NaN]) {
      expect(() => planPolymarketMirrorBound({ ...BASE, toleranceBps })).toThrow(
        /POLYMARKET_MIRROR_TOLERANCE_BPS/
      );
    }
  });

  it('refuses a tick size that does not divide the price range', () => {
    // 0.03 is not a documented increment and does not tile [0,1); landing a bound
    // on that grid would be a guess.
    expect(() => planPolymarketMirrorBound({ ...BASE, tickSize: 0.03 })).toThrow(
      /does not divide the price range/
    );
  });

  it('reads the tolerance from the environment and falls back to the default', () => {
    expect(resolvePolymarketMirrorToleranceBps({})).toBe(POLYMARKET_MIRROR_DEFAULT_TOLERANCE_BPS);
    expect(resolvePolymarketMirrorToleranceBps({ POLYMARKET_MIRROR_TOLERANCE_BPS: '250' })).toBe(250);
    expect(() =>
      resolvePolymarketMirrorToleranceBps({ POLYMARKET_MIRROR_TOLERANCE_BPS: 'wide' })
    ).toThrow(/POLYMARKET_MIRROR_TOLERANCE_BPS/);
  });

  it('lands on the documented tick grid in both directions', () => {
    expect(floorToPolymarketTick(0.4237, 0.01)).toBeCloseTo(0.42, 10);
    expect(ceilToPolymarketTick(0.4237, 0.01)).toBeCloseTo(0.43, 10);
    expect(floorToPolymarketTick(0.4975, 0.0025)).toBeCloseTo(0.4975, 10);
    expect(ceilToPolymarketTick(0.4975, 0.0025)).toBeCloseTo(0.4975, 10);
  });
});

==> apps/trade-executor/src/polymarket-mirror-bound.ts <==
import { UnrecoverableError } from 'bullmq';

/**
 * The protective price bound a Polymarket mirror submits, derived from the
 * master's fill rather than from our own order-book snapshot (checklist
 * `S4-M16`).
 *
 * **Why the bound cannot come from the book.** `planPolymarketBookOrder` already
 * walks the book and produces `limitPrice` ‚Äî the worst level our size has to
 * reach. Submitting that as `maxPrice` bounds the order against *our snapshot*,
 * which is the wrong reference twice over:
 *
 *   * It is stale. The book we walked is up to `POLYMARKET_MAX_BOOK_AGE_MS` old,
 *     so a bound equal to the walked level turns any adverse tick between the
 *     walk and the submission into a no-fill ‚Äî a missed mirror caused by our own
 *     latency rather than by the market.
 *   * It has no relationship to what the user was promised. A copy trade's
 *     premise is "you get what your master got, within a stated tolerance". A
 *     book-derived bound will happily pay 0.71 for an outcome the master bought
 *     at 0.42, because the book says 0.71 is available. That is chasing, and it
 *     is the single most expensive way to mirror.
 *
 * So the bound is `master fill √ó (1 ¬± tolerance)`, and the book walk keeps its
 * separate job of proving the depth exists.
 *
 * **Why FAK and not a resting order.** A resting order is not mirroring: it
 * converts "buy what he bought" into "maybe buy it later, at a price nobody
 * sanctioned". Worse, on a market heading to resolution a late fill is exactly
 * the stale-signal failure `S4-P15` rejected queuing for ‚Äî the order fills
 * precisely when the outcome is no longer uncertain. `OrderType.FAK` takes the
 * liquidity that exists now and cancels the remainder, which is verified in the
 * live docs (`trading/place-orders` ‚Üí *Market Order Types*) as
 * "fills against the available liquidity immediately and cancels any unfilled
 * remainder", with `maxPrice` documented as preventing "a BUY from crossing a
 * higher price" and `minPrice` the mirror of that for a SELL.
 *
 * **Why off-tick and sub-minimum skip instead of rounding.** Rounding a bound to
 * the grid in the loosening direction pays a price the user never agreed to, and
 * rounding a *size* up sells shares the position does not hold. The venue
 * contract (`trading/place-orders`, verified) is that `min_order_size` is a
 * minimum **share count** and that a price must be a multiple of the market's
 * current tick ‚Äî so an order that cannot be expressed on that grid inside the
 * mirror tolerance is refused with a reason, never nudged until it fits.
 *
 * The one grid move this module *does* make is conservative by construction: a
 * BUY ceiling is floored to the grid and a SELL floor is raised to it, so the
 * selected bound is never looser than the tolerance the user was quoted. That is
 * a tightening, not a re-pricing.
 *
 * Pure and dependency-injected: every input is a parameter, so Stage 4 can pass
 * a per-user tolerance with no call-site change (Standing Rule 2).
 */

/** Default mirror tolerance. Deliberately tighter than the 200 bps book-walk slippage cap. */
export const POLYMARKET_MIRROR_DEFAULT_TOLERANCE_BPS = 150;

export type PolymarketMirrorSkipCode =
  /** The mirror path ran without the master's fill price. Fails closed. */
  | 'master-fill-price-unavailable'
  /** A price outside (0,1) is not an outcome price, so no bound can be derived. */
  | 'master-fill-price-invalid'
  /** The book has already moved past what the master's fill justifies paying. */
  | 'book-moved-past-master-fill'
  /** No price on the market's tick grid sits inside the mirror tolerance. */
  | 'no-tick-inside-mirror-tolerance'
  /** Below the venue's minimum share count after the documented downward rounding. */
  | 'below-venue-minimum-order-size';

export interface PolymarketMirrorBoundSubmit {
  readonly kind: 'submit';
  /** `maxPrice` for a BUY, `minPrice` for a SELL. Always on the tick grid. */
  readonly boundPrice: number;
  readonly masterFillPrice: number;
  readonly toleranceBps: number;
  /**
   * Signed distance from the master's fill to our bound, in basis points, and
   * positive when the bound is worse for the user than the master's fill. This
   * is the pre-trade half of the tracking difference `S4-M23` surfaces.
   */
  readonly trackingBps: number;
}

export interface PolymarketMirrorBoundSkip {
  readonly kind: 'skip';
  readonly code: PolymarketMirrorSkipCode;
  /** Operator- and user-readable, and specific enough to act on. */
  readonly reason: string;
}

export type PolymarketMirrorBoundDecision =
  | PolymarketMirrorBoundSubmit
  | PolymarketMirrorBoundSkip;

export interface PolymarketMirrorBoundInput {
  readonly direction: 'buy' | 'sell';
  /** The master's realized price for the event being mirrored. */
  readonly masterFillPrice: number | null | undefined;
  /** Worst level the requested size must reach, from `planPolymarketBookOrder`. */
  readonly bookLimitPrice: number;
  /** The market's current tick size, as reported by the order book. */
  readonly tickSize: number;
  /** Share count after the venue's documented round-down. */
  readonly shares: number;
  /** `min_order_size` from the order book ‚Äî a share count, not a notional. */
  readonly minimumShares: number;
  readonly toleranceBps?: number;
}

const TOLERANCE_EPSILON = 1e-9;

function ticksPerUnit(tickSize: number): number {
  if (!Number.isFinite(tickSize) || tickSize <= 0 || tickSize >= 1) {
    throw new UnrecoverableError(`Polymarket tick size ${tickSize} is not a valid price increment`);
  }
  const reciprocal = 1 / tickSize;
  const rounded = Math.round(reciprocal);
  // Every documented increment (0.1, 0.01, 0.005, 0.0025, 0.001, 0.0001) divides
  // 1 exactly. An increment that does not means the grid is not the one this
  // module knows how to land on, so it refuses rather than guessing.
  if (rounded < 1 || Math.abs(reciprocal - rounded) > 1e-6) {
    throw new UnrecoverableError(`Polymarket tick size ${tickSize} does not divide the price range`);
  }
  return rounded;
}

/** Largest grid price at or below `price`. */
export function floorToPolymarketTick(price: number, tickSize: number): number {
  const scale = ticksPerUnit(tickSize);
  return Math.floor(price * scale + 1e-6) / scale;
}

/** Smallest grid price at or above `price`. */
export function ceilToPolymarketTick(price: number, tickSize: number): number {
  const scale = ticksPerUnit(tickSize);
  return Math.ceil(price * scale - 1e-6) / scale;
}

function resolveToleranceBps(value: number | undefined): number {
  const toleranceBps = value ?? POLYMARKET_MIRROR_DEFAULT_TOLERANCE_BPS;
  // A misconfigured tolerance is an operator error, not a market condition.
  // Returning a skip would silently disable mirroring for every trade, so this
  // raises instead.
  if (!Number.isInteger(toleranceBps) || toleranceBps < 0 || toleranceBps > 5_000) {
    throw new UnrecoverableError(
      'POLYMARKET_MIRROR_TOLERANCE_BPS must be an integer from 0 to 5000'
    );
  }
  return toleranceBps;
}

export function planPolymarketMirrorBound(
  input: PolymarketMirrorBoundInput
): PolymarketMirrorBoundDecision {
  const toleranceBps = resolveToleranceBps(input.toleranceBps);

  if (input.masterFillPrice === null || input.masterFillPrice === undefined) {
    return {
      kind: 'skip',
      code: 'master-fill-price-unavailable',
      reason: 'the price the tracked wallet filled at is not recorded, so this copy has no reference price to bound against'
    };
  }
  const masterFillPrice = input.masterFillPrice;
  if (!Number.isFinite(masterFillPrice) || masterFillPrice <= 0 || masterFillPrice >= 1) {
    return {
      kind: 'skip',
      code: 'master-fill-price-invalid',
      reason: `the tracked wallet's recorded fill price ${masterFillPrice} is not a valid outcome price between 0 and 1`
    };
  }
  if (!Number.isFinite(input.bookLimitPrice) || input.bookLimitPrice <= 0 || input.bookLimitPrice >= 1) {
    throw new UnrecoverableError(
      `Polymarket book limit price ${input.bookLimitPrice} is not a valid outcome price`
    );
  }
  // Caller contract, not a market condition: `planPolymarketBookOrder` already
  // refuses a book whose levels are off the grid, so an off-grid level here means
  // the bound was derived from something other than a validated book walk. Stated
  // as a precondition because the grid arithmetic below relies on it ‚Äî with an
  // on-grid book level, a floored BUY ceiling can never land under the level the
  // order must reach, which is what makes that branch unnecessary rather than
  // untested.
  if (
    Math.abs(input.bookLimitPrice - floorToPolymarketTick(input.bookLimitPrice, input.tickSize))
    > TOLERANCE_EPSILON
  ) {
    throw new UnrecoverableError(
      `Polymarket book limit price ${input.bookLimitPrice} is off the ${input.tickSize} tick grid`
    );
  }
  if (!Number.isFinite(input.shares) || input.shares <= 0) {
    throw new UnrecoverableError('Polymarket mirror share quantity must be positive');
  }
  if (!Number.isFinite(input.minimumShares) || input.minimumShares <= 0) {
    throw new UnrecoverableError('Polymarket minimum order size must be positive');
  }

  // Checked before the price work so a sub-minimum order reports the reason the
  // user can act on (raise the per-trade size) rather than a price complaint.
  if (input.shares + 1e-9 < input.minimumShares) {
    return {
      kind: 'skip',
      code: 'below-venue-minimum-order-size',
      reason: `this copy comes to ${input.shares} shares, below Polymarket's ${input.minimumShares}-share minimum for this market; a larger per-trade size would clear it`
    };
  }

  const toleranceFactor = toleranceBps / 10_000;
  const tolerated = input.direction === 'buy'
    ? masterFillPrice * (1 + toleranceFactor)
    : masterFillPrice * (1 - toleranceFactor);

  // Grid selection, always in the direction that cannot loosen the bound: a BUY
  // ceiling floors down, a SELL floor ceilings up. Neither can pay a worse price
  // than the tolerance the user was quoted.
  const boundPrice = input.direction === 'buy'
    ? floorToPolymarketTick(tolerated, input.tickSize)
    : ceilToPolymarketTick(tolerated, input.tickSize);

  // The market's grid cannot express a mirror of this fill at all ‚Äî the whole
  // tolerance window falls between 0 and the first grid line, or above the last.
  // Checked before the book comparison because it is a property of the market and
  // the master's fill, true no matter where the book sits, and the operator's fix
  // is different: widen the tolerance, not wait for the book.
  if (boundPrice <= 0 || boundPrice >= 1) {
    return {
      kind: 'skip',
      code: 'no-tick-inside-mirror-tolerance',
      reason: `no price on this market's ${input.tickSize} tick grid sits inside the ${toleranceBps} bps mirror tolerance around ${masterFillPrice}; rounding to the grid would change the price you pay`
    };
  }

  // The book has run away from the bound we are willing to sign. This is the case
  // a resting order would "solve" by waiting, which is the failure the FAK
  // decision exists to prevent, so it is a skip rather than a queued order.
  if (input.direction === 'buy' && input.bookLimitPrice > boundPrice + TOLERANCE_EPSILON) {
    return {
      kind: 'skip',
      code: 'book-moved-past-master-fill',
      reason: `the cheapest available price ${input.bookLimitPrice} is above the ${toleranceBps} bps mirror tolerance around the tracked wallet's fill at ${masterFillPrice}`
    };
  }
  if (input.direction === 'sell' && input.bookLimitPrice < boundPrice - TOLERANCE_EPSILON) {
    return {
      kind: 'skip',
      code: 'book-moved-past-master-fill',
      reason: `the best available price ${input.bookLimitPrice} is below the ${toleranceBps} bps mirror tolerance around the tracked wallet's fill at ${masterFillPrice}`
    };
  }

  const trackingBps = input.direction === 'buy'
    ? ((boundPrice / masterFillPrice) - 1) * 10_000
    : (1 - (boundPrice / masterFillPrice)) * 10_000;

  return { kind: 'submit', boundPrice, masterFillPrice, toleranceBps, trackingBps };
}

/**
 * Read the mirror tolerance from the environment.
 *
 * Separate from `planPolymarketMirrorBound` so the planner stays pure and a
 * per-user tolerance can be threaded through the same parameter later.
 */
export function resolvePolymarketMirrorToleranceBps(
  env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = process.env
): number {
  const raw = env.POLYMARKET_MIRROR_TOLERANCE_BPS?.trim();
  if (!raw) return POLYMARKET_MIRROR_DEFAULT_TOLERANCE_BPS;
  return resolveToleranceBps(Number(raw));
}

describe('polymarket staleness at the submission boundary (S4-M18)', () => {

      closed: false,
      acceptingOrders: true,
      resolutionStatus: 'unresolved',
      endDate: new Date(NOW + ms),
      secondsDelay: null
    });
  }

  // The item's whole claim, pinned at the wiring rather than in the library:
  // `polymarket-staleness.test.ts` proves the budget curve, this proves a real
  // order is measured against it. The same signal age must survive on a
  // long-dated market and be refused near resolution.
  it('accepts a signal age on a long-dated market that it refuses near resolution', async () => {
    const client = clientWithBook(orderBook({ asks: [{ price: '0.40', size: '1000' }] }));
    const signalAt = new Date(NOW - 5 * MINUTE);

    marketResolvingIn(30 * 24 * 60 * MINUTE);
    await triggerPolymarket({
      signalId: 'sig-fresh-long-dated',
      tokenID: TOKEN_ID,
      spendAmountUsd: 20,
      direction: 'buy',
      mirror: { sourceTradeId: 'src-1', masterFillPriceUsd: 0.44, toleranceBps: 500 },
      sourceEventAt: signalAt,
      now: () => NOW
    });
    expect(client.createMarketOrder).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);

    vi.clearAllMocks();
    const nearClient = clientWithBook(orderBook({ asks: [{ price: '0.40', size: '1000' }] }));
    actionMocks.fetchBalanceAllowance.mockResolvedValue({ balance: '1000000000', allowances: {} });
    dbMocks.query.mockResolvedValue([]);
    marketResolvingIn(10 * MINUTE);

    await expect(triggerPolymarket({
      signalId: 'sig-stale-near-resolution',
      tokenID: TOKEN_ID,
      spendAmountUsd: 20,
      direction: 'buy',
      mirror: { sourceTradeId: 'src-2', masterFillPriceUsd: 0.44, toleranceBps: 500 },
      sourceEventAt: signalAt,
      now: () => NOW
    })).rejects.toThrow(/Polymarket Protection/);

    // Nothing may reach the venue once the budget is exceeded.
    expect(nearClient.createMarketOrder).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
    expect(nearClient.postOrder).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  });

  it('carries the reason code, so the skip is actionable rather than generic', async () => {
    // S4-M24: a skip reason has to name what happened. The marker is what makes
    // the executor record a skipped trade instead of failing the job and retrying
    // into an even older signal.
    clientWithBook(orderBook({ asks: [{ price: '0.40', size: '1000' }] }));
    marketResolvingIn(10 * MINUTE);

    await expect(triggerPolymarket({
      signalId: 'sig-stale-code',
      tokenID: TOKEN_ID,
      spendAmountUsd: 20,
      direction: 'buy',
      mirror: { sourceTradeId: 'src-3', masterFillPriceUsd: 0.44, toleranceBps: 500 },
      sourceEventAt: new Date(NOW - 5 * MINUTE),
      now: () => NOW
    })).rejects.toThrow(/signal-age-exceeds/);
  });

  it('leaves an order with no source event alone', async () => {
    // A manual execute or a stop-loss exit has no master and no source event.
    // Gating those on a timestamp that does not exist would refuse every one of
    // them, which is why `sourceEventAt` is optional rather than defaulted.
    const client = clientWithBook(orderBook({ asks: [{ price: '0.40', size: '1000' }] }));
    marketResolvingIn(10 * MINUTE);

    await triggerPolymarket({
      signalId: 'sig-manual-no-source',
      tokenID: TOKEN_ID,
      spendAmountUsd: 20,
      direction: 'buy',
      now: () => NOW
    });

    expect(client.createMarketOrder).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1);
  });
});

import { AssetType } from '@polymarket/bindings/clob';
import { beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';

// `polymarket.ts` constructs an ethers.Wallet at module scope, so this must be a
// well-formed 32-byte key. Deliberately a throwaway constant, never funded.

const dbMocks = vi.hoisted(() => ({
  query: vi.fn(),
  recordCopyExecutionEvidence: vi.fn(),
  transitionCopyExecution: vi.fn()

  fetchBalanceAllowance: vi.fn(),
  fetchBuilderFeeRates: vi.fn()

// The live market-state read has its own suite in polymarket-market-state.test.ts.

const {
  planPolymarketBookOrder,
  setPolymarketClientForTesting,
  setPolymarketLiveReadiness,
  triggerPolymarket
} = await import('./polymarket.js');

/**
 * Binary + neg-risk entry/exit matrix (checklist S3-18 remainder).
 *
 * A neg-risk market signs against a different EIP-712 verifying contract than a
 * standard one ‚Äî `0xE1111800...` versus `0xe2222d27...` per `trading/place-orders`.
 * The SDK makes that choice from the token; `PrepareMarketOrderRequest` has no
 * field through which a caller could override it. Duplicating the mapping on our
 * side would therefore be unreachable at best and silently divergent if
 * Polymarket ever remapped it, which is exactly the failure the redemption sweep
 * already guards against for the collateral adapter. Both exchange addresses are
 * pinned and attested once at startup (`polymarket-startup.ts`), not chosen per
 * order.
 *
 * So the matrix asserts an asymmetry: **neg-risk is a no-op axis** ‚Äî the plan and
 * the signed request must be byte-identical to the binary case ‚Äî while **entry
 * versus exit is the real axis**, differing in units, balance source, protective
 * bound, and required inputs.
 */

const TOKEN_ID = 'token-matrix';
const BUILDER_CODE = `0x${'a'.repeat(64)}`;
const CONDITION_ID = `0x${'1'.repeat(64)}`;

// 20 USD at 0.40 and 50 shares at 0.60 both come to 50 shares, so an entry and an
// exit can be compared without a quantity difference confounding the direction.
const ENTRY_USD = 20;
const EXIT_SHARES = 50;
const ENTRY_ASKS = [{ price: '0.40', size: '1000' }];
const EXIT_BIDS = [{ price: '0.60', size: '1000' }];

const MARKETS = [
  { label: 'binary', negRisk: false },
  { label: 'neg-risk', negRisk: true }
] as const;

// Keys a caller could plausibly reach for when hand-rolling the neg-risk split.
// None of them exists on `PrepareMarketOrderRequest`; sending one would be a
// silent no-op the venue never sees.
const VENUE_SELECTION_KEYS = [
  'negRisk',
  'neg_risk',
  'exchange',
  'exchangeAddress',
  'adapter',
  'verifyingContract'
];

type Level = { price: string; size: string };

function paginator(items: unknown[]) {
  const page = { items, hasMore: false };
  return {
    firstPage: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(page),
    from: vi.fn(),
    async *[Symbol.asyncIterator]() {
      yield page;
    }
  };
}

function orderBook(params: {
  negRisk: boolean;
  asks?: Level[];
  bids?: Level[];
  tickSize?: string;
  timestamp?: number;
}) {
  return {
    conditionId: CONDITION_ID,
    tokenId: TOKEN_ID,
    timestamp: params.timestamp ?? Date.now(),
    asks: params.asks ?? [],
    bids: params.bids ?? [],
    minOrderSize: '1',
    tickSize: params.tickSize ?? '0.01',
    negRisk: params.negRisk,
    hash: 'a'.repeat(40)
  } as Parameters<typeof planPolymarketBookOrder>[0];
}

function createMockClient() {
  return {
    fetchOrderBook: vi.fn(),
    listOpenOrders: vi.fn().mockReturnValue(paginator([])),
    createMarketOrder: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue({ builder: BUILDER_CODE }),
    postOrder: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue({
      ok: true,
      orderId: 'order-id',
      status: 'live',
      transactionsHashes: [],
      tradeIds: []
    }),
    waitForOrderFillSettlement: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue([]),
    listAccountTrades: vi.fn().mockReturnValue(paginator([]))
  };
}

type MockClient = ReturnType<typeof createMockClient>;

function installClient(mock: MockClient): void {
  setPolymarketClientForTesting(
    mock as unknown as Parameters<typeof setPolymarketClientForTesting>[0]
  );
}

function clientWithBook(params: {
  negRisk: boolean;
  asks?: Level[];
  bids?: Level[];
  tickSize?: string;
}): MockClient {
  const mock = createMockClient();
  mock.fetchOrderBook.mockResolvedValue(orderBook(params));
  installClient(mock);
  return mock;
}

function configureConfirmedFill(params: {
  client: MockClient;
  price: string;
  size: string;
  side: 'BUY' | 'SELL';
}) {
  const transactionHash = `0x${'2'.repeat(64)}`;
  params.client.postOrder.mockResolvedValue({
    ok: true,
    orderId: 'order-id',
    status: 'matched',
    transactionsHashes: [],
    tradeIds: ['trade-id']
  });
  params.client.waitForOrderFillSettlement.mockResolvedValue([transactionHash]);
  params.client.listAccountTrades.mockReturnValue(paginator([{
    id: 'trade-id',
    conditionId: CONDITION_ID,
    tokenId: TOKEN_ID,
    owner: 'owner',
    takerOrderId: 'order-id',
    side: params.side,
    traderSide: 'TAKER',
    price: params.price,
    size: params.size,
    outcome: 'Yes',
    status: 'CONFIRMED',
    feeRateBps: '0',
    bucketIndex: 0,
    transactionHash,
    makerOrders: [],
    matchedAt: new Date().toISOString(),
    updatedAt: new Date().toISOString()
  }]));
}

async function submittedOrderRequest(
  negRisk: boolean,
  direction: 'buy' | 'sell'
): Promise<Record<string, unknown>> {
  const mock = clientWithBook({ negRisk, asks: ENTRY_ASKS, bids: EXIT_BIDS });
  await triggerPolymarket({
    signalId: `sig-${direction}-${String(negRisk)}`,
    tokenID: TOKEN_ID,
    spendAmountUsd: ENTRY_USD,
    direction,
    ...(direction === 'sell' ? { sellShares: EXIT_SHARES } : {})
  });
  return mock.createMarketOrder.mock.calls[0]![0] as Record<string, unknown>;
}

describe('polymarket binary and neg-risk entry-exit matrix', () => {
  describe('neg-risk is not a decision this code makes', () => {
    it.each([
      { direction: 'buy' as const, amount: ENTRY_USD },
      { direction: 'sell' as const, amount: EXIT_SHARES }
    ])('plans a $direction identically on a binary and a neg-risk book', ({ direction, amount }) => {
      // Same levels, same size, one flag apart. If anyone ever branches the depth
      // walk, the slippage cap, or the rounding on `negRisk`, these diverge.
      const now = Date.now();
      const levels = { asks: ENTRY_ASKS, bids: EXIT_BIDS, timestamp: now };
      const binary = planPolymarketBookOrder(
        orderBook({ negRisk: false, ...levels }), direction, amount, 200, now
      );
      const negRisk = planPolymarketBookOrder(
        orderBook({ negRisk: true, ...levels }), direction, amount, 200, now
      );

      expect(negRisk).toEqual(binary);
    });

    it.each([
      {
        direction: 'buy' as const,
        keys: ['amount', 'builderCode', 'maxPrice', 'maxSpend', 'orderType', 'side', 'tokenId']
      },
      {
        direction: 'sell' as const,
        keys: ['builderCode', 'minPrice', 'orderType', 'shares', 'side', 'tokenId']
      }
    ])('signs an identical $direction request on both market kinds', async ({ direction, keys }) => {
      const binary = await submittedOrderRequest(false, direction);
      const negRisk = await submittedOrderRequest(true, direction);

      // The regression guard. An added `negRisk`/`exchange`/`adapter` key would be
      // dropped on the floor by the SDK while reading as though we had handled the
      // split ourselves.
      expect(Object.keys(negRisk).sort()).toEqual(keys);
      for (const forbidden of VENUE_SELECTION_KEYS) {
        expect(negRisk).not.toHaveProperty(forbidden);
      }
      expect(negRisk).toEqual(binary);
    });
  });

  describe.each(MARKETS)('$label market', ({ negRisk }) => {
    it('enters by spending USD off ask depth, capped by maxPrice', async () => {
      const client = clientWithBook({ negRisk, asks: ENTRY_ASKS });
      configureConfirmedFill({ client, price: '0.40', size: '50', side: 'BUY' });

      const result = await triggerPolymarket({
        signalId: 'sig-entry',
        tokenID: TOKEN_ID,
        spendAmountUsd: ENTRY_USD,
        direction: 'buy'
      });

      // An entry spends collateral, so the balance read is the account's pUSD, not
      // a per-outcome holding.
      expect(actionMocks.fetchBalanceAllowance).toHaveBeenCalledWith(client, {
        assetType: AssetType.COLLATERAL
      });
      expect(client.createMarketOrder).toHaveBeenCalledWith({
        tokenId: TOKEN_ID,
        side: OrderSide.BUY,
        amount: ENTRY_USD,
        maxSpend: ENTRY_USD,
        maxPrice: 0.4,
        orderType: OrderType.FAK,
        builderCode: BUILDER_CODE
      });
      expect(marketStateMocks.assertPolymarketMarketOpenForSubmission)
        .toHaveBeenCalledWith(expect.objectContaining({ conditionId: CONDITION_ID }));
      expect(result.executionStatus).toBe('filled');
      expect(result.shares).toBe(50);
      expect(result.spendAmountUsd).toBe(20);
      // An entry is requested in dollars and discovers its share count; the exit
      // below is the mirror image.
      expect(result.requestedSpendAmountUsd).toBe(ENTRY_USD);
      expect(result.requestedShares).toBe(50);
    });

    it('exits by disposing shares off bid depth, floored by minPrice', async () => {
      const client = clientWithBook({ negRisk, bids: EXIT_BIDS });
      configureConfirmedFill({ client, price: '0.60', size: '50', side: 'SELL' });

      const result = await triggerPolymarket({
        signalId: 'sig-exit',
        tokenID: TOKEN_ID,
        spendAmountUsd: ENTRY_USD,
        direction: 'sell',
        sellShares: EXIT_SHARES
      });

      // An exit disposes of a specific outcome token, so the balance that bounds
      // it is that token's, keyed by id ‚Äî a neg-risk event has one such holding
      // per outcome and they are not fungible with each other.
      expect(actionMocks.fetchBalanceAllowance).toHaveBeenCalledWith(client, {
        assetType: AssetType.CONDITIONAL,
        tokenId: TOKEN_ID
      });
      expect(client.createMarketOrder).toHaveBeenCalledWith({
        tokenId: TOKEN_ID,
        side: OrderSide.SELL,
        shares: EXIT_SHARES,
        minPrice: 0.6,
        orderType: OrderType.FAK,
        builderCode: BUILDER_CODE
      });
      expect(marketStateMocks.assertPolymarketMarketOpenForSubmission)
        .toHaveBeenCalledWith(expect.objectContaining({ conditionId: CONDITION_ID }));
      expect(result.executionStatus).toBe('filled');
      expect(result.shares).toBe(50);
      expect(result.spendAmountUsd).toBe(30);
      // Requested in shares, with the dollar figure derived ‚Äî the inverse of the
      // entry.
      expect(result.requestedShares).toBe(EXIT_SHARES);
      expect(result.requestedSpendAmountUsd).toBe(30);
    });

    it('reads the same requested amount as dollars on entry and shares on exit', async () => {
      // Depth is priced in USD (size √ó price) on the ask side and in shares on the
      // bid side, so the same number means different things by direction. Feeding
      // both sides the same book and the same `10` proves the units are not
      // interchangeable.
      const now = Date.now();
      const book = orderBook({
        negRisk,
        asks: [{ price: '0.50', size: '10' }, { price: '0.52', size: '10' }],
        bids: [{ price: '0.52', size: '10' }, { price: '0.50', size: '10' }],
        timestamp: now
      });

      const entry = planPolymarketBookOrder(book, 'buy', 10, 500, now);
      const exit = planPolymarketBookOrder(book, 'sell', 10, 500, now);

      // $10 clears the 0.50 level ($5) and part of 0.52, so the entry crosses two
      // levels and pays 400 bps of slippage.
      expect(entry.estimatedNotionalUsd).toBeCloseTo(10);
      expect(entry.estimatedShares).toBe(19.61);
      expect(entry.limitPrice).toBe(0.52);
      expect(entry.slippageBps).toBeCloseTo(400);
      // 10 shares clear the top bid alone, so the exit never leaves the best level.
      expect(exit.estimatedShares).toBe(10);
      expect(exit.estimatedNotionalUsd).toBeCloseTo(5.2);
      expect(exit.limitPrice).toBe(0.52);
      expect(exit.slippageBps).toBeCloseTo(0);
    });

    it('refuses 0.98 as an entry while accepting it as an exit', async () => {
      // The bounds are directional, not symmetric: paying 0.98 for a share risks
      // 0.98 to win 0.02, while selling at 0.98 is the good end of that trade.
      clientWithBook({ negRisk, asks: [{ price: '0.98', size: '1000' }] });
      await expect(triggerPolymarket({
        signalId: 'sig-entry-bound',
        tokenID: TOKEN_ID,
        spendAmountUsd: ENTRY_USD,
        direction: 'buy'
      })).rejects.toThrow('outside safe bounds');

      const exitClient = clientWithBook({ negRisk, bids: [{ price: '0.98', size: '1000' }] });
      await triggerPolymarket({
        signalId: 'sig-exit-high',
        tokenID: TOKEN_ID,
        spendAmountUsd: ENTRY_USD,
        direction: 'sell',
        sellShares: 20
      });

      expect(exitClient.createMarketOrder).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
        expect.objectContaining({ side: OrderSide.SELL, minPrice: 0.98 })
      );
    });

    it('refuses 0.005 as an exit while accepting it as an entry', async () => {
      // Mirror of the case above. A 0.005 bid is close enough to worthless that
      // exiting there is usually a fat-finger or a dead book; entering there is a
      // cheap lottery ticket, which is a position the executor is allowed to take.
      clientWithBook({
        negRisk,
        tickSize: '0.001',
        bids: [{ price: '0.005', size: '10000' }]
      });
      await expect(triggerPolymarket({
        signalId: 'sig-exit-bound',
        tokenID: TOKEN_ID,
        spendAmountUsd: ENTRY_USD,
        direction: 'sell',
        sellShares: 20
      })).rejects.toThrow('outside safe bounds');

      const entryClient = clientWithBook({
        negRisk,
        tickSize: '0.001',
        asks: [{ price: '0.005', size: '10000' }]
      });
      await triggerPolymarket({
        signalId: 'sig-entry-low',
        tokenID: TOKEN_ID,
        spendAmountUsd: ENTRY_USD,
        direction: 'buy'
      });

      expect(entryClient.createMarketOrder).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
        expect.objectContaining({ side: OrderSide.BUY, maxPrice: 0.005 })
      );
    });

    it('requires an explicit share quantity to exit, and none to enter', async () => {
      // An entry can be sized down to whatever collateral is left, but an exit
      // names a real position. Inferring the quantity would sell something the
      // position may not hold.
      clientWithBook({ negRisk, asks: ENTRY_ASKS, bids: EXIT_BIDS });

      await expect(triggerPolymarket({
        signalId: 'sig-no-shares',
        tokenID: TOKEN_ID,
        spendAmountUsd: ENTRY_USD,
        direction: 'sell'
      })).rejects.toThrow('require an exact requested share quantity');

      await expect(triggerPolymarket({
        signalId: 'sig-entry-no-shares',
        tokenID: TOKEN_ID,
        spendAmountUsd: ENTRY_USD,
        direction: 'buy'
      })).resolves.toBeDefined();
    });
  });
});

  describe('evaluatePerpsMarginHealth', () => {
    it('approves a healthy account with low margin ratio', () => {
      const portfolio = {
        margin: {
          totalAccountValue: '1000',
          totalInitialMargin: '200',
          totalMaintenanceMargin: '100',
          totalPositionValue: '200'
        },
        withdrawable: '800',
        inLiquidation: false
      };
      const result = evaluatePerpsMarginHealth(portfolio);
      expect(result.safe).toBe(true);
      expect(result.marginRatio).toBe(0.1);
      expect(result.availableMargin).toBe(800);

    it('rejects an account actively in liquidation', () => {

        margin: {
          totalAccountValue: '200',
          totalInitialMargin: '180',
          totalMaintenanceMargin: '180',
          totalPositionValue: '180'
        },
        withdrawable: '0',
        inLiquidation: true
      };
      const result = evaluatePerpsMarginHealth(portfolio);
      expect(result.safe).toBe(false);
      expect(result.inLiquidation).toBe(true);
      expect(result.reason).toContain('in liquidation');

    it('rejects an account exceeding 85% maintenance margin threshold', () => {

        margin: {
          totalAccountValue: '1000',
          totalInitialMargin: '900',
          totalMaintenanceMargin: '880',
          totalPositionValue: '900'
        },
        withdrawable: '50',
        inLiquidation: false
      };
      const result = evaluatePerpsMarginHealth(portfolio);
      expect(result.safe).toBe(false);
      expect(result.marginRatio).toBe(0.88);
      expect(result.reason).toContain('Critical margin utilization');
    });

    it('rejects a depleted account with zero account value', () => {
      const portfolio = {
        margin: {
          totalAccountValue: '0',
          totalInitialMargin: '0',
          totalMaintenanceMargin: '0',
          totalPositionValue: '0'
        },
        withdrawable: '0',
        inLiquidation: false
      };
      const result = evaluatePerpsMarginHealth(portfolio);
      expect(result.safe).toBe(false);
      expect(result.reason).toContain('depleted or zero');
    });
  });

  describe('calculateApproxLiquidationPrice', () => {

      expect(liq).toBe('0');
    });

    it('calculates long liquidation price correctly for 10x leverage', () => {
      // 65000 * (1 - 1/10 + 0.05) = 65000 * 0.95 = 61750

    it('calculates short liquidation price correctly for 10x leverage', () => {

      expect(liq).toBe('68250.00');
    });

  describe('openAttributedPerpsSession', () => {

      const session = await openAttributedPerpsSession(mockClient as any, builder);

      expect(mockClient.openPerpsSession).toHaveBeenCalledWith({
        label: 'swat-builder-0x12345678'
      });
      expect(session).toBe(mockSession);
    });
  });

  describe('executePerpsOrder', () => {
    let mockSession: any;

    beforeEach(() => {
      mockSession = {
        fetchPortfolio: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue({
          margin: {
            totalAccountValue: '5000',
            totalInitialMargin: '1000',
            totalMaintenanceMargin: '500',
            totalPositionValue: '1000'
          },
          withdrawable: '3000',
          inLiquidation: false
        }),
        placeOrder: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue({
          order: {
            id: 12345,
            price: '65000',
            quantity: '0.1',
            filledQuantity: '0.1',
            status: 'filled',
            clientOrderId: 'test-client-id'
          }
        })
      };
    });

    it('rejects order when margin required exceeds available margin', async () => {
      // 0.1 BTC at $65000 with 1x leverage = $6500 required margin, but only $3000 available
      await expect(
        executePerpsOrder({
          userId: 'user-1',
          session: mockSession,
          instrumentId: 1,
          symbol: 'BTC-PERP',
          side: OrderSide.BUY,
          quantity: '0.1',
          price: '65000',
          leverage: 1
        })
      ).rejects.toThrow('Perps Margin Insufficient');
    });

    it('successfully places and records order with 5x leverage and take-profit/stop-loss', async () => {
      // 0.1 BTC at $65000 with 5x leverage = $1300 required margin, well within $3000 available
      const result = await executePerpsOrder({
        userId: 'user-1',
        session: mockSession,
        instrumentId: 1,
        symbol: 'BTC-PERP',
        side: OrderSide.BUY,
        quantity: '0.1',
        price: '65000',
        leverage: 5,
        takeProfitPrice: '70000',

          timeInForce: PerpsTimeInForce.IOC,
          takeProfit: { triggerPrice: '70000' },
          stopLoss: { triggerPrice: '62000' }
        })
      );
      expect(result.orderId).toBe(12345);
      expect(result.status).toBe('filled');
    });
  });
});

==> apps/trade-executor/src/polymarket-perps.ts <==
import {
  OrderSide,
  PerpsTimeInForce,
  type SecureClient,
  type PublicClient
} from '@polymarket/client';
import {
  upsertPerpsInstrument,
  upsertPerpsAccount,
  upsertPerpsPosition,
  recordPerpsOrder,
  getPerpsInstrumentBySymbol,
  type PerpsInstrumentRecord
} from '@swat/db';

export const POLYMARKET_PERPS_API_HOST = 'https://api.perpetuals.polymarket.com/v1';
export const POLYMARKET_PERPS_MAX_BUILDER_FEE_RATE = '0.001'; // 10 bps max per docs

export type PerpsSession = Awaited<ReturnType<SecureClient['openPerpsSession']>>;

export interface PerpsExecutionPlan {
  instrumentId: number;
  symbol: string;
  side: OrderSide;
  quantity: string;
  price: string;
  leverage: number;
  timeInForce: PerpsTimeInForce;
  takeProfitPrice?: string;
  stopLossPrice?: string;
}

export interface PerpsRiskEvaluation {
  safe: boolean;
  marginRatio: number;
  inLiquidation: boolean;
  totalAccountValue: number;
  availableMargin: number;
  reason?: string;
}

/**
 * Open an authenticated Perps session with optional credentials/expiration.
 */
export async function openAttributedPerpsSession(
  client: SecureClient,
  builderAddress?: string
): Promise<PerpsSession> {
  const session = await client.openPerpsSession({
    label: builderAddress ? `swat-builder-${builderAddress.slice(0, 10)}` : 'swat-perps-session'
  });
  return session;
}

/**
 * Sync instruments catalogue from Polymarket to PostgreSQL.
 */
export async function syncPerpsInstrumentsCatalogue(
  client: PublicClient | SecureClient
): Promise<PerpsInstrumentRecord[]> {
  const instruments = await client.fetchPerpsInstruments();
  const records: PerpsInstrumentRecord[] = [];

  for (const inst of instruments) {
    const record = await upsertPerpsInstrument({
      instrumentId: inst.id,
      symbol: inst.symbol,
      category: inst.category ?? 'crypto',
      baseAsset: inst.baseAsset,
      quoteAsset: inst.quoteAsset ?? 'USD',
      priceDecimals: inst.priceDecimals,
      quantityDecimals: inst.quantityDecimals,
      maxLeverage: inst.maxLeverage ?? 10,
      minNotional: inst.minNotional ?? '1',
      maxMarketNotional: inst.maxMarketNotional ?? '100000',
      isActive: true
    });
    records.push(record);
  }

  return records;
}

/**
 * Evaluate portfolio health, margin utilization, and liquidation risk.
 */
export function evaluatePerpsMarginHealth(portfolio: {
  margin: {
    totalAccountValue: string;
    totalInitialMargin: string;
    totalMaintenanceMargin: string;
    totalPositionValue: string;
  };
  inLiquidation: boolean;
  withdrawable?: string;
}): PerpsRiskEvaluation {
  const accountValue = Number(portfolio.margin.totalAccountValue) || 0;
  const maintenanceMargin = Number(portfolio.margin.totalMaintenanceMargin) || 0;
  const availableMargin = Number(portfolio.withdrawable) || Math.max(0, accountValue - Number(portfolio.margin.totalInitialMargin));

  if (portfolio.inLiquidation) {
    return {
      safe: false,
      marginRatio: 1,
      inLiquidation: true,
      totalAccountValue: accountValue,
      availableMargin,
      reason: 'Account is actively in liquidation'
    };
  }

  if (accountValue <= 0) {
    return {
      safe: false,
      marginRatio: 1,
      inLiquidation: false,
      totalAccountValue: accountValue,
      availableMargin,
      reason: 'Total account value is depleted or zero'
    };
  }

  const marginRatio = maintenanceMargin / accountValue;

  // Emergency safety trigger: > 85% maintenance margin used
  if (marginRatio > 0.85) {
    return {
      safe: false,
      marginRatio,
      inLiquidation: false,
      totalAccountValue: accountValue,
      availableMargin,
      reason: `Critical margin utilization: ${(marginRatio * 100).toFixed(1)}% of equity consumed by maintenance margin`
    };
  }

  return {
    safe: true,
    marginRatio,
    inLiquidation: false,
    totalAccountValue: accountValue,
    availableMargin
  };
}

/**
 * Execute a leveraged Perps copy trade order.
 */
export async function executePerpsOrder(params: {
  userId: string;
  session: PerpsSession;
  instrumentId: number;
  symbol: string;
  side: OrderSide;
  quantity: string;
  price: string;
  leverage?: number;
  timeInForce?: PerpsTimeInForce;
  takeProfitPrice?: string;
  stopLossPrice?: string;
  builderAddress?: string;
  clientOrderId?: string;
}) {
  // 1. Fetch live portfolio and check margin safety
  const portfolio = await params.session.fetchPortfolio();
  const risk = evaluatePerpsMarginHealth(portfolio);
  if (!risk.safe) {
    throw new Error(`Perps Pre-Trade Risk Refusal: ${risk.reason}`);
  }

  // 2. Check available order margin
  const notionalUsd = Number(params.price) * Number(params.quantity);
  const leverage = params.leverage ?? 1;
  const requiredInitialMargin = notionalUsd / leverage;

  if (requiredInitialMargin > risk.availableMargin) {
    throw new Error(
      `Perps Margin Insufficient: order requires $${requiredInitialMargin.toFixed(2)} initial margin, but available margin is $${risk.availableMargin.toFixed(2)}`
    );
  }

  // 3. Build and place order on Polymarket Perps
  const orderPayload: any = {
    instrumentId: params.instrumentId,
    side: params.side,
    quantity: params.quantity,
    price: params.price,
    timeInForce: params.timeInForce ?? PerpsTimeInForce.IOC
  };

  if (params.takeProfitPrice) {
    orderPayload.takeProfit = { triggerPrice: params.takeProfitPrice };
  }
  if (params.stopLossPrice) {
    orderPayload.stopLoss = { triggerPrice: params.stopLossPrice };
  }

  const result = await params.session.placeOrder(orderPayload);
  const order = result.order;

  // 4. Record order execution to database
  const recordedOrder = await recordPerpsOrder({
    userId: params.userId,
    clientOrderId: params.clientOrderId ?? order.clientOrderId,
    venueOrderId: String(order.id),
    instrumentId: params.instrumentId,
    symbol: params.symbol,
    side: params.side === OrderSide.BUY ? 'BUY' : 'SELL',
    orderType: params.timeInForce === PerpsTimeInForce.GTC ? 'GTC' : 'IOC',
    price: order.price,
    quantity: order.quantity,
    filledQuantity: order.filledQuantity,
    status: order.status,
    builderAddress: params.builderAddress,
    builderFeeRate: POLYMARKET_PERPS_MAX_BUILDER_FEE_RATE,
    rawResponse: order as unknown as Record<string, unknown>
  });

  // 5. If filled, update position in database
  if (order.status === 'filled' || Number(order.filledQuantity) > 0) {
    await upsertPerpsPosition({
      userId: params.userId,
      instrumentId: params.instrumentId,
      symbol: params.symbol,
      side: params.side === OrderSide.BUY ? 'LONG' : 'SHORT',
      size: order.filledQuantity,
      entryPrice: order.price,
      leverage,
      initialMargin: requiredInitialMargin.toFixed(6),
      maintenanceMargin: (requiredInitialMargin * 0.5).toFixed(6),
      liquidationPrice: calculateApproxLiquidationPrice(
        params.side,
        Number(order.price),
        leverage
      ),
      unrealizedPnl: '0',
      takeProfitPrice: params.takeProfitPrice,
      stopLossPrice: params.stopLossPrice,
      status: 'open'
    });
  }

  // 6. Sync updated account margin state
  await upsertPerpsAccount({
    userId: params.userId,
    totalAccountValue: portfolio.margin.totalAccountValue,
    availableOrderMargin: String(risk.availableMargin),
    totalInitialMargin: portfolio.margin.totalInitialMargin,
    totalMaintenanceMargin: portfolio.margin.totalMaintenanceMargin,
    withdrawable: portfolio.withdrawable ?? '0',
    inLiquidation: portfolio.inLiquidation ?? false
  });

  return {
    orderId: order.id,
    status: order.status,
    filledQuantity: order.filledQuantity,
    price: order.price,
    recordedOrderId: recordedOrder.id
  };
}

/**
 * Approximate liquidation price calculation for leveraged perps.
 */
export function calculateApproxLiquidationPrice(
  side: OrderSide,
  entryPrice: number,
  leverage: number,
  maintenanceMarginRatio = 0.05
): string {
  if (leverage <= 1) return '0';
  // Long liquidation = entryPrice * (1 - 1/leverage + maintenanceMarginRatio)
  // Short liquidation = entryPrice * (1 + 1/leverage - maintenanceMarginRatio)
  if (side === OrderSide.BUY) {
    const liq = entryPrice * (1 - (1 / leverage) + maintenanceMarginRatio);
    return Math.max(0, liq).toFixed(2);
  } else {
    const liq = entryPrice * (1 + (1 / leverage) - maintenanceMarginRatio);
    return Math.max(0, liq).toFixed(2);
  }
}

import { describe, it, expect, vi } from 'vitest';

// `polymarket.ts` constructs an ethers.Wallet at module scope, so this must be a
// well-formed 32-byte key. Deliberately a throwaway constant, never funded.
process.env.EVM_PRIVATE_KEY = `0x${'1'.repeat(64)}`;
process.env.POLYMARKET_SIGNATURE_TYPE = 'EOA';
process.env.POLYMARKET_BUILDER_CODE = `0x${'a'.repeat(64)}`;

// `polymarket.js` reaches @swat/db, which opens a pool at import time. Stubbed
// as `polymarket.test.ts` does ‚Äî `planPolymarketBookOrder` is pure and touches
// no database.
vi.mock('@swat/db', () => ({
  recordConfirmedPolymarketTrade: vi.fn(),
  getPolymarketOutcomeContext: vi.fn(),
  getPolymarketMarket: vi.fn(),
  listRedeemablePolymarketMarkets: vi.fn(),
  claimPolymarketRedemption: vi.fn(),
  confirmPolymarketRedemption: vi.fn(),
  failPolymarketRedemption: vi.fn(),
  releaseStalePolymarketRedemptionClaims: vi.fn(),
  query: vi.fn(),
  pool: {}
}));

const { planPolymarketBookOrder, POLYMARKET_SHARE_DECIMALS } = await import('./polymarket.js');

/**
 * Venue precision parity (checklist S3-19 / audit G3-P10).
 *
 * Pins our rounding against the published contract in `trading/place-orders`:
 *
 *   | Tick size | Price decimals | Size decimals | Amount decimals |
 *   | 0.1       | 1              | 2             | 3               |
 *   | 0.01      | 2              | 2             | 4               |
 *   | 0.005     | 3              | 2             | 5               |
 *   | 0.0025    | 4              | 2             | 6               |
 *   | 0.001     | 3              | 2             | 5               |
 *   | 0.0001    | 4              | 2             | 6               |
 *
 * **Size decimals are 2 for every tick size**, which is why a single
 * `POLYMARKET_SHARE_DECIMALS` constant is correct rather than a lookup table.
 *
 * We deliberately do *not* implement the price-decimals column. Instead the book
 * walk rejects any price off the current tick grid, which is strictly stronger:
 * a price on a `0.0025` grid can never exceed 4 decimals, and off-grid prices
 * with the "right" decimal count (0.0026 under a 0.0025 tick) are still refused.
 * The equivalence is proven exhaustively by the last test in this file, so the
 * stronger check cannot silently drift from the documented one.
 */

const DOCS_PRECISION = [
  { tickSize: '0.1', priceDecimals: 1 },
  { tickSize: '0.01', priceDecimals: 2 },
  { tickSize: '0.005', priceDecimals: 3 },
  { tickSize: '0.0025', priceDecimals: 4 },
  { tickSize: '0.001', priceDecimals: 3 },
  { tickSize: '0.0001', priceDecimals: 4 }
] as const;

function book(params: {
  tickSize: string;
  asks?: Array<{ price: string; size: string }>;
  bids?: Array<{ price: string; size: string }>;
  minimumShares?: string;
}) {
  return {
    conditionId: `0x${'1'.repeat(64)}`,
    tokenId: 'token-precision',
    timestamp: Date.now(),
    asks: params.asks ?? [],
    bids: params.bids ?? [],
    minOrderSize: params.minimumShares ?? '1',
    tickSize: params.tickSize,
    negRisk: false,
    hash: 'a'.repeat(40)
  } as Parameters<typeof planPolymarketBookOrder>[0];
}

function plan(bookInput: ReturnType<typeof book>, direction: 'buy' | 'sell', amount: number) {
  return planPolymarketBookOrder(bookInput, direction, amount, 5_000, Date.now());
}

describe('polymarket venue precision parity', () => {
  it.each(DOCS_PRECISION)(
    'accepts an on-grid price at tick $tickSize',
    ({ tickSize }) => {
      const tick = Number(tickSize);
      // Two ticks in, so the price is unambiguously on-grid and below 1.
      const price = (tick * 2).toFixed(10).replace(/0+$/, '').replace(/\.$/, '');
      // Depth is priced in USD (size √ó price), so a fixed share count starves a
      // low-tick book: at tick 0.0001, 1000 shares at 0.0002 is $0.20. Size the
      // level to the notional under test instead.
      const size = String(Math.ceil(10 / (tick * 2)) * 2);
      const result = plan(
        book({ tickSize, asks: [{ price, size }] }),
        'buy',
        10
      );
      expect(result.estimatedShares).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    }
  );

  it.each(DOCS_PRECISION)(
    'rejects an off-grid price at tick $tickSize even when its decimal count looks legal',
    ({ tickSize, priceDecimals }) => {
      // Half a tick off. This has at most `priceDecimals + 1` decimals, so a
      // decimals-only check would wave some of these through; the CLOB would
      // then reject the order at submission.
      const offGrid = (Number(tickSize) * 2.5).toFixed(priceDecimals + 1);
      expect(() =>
        plan(book({ tickSize, asks: [{ price: offGrid, size: '1000' }] }), 'buy', 10)
      ).toThrow(/tick-size grid/);
    }
  );

  it('rounds shares DOWN to 2 decimals, never up', () => {
    // Rounding up would sell shares the position does not hold, or buy more
    // than the sized notional pays for.
    const result = plan(
      book({ tickSize: '0.01', asks: [{ price: '0.03', size: '1000' }] }),
      'buy',
      1
    );
    // 1 / 0.03 = 33.333‚Ä¶; floor at 2dp is 33.33.
    expect(result.estimatedShares).toBe(33.33);
    expect(POLYMARKET_SHARE_DECIMALS).toBe(2);
  });

  it('rejects an order that falls below the minimum after rounding', () => {
    // The rounding itself can push a marginal order under the venue floor, and
    // submitting it would be a guaranteed rejection.
    expect(() =>
      plan(
        book({ tickSize: '0.01', minimumShares: '5', asks: [{ price: '0.5', size: '1000' }] }),
        'buy',
        1
      )
    ).toThrow(/below the 5-share minimum/);
  });

  it('rejects a price at or above 1, which is not a valid outcome price', () => {
    expect(() =>
      plan(book({ tickSize: '0.01', asks: [{ price: '1', size: '10' }] }), 'buy', 1)
    ).toThrow(/invalid order-book price/);
  });

  it('proves tick-grid conformance implies the documented price decimals', () => {
    // The justification for not implementing the price-decimals column. If a
    // future tick size broke this, the stronger check would stop being a
    // superset and this test would catch it.
    for (const { tickSize, priceDecimals } of DOCS_PRECISION) {
      const tick = Number(tickSize);
      let maxDecimals = 0;
      for (let step = 1; step * tick < 1; step++) {
        const price = Number((step * tick).toFixed(10));
        const text = price.toString();
        const decimals = text.includes('.') ? text.split('.')[1]!.length : 0;
        if (decimals > maxDecimals) maxDecimals = decimals;
      }
      expect(
        maxDecimals,
        `at tick ${tickSize} exceeds ${priceDecimals} decimals`
      ).toBeLessThanOrEqual(priceDecimals);
    }
  }, 15_000);
});

import { describe, it, expect, vi, beforeEach } from 'vitest';
import {
  runPolymarketRedemptionSweep,
  type PolymarketPositionExitClaimed,
  type PolymarketPositionExitPorts,
  type PolymarketRedemptionClient
} from './polymarket-redemption.js';
import type { RedeemableMarket, RedeemablePosition } from '@swat/db';

/**
 * The sweep after the `S4-M37` inversion: it is driven by the positions **we**
 * hold, not by the master's observed trades, and every position it is about to
 * exit is claimed position-scoped first so the `S4-M19` race has exactly one
 * winner per position rather than one per trigger.
 *
 * These fixtures therefore carry real condition ids and real outcome token ids.
 * `parsePolymarketOutcomePosition` refuses anything ambiguous ‚Äî a `0x‚Ä¶` where a
 * token id belongs, an unnamed outcome ‚Äî so a market fixture that would not
 * survive the fan-out cannot pass here either, which is the point.
 */

const mocks = vi.hoisted(() => ({
  listRedeemablePolymarketMarkets: vi.fn(),
  claimPolymarketRedemption: vi.fn(),
  confirmPolymarketRedemption: vi.fn(),
  failPolymarketRedemption: vi.fn(),
  releaseStalePolymarketRedemptionClaims: vi.fn()
}));

vi.mock('@swat/db', () => mocks);

const CONDITION = `0x${'a'.repeat(64)}`;
const OTHER_CONDITION = `0x${'b'.repeat(64)}`;

function heldPosition(overrides: Partial<RedeemablePosition> = {}): RedeemablePosition {
  return {
    positionId: 'pos-1',
    conditionId: CONDITION,
    userId: null,
    targetAccount: 'polygon:0x1111111111111111111111111111111111111111',
    tokenMint: 'polygon:1001',
    tokenId: '1001',
    outcome: 'Yes',
    outcomeIndex: 0,
    heldShares: '40',
    reservedSellShares: '0',
    ...overrides
  };
}

function market(overrides: Partial<RedeemableMarket> = {}): RedeemableMarket {
  return {
    conditionId: CONDITION,
    winningTokenId: '1001',
    resolvedOutcome: 'Yes',
    negRisk: false,
    positions: [heldPosition()],
    ...overrides
  };
}

function client(
  overrides?: Partial<PolymarketRedemptionClient>
): PolymarketRedemptionClient {
  return {
    redeemPositions: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue({
      wait: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue({ transactionHash: '0xabc', transactionId: 'tx-1' })
    }),
    ...overrides
  };
}

/**
 * Fakes for the three position-exit claim operations the sweep injects.
 *
 * Wired in every test that expects a redemption, because the sweep refuses to
 * redeem without them ‚Äî see the fail-closed test below, which is the one place
 * they are deliberately left out.
 */
function exitPorts(
  overrides: Partial<PolymarketPositionExitPorts> = {}
): PolymarketPositionExitPorts & {
  claimPositionExit: ReturnType<typeof vi.fn>;
  confirmPositionExit: ReturnType<typeof vi.fn>;
  releasePositionExit: ReturnType<typeof vi.fn>;
} {
  let issued = 0;
  return {
    claimPositionExit: vi.fn(async (input: {
      positionKey: string;
      exitTrigger: PolymarketPositionExitClaimed['exitTrigger'];
    }) => {
      issued += 1;
      return {
        id: `exit-${issued}`,
        positionKey: input.positionKey,
        exitTrigger: input.exitTrigger
      };
    }),
    confirmPositionExit: vi.fn(async () => {}),
    releasePositionExit: vi.fn(async () => {}),
    ...overrides
  } as never;
}

beforeEach(() => {
  vi.clearAllMocks();
  mocks.releaseStalePolymarketRedemptionClaims.mockResolvedValue(0);
  mocks.listRedeemablePolymarketMarkets.mockResolvedValue([]);
  mocks.claimPolymarketRedemption.mockResolvedValue({

    conditionId: CONDITION,
    userId: null
  });

  mocks.failPolymarketRedemption.mockResolvedValue(undefined);
});

  it('redeems a resolved market and records its transaction hash', async () => {
    mocks.listRedeemablePolymarketMarkets.mockResolvedValue([market()]);
    const sdk = client();
    const ports = exitPorts();

    const result = await runPolymarketRedemptionSweep({ client: sdk, ...ports });

    expect(sdk.redeemPositions).toHaveBeenCalledWith({ conditionId: CONDITION });
    expect(mocks.confirmPolymarketRedemption).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
      expect.objectContaining({ id: 'claim-1', transactionHash: '0xabc', winningTokenId: '1001' })
    );
    // The position-scoped exit is confirmed too: the redemption transaction is the
    // evidence for the position, not merely for the condition.
    expect(ports.confirmPositionExit).toHaveBeenCalledWith({
      id: 'exit-1',
      transactionHash: '0xabc'
    });
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ scanned: 1, redeemed: 1, failed: 0, skipped: 0 });
  });

  it('claims the position before calling the venue, keyed on the outcome token', async () => {
    // `S4-M19`: one winner per position. The claim is position-keyed
    // (`polygon:<outcomeTokenId>`) and must be taken before the on-chain call,
    // because after it there is nothing left to stand down from.
    mocks.listRedeemablePolymarketMarkets.mockResolvedValue([market()]);
    const sdk = client();
    const ports = exitPorts();

    await runPolymarketRedemptionSweep({ client: sdk, ...ports });

    expect(ports.claimPositionExit).toHaveBeenCalledWith({

      outcomeTokenId: '1001',
      exitTrigger: 'redemption',
      userId: null
    });
    const claimOrder = ports.claimPositionExit.mock.invocationCallOrder[0]!;
    const redeemOrder = vi.mocked(sdk.redeemPositions).mock.invocationCallOrder[0]!;
    expect(claimOrder).toBeLessThan(redeemOrder);
  });

  it('never passes an amount ‚Äî redemption covers both outcomes', async () => {
