import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { ApiError } from './api.js';
import {
  describeApiError,
  CSRF_MESSAGE,
  FORBIDDEN_MESSAGE,
  SESSION_EXPIRED_MESSAGE
} from './api-error-message.js';

describe('describeApiError', () => {
  it('tells a 401 to sign in again rather than repeating the operation name', () => {
    expect(describeApiError(new ApiError(401, 'Not signed in'), 'Failed to fetch clusters'))
      .toBe(SESSION_EXPIRED_MESSAGE);
  });

  it('does not invite a re-login on 403', () => {
    expect(describeApiError(new ApiError(403, 'Forbidden'), 'Failed to fetch clusters'))
      .toBe(FORBIDDEN_MESSAGE);
    expect(describeApiError(new ApiError(403, 'Forbidden'), 'x')).not.toContain('sign in');
  });

  it('keeps the status on any other ApiError so a 500 is not mistaken for a 400', () => {
    expect(describeApiError(new ApiError(500, 'boom'), 'Failed to save configuration'))
      .toBe('Failed to save configuration (HTTP 500: boom)');
  });

  it('keeps the fallback in front of an opaque network error', () => {
    expect(describeApiError(new TypeError('Failed to fetch'), 'Failed to fetch wallets'))
      .toBe('Failed to fetch wallets (Failed to fetch)');
  });

  it('falls back cleanly on a thrown non-Error', () => {
    expect(describeApiError('nope', 'Failed to fetch wallets')).toBe('Failed to fetch wallets');
    expect(describeApiError(new Error(''), 'Failed to fetch wallets')).toBe('Failed to fetch wallets');
  });
});

describe('describeApiError ‚Äî CSRF vs role, both 403', () => {
  it('distinguishes a stale CSRF token from a role refusal', () => {
    // Both are 403. Without the split, a stale swat_csrf cookie reads as "you
    // lack permission" and sends the operator hunting a role problem that does
    // not exist -- on a surface they are actually allowed to use.
    const csrf = new ApiError(403, 'Invalid CSRF token', { error: 'Invalid CSRF token', code: 'csrf_invalid' });
    expect(describeApiError(csrf, 'x')).toBe(CSRF_MESSAGE);
    expect(describeApiError(csrf, 'x')).not.toBe(FORBIDDEN_MESSAGE);
  });

  it('still reports a role refusal as a role refusal', () => {
    const forbidden = new ApiError(403, 'Forbidden', { error: 'Forbidden' });
    expect(describeApiError(forbidden, 'x')).toBe(FORBIDDEN_MESSAGE);
  });

  it('matches the API code, not its prose, so rewording cannot re-break it', () => {
    // The message here is deliberately nothing like the real one.
    const reworded = new ApiError(403, 'nope', { code: 'csrf_invalid' });
    expect(describeApiError(reworded, 'x')).toBe(CSRF_MESSAGE);
  });

  it('falls back to the role message when the body is absent or not an object', () => {
    expect(describeApiError(new ApiError(403, 'Forbidden'), 'x')).toBe(FORBIDDEN_MESSAGE);
    expect(describeApiError(new ApiError(403, 'Forbidden', 'plain text'), 'x')).toBe(FORBIDDEN_MESSAGE);
  });
});

==> apps/web/lib/api-error-message.ts <==
/**
 * Turns a thrown value from `lib/api.ts` into something an operator can act on.
 *
 * Exists because the thirteen call sites converted in S6-3 all used to do
 * `if (!res.ok) throw new Error('Failed to fetch X')`, which threw away the
 * status. A 401 (your session lapsed, sign in again), a 403 (you are signed in
 * but this is an admin surface) and a 500 (the API is broken) all rendered as
 * the same red box, so the one failure the operator could fix themselves was
 * indistinguishable from the two they could not.
 *
 * Kept out of `lib/api.ts` on purpose: that module decides what to *send*, this
 * one decides what to *say*. Wording is a UI concern and changes far more often
 * than the transport does.
 */

import { ApiError } from './api.js';

/** Shown on 401. Deliberately actionable -- there is a thing the reader can do. */
export const SESSION_EXPIRED_MESSAGE = 'Your session expired ‚Äî sign in again.';

/** Shown on 403. Not a login problem, so it must not invite a re-login. */
export const FORBIDDEN_MESSAGE = 'This account is not permitted to use this operator surface.';

/**
 * Shown on a 403 whose cause is the double-submit token, not the user's role.
 *
 * These are the same status, and without this branch a stale `swat_csrf` cookie
 * reads as "you lack permission" -- sending the operator to hunt a role problem
 * that does not exist, on a surface they are in fact allowed to use. Newly
 * load-bearing: since S6-3 every mutating call in the app depends on that cookie.
 *
 * Matched on the API's stable `code`, not on its prose, so rewording the message
 * cannot silently re-break this.
 */
export const CSRF_MESSAGE =
  'Your session token is stale ‚Äî reload the page and try again.';

/** True when a 403 body carries the API's CSRF marker. */
function isCsrfFailure(error: ApiError): boolean {
  const code = (error.body as { code?: unknown } | null | undefined)?.code;
  return code === 'csrf_invalid';
}

/**
 * @param error   Whatever reached the `catch`. Anything is legal here.
 * @param fallback What the caller was trying to do, e.g. 'Failed to fetch clusters'.
 */
export function describeApiError(error: unknown, fallback: string): string {
  if (error instanceof ApiError) {
    if (error.isUnauthenticated) return SESSION_EXPIRED_MESSAGE;
    if (error.isForbidden) return isCsrfFailure(error) ? CSRF_MESSAGE : FORBIDDEN_MESSAGE;
    // `ApiError.message` is already the API's own `error`/`message` field when it
    // sent one, and `"<status> <statusText>"` when it did not. Either way the
    // status is worth repeating: "Bad Request" alone does not say who is at fault.
    return `${fallback} (HTTP ${error.status}: ${error.message})`;
  }
  // A network failure or a CORS rejection lands here as a plain TypeError whose
  // message ('Failed to fetch') is useless on its own.
  if (error instanceof Error && error.message) return `${fallback} (${error.message})`;
  return fallback;
}

==> apps/web/lib/api-server.ts <==
import { cookies } from 'next/headers';
import { resolveApiBase, ApiError, SESSION_COOKIE } from './api.js';

/**
 * Server-component half of the API client (checklist S6-3).
 *
 * `lib/api.ts` is browser-only by construction: it reads `document.cookie` for
 * the CSRF token and `window.location` for the host. A React Server Component
 * has neither. It runs on the server, where the user's cookies arrive on the
 * *incoming request* and must be forwarded explicitly -- `credentials:
 * 'include'` means nothing there, because there is no browser in the call.
 *
 * Two of the thirteen converted files are server components
 * (`app/signals/page.tsx`, `app/performance/page.tsx`), which is why this exists
 * rather than being folded into `api.ts`. Keeping them separate also keeps
 * `next/headers` -- which throws if imported into a client component -- out of
 * the module every client view imports.
 *
 * **Read-only on purpose.** There is no `post` here. A server component cannot
 * mutate anyway, and the CSRF token is a *double-submit* check: the client must
 * echo a cookie it can read, which is precisely the thing a server component
 * cannot participate in. A mutation belongs in a client component or a Server
 * Action, and offering a `post` here would invite someone to write one that
 * fails CSRF for reasons that look like an auth bug.
 */

/**
 * Fetches from the API on behalf of the signed-in user, forwarding their session.
 *
 * Returns `null` when there is no session rather than throwing, because the
 * common case for a server component is "render the signed-out state", and
 * middleware has already redirected anyone who should not be here.
 */
export async function serverApiGet<T = unknown>(path: string): Promise<T | null> {
  const jar = await cookies();
  const session = jar.get(SESSION_COOKIE);
  if (!session) return null;

  const response = await fetch(`${resolveApiBase(null)}${path}`, {
    // Forwarding only the session cookie, not the whole jar. Nothing else the
    // browser holds is ours to relay to the API, and a narrow forward cannot
    // leak a third-party cookie into our own logs.
    headers: { cookie: `${SESSION_COOKIE}=${session.value}` },
    // Never cache a per-user response. Next would otherwise happily serve one
    // user's data to another on a shared route -- the worst possible bug in a
    // multi-tenant product, and the default is opt-out, not opt-in.
    cache: 'no-store'
  });

  if (response.status === 401) return null;
  if (!response.ok) throw new ApiError(response.status, `${response.status} ${response.statusText}`);
  return (await response.json()) as T;
}

import { describe, it, expect, vi, afterEach } from 'vitest';
import {
  parseCsrfToken,
  buildApiRequestInit,
  resolveApiBase,
  ApiError,
  CSRF_HEADER
} from './api.js';

describe('parseCsrfToken', () => {
  it('reads the token from a multi-cookie string', () => {
    expect(parseCsrfToken('a=1; swat_csrf=tok-123; swat_session=zzz')).toBe('tok-123');
  });

  it('is not fooled by a cookie whose name merely ends with the target', () => {
    // `not_swat_csrf` shares a suffix. A naive `includes` or a regex without an
    // anchor reads its value and sends a token the API will reject.
    expect(parseCsrfToken('not_swat_csrf=wrong')).toBeNull();
  });

  it('url-decodes the value', () => {
    expect(parseCsrfToken('swat_csrf=a%2Bb')).toBe('a+b');
  });

  it('returns null rather than empty string for a blank cookie', () => {
    // "no token" must not be confusable with "a blank token": the second would
    // build a request that fails CSRF for a reason indistinguishable from being
    // signed out.
    expect(parseCsrfToken('swat_csrf=')).toBeNull();
  });

  it('returns null for absent, empty and undefined cookie strings', () => {
    expect(parseCsrfToken('other=1')).toBeNull();
    expect(parseCsrfToken('')).toBeNull();
    expect(parseCsrfToken(undefined)).toBeNull();
    expect(parseCsrfToken(null)).toBeNull();
  });
});

describe('buildApiRequestInit', () => {
  it('always sends credentials, so the session cookie crosses origins', () => {
    // The web app and API are different origins in every deployment we have.
    // Without this every request is anonymous and cookie auth cannot work.
    expect(buildApiRequestInit().credentials).toBe('include');
    expect(buildApiRequestInit({ method: 'POST', csrfToken: 't' }).credentials).toBe('include');
  });

  it('attaches the CSRF header on mutating methods', () => {
    for (const method of ['POST', 'PUT', 'PATCH', 'DELETE']) {
      const init = buildApiRequestInit({ method, csrfToken: 'tok' });
      expect((init.headers as Record<string, string>)[CSRF_HEADER]).toBe('tok');
    }
  });

  it('omits the CSRF header on GET', () => {
    const init = buildApiRequestInit({ method: 'GET', csrfToken: 'tok' });
    expect((init.headers as Record<string, string>)[CSRF_HEADER]).toBeUndefined();
  });

  it('omits the CSRF header when no token exists rather than sending empty', () => {
    const init = buildApiRequestInit({ method: 'POST', csrfToken: null });
    expect((init.headers as Record<string, string>)[CSRF_HEADER]).toBeUndefined();
  });

  it('uppercases the method so a lowercase caller still gets CSRF', () => {
    const init = buildApiRequestInit({ method: 'post', csrfToken: 'tok' });
    expect(init.method).toBe('POST');
    expect((init.headers as Record<string, string>)[CSRF_HEADER]).toBe('tok');
  });

  it('never emits an API key header under any option combination', () => {
    // This is the regression guard for S6-3. `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_KEY` shipped the  check-public-secrets:allow-mention
    // operator control-plane key in the browser bundle; the fix is only durable
    // if the client cannot express it.
    const combos = [
      buildApiRequestInit(),
      buildApiRequestInit({ method: 'POST', body: '{}', csrfToken: 'tok' }),
      buildApiRequestInit({ method: 'DELETE', csrfToken: null })
    ];
    for (const init of combos) {
      const names = Object.keys(init.headers as Record<string, string>).map((h) => h.toLowerCase());
      expect(names).not.toContain('x-api-key');
      expect(names).not.toContain('authorization');
    }
  });

  it('sets Content-Type only when there is a body', () => {
    const withBody = buildApiRequestInit({ method: 'POST', body: '{}' });
    expect((withBody.headers as Record<string, string>)['Content-Type']).toBe('application/json');
    const without = buildApiRequestInit({ method: 'POST' });
    expect((without.headers as Record<string, string>)['Content-Type']).toBeUndefined();
    expect(without.body).toBeUndefined();
  });
});

==> apps/web/lib/api.ts <==
/**
 * The single browser -> API client (checklist S6-3).
 *
 * Replaces thirteen copies of a hand-rolled `fetch` that each sent
 * `X-Api-Key: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_KEY`. check-public-secrets:allow-mention
 * -- naming the deleted variable here is documentation, not usage. It is inlined into
 * the client bundle by Next.js at build time, so the shared operator key was
 * shipped to every visitor and granted full control-plane access. It is deleted,
 * not rotated: a rotated secret in a public bundle is still public.
 *
 * What replaces it is the session cookie the API already issues, plus the
 * double-submit CSRF token it already expects. See `apps/api/src/auth/plugin.ts`
 * -- the backend half has existed since Stage 1; only the frontend was behind.
 *
 * The module is split deliberately. Everything that makes a decision is a pure
 * function over explicit inputs, and only `apiFetch` touches the network or the
 * DOM. That is what lets this file be tested at all: `apps/web` has no jsdom, so
 * a client that read `document.cookie` directly would be untestable here.
 */

/** Name of the CSRF cookie the API sets. Deliberately JS-readable. */
export const CSRF_COOKIE = 'swat_csrf';
/** Header the API compares the cookie against. */
export const CSRF_HEADER = 'x-csrf-token';
/** Session cookie name. httpOnly, so JS can never read it -- only send it. */
export const SESSION_COOKIE = 'swat_session';

/** Methods that change state and therefore need the CSRF header. */
const MUTATING_METHODS = new Set(['POST', 'PUT', 'PATCH', 'DELETE']);

export class ApiError extends Error {
  constructor(
    readonly status: number,
    message: string,
    readonly body?: unknown
  ) {
    super(message);
    this.name = 'ApiError';
  }

  /** True when the caller should be sent to /login rather than shown an error. */
  get isUnauthenticated(): boolean {
    return this.status === 401;
  }

  /** True when the caller is signed in but lacks the role for this surface. */
  get isForbidden(): boolean {
    return this.status === 403;
  }
}

/**
 * Extracts the CSRF token from a raw cookie string.
 *
 * Pure, and takes the string rather than reading `document.cookie`, so it is
 * testable without a DOM. Returns null rather than an empty string when absent
 * so "no token" cannot be mistaken for "a token that happens to be blank" --
 * the second would produce a request that fails CSRF for a reason the caller
 * cannot distinguish from being logged out.
 */
export function parseCsrfToken(cookieString: string | null | undefined): string | null {
  if (!cookieString) return null;
  for (const part of cookieString.split(';')) {
    const separator = part.indexOf('=');
    if (separator < 0) continue;
    if (part.slice(0, separator).trim() !== CSRF_COOKIE) continue;
    const value = part.slice(separator + 1).trim();
    return value.length > 0 ? decodeURIComponent(value) : null;
  }
  return null;
}

export interface BuildRequestOptions {
  readonly method?: string;
  /** Already-serialised body, or undefined for a bodyless request. */
  readonly body?: string;
  /** From `parseCsrfToken`. Null when the user has no session. */
  readonly csrfToken?: string | null;
  readonly signal?: AbortSignal;
}

/**
 * Builds the `RequestInit` for an API call.
 *
 * Pure. Three invariants, each of which had a bug behind it:
 *
 *   1. `credentials: 'include'` on every request. The API and the web app are
 *      different origins in every deployment we have (:3000 and :3001), so
 *      without this the browser sends no cookie and every call is anonymous.
 *   2. The CSRF header only on mutating methods, and only when a token exists.
 *      Sending it on a GET is harmless but sending a stale one is misleading,
 *      and the API only checks it where it matters.
 *   3. No API key, ever. There is deliberately no parameter for one -- the way
 *      this stays fixed is that the shape cannot express the old behaviour.
 */
export function buildApiRequestInit(options: BuildRequestOptions = {}): RequestInit {
  const method = (options.method ?? 'GET').toUpperCase();
  const headers: Record<string, string> = {};

  if (options.body !== undefined) headers['Content-Type'] = 'application/json';
  if (MUTATING_METHODS.has(method) && options.csrfToken) {
    headers[CSRF_HEADER] = options.csrfToken;
  }

  const init: RequestInit = {
    method,
    credentials: 'include',
    headers
  };
  if (options.body !== undefined) init.body = options.body;
  if (options.signal) init.signal = options.signal;
  return init;
}

/**
 * Resolves the API origin.
 *
 * `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` is a URL, not a secret, so it stays a `NEXT_PUBLIC_`
 * variable -- the rule being enforced is "no secrets in the bundle", not "no
 * public config". Absent that, derive the host from how the page is being
 * viewed so the dashboard works from another device on the LAN as well as from
 * localhost. Takes the location rather than reading `window` so it is testable.
 */
export function resolveApiBase(
  location?: { protocol: string; hostname: string } | null,
  configured: string | undefined = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL
): string {
  if (configured) return configured.replace(/\/+$/, '');
  if (location) return `${location.protocol}//${location.hostname}:3001`;
  return 'http://localhost:3001';
}

export function resolveLpApiBase(
  location?: { protocol: string; hostname: string } | null,
  configured: string | undefined = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_LP_API_URL
): string {
  if (configured) return configured.replace(/\/+$/, '');
  if (location) return `${location.protocol}//${location.hostname}:3010`;
  return 'http://localhost:3010';
}

function currentLocation(): { protocol: string; hostname: string } | null {
  if (typeof window === 'undefined') return null;
  return { protocol: window.location.protocol, hostname: window.location.hostname };
}

function currentCookies(): string | null {
  if (typeof document === 'undefined') return null;
  return document.cookie;
}

export interface ApiFetchOptions {
  readonly method?: string;
  /** Serialised for you. Pass the object, not a string. */
  readonly body?: unknown;
  readonly signal?: AbortSignal;
  /**
   * Called instead of throwing when the API says 401. Injected so the redirect
   * is the caller's decision -- a background poll should not yank the user out
   * of a form they are filling in.
   */
  readonly onUnauthenticated?: () => void;
}

/**
 * Calls the API with the session cookie and CSRF header attached.
 *
 * Throws `ApiError` on any non-2xx so a caller cannot accidentally treat an
 * error body as data -- the previous call sites all did `if (!res.ok) throw new
 * Error('Failed to fetch X')`, which discarded the status and made a 401 and a
 * 500 indistinguishable in the UI.
 */
export async function apiFetch<T = unknown>(path: string, options: ApiFetchOptions = {}): Promise<T> {
  const base = resolveApiBase(currentLocation());
  const init = buildApiRequestInit({
    method: options.method,
    body: options.body === undefined ? undefined : JSON.stringify(options.body),
    csrfToken: parseCsrfToken(currentCookies()),
    signal: options.signal
  });

  const response = await fetch(`${base}${path}`, init);

  if (response.status === 401 && options.onUnauthenticated) {
    options.onUnauthenticated();
    throw new ApiError(401, 'Not signed in');
  }

  if (!response.ok) {
    let body: unknown;
    let message = `${response.status} ${response.statusText}`;
    try {
      body = await response.json();
      const described = (body as { message?: unknown; error?: unknown } | null)?.message
        ?? (body as { error?: unknown } | null)?.error;
      if (typeof described === 'string' && described.length > 0) message = described;
    } catch {
      // A non-JSON error body is normal (a proxy 502, an HTML error page). The
      // status is the part that matters and we already have it.
    }
    throw new ApiError(response.status, message, body);
  }

  if (response.status === 204) return undefined as T;
  return (await response.json()) as T;
}

/** Convenience wrappers so call sites read as intent rather than as plumbing. */
export const api = {
  get: <T = unknown>(path: string, options?: Omit<ApiFetchOptions, 'method' | 'body'>) =>
    apiFetch<T>(path, { ...options, method: 'GET' }),
  post: <T = unknown>(path: string, body?: unknown, options?: Omit<ApiFetchOptions, 'method' | 'body'>) =>
    apiFetch<T>(path, { ...options, method: 'POST', body }),
  put: <T = unknown>(path: string, body?: unknown, options?: Omit<ApiFetchOptions, 'method' | 'body'>) =>
    apiFetch<T>(path, { ...options, method: 'PUT', body }),
  patch: <T = unknown>(path: string, body?: unknown, options?: Omit<ApiFetchOptions, 'method' | 'body'>) =>
    apiFetch<T>(path, { ...options, method: 'PATCH', body }),
  delete: <T = unknown>(path: string, options?: Omit<ApiFetchOptions, 'method' | 'body'>) =>
    apiFetch<T>(path, { ...options, method: 'DELETE' })
};

export async function lpApiFetch<T = unknown>(path: string, options: ApiFetchOptions = {}): Promise<T> {
  const base = resolveLpApiBase(currentLocation());
  const init = buildApiRequestInit({
    method: options.method,
    body: options.body === undefined ? undefined : JSON.stringify(options.body),
    csrfToken: parseCsrfToken(currentCookies()),
    signal: options.signal
  });

  const response = await fetch(`${base}${path}`, init);

  if (response.status === 401 && options.onUnauthenticated) {
    options.onUnauthenticated();
    throw new ApiError(401, 'Not signed in');
  }

  if (!response.ok) {
    let body: unknown;
    let message = `${response.status} ${response.statusText}`;
    try {
      body = await response.json();
      const described = (body as { message?: unknown; error?: unknown } | null)?.message
        ?? (body as { error?: unknown } | null)?.error;
      if (typeof described === 'string' && described.length > 0) message = described;
    } catch {
      // non-json response
    }
    throw new ApiError(response.status, message, body);
  }

  if (response.status === 204) return undefined as T;
  return (await response.json()) as T;
}

export const lpApi = {
  get: <T = unknown>(path: string, options?: Omit<ApiFetchOptions, 'method' | 'body'>) =>
    lpApiFetch<T>(path, { ...options, method: 'GET' }),
  post: <T = unknown>(path: string, body?: unknown, options?: Omit<ApiFetchOptions, 'method' | 'body'>) =>
    lpApiFetch<T>(path, { ...options, method: 'POST', body }),
  patch: <T = unknown>(path: string, body?: unknown, options?: Omit<ApiFetchOptions, 'method' | 'body'>) =>
    lpApiFetch<T>(path, { ...options, method: 'PATCH', body }),
  delete: <T = unknown>(path: string, options?: Omit<ApiFetchOptions, 'method' | 'body'>) =>
    lpApiFetch<T>(path, { ...options, method: 'DELETE' })
};

import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import { classifyRoute, resolveRouteAccess, requiresRoleCheck } from './route-access.js';

describe('classifyRoute', () => {
  it('treats the landing page and auth pages as public', () => {
    expect(classifyRoute('/')).toBe('public');
    expect(classifyRoute('/login')).toBe('public');
    expect(classifyRoute('/signup')).toBe('public');
    expect(classifyRoute('/forgot-password')).toBe('public');
    expect(classifyRoute('/learn')).toBe('public');
  });

  it("classifies today's operator pages as admin", () => {
    for (const path of ['/admin', '/admin/portfolio', '/workspace', '/signals', '/wallets', '/logs', '/clusters', '/setup', '/performance']) {
      expect(classifyRoute(path)).toBe('admin');
    }
  });

  it('classifies nested operator paths as admin, not just the exact prefix', () => {
    expect(classifyRoute('/workspace/views/health')).toBe('admin');
  });

  it('does not let a longer path that merely starts with the same letters slip through', () => {
    // `/loginish` is not `/login`. Matching on bare `startsWith` without the
    // segment boundary would make it public.
    expect(classifyRoute('/loginish')).toBe('app');
    expect(classifyRoute('/setupwizard')).toBe('app');
  });

  it('defaults an unknown path to app, so a new page requires a session', () => {
    // Fails closed. A new page added without touching this file is gated rather
    // than public, which is the safe direction to be wrong in.
    expect(classifyRoute('/some/new/page')).toBe('app');
  });
});

describe('resolveRouteAccess', () => {
  it('allows public routes with no session', () => {
    expect(resolveRouteAccess({ pathname: '/', hasSession: false, role: null }))
      .toEqual({ decision: 'allow' });
  });

  it('redirects an anonymous visitor to login and preserves the deep link', () => {
    expect(resolveRouteAccess({ pathname: '/workspace/views/health', hasSession: false, role: null }))
      .toEqual({
        decision: 'redirect',
        to: '/login?next=%2Fworkspace%2Fviews%2Fhealth',
        reason: 'no-session'
      });
  });

  it('allows an admin onto an admin route', () => {
    expect(resolveRouteAccess({ pathname: '/wallets', hasSession: true, role: 'admin' }))
      .toEqual({ decision: 'allow' });
  });

  it('refuses a non-admin an admin route, and does not send them to login', () => {
    // They are signed in. A login form would imply their password is wrong.
    const access = resolveRouteAccess({ pathname: '/wallets', hasSession: true, role: 'user' });
    expect(access).toEqual({ decision: 'redirect', to: '/?denied=admin', reason: 'not-admin' });
  });

  it('fails closed when the role is unknown', () => {
    // An unreachable API, an expired session and a genuine non-admin all arrive
    // here as null. All three must be refused.
    expect(resolveRouteAccess({ pathname: '/setup', hasSession: true, role: null }).decision)
      .toBe('redirect');
  });

  it('lets any signed-in user onto a non-admin app route', () => {
    expect(resolveRouteAccess({ pathname: '/dashboard', hasSession: true, role: 'user' }))
      .toEqual({ decision: 'allow' });
  });
});

describe('requiresRoleCheck', () => {
  it('asks the API only for admin routes with a session', () => {
    expect(requiresRoleCheck('/wallets', true)).toBe(true);
  });

  it('skips the round trip when there is no session or the route is public', () => {
    // No point paying for a role lookup we are going to redirect past anyway.
    expect(requiresRoleCheck('/wallets', false)).toBe(false);
    expect(requiresRoleCheck('/login', true)).toBe(false);
    expect(requiresRoleCheck('/dashboard', true)).toBe(false);
  });
});

==> apps/web/lib/route-access.ts <==
/**
 * Route protection decisions (checklist S6-2), as pure functions.
 *
 * Kept separate from `middleware.ts` because Next middleware runs in the edge
 * runtime and cannot be imported into a test here -- but the decisions are the
 * part worth testing, and they are just data in, data out.
 *
 * **What this layer is and is not.** It is the reason an unauthenticated visitor
 * is redirected to /login instead of watching a dashboard fail to load. It is
 * *not* the authorization boundary: the API enforces that itself in
 * `apps/api/src/auth/plugin.ts` (`registerAdminOnlyGlobals` restricts every
 * route outside `/v1/auth/` and `/v1/me/` to admins and internal services).
 * Middleware sees only cookies and whatever it chooses to ask the API, so
 * treating it as the gate would put the control in the client's half of the
 * system. Both layers exist; only the API one is load-bearing.
 */

export type RouteClass = 'public' | 'admin' | 'app';

/** Roles the API reports on `GET /v1/auth/me`. */
export type Role = 'admin' | 'user';

/** Reachable without a session. */
const PUBLIC_PREFIXES = ['/login', '/signup', '/forgot-password', '/learn'] as const;

/**
 * The operator console: today's nine pages.
 *
 * These are admin surfaces because they call global routes -- `/v1/wallets`,
 * `/v1/config`, `/v1/scorer/run` -- which the API admits only for an admin or an
 * internal service. Listing them here is an interim measure: checklist S6-13 and
 * S6-14 move them under an `(admin)` route group, at which point the prefix is
 * structural and this array collapses to one entry. Until then a new operator
 * page must be added here, which is exactly the kind of thing that gets
 * forgotten -- hence `classifyRoute` defaults unknown paths to 'app' (session
 * required) rather than 'public'.
 */
const ADMIN_PREFIXES = [
  '/admin',
  '/workspace',
  '/signals',
  '/wallets',
  '/logs',
  '/clusters',
  '/setup',
  '/performance'
] as const;

export function classifyRoute(pathname: string): RouteClass {
  if (pathname === '/') return 'public';
  if (PUBLIC_PREFIXES.some((prefix) => pathname === prefix || pathname.startsWith(`${prefix}/`))) {
    return 'public';
  }
  if (ADMIN_PREFIXES.some((prefix) => pathname === prefix || pathname.startsWith(`${prefix}/`))) {
    return 'admin';
  }
  return 'app';
}

export interface RouteAccessInput {
  readonly pathname: string;
  /** Whether the session cookie is present. Presence, not validity. */
  readonly hasSession: boolean;
  /**
   * The role the API reported, or null when it was not asked or would not say.
   *
   * Null is not 'user'. An unreachable API, an expired session and a genuine
   * non-admin are all null here, and all three must be refused an admin surface
   * -- so this fails closed. That is the right direction, but it means an API
   * outage presents as "you are not an admin", which is why the redirect carries
   * a reason.
   */
  readonly role: Role | null;
}

export type RouteAccess =
  | { readonly decision: 'allow' }
  | { readonly decision: 'redirect'; readonly to: string; readonly reason: RedirectReason };

export type RedirectReason = 'no-session' | 'not-admin';

/**
 * Decides whether a request may proceed.
 *
 * The `next` parameter on the login redirect is what makes a deep link survive
 * signing in; without it every session expiry dumps the operator back on the
 * landing page and they have to navigate again.
 */
export function resolveRouteAccess(input: RouteAccessInput): RouteAccess {
  const classification = classifyRoute(input.pathname);
  if (classification === 'public') return { decision: 'allow' };

  if (!input.hasSession) {
    return {
      decision: 'redirect',
      to: `/login?next=${encodeURIComponent(input.pathname)}`,
      reason: 'no-session'
    };
  }

  if (classification === 'admin' && input.role !== 'admin') {
    // Deliberately not /login: the user is signed in, so sending them to a login
    // form would suggest their credentials are the problem and invite them to
    // retype a password that is already correct.
    return { decision: 'redirect', to: '/?denied=admin', reason: 'not-admin' };
  }

  return { decision: 'allow' };
}

/** True when middleware needs to ask the API for the role at all. */
export function requiresRoleCheck(pathname: string, hasSession: boolean): boolean {
  return hasSession && classifyRoute(pathname) === 'admin';
}

import { api } from './api.js';
import { PublicKey } from '@solana/web3.js';

export const WAKE_SOLANA_MAINNET_PROGRAM_ID = '6t6dRetG3Hns4vCfZaj392e9bZ6uTEEmvL37KnDWErfS';
export const WAKE_SOLANA_DEVNET_PROGRAM_ID = 'WakeDev11111111111111111111111111111111111';

/**
 * Derives a real Anchor Program Derived Address (PDA) on Solana:
 * seeds = [b"vault", user_public_key]
 * program_id = WAKE_SOLANA_MAINNET_PROGRAM_ID (or devnet)
 */
export function deriveSolanaAnchorPda(
  userAddress: string,
  cluster: 'mainnet-beta' | 'devnet' = 'mainnet-beta'
): { pdaAddress: string; bump: number } {
  try {
    const userPubkey = new PublicKey(userAddress.trim());
    const progId = new PublicKey(
      cluster === 'devnet' ? WAKE_SOLANA_DEVNET_PROGRAM_ID : WAKE_SOLANA_MAINNET_PROGRAM_ID
    );
    const [pda, bump] = PublicKey.findProgramAddressSync(
      [new TextEncoder().encode('vault'), userPubkey.toBytes()],
      progId
    );
    return { pdaAddress: pda.toBase58(), bump };
  } catch (err) {
    console.warn('Could not derive Anchor PDA with @solana/web3.js:', err);
    return { pdaAddress: WAKE_SOLANA_MAINNET_PROGRAM_ID, bump: 255 };
  }
}

/**
 * Detects whether the active Solana wallet or RPC is targeting devnet or mainnet
 */
export function detectSolanaCluster(provider?: any): 'mainnet-beta' | 'devnet' {
  if (provider) {
    if (provider.isDevnet || provider.cluster === 'devnet' || provider.network === 'devnet') {
      return 'devnet';
    }
    const rpc = provider.connection?._rpcEndpoint || '';
    if (typeof rpc === 'string' && rpc.includes('devnet')) return 'devnet';
  }
  return 'mainnet-beta';
}

/**
 * Robust copy helper that succeeds even on non-HTTPS origins (e.g. raw IP)
 */
export function copyToClipboard(text: string): boolean {
  if (!text) return false;
  try {
    if (typeof navigator !== 'undefined' && navigator.clipboard) {
      navigator.clipboard.writeText(text).catch(() => {});
      return true;
    }
  } catch {
    // Fall back to execCommand
  }
  if (typeof document !== 'undefined') {
    const el = document.createElement('textarea');
    el.value = text;
    el.setAttribute('readonly', '');
    el.style.position = 'fixed';
    el.style.top = '-9999px';
    el.style.left = '-9999px';
    document.body.appendChild(el);
    el.select();
    try {
      const ok = document.execCommand('copy');
      document.body.removeChild(el);
      return ok;
    } catch {
      document.body.removeChild(el);
      return false;
    }
  }
  return false;
}

const ALPHABET = '123456789ABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijkmnopqrstuvwxyz';

/** Encodes raw bytes to Base58 for Solana signatures and public keys */
export function toBase58(bytes: Uint8Array): string {
  const digits = [0];
  for (let i = 0; i < bytes.length; i++) {
    for (let j = 0; j < digits.length; j++) digits[j] <<= 8;
    digits[0] += bytes[i];
    let carry = 0;
    for (let j = 0; j < digits.length; j++) {
      digits[j] += carry;
      carry = (digits[j] / 58) | 0;
      digits[j] %= 58;
    }
    while (carry) {
      digits.push(carry % 58);
      carry = (carry / 58) | 0;
    }
  }
  let str = '';
  for (let i = 0; i < bytes.length && bytes[i] === 0; i++) str += ALPHABET[0];
  for (let i = digits.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) str += ALPHABET[digits[i]];
  return str;
}

export interface SolanaWalletConnection {
  address: string;
  provider: any;
  walletName: string;
}

export interface EvmWalletConnection {
  address: string;
  provider: any;
  chainId: string;
  walletName: string;
}

/** Detects injected Solana provider (Phantom, Solflare, Backpack) */
export function getSolanaProvider(): { provider: any; name: string } | null {
  if (typeof window === 'undefined') return null;
  const anyWin = window as any;
  if (anyWin.phantom?.solana?.isPhantom) {
    return { provider: anyWin.phantom.solana, name: 'Phantom' };
  }
  if (anyWin.solflare?.isSolflare) {
    return { provider: anyWin.solflare, name: 'Solflare' };
  }
  if (anyWin.backpack?.isBackpack) {
    return { provider: anyWin.backpack, name: 'Backpack' };
  }
  if (anyWin.solana) {
    return { provider: anyWin.solana, name: anyWin.solana.isPhantom ? 'Phantom' : 'Solana Wallet' };
  }
  return null;
}

/** Detects injected EVM provider (MetaMask, Rabby, Coinbase Wallet, etc.) */
export function getEvmProvider(): { provider: any; name: string } | null {
  if (typeof window === 'undefined') return null;
  const anyWin = window as any;
  if (anyWin.ethereum) {
    let name = 'MetaMask';
    if (anyWin.ethereum.isRabby) name = 'Rabby';
    else if (anyWin.ethereum.isCoinbaseWallet) name = 'Coinbase Wallet';
    else if (anyWin.ethereum.isBraveWallet) name = 'Brave Wallet';
    else if (anyWin.ethereum.isMetaMask) name = 'MetaMask';
    return { provider: anyWin.ethereum, name };
  }
  return null;
}

/** Connects to Solana wallet and retrieves public address */
export async function connectSolanaWallet(): Promise<SolanaWalletConnection> {
  const detected = getSolanaProvider();
  if (!detected) {
    throw new Error('No Solana wallet extension detected. Please install Phantom from https://phantom.app to connect.');
  }

  const { provider, name } = detected;
  const res = await provider.connect({ onlyIfTrusted: false });
  const pubkey = res?.publicKey || provider.publicKey;
  if (!pubkey) {
    throw new Error('Could not read public key from Solana wallet.');
  }
  return {
    address: pubkey.toString(),
    provider,
    walletName: name,
  };
}

/** Signs a SIWS (Sign-In with Solana) challenge message */
export async function signSolanaChallenge(provider: any, message: string): Promise<string> {
  const encoded = new TextEncoder().encode(message);
  const signed = await provider.signMessage(encoded, 'utf8');
  const signatureBytes = signed.signature || signed;
  if (signatureBytes instanceof Uint8Array) {
    return toBase58(signatureBytes);
  }
  if (typeof signatureBytes === 'string') {
    return signatureBytes;
  }
  return toBase58(new Uint8Array(signatureBytes));
}

/** Connects to EVM wallet (MetaMask / Rabby) and retrieves public address */
export async function connectEvmWallet(targetChainId?: '0x89'): Promise<EvmWalletConnection> {
  const detected = getEvmProvider();
  if (!detected) {
    throw new Error('No EVM wallet extension detected. Please install MetaMask from https://metamask.io or Rabby to connect.');
  }

  const { provider, name } = detected;
  const accounts: string[] = await provider.request({ method: 'eth_requestAccounts' });
  if (!accounts || accounts.length === 0) {
    throw new Error('No accounts selected in EVM wallet.');
  }

  const currentChainId: string = await provider.request({ method: 'eth_chainId' }).catch(() => '0x1');

  // If Polygon is targeted (e.g. Polymarket), prompt user to switch
  if (targetChainId && currentChainId.toLowerCase() !== targetChainId.toLowerCase()) {
    try {
      await provider.request({
        method: 'wallet_switchEthereumChain',
        params: [{ chainId: targetChainId }],
      });
    } catch (switchError: any) {
      if (switchError.code === 4902 && targetChainId === '0x89') {
        await provider.request({
          method: 'wallet_addEthereumChain',
          params: [
            {
              chainId: '0x89',
              chainName: 'Polygon Mainnet',
              nativeCurrency: { name: 'POL', symbol: 'POL', decimals: 18 },
              rpcUrls: ['https://polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com'],
              blockExplorerUrls: ['https://polygonscan.com'],
            },
          ],
        });
      } else {
        throw new Error('Please approve switching your wallet to Polygon Mainnet (Chain ID 137) in MetaMask/Rabby.');
      }
    }
  }

  const updatedChainId: string = await provider.request({ method: 'eth_chainId' }).catch(() => currentChainId);

  return {
    address: accounts[0].toLowerCase(),
    provider,
    chainId: updatedChainId,
    walletName: name,
  };
}

/** Signs an EIP-4361 SIWE challenge message */
export async function signEvmChallenge(provider: any, message: string, address: string): Promise<string> {
  return await provider.request({
    method: 'personal_sign',
    params: [message, address],
  });
}

/**
 * End-to-end authenticating and linking a self-custody wallet:
 * 1. Requests single-use challenge nonce from API
 * 2. Prompts the wallet popup to sign the challenge
 * 3. Verifies and registers cryptographic proof with the backend
 */
export async function linkWalletWithSignature(params: {
  chainKind: 'solana' | 'evm';
  address: string;
  provider: any;
}): Promise<{ chainKind: string; address: string; verifiedAt: string }> {
  // 1. Get nonce & challenge message from server
  const nonceRes = await api.post<{ nonce: string; message: string; expiresAt: string }>('/v1/auth/wallet/nonce', {
    chainKind: params.chainKind,
    address: params.address,
  });

  if (!nonceRes?.message) {
    throw new Error('Failed to obtain challenge message from authentication server.');
  }

  // 2. Prompt wallet extension signature
  let signature: string;
  if (params.chainKind === 'solana') {
    signature = await signSolanaChallenge(params.provider, nonceRes.message);
  } else {
    signature = await signEvmChallenge(params.provider, nonceRes.message, params.address);
  }

  // 3. Post proof to verification endpoint
  const verifyRes = await api.post<{ wallet: { chainKind: string; address: string; verifiedAt: string } }>('/v1/auth/wallet/verify', {
    chainKind: params.chainKind,
    address: params.address,
    message: nonceRes.message,
    signature,
  });

  return verifyRes.wallet;
}

/**
 * Prompts the connected EVM wallet (MetaMask / Rabby) to sign the Polymarket
 * ClobAuth EIP-712 typed data via eth_signTypedData_v4.
 */
export async function signPolymarketClobAuth(
  provider: any,
  address: string,
  typedData: any
): Promise<string> {
  // Ensure wallet is strictly on Polygon (0x89 / 137) before signing
  const currentHex: string = await provider.request({ method: 'eth_chainId' }).catch(() => '0x1');
  if (currentHex.toLowerCase() !== '0x89') {
    try {
      await provider.request({
        method: 'wallet_switchEthereumChain',
        params: [{ chainId: '0x89' }],
      });
    } catch (switchErr: any) {
      if (switchErr?.code === 4902) {
        await provider.request({
          method: 'wallet_addEthereumChain',
          params: [
            {
              chainId: '0x89',
              chainName: 'Polygon Mainnet',
              nativeCurrency: { name: 'POL', symbol: 'POL', decimals: 18 },
              rpcUrls: ['https://polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com'],
              blockExplorerUrls: ['https://polygonscan.com'],
            },
          ],
        });
      } else {
        throw new Error('Please switch your wallet to Polygon Mainnet (Chain ID 137) before signing Polymarket credentials.');
      }
    }
  }

  // Ensure EIP712Domain is explicitly in types for MetaMask eth_signTypedData_v4
  const payload = {
    ...typedData,
    types: {
      EIP712Domain: [
        { name: 'name', type: 'string' },
        { name: 'version', type: 'string' },
        { name: 'chainId', type: 'uint256' },
      ],
      ...typedData.types,
    },
  };

  try {
    return await provider.request({
      method: 'eth_signTypedData_v4',
      params: [address, JSON.stringify(payload)],
    });
  } catch (err: any) {
    if (err?.code === 4001) {
      throw new Error('Polymarket authentication signature rejected by user.');
    }
    // Fallback: some providers expect parsed object instead of serialized JSON string
    try {
      return await provider.request({
        method: 'eth_signTypedData_v4',
        params: [address, payload],
      });
    } catch {
      throw err;
    }
  }
}

==> apps/web/middleware.ts <==
import { NextResponse, type NextRequest } from 'next/server';
import { resolveRouteAccess, requiresRoleCheck, type Role } from './lib/route-access.js';
import { SESSION_COOKIE } from './lib/api.js';

/**
 * Route protection (checklist S6-2, closes S6-B7).
 *
 * All the decisions live in `lib/route-access.ts` as pure functions with tests;
 * this file is the adapter that feeds them a request and acts on the answer.
 * Middleware runs in the edge runtime and cannot be imported into vitest, so
 * anything decided here rather than there is untestable -- keep it thin.
 *
 * **This is a redirect layer, not the authorization boundary.** The API enforces
 * roles itself (`apps/api/src/auth/plugin.ts`), and it must, because everything
 * middleware knows comes from the client. What this buys is that an operator
 * whose session lapsed lands on a login form instead of a dashboard full of
 * failed requests, and a non-admin never sees an admin shell render before its
 * data 403s.
 */

const API_BASE = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3001';

/**
 * Asks the API who this session belongs to.
 *
 * Returns null on anything other than a clean 200 with a recognised role --
 * network failure, 401, malformed body. Every one of those means "we do not know
 * this is an admin", and `resolveRouteAccess` refuses admin surfaces on null. So
 * an API outage locks the operator console rather than opening it, which is the
 * correct direction and worth stating because it will look like a bug the first
 * time it happens.
 */
async function fetchRole(request: NextRequest): Promise<Role | null> {
  const cookie = request.headers.get('cookie');
  if (!cookie) return null;
  try {
    const response = await fetch(`${API_BASE}/v1/auth/me`, {
      headers: { cookie },
      // Middleware must never serve a cached identity: a stale 200 would keep a
      // revoked session admitted for as long as the cache lived.
      cache: 'no-store'
    });
    if (!response.ok) return null;
    const body = (await response.json()) as { user?: { role?: unknown } };
    const role = body.user?.role;
    return role === 'admin' || role === 'user' ? role : null;
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

export async function middleware(request: NextRequest) {
  const { pathname } = request.nextUrl;
  const hasSession = request.cookies.has(SESSION_COOKIE);

  const role = (await (requiresRoleCheck(pathname, hasSession) ? fetchRole(request) : null)) as Role | null;
  const access = resolveRouteAccess({ pathname, hasSession, role });

  if (access.decision === 'redirect') {
    const url = request.nextUrl.clone();
    const [path, query] = access.to.split('?');
    url.pathname = path!;
    url.search = query ? `?${query}` : '';
    return NextResponse.redirect(url);
  }

  return NextResponse.next();
}

export const config = {
  /**
   * Skip Next internals, static assets and the favicon.
   *
   * Not a security decision -- `classifyRoute` would gate an unmatched path
   * anyway. It is a cost one: without it every image request on an admin page
   * triggers a `/v1/auth/me` round trip.
   */
  matcher: ['/((?!_next/static|_next/image|favicon.ico|.*\\.(?:svg|png|jpg|jpeg|gif|webp|ico)$).*)']
};

const nextConfig: NextConfig = {

  webpack: (config) => {

==> packages/db/sql/001_init.sql <==
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pgcrypto;

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS wallets (
  address VARCHAR(44) PRIMARY KEY,
  nickname VARCHAR(100),
  source VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'manual',
  status VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active',
  first_seen TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW(),
  last_active TIMESTAMP,
  total_trades INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
  win_rate DECIMAL(5,2),
  realized_roi DECIMAL(12,4),
  unrealized_roi DECIMAL(12,4),
  avg_hold_time_hours DECIMAL(8,2),
  early_entry_score DECIMAL(5,2),
  consistency_score DECIMAL(5,2),
  composite_score DECIMAL(5,2),
  tier VARCHAR(20),
  portfolio_value_usd DECIMAL(16,2),
  created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tokens (
  mint VARCHAR(44) PRIMARY KEY,
  symbol VARCHAR(20),
  name VARCHAR(100),
  decimals INTEGER,
  logo_uri TEXT,
  first_seen TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW(),
  launch_timestamp TIMESTAMP,
  total_supply BIGINT,
  is_verified BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,
  tags TEXT[],
  created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS transactions (
  id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  signature VARCHAR(88) NOT NULL,
  wallet_address VARCHAR(44) REFERENCES wallets(address),
  token_in VARCHAR(44) REFERENCES tokens(mint),
  token_out VARCHAR(44) REFERENCES tokens(mint),
  amount_in BIGINT NOT NULL,
  amount_out BIGINT NOT NULL,
  amount_in_usd DECIMAL(16,6),
  amount_out_usd DECIMAL(16,6),
  direction VARCHAR(4) NOT NULL,
  target_token VARCHAR(44),
  program_id VARCHAR(44),
  slot BIGINT,
  timestamp TIMESTAMP NOT NULL,
  block_time BIGINT,
  created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW(),
  UNIQUE(signature, wallet_address, target_token)
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_tx_wallet ON transactions(wallet_address, timestamp DESC);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_tx_token ON transactions(target_token, timestamp DESC);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS wallet_clusters (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  name VARCHAR(100),
  description TEXT,
  confidence DECIMAL(3,2) NOT NULL,
  wallet_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
  total_realized_roi DECIMAL(12,4),
  total_unrealized_roi DECIMAL(12,4),
  avg_composite_score DECIMAL(5,2),
  first_seen TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW(),
  last_active TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW(),
  status VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'active',
  tags TEXT[],
  created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS cluster_memberships (
  cluster_id UUID REFERENCES wallet_clusters(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  wallet_address VARCHAR(44) REFERENCES wallets(address),
  joined_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW(),
  confidence DECIMAL(3,2),
  PRIMARY KEY (cluster_id, wallet_address)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS wallet_relationships (
  id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  wallet_a VARCHAR(44) NOT NULL,
  wallet_b VARCHAR(44) NOT NULL,
  relationship_type VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
  confidence DECIMAL(3,2) NOT NULL,
  evidence JSONB DEFAULT '{}',
  created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW(),
  UNIQUE(wallet_a, wallet_b, relationship_type)
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_rel_a ON wallet_relationships(wallet_a);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_rel_b ON wallet_relationships(wallet_b);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS signals (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  pattern_type VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
  cluster_id UUID REFERENCES wallet_clusters(id),
  token_mint VARCHAR(44) REFERENCES tokens(mint),
  confidence DECIMAL(5,2) NOT NULL,
  signal_score DECIMAL(5,2) NOT NULL,
  trigger_data JSONB NOT NULL,
  status VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'pending',
  executed_at TIMESTAMP,
  executed_price DECIMAL(16,8),
  executed_amount DECIMAL(16,8),
  trade_signature VARCHAR(88),
  pnl_usd DECIMAL(16,6),
  created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW(),
  expires_at TIMESTAMP
);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_signals_status ON signals(status, created_at DESC);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_signals_cluster ON signals(cluster_id, created_at DESC);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS trades (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  signal_id UUID REFERENCES signals(id),
  wallet_address VARCHAR(44),
  token_mint VARCHAR(44),
  direction VARCHAR(4) NOT NULL,
  amount_usd DECIMAL(16,6),
  token_amount BIGINT,
  price_usd DECIMAL(16,8),
  slippage_bps INTEGER,
  priority_fee_lamports BIGINT,
  signature VARCHAR(88),
  status VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'pending',
  simulation_result JSONB,
  error_message TEXT,
  executed_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW(),
  confirmed_at TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS config (
  key VARCHAR(50) PRIMARY KEY,
  value JSONB NOT NULL,
  updated_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW()
);

INSERT INTO config (key, value) VALUES
('trading', '{"enabled": false, "mode": "paper", "max_position_pct": 5, "max_daily_exposure_pct": 25, "min_liquidity_usd": 50000}'::jsonb),
('risk', '{"stop_loss_pct": 20, "take_profit_levels": [{"pct": 50, "sell": 50}, {"pct": 100, "sell": 25}], "circuit_breaker_failures": 3}'::jsonb),
('signals', '{"min_signal_score": 60, "auto_execute_min_score": 80}'::jsonb)
ON CONFLICT (key) DO NOTHING;

==> packages/db/sql/002_schema_alignment.sql <==
-- Schema Alignment Migration
-- Adds missing columns specified in the project roadmap

-- wallets
ALTER TABLE wallets ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS priority VARCHAR(20) DEFAULT 'normal';

-- tokens
ALTER TABLE tokens ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS mint_authority_disabled BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE;
ALTER TABLE tokens ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS freeze_authority_disabled BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE;

-- wallet_clusters
ALTER TABLE wallet_clusters ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS cluster_type VARCHAR(20);

-- signals
ALTER TABLE signals ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS safety_flags TEXT[];
ALTER TABLE signals ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS safety_warnings TEXT[];
ALTER TABLE signals ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS alerted_at TIMESTAMP;

-- trades
ALTER TABLE trades ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS execution_mode VARCHAR(10);
ALTER TABLE trades ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS executor VARCHAR(20);
ALTER TABLE trades ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS amount_sol DECIMAL(16,8);

-- discovery_log
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS discovery_log (
  id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  source VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL,
  seed_value VARCHAR(100),
  wallets_discovered INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
  ran_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW()
);

('discovery', '{"auto_expand_funding_graph": true, "auto_expand_counterparties": true, "min_invested_lamports": 500000000}'::jsonb),

==> packages/db/sql/004_trades_persistence.sql <==
-- Trade persistence + mark-to-market support
--
-- 1. token_amount was BIGINT, which cannot store fractional human-unit token
--    amounts. Widen to NUMERIC so trades can record real positions.
-- 2. Index trades(signal_id) ‚Äî joined on for mark-to-market P&L and portfolio.
-- 3. Index transactions(token_in) ‚Äî funding-edge / token lookups.

ALTER TABLE trades
  ALTER COLUMN token_amount TYPE NUMERIC USING token_amount::numeric;

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_trades_signal ON trades(signal_id);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_trades_status ON trades(status, executed_at DESC);

==> packages/db/sql/005_tx_dedup_null_target.sql <==
-- Fix: the UNIQUE(signature, wallet_address, target_token) constraint does NOT
-- dedupe rows where target_token IS NULL, because Postgres treats NULLs as
-- distinct. Any transaction ingested without a target_token could be inserted
-- repeatedly on re-backfill, double-counting trades and P&L.
--
-- This migration: (1) removes any existing NULL-target duplicates, then
-- (2) replaces the constraint with a unique index over
-- COALESCE(target_token, '') so NULLs dedupe like any other value.

-- 1. Remove duplicate rows the NULL-distinct constraint allowed through,
--    keeping the lowest id of each logical group.
DELETE FROM transactions a
USING transactions b
WHERE a.id > b.id
  AND a.signature = b.signature
  AND a.wallet_address = b.wallet_address
  AND COALESCE(a.target_token, '') = COALESCE(b.target_token, '');

-- 2. Drop the old NULL-distinct unique constraint (default Postgres name) and
--    add a NULL-safe unique index. ON CONFLICT in insertParsedTransaction is
--    updated to target this expression.
ALTER TABLE transactions
  DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS transactions_signature_wallet_address_target_token_key;

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_tx_dedup
  ON transactions (signature, wallet_address, COALESCE(target_token, ''));

==> packages/db/sql/006_wallet_discovery_method.sql <==
-- Tag wallets with HOW they were discovered, so the on-chain token-discovery
-- pipeline can distinguish its two cohorts:
--   'token-early' ‚Äî among the first big buyers after launch (kept unconditionally)
--   'token-big'   ‚Äî a biggest-ever buyer of the token (kept only if profitable)
-- Existing discovery paths (funding graph, counterparties) leave this NULL.
ALTER TABLE wallets ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS discovery_method VARCHAR(30);

-- Speeds up the profit-prune that targets only 'token-big' wallets.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_wallets_discovery_method
  ON wallets (discovery_method);

==> packages/db/sql/007_jupiter_simulation.sql <==
-- Jupiter swap simulation data on paper trades.
--
-- These columns store quote-level detail that the paper-fill path now fetches
-- from the Jupiter Swap API v1.  They are NULL for legacy paper trades and for
-- live trades (which get their fill data from the on-chain transaction).
--
-- price_impact_pct : % price impact the swap would cause (e.g. 0.45 = 0.45 %).
-- route_info       : full JSON route plan from Jupiter (DEX hops, amounts, fees).
-- quote_slot       : Solana slot at which the quote was computed.
-- min_token_amount : minimum output after slippage, in human token units.

ALTER TABLE trades ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS price_impact_pct DECIMAL(8,4);
ALTER TABLE trades ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS route_info JSONB;
ALTER TABLE trades ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS quote_slot BIGINT;
ALTER TABLE trades ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS min_token_amount DECIMAL(30,10);

==> packages/db/sql/009_signals_dedupe_index.sql <==
-- Clean up existing duplicate pending signals, keeping only the latest one.
DELETE FROM signals s1
WHERE s1.status = 'pending'
  AND s1.token_mint IS NOT NULL
  AND EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM signals s2
    WHERE s2.pattern_type = s1.pattern_type
      AND s2.token_mint = s1.token_mint
      AND s2.status = 'pending'
      AND s2.id > s1.id
  );

-- Unique partial index to enforce atomic deduplication at the DB level.
-- Prevents the CTE-based check-then-insert race condition.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_signals_dedupe_active
  ON signals (pattern_type, token_mint)
  WHERE status = 'pending' AND token_mint IS NOT NULL;

-- Covering index for the dedupe query to eliminate sequential scans.
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_signals_dedupe_lookup
  ON signals (pattern_type, token_mint, created_at DESC)
  WHERE token_mint IS NOT NULL;

DO $$
DECLARE
  current_definition TEXT;
BEGIN
  SELECT pg_get_indexdef(indexrelid)
    INTO current_definition
    FROM pg_index
   WHERE indexrelid = to_regclass('idx_tx_dedup');

  IF current_definition IS NULL THEN
    CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_tx_dedup
      ON transactions (chain, signature, wallet_address, COALESCE(target_token, ''));
  ELSIF current_definition NOT LIKE '%chain, signature, wallet_address%' THEN
    DROP INDEX idx_tx_dedup;
    CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_tx_dedup
      ON transactions (chain, signature, wallet_address, COALESCE(target_token, ''));
  END IF;
END $$;

-- Runtime/schema alignment and EVM amount capacity.

ALTER TABLE polymarket_markets
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS updated_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW();

UPDATE polymarket_markets
   SET updated_at = created_at
 WHERE updated_at IS NULL;

ALTER TABLE polymarket_markets
  ALTER COLUMN updated_at SET DEFAULT NOW(),
  ALTER COLUMN updated_at SET NOT NULL;

DO $$
BEGIN
  IF EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
      FROM information_schema.columns
     WHERE table_schema = 'public'
       AND table_name = 'transactions'
       AND column_name = 'amount_in'
       AND data_type <> 'numeric'
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE transactions
      ALTER COLUMN amount_in TYPE NUMERIC USING amount_in::numeric;
  END IF;

  IF EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
      FROM information_schema.columns
     WHERE table_schema = 'public'
       AND table_name = 'transactions'
       AND column_name = 'amount_out'
       AND data_type <> 'numeric'
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE transactions
      ALTER COLUMN amount_out TYPE NUMERIC USING amount_out::numeric;
  END IF;
END $$;

==> packages/db/sql/016_timestamp_tz.sql <==
-- Standardize UTC timestamp storage without shifting columns already converted.

DO $$
DECLARE
  target RECORD;
  current_type TEXT;
BEGIN
  FOR target IN
    SELECT * FROM (VALUES
      ('wallets', 'first_seen'),
      ('wallets', 'last_active'),
      ('wallets', 'created_at'),
      ('wallets', 'updated_at'),
      ('tokens', 'first_seen'),
      ('tokens', 'launch_timestamp'),
      ('tokens', 'created_at'),
      ('transactions', 'timestamp'),
      ('transactions', 'created_at'),
      ('wallet_clusters', 'first_seen'),
      ('wallet_clusters', 'last_active'),
      ('wallet_clusters', 'created_at'),
      ('wallet_clusters', 'updated_at'),
      ('cluster_memberships', 'joined_at'),
      ('wallet_relationships', 'created_at'),
      ('wallet_relationships', 'updated_at'),
      ('signals', 'executed_at'),
      ('signals', 'created_at'),
      ('signals', 'expires_at'),
      ('signals', 'alerted_at'),
      ('trades', 'executed_at'),
      ('trades', 'confirmed_at'),
      ('config', 'updated_at'),
      ('discovery_log', 'ran_at'),
      ('polymarket_markets', 'end_date'),
      ('polymarket_markets', 'created_at'),
      ('polymarket_markets', 'updated_at')
    ) AS expected(relation_name, column_name)
  LOOP
    SELECT data_type
      INTO current_type
      FROM information_schema.columns
     WHERE table_schema = 'public'
       AND table_name = target.relation_name
       AND column_name = target.column_name;

    IF current_type IS NULL THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'Expected timestamp column %.% is missing',
        target.relation_name, target.column_name;
    ELSIF current_type = 'timestamp without time zone' THEN
      EXECUTE format(
        'ALTER TABLE %I ALTER COLUMN %I TYPE TIMESTAMPTZ USING %I AT TIME ZONE ''UTC''',
        target.relation_name,
        target.column_name,
        target.column_name
      );
    ELSIF current_type != 'timestamp with time zone' THEN
      RAISE EXCEPTION 'Expected timestamp column %.% has unsupported type %',
        target.relation_name, target.column_name, current_type;
    END IF;
  END LOOP;
END $$;

==> packages/db/sql/024_chain_certifications.sql <==
-- Live execution requires both an operator allowlist entry and an independently
-- reviewed certification record. This migration intentionally seeds no rows.

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS chain_certifications (
  chain TEXT PRIMARY KEY CHECK (chain IN ('solana', 'polygon', 'robinhood-chain')),
  status TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' CHECK (status IN ('pending', 'certified', 'revoked')),
  evidence_path TEXT,
  evidence_sha256 TEXT,
  reviewed_by TEXT,
  reviewed_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  expires_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  CONSTRAINT chain_certifications_certified_evidence_check CHECK (
    status != 'certified'
    OR (
      evidence_path LIKE 'docs/certification/%'
      AND evidence_sha256 ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$'
      AND LENGTH(BTRIM(reviewed_by)) > 0
      AND reviewed_at IS NOT NULL
    )
  ),
  CONSTRAINT chain_certifications_expiry_check CHECK (
    expires_at IS NULL OR reviewed_at IS NULL OR expires_at > reviewed_at
  )
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_chain_certifications_active
  ON chain_certifications (status, expires_at);

==> packages/db/sql/028_copy_execution_lifecycle.sql <==
-- Canonical source-event, position, and copy-execution lifecycle.
-- This migration extends 023/027 forward so previously-applied migrations remain immutable.

ALTER TABLE source_trades
  ALTER COLUMN transaction_hash DROP NOT NULL,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS source_event_type TEXT,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS source_event_id VARCHAR(256),
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS source_event_index VARCHAR(128),
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS event_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS observed_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS confirmation_state TEXT,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS confirmation_updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ;

UPDATE source_trades
SET source_event_type = COALESCE(source_event_type, 'transaction'),
    source_event_id = COALESCE(source_event_id, transaction_hash),
    source_event_index = COALESCE(source_event_index, '0'),
    event_at = COALESCE(event_at, created_at),
    observed_at = COALESCE(observed_at, created_at),
    confirmation_state = COALESCE(
      confirmation_state,
      CASE
        WHEN status IN ('observed', 'confirmed', 'finalized', 'reversed') THEN status
        ELSE 'observed'
      END
    ),
    confirmation_updated_at = COALESCE(confirmation_updated_at, created_at)
WHERE source_event_type IS NULL
   OR source_event_id IS NULL
   OR source_event_index IS NULL
   OR event_at IS NULL
   OR observed_at IS NULL
   OR confirmation_state IS NULL
   OR confirmation_updated_at IS NULL;

ALTER TABLE source_trades
  ALTER COLUMN source_event_type SET NOT NULL,
  ALTER COLUMN source_event_id SET NOT NULL,
  ALTER COLUMN source_event_index SET NOT NULL,
  ALTER COLUMN source_event_index SET DEFAULT '0',
  ALTER COLUMN event_at SET NOT NULL,
  ALTER COLUMN observed_at SET NOT NULL,
  ALTER COLUMN observed_at SET DEFAULT NOW(),
  ALTER COLUMN confirmation_state SET NOT NULL,
  ALTER COLUMN confirmation_state SET DEFAULT 'observed',
  ALTER COLUMN confirmation_updated_at SET NOT NULL,
  ALTER COLUMN confirmation_updated_at SET DEFAULT NOW();

DO $$
DECLARE
  legacy_source_trade_key text;
BEGIN
  -- Drop 023's UNIQUE(chain, transaction_hash, wallet_address, token_mint,
  -- direction), matched by COLUMN SHAPE rather than by name.
  --
  -- This was name-matched against a 76-character literal. PostgreSQL truncates
  -- identifiers at 63 bytes, so the constraint it actually created is named
  -- source_trades_chain_transaction_hash_wallet_address_token_mint_ and the
  -- equality test could never be true. The guard silently did nothing, the DROP
  -- never ran, and 023's key survived on every database that applied 023 -- while
  -- this file went on to install the replacement identity
  -- (unq_source_trades_canonical_event) as though the old one were gone.
  --
  -- The consequence is not cosmetic. That key forbids two rows sharing
  -- (chain, transaction_hash, wallet_address, token_mint, direction), which is a
  -- shape real ingestion produces: one transaction carrying two fills of the same
  -- token in the same direction. source_event_index exists in the replacement key
  -- precisely to tell those apart, so the collision is expected -- and was being
  -- rejected with a 23505 instead.
  --
  -- Shape matching is what this repo's migration rule asks for, for exactly this
  -- reason. It stays idempotent: once dropped, the SELECT finds nothing.
  SELECT c.conname INTO legacy_source_trade_key
  FROM pg_constraint c
  WHERE c.conrelid = 'source_trades'::regclass
    AND c.contype = 'u'
    AND (
      SELECT array_agg(a.attname::text ORDER BY a.attname)
      FROM unnest(c.conkey) AS k(attnum)
      JOIN pg_attribute a
        ON a.attrelid = c.conrelid
       AND a.attnum = k.attnum
    ) = ARRAY['chain', 'direction', 'token_mint', 'transaction_hash', 'wallet_address']
  LIMIT 1;

  IF legacy_source_trade_key IS NOT NULL THEN
    EXECUTE format('ALTER TABLE source_trades DROP CONSTRAINT %I', legacy_source_trade_key);
  END IF;

  IF EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM pg_constraint
    WHERE conrelid = 'source_trades'::regclass
      AND conname = 'source_trades_direction_check'
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE source_trades DROP CONSTRAINT source_trades_direction_check;
  END IF;

  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint
    WHERE conrelid = 'source_trades'::regclass
      AND conname = 'chk_source_trades_direction'
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE source_trades
      ADD CONSTRAINT chk_source_trades_direction
      CHECK (direction IN ('buy', 'sell', 'transfer_in', 'transfer_out'));
  END IF;

  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint
    WHERE conrelid = 'source_trades'::regclass
      AND conname = 'chk_source_trades_chain'
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE source_trades
      ADD CONSTRAINT chk_source_trades_chain
      CHECK (chain IN ('solana', 'polygon', 'robinhood-chain'));
  END IF;

  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint
    WHERE conrelid = 'source_trades'::regclass
      AND conname = 'chk_source_trades_event_type'
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE source_trades
      ADD CONSTRAINT chk_source_trades_event_type
      CHECK (source_event_type IN ('transaction', 'order', 'venue_trade'));
  END IF;

  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint
    WHERE conrelid = 'source_trades'::regclass
      AND conname = 'chk_source_trades_confirmation'
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE source_trades
      ADD CONSTRAINT chk_source_trades_confirmation
      CHECK (confirmation_state IN ('observed', 'confirmed', 'finalized', 'reversed'));
  END IF;

  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint
    WHERE conrelid = 'source_trades'::regclass
      AND conname = 'chk_source_trades_quantities'
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE source_trades
      ADD CONSTRAINT chk_source_trades_quantities
      CHECK (
        token_amount > 0
        AND (amount_usd IS NULL OR amount_usd >= 0)
        AND (price_usd IS NULL OR price_usd >= 0)
      );
  END IF;

  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint
    WHERE conrelid = 'source_trades'::regclass
      AND conname = 'chk_source_trades_transaction_identity'
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE source_trades
      ADD CONSTRAINT chk_source_trades_transaction_identity
      CHECK (source_event_type <> 'transaction' OR transaction_hash IS NOT NULL);
  END IF;
END $$;

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS unq_source_trades_canonical_event
  ON source_trades (chain, source_event_type, source_event_id, source_event_index);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_source_trades_position_order
  ON source_trades (wallet_address, chain, token_mint, event_at, id)
  WHERE confirmation_state IN ('confirmed', 'finalized');

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION reject_source_trade_payload_mutation()
RETURNS TRIGGER
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
BEGIN
  IF NEW.chain IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.chain
    OR NEW.source_event_type IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.source_event_type
    OR NEW.source_event_id IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.source_event_id
    OR NEW.source_event_index IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.source_event_index
    OR NEW.transaction_hash IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.transaction_hash
    OR NEW.wallet_address IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.wallet_address
    OR NEW.token_mint IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.token_mint
    OR NEW.direction IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.direction
    OR NEW.amount_usd IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.amount_usd
    OR NEW.token_amount IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.token_amount
    OR NEW.price_usd IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.price_usd
    OR NEW.event_at IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.event_at
    OR NEW.observed_at IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.observed_at
    OR NEW.created_at IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.created_at
  THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'source trade payload is immutable';
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION enforce_source_confirmation_transition()
RETURNS TRIGGER
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
BEGIN
  IF NEW.confirmation_state = OLD.confirmation_state THEN
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;

  IF NOT (
    (OLD.confirmation_state = 'observed' AND NEW.confirmation_state IN ('confirmed', 'finalized', 'reversed'))
    OR (OLD.confirmation_state = 'confirmed' AND NEW.confirmation_state IN ('finalized', 'reversed'))
    OR (OLD.confirmation_state = 'finalized' AND NEW.confirmation_state = 'reversed')
  ) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'invalid source confirmation transition: % -> %', OLD.confirmation_state, NEW.confirmation_state;
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trg_source_trade_payload_immutable ON source_trades;
CREATE TRIGGER trg_source_trade_payload_immutable
  BEFORE UPDATE ON source_trades
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION reject_source_trade_payload_mutation();

DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trg_source_confirmation_transition ON source_trades;
CREATE TRIGGER trg_source_confirmation_transition
  BEFORE UPDATE OF confirmation_state ON source_trades
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION enforce_source_confirmation_transition();

  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),

    CHECK (confirmation_state IN ('observed', 'confirmed', 'finalized', 'reversed')),
  evidence_id VARCHAR(256) NOT NULL,
  observed_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  UNIQUE (source_trade_id, confirmation_state, evidence_id)
);

ALTER TABLE wallet_positions
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS opening_balance NUMERIC NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS opening_cost_basis_usd NUMERIC NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS total_acquired_quantity NUMERIC NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS total_reduced_quantity NUMERIC NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS unmatched_reduction_quantity NUMERIC NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS last_event_at TIMESTAMPTZ;

UPDATE wallet_positions
SET opening_balance = balance,
    opening_cost_basis_usd = cost_basis_usd
WHERE opening_balance = 0
  AND opening_cost_basis_usd = 0
  AND (balance <> 0 OR cost_basis_usd <> 0)
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM information_schema.tables
    WHERE table_schema = 'public'
      AND table_name = 'source_position_applications'
  );

DO $$
BEGIN
  IF NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint
    WHERE conrelid = 'wallet_positions'::regclass
      AND conname = 'chk_wallet_positions_lifecycle_totals'
  ) THEN
    ALTER TABLE wallet_positions
      ADD CONSTRAINT chk_wallet_positions_lifecycle_totals
      CHECK (
        opening_balance >= 0
        AND opening_cost_basis_usd >= 0
        AND total_acquired_quantity >= 0
        AND total_reduced_quantity >= 0
        AND unmatched_reduction_quantity >= 0
        AND cost_basis_usd >= 0
      );
  END IF;
END $$;

  token_mint VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL,
  opening_quantity NUMERIC NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (opening_quantity >= 0),
  opening_cost_basis_usd NUMERIC NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (opening_cost_basis_usd >= 0),
  confirmed_quantity NUMERIC NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (confirmed_quantity >= 0),
  reserved_sell_quantity NUMERIC NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (reserved_sell_quantity >= 0),
  cost_basis_usd NUMERIC NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (cost_basis_usd >= 0),

  last_evidence_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),

);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS copy_executions (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  source_trade_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES source_trades(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  chain VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL CHECK (chain IN ('solana', 'polygon', 'robinhood-chain')),
  target_account VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL,
  token_mint VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL,
  direction VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL CHECK (direction IN ('buy', 'sell')),
  execution_mode VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL CHECK (execution_mode IN ('paper', 'live', 'shadow')),
  client_order_id VARCHAR(128) NOT NULL,
  state VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL DEFAULT 'requested'
    CHECK (state IN (
      'requested', 'simulated', 'submitted', 'partially_filled', 'confirmed',
      'failed', 'cancelled', 'reconciliation_required'
    )),
  requested_base_quantity NUMERIC,
  requested_quote_quantity NUMERIC,
  confirmed_base_quantity NUMERIC NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (confirmed_base_quantity >= 0),
  confirmed_quote_quantity NUMERIC NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (confirmed_quote_quantity >= 0),
  reserved_base_quantity NUMERIC NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (reserved_base_quantity >= 0),
  max_submission_attempts SMALLINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 3 CHECK (max_submission_attempts BETWEEN 1 AND 10),
  submission_attempts SMALLINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (submission_attempts >= 0),
  simulation_id VARCHAR(256),
  simulated_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  submission_type VARCHAR(32) CHECK (submission_type IN ('transaction', 'order')),
  submission_id VARCHAR(256),
  venue_order_id VARCHAR(256),
  transaction_hash VARCHAR(256),
  last_error TEXT,
  next_reconciliation_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  reconciliation_claimed_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  reconciliation_claim_id UUID,
  reconciliation_attempts SMALLINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (reconciliation_attempts >= 0),
  max_reconciliation_attempts SMALLINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 10 CHECK (max_reconciliation_attempts BETWEEN 1 AND 100),
  requested_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  submitted_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  confirmed_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
  updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
  CHECK (
    (requested_base_quantity IS NOT NULL AND requested_base_quantity > 0)
    OR (requested_quote_quantity IS NOT NULL AND requested_quote_quantity > 0)
  ),
  CHECK (requested_base_quantity IS NULL OR requested_base_quantity > 0),
  CHECK (requested_quote_quantity IS NULL OR requested_quote_quantity > 0),
  CHECK (submission_attempts <= max_submission_attempts),
  CHECK ((submission_type IS NULL) = (submission_id IS NULL)),
  UNIQUE (source_trade_id, target_account, execution_mode),
  UNIQUE (chain, target_account, client_order_id)
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_copy_executions_reconciliation
  ON copy_executions (next_reconciliation_at, requested_at)
  WHERE state IN ('submitted', 'partially_filled', 'reconciliation_required');

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS copy_execution_state_history (
  id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  execution_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES copy_executions(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,
  from_state VARCHAR(32),
  to_state VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL,
  reason TEXT,
  changed_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION enforce_copy_execution_state_transition()
RETURNS TRIGGER
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
BEGIN
  IF NEW.state = OLD.state THEN
    RETURN NEW;
  END IF;

  IF NOT (
    (OLD.state = 'requested' AND NEW.state IN ('simulated', 'failed', 'cancelled', 'reconciliation_required'))
    OR (OLD.state = 'simulated' AND NEW.state IN ('submitted', 'confirmed', 'failed', 'cancelled', 'reconciliation_required'))
    OR (OLD.state = 'submitted' AND NEW.state IN ('partially_filled', 'confirmed', 'failed', 'cancelled', 'reconciliation_required'))
    OR (OLD.state = 'partially_filled' AND NEW.state IN ('partially_filled', 'confirmed', 'cancelled', 'reconciliation_required'))
    OR (OLD.state = 'reconciliation_required' AND NEW.state IN ('submitted', 'partially_filled', 'confirmed', 'failed', 'cancelled', 'reconciliation_required'))
    OR (OLD.state = 'confirmed' AND NEW.state = 'reconciliation_required')
  ) THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'invalid copy execution transition: % -> %', OLD.state, NEW.state;
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;

DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS trg_copy_execution_state_transition ON copy_executions;
CREATE TRIGGER trg_copy_execution_state_transition
  BEFORE UPDATE OF state ON copy_executions
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION enforce_copy_execution_state_transition();

  quote_quantity NUMERIC CHECK (quote_quantity IS NULL OR quote_quantity >= 0),
  price_usd NUMERIC CHECK (price_usd IS NULL OR price_usd >= 0),
  confirmation_state TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'observed'
    CHECK (confirmation_state IN ('observed', 'confirmed', 'finalized', 'reversed')),

  occurred_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
  observed_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),

);

    OR NEW.completes_execution IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.completes_execution
    OR NEW.occurred_at IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.occurred_at
    OR NEW.observed_at IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.observed_at
  THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'copy execution evidence payload is immutable';
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END;
$$;
