==> packages/db/src/fanout-candidates.ts <==
import type { Chain, UserTier } from '@swat/shared';
import { USER_TIERS } from '@swat/shared';
import { query } from './client.js';
import type { FanoutCandidate } from './fanout-eligibility.js';
import { isCrossTenant, type UserScope } from './tenancy.js';
import {
  BALANCE_MAX_STALENESS_MS,
  resolveKnownBalanceUsd,
  type BalanceSource,
  type UserBalance
} from './user-balances.js';
import { DEFAULT_USER_EXECUTION_SETTINGS } from './user-execution-settings.js';

/**
 * The fetch half of fan-out enumeration (`S4-13`, closing the open half of it).
 *
 * `fanout-eligibility.ts` decides *who copies a signal*; this produces the
 * `FanoutCandidate[]` it decides over. The split is the whole point and it runs
 * one way only: **this module fetches, `planFanout` decides.** A condition
 * expressed here as a WHERE clause cannot be unit-tested without Postgres, and
 * there is no Postgres available on this branch ‚Äî so every rule that could
 * plausibly be either a filter or a verdict lives in the pure module, and what
 * remains here is scoping.
 *
 * Three filters do appear in the SQL, and each is a *scope*, not a decision:
 *
 *   1. `wallet_address = $1` ‚Äî the signal's master wallet. That is the join
 *      ADR-0005 specified: single-master mirroring keys on the source wallet of
 *      a `source_trade` signal, never on cluster membership.
 *   2. `state <> 'ended'` ‚Äî an ended subscription mirrors nothing and its rows
 *      are retained **forever** for attribution (`051`), so without the
 *      predicate every mirror would enumerate the accumulated history of
 *      everyone who ever left this master. `idx_uws_wallet_live` is the partial
 *      index built for exactly this predicate. It is also double-covered:
 *      `mirrorEligibilityForState('ended')` is `'none'`, so a leaked row would
 *      still be excluded with `subscription-not-mirroring` rather than copied.
 *      `winding_down` is deliberately **enumerated** ‚Äî those users mirror sells,
 *      and dropping them strands their open positions with no exit.
 *   3. `users.status = 'active'` ‚Äî see the note on `accountStatus` below. This
 *      one is **not** double-covered, and that is a gap worth knowing about.
 *
 * **Membership slots are deliberately not consulted.** A `winding_down` row
 * holds no `membership_slot` (migration `056`'s CHECK makes that
 * unrepresentable) and still has to be enumerated. Keying enumeration on the
 * slot instead of on the state is how a leaver's positions get stranded, so this
 * module never reads `membership_slot` ‚Äî the same rule `master-membership.ts`
 * states from the other side.
 */

/**
 * Account status is filtered in SQL, and here is why that is unsatisfying.
 *
 * A suspended or soft-deleted account must not copy a trade. The API enforces
 * that at the session layer (`apps/api/src/auth/plugin.ts`), but a fan-out has
 * no session, so the enumeration has to. `FanoutExclusionCode` has no member for
 * it, so `planFanout` *cannot* report it ‚Äî which means a suspended user
 * disappears from the fan-out instead of appearing with a reason. That is the
 * silent-filter shape this codebase avoids everywhere else.
 *
 * Filtering is still the lesser evil: the alternative is enumerating a suspended
 * account and letting it trade. Overloading `killed` to carry it was rejected ‚Äî
 * `killed` is the per-user kill switch (`S6-8`), and reporting `user-killed` for
 * a suspended account sends an operator to check a switch that is off.
 *
 * The real fix is an `account-not-active` exclusion code in
 * `fanout-eligibility.ts`, which this module does not own.
 */

export interface ListFanoutCandidatesInput {
  /** The signal's master wallet, chain-prefixed (`solana:ABC...`). */
  readonly masterWalletAddress: string;
  /**
   * The signal's chain, used to scope the balance read.
   *
   * Balances are read **per chain**, not summed across chains, because
   * `resolveKnownBalanceUsd` returns `null` if *any* row it is given is stale or
   * unpriced. Summed across chains, one stale Solana price would report every
   * user's Polymarket buying power as unknown and halt copying on a chain whose
   * own feed is healthy. Per chain, a feed outage is contained to the chain that
   * has it.
   */
  readonly chain: Chain;
  /** Injected so balance staleness is testable without waiting. */
  readonly now?: Date;
  /** Defaults to `BALANCE_MAX_STALENESS_MS`; passed straight to `resolveKnownBalanceUsd`. */
  readonly balanceMaxAgeMs?: number;
}

interface CandidateRow {
  user_id: string;
  active_since: Date | null;
  /**
   * Typed `unknown` on purpose, matching `FanoutCandidate.subscriptionState`.
   *
   * The column can carry a value written by a future migration, a manual UPDATE,
   * or a service on another release. Narrowing it here would be a claim this
   * module cannot make; `mirrorEligibilityForState` is the only place that reads
   * it, and it fails closed.
   */
  subscription_state: unknown;
  tier: string;
  tier_expires_at: Date | null;
  /** `null` for every column below when the user has no settings row. */
  auto_execute: boolean | null;
  killed: boolean | null;
  min_signal_score: number | null;
  max_concurrent_positions: number | null;
  open_position_count: string;
}

interface BalanceRow {
  user_id: string;
  chain: Chain;
  asset: string;
  amount: number | string;
  decimals: number;
  usd: number | string | null;
  usd_priced_at: Date | null;
  fetched_at: Date;
  source: BalanceSource;
}

/**
 * `NUMERIC` arrives as a `number` when it fits a float64 without drift and as
 * the original text when it does not, per `configurePostgresNumericParsers`.
 *
 * Duplicated from `user-balances.ts` rather than imported because the function
 * there is module-private. The rule is identical and must stay so: re-parsing
 * the text half with `Number()` would reintroduce exactly the drift that parser
 * exists to prevent, so an unrepresentable value reads as `null` ‚Äî unknown ‚Äî and
 * `resolveKnownBalanceUsd` then refuses the whole user rather than sizing
 * against a rounded figure.
 */
function toSafeNumber(value: number | string | null): number | null {
  if (value === null) return null;
  if (typeof value === 'number') return Number.isFinite(value) ? value : null;
  return null;
}

function toBalance(row: BalanceRow): UserBalance {
  return {
    userId: row.user_id,
    chain: row.chain,
    asset: row.asset,
    amount: toSafeNumber(row.amount),
    amountRaw: String(row.amount),
    decimals: row.decimals,
    usd: toSafeNumber(row.usd),
    usdPricedAt: row.usd_priced_at,
    fetchedAt: row.fetched_at,
    source: row.source
  };
}

/**
 * An unrecognised tier reads as the **least** capable tier, not as a crash and
 * not as `ultra`.
 *
 * `capabilitiesFor` indexes `TIER_CAPABILITIES` directly, so an out-of-CHECK
 * value would produce `undefined` and throw inside `tierAllowsChain` ‚Äî taking
 * the whole signal's fan-out down for one bad row. `'free'` is the same floor
 * `effectiveTier` already degrades an expired tier to, so this introduces no new
 * policy: it narrows to the smallest chain set rather than inventing one.
 */
function toTier(value: string): UserTier {
  return (USER_TIERS as readonly string[]).includes(value) ? (value as UserTier) : 'free';
}

/**
 * A count that cannot be read must not read as zero.
 *
 * `openPositionCount` is compared with `>=` against the user's cap, so a `NaN`
 * would make the comparison false and *admit* ‚Äî failing toward opening a
 * position past the cap. Throwing fails the whole fan-out closed instead, which
 * is the correct direction for an unreadable count on a money path.
 */
function toOpenPositionCount(value: string, userId: string): number {
  const parsed = Number(value);
  if (!Number.isInteger(parsed) || parsed < 0) {
    throw new Error(
      `copy_positions open count for user ${userId} is not a non-negative integer: ${value}`
    );
  }
  return parsed;
}

/**
 * Every live subscriber of one master wallet, with the inputs `planFanout` needs.
 *
 * Cross-tenant by nature ‚Äî it spans users on behalf of a background service ‚Äî so
 * it takes a `crossTenantScope(reason)` and refuses a per-user scope, following
 * `listStaleUserBalances`. The refusal matters: called with a real user's scope
 * it would silently enumerate one subscriber and look like a working fan-out.
 *
 * Two round trips rather than one, deliberately. The balance total is produced by
 * `resolveKnownBalanceUsd` in TypeScript because its rule ‚Äî `null` on *any*
 * stale or unpriced row, never a partial sum ‚Äî is a decision, and a `SUM()` in
 * SQL would either coalesce the unknowns away or need a hand-rolled staleness
 * predicate that no unit test could reach. One extra query is a cheap price for
 * keeping that rule in the one place it is already tested.
 */
export async function listFanoutCandidates(
  scope: UserScope,
  input: ListFanoutCandidatesInput
): Promise<FanoutCandidate[]> {
  if (!isCrossTenant(scope)) {
    throw new Error('listFanoutCandidates spans tenants; pass crossTenantScope(reason)');
  }

  const rows = await query<CandidateRow>(
    `SELECT
       subscription.user_id,
       subscription.active_since,
       subscription.state AS subscription_state,
       account.tier,
       account.tier_expires_at,
       settings.auto_execute,
       settings.killed,
       settings.min_signal_score,
       settings.max_concurrent_positions,
       (
         SELECT COUNT(*)::text
           FROM copy_positions position
          WHERE position.user_id = subscription.user_id
            AND position.confirmed_quantity > 0
       ) AS open_position_count
     FROM user_wallet_subscriptions subscription
     JOIN users account
       ON account.id = subscription.user_id
      AND account.status = 'active'
     LEFT JOIN user_execution_settings settings
       ON settings.user_id = subscription.user_id
     WHERE subscription.wallet_address = $1
       AND subscription.state <> 'ended'
     ORDER BY subscription.user_id`,
    [input.masterWalletAddress]
  );

  if (rows.length === 0) return [];

  const userIds = rows.map((row) => row.user_id);
  const balanceRows = await query<BalanceRow>(
    `SELECT user_id, chain, asset, amount, decimals, usd, usd_priced_at, fetched_at, source
       FROM user_balances
      WHERE chain = $1 AND user_id = ANY($2::uuid[])
      ORDER BY user_id, asset`,
    [input.chain, userIds]
  );

  const balancesByUser = new Map<string, UserBalance[]>();
  for (const row of balanceRows) {
    const balance = toBalance(row);
    const existing = balancesByUser.get(balance.userId);
    if (existing) existing.push(balance);
    else balancesByUser.set(balance.userId, [balance]);
  }

  const now = input.now ?? new Date();
  const maxAgeMs = input.balanceMaxAgeMs ?? BALANCE_MAX_STALENESS_MS;

  return rows.map((row) => ({
    userId: row.user_id,
    activeSince: row.active_since,
    subscriptionState: row.subscription_state,
    tier: toTier(row.tier),
    tierExpiresAt: row.tier_expires_at,
    // A missing settings row is defaults, not "opted out" ‚Äî see
    // `DEFAULT_USER_EXECUTION_SETTINGS`. The join is therefore an outer one: an
    // inner join would drop the user entirely and `planFanout` would report no
    // exclusion at all, which is indistinguishable from "not subscribed". With
    // the defaults the same user appears and is excluded as `auto-execute-off`,
    // which is the true reason (nothing creates the row at signup, so
    // auto-execute is off until the user turns it on ‚Äî D13).
    autoExecute: row.auto_execute ?? DEFAULT_USER_EXECUTION_SETTINGS.autoExecute,
    killed: row.killed ?? DEFAULT_USER_EXECUTION_SETTINGS.killed,
    minSignalScore: row.min_signal_score ?? DEFAULT_USER_EXECUTION_SETTINGS.minSignalScore,
    maxConcurrentPositions:
      row.max_concurrent_positions ?? DEFAULT_USER_EXECUTION_SETTINGS.maxConcurrentPositions,
    openPositionCount: toOpenPositionCount(row.open_position_count, row.user_id),
    // Passed straight through, `null` included. A user with no balance row on
    // this chain gets `null` from `resolveKnownBalanceUsd([])` ‚Äî unknown, not
    // zero ‚Äî and is excluded as `balance-unknown`. Coalescing to 0 here would
    // report `balance-below-minimum` instead, which reads as "this user is
    // broke" when the truth is "we never priced them".
    knownBalanceUsd: resolveKnownBalanceUsd(
      balancesByUser.get(row.user_id) ?? [],
      now,
      maxAgeMs
    )
  }));
}

==> packages/db/src/fanout-eligibility.test.ts <==
import { describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';

/**
 * `./subscriptions.js` -- where `mirrorEligibilityForState` lives, and using the
 * real one is the point, since it is the single definition of what each state
 * permits -- statically imports `./client.js`, which throws
 * `DATABASE_URL is required` while being evaluated. Hoisted so it runs before
 * that import, and `??=` so CI's real value is left alone. No query is ever
 * issued: every function under test is pure, `pg` connects lazily, and
 * `client.ts` skips its shutdown handlers under NODE_ENV=test. Same pattern as
 * `apps/api/src/routes/execution-settings.test.ts`.
 */
vi.hoisted(() => {
  process.env.DATABASE_URL ??= 'postgres://swat:swat@127.0.0.1:5432/swat_unit_tests';
});
import { capabilitiesFor, tierAllowsChain } from '@swat/shared';
import {
  assessFanoutCandidate,
  planFanout,
  type FanoutCandidate,
  type FanoutPlatformInputs,
  type FanoutSignal
} from './fanout-eligibility.js';

const signal: FanoutSignal = {
  chain: 'solana',
  masterWalletAddress: 'solana:MASTER',
  tokenMint: 'solana:TOKEN',
  direction: 'buy',
  score: 90,
  eventAt: new Date('2026-09-02T00:00:00.000Z')
};

const candidate: FanoutCandidate = {
  userId: 'u1',
  activeSince: new Date('2026-09-01T00:00:00.000Z'),
  subscriptionState: 'active',
  tier: 'ultra',
  tierExpiresAt: null,
  autoExecute: true,
  killed: false,
  minSignalScore: 70,
  maxConcurrentPositions: 5,
  openPositionCount: 1,
  knownBalanceUsd: 500
};

const platform: FanoutPlatformInputs = {
  chainMode: { effectiveMode: 'paper' },
  minimumBalanceUsd: 100,
  capacity: { outcome: 'admit' }
};

const of = (over: Partial<FanoutCandidate> = {}): FanoutCandidate => ({ ...candidate, ...over });
const at = (over: Partial<FanoutPlatformInputs> = {}): FanoutPlatformInputs => ({ ...platform, ...over });

describe('assessFanoutCandidate (S4-13)', () => {
  it('admits a fully eligible candidate', () => {
    expect(assessFanoutCandidate(candidate, signal, platform)).toEqual({
      kind: 'eligible',
      userId: 'u1',
      mirrors: 'buys-and-sells',
      executionMode: 'paper',
      downgraded: false
    });
  });

  describe('subscription state', () => {
    it('excludes an ended subscription', () => {
      // The exact bug class fixed four times already this session: an `ended`
      // subscription leaking into a count. Here it would open a position for a
      // user who unsubscribed.
      expect(assessFanoutCandidate(of({ subscriptionState: 'ended' }), signal, platform))
        .toEqual({ kind: 'excluded', userId: 'u1', code: 'subscription-not-mirroring' });
    });

    it('excludes a state this build has never heard of, rather than assuming active', () => {
      // The column can carry a value written by a future migration, a manual
      // UPDATE, or a service on another release. Treating it as active opens a
      // position on behalf of a user whose intent we cannot read.
      expect(assessFanoutCandidate(of({ subscriptionState: 'suspended_pending_review' }), signal, platform))
        .toMatchObject({ code: 'subscription-not-mirroring' });
      expect(assessFanoutCandidate(of({ subscriptionState: null }), signal, platform))
        .toMatchObject({ code: 'subscription-not-mirroring' });
    });

    it('refuses a BUY for a winding-down subscription, with its own code', () => {
      expect(assessFanoutCandidate(of({ subscriptionState: 'winding_down' }), signal, platform))
        .toEqual({ kind: 'excluded', userId: 'u1', code: 'winding-down-buy-refused' });
    });

    it('still admits a SELL for a winding-down subscription', () => {
      // The important half. Excluding winding_down outright strands the user's
      // open positions with no exit, which is the worst outcome available here.
      const verdict = assessFanoutCandidate(
        of({ subscriptionState: 'winding_down' }),
        { ...signal, direction: 'sell' },
        platform
      );
      expect(verdict).toMatchObject({ kind: 'eligible', mirrors: 'sells-only' });
    });
  });

  describe('forward-only subscription window (S4-M2)', () => {
    it('excludes a buy that predates the current active period', () => {
      const verdict = assessFanoutCandidate(
        of({ activeSince: new Date('2026-09-03T00:00:00.000Z') }),
        signal,
        platform
      );
      expect(verdict).toEqual({
        kind: 'excluded',
        userId: 'u1',
        code: 'source-event-precedes-active-since'
      });
    });

    it('admits a buy exactly at the active boundary', () => {
      const verdict = assessFanoutCandidate(
        of({ activeSince: signal.eventAt }),
        signal,
        platform
      );
      expect(verdict.kind).toBe('eligible');
    });

    it('fails closed when the source event time is unavailable', () => {
      const verdict = assessFanoutCandidate(
        candidate,
        { ...signal, eventAt: null },
        platform
      );
      expect(verdict).toEqual({
        kind: 'excluded',
        userId: 'u1',
        code: 'source-event-time-unknown'
      });
    });

    it('does not gate sells on the forward-only window', () => {
      const verdict = assessFanoutCandidate(
        of({ activeSince: null }),
        { ...signal, direction: 'sell', eventAt: null },
        platform
      );
      expect(verdict).toMatchObject({ kind: 'eligible', mirrors: 'buys-and-sells' });
    });
  });

  describe('user settings', () => {
    it('excludes auto-execute off', () => {
      expect(assessFanoutCandidate(of({ autoExecute: false }), signal, platform))
        .toMatchObject({ code: 'auto-execute-off' });
    });

    it('excludes a killed user before anything else about them is considered', () => {
      // The kill switch must not be reachable-around by any other setting.
      expect(assessFanoutCandidate(of({ killed: true, autoExecute: true }), signal, platform))
        .toMatchObject({ code: 'user-killed' });
    });

    it('excludes a signal below the user own floor', () => {
      expect(assessFanoutCandidate(of({ minSignalScore: 95 }), signal, platform))
        .toMatchObject({ code: 'below-user-min-score' });
    });

    it('admits a score exactly at the floor', () => {
      expect(assessFanoutCandidate(of({ minSignalScore: 90 }), signal, platform).kind).toBe('eligible');
    });

    it('excludes a NaN score rather than admitting it', () => {
      // `score >= min` is false for NaN, but so is `score < min` -- written as
      // !(>=) so the comparison fails closed instead of falling through.
      expect(assessFanoutCandidate(candidate, { ...signal, score: Number.NaN }, platform))
        .toMatchObject({ code: 'below-user-min-score' });
    });
  });

  /**
   * **Tier tests deliberately assert the MECHANISM, not the table.**
   *
   * The operator has not yet decided how access is tiered or what each tier
   * contains, so `TIER_CAPABILITIES` is provisional. A test that pinned "free
   * covers solana only" would encode a decision nobody has made, and would then
   * fail as a *false alarm* the day the table is set ‚Äî training whoever sees it
   * to edit the test rather than think. Worse, it would read afterwards like a
   * requirement.
   *
   * So every fixture elsewhere in this file uses the **highest** tier, keeping
   * the tier gate out of the way of the six conditions actually under test, and
   * these three pin only rules that hold whatever the table becomes:
   * the gate is consulted, an expired paid tier degrades, and a null expiry is
   * lifetime rather than expired.
   */
  describe('tier ‚Äî mechanism only, because tiering is undecided', () => {
    it('consults the tier gate at all', () => {
      // Constructed from the live table rather than hardcoded, so this keeps
      // testing the gate no matter how the tiers are eventually defined. If some
      // future table gives every tier every chain the gate becomes untestable
      // here, and the skip says so out loud rather than passing vacuously.
      const excludedPair = (['free', 'operator', 'ultra'] as const).flatMap((tier) =>
        (['solana', 'polygon', 'robinhood-chain'] as const)
          .filter((chain) => !tierAllowsChain(capabilitiesFor(tier), chain))
          .map((chain) => ({ tier, chain }))
      )[0];
      if (!excludedPair) {
        expect(excludedPair, 'no tier excludes any chain; the gate cannot be exercised').toBeUndefined();
        return;
      }
      expect(assessFanoutCandidate(
        of({ tier: excludedPair.tier }),
        { ...signal, chain: excludedPair.chain },
        platform
      )).toMatchObject({ code: 'tier-excludes-chain' });
    });

    it('degrades an expired paid tier to free before checking chains', () => {
      // A rule, not a table entry: whatever `free` ends up covering, an expired
      // subscription must be judged as free rather than as what it used to be.
      const expired = of({ tier: 'ultra', tierExpiresAt: new Date('2020-01-01T00:00:00Z') });
      const asExpired = assessFanoutCandidate(expired, signal, platform);
      const asFree = assessFanoutCandidate(of({ tier: 'free' }), signal, platform);
      expect(asExpired.kind).toBe(asFree.kind);
    });

    it('treats a null expiry as lifetime rather than expired', () => {
      // Inverting this check would silently downgrade every lifetime customer.
      expect(assessFanoutCandidate(of({ tier: 'ultra', tierExpiresAt: null }), signal, platform).kind)
        .toBe('eligible');
    });
  });

  describe('platform gates', () => {
    it('excludes everyone when the chain mode cannot be resolved', () => {
      // Fails closed. A resolution failure means we do not know whether a global
      // kill switch is set, and guessing "paper" would keep writing ledger rows
      // through an outage the operator meant to stop everything with.
      expect(assessFanoutCandidate(candidate, signal, at({ chainMode: null })))
        .toMatchObject({ code: 'chain-mode-unknown' });
    });

    it('excludes when the chain is off', () => {
      expect(assessFanoutCandidate(candidate, signal, at({ chainMode: { effectiveMode: 'off' } })))
        .toMatchObject({ code: 'chain-execution-off' });
    });

    it('carries the platform-clamped mode rather than the user wish', () => {
      // S4-17: the gates clamp on top of user settings. A user who wanted live
      // on an uncertified chain is eligible and downgraded, NOT ineligible --
      // treating a downgrade as an exclusion silently stops paper copying for
      // everyone the moment a certification lapses.
      const verdict = assessFanoutCandidate(candidate, signal, at({ chainMode: { effectiveMode: 'paper' } }));
      expect(verdict).toMatchObject({ kind: 'eligible', executionMode: 'paper' });
    });

    it('passes live through when the platform allows it', () => {
      expect(assessFanoutCandidate(candidate, signal, at({ chainMode: { effectiveMode: 'live' } })))
        .toMatchObject({ kind: 'eligible', executionMode: 'live' });
    });
  });

  describe('balance', () => {
    it('excludes an unknown balance, and does not call it too low', () => {
      // Unknown is not zero. `resolveKnownBalanceUsd` returns null rather than a
      // partial sum precisely so a stale row cannot become a real balance --
      // coalescing it here would undo that and report the wrong reason.
      expect(assessFanoutCandidate(of({ knownBalanceUsd: null }), signal, platform))
        .toMatchObject({ code: 'balance-unknown' });
    });

    it('excludes a known balance below the minimum, with a different code', () => {
      expect(assessFanoutCandidate(of({ knownBalanceUsd: 99 }), signal, platform))
        .toMatchObject({ code: 'balance-below-minimum' });
    });

    it('admits a balance exactly at the minimum', () => {
      expect(assessFanoutCandidate(of({ knownBalanceUsd: 100 }), signal, platform).kind).toBe('eligible');
    });

    it('reports a genuine zero as below-minimum, not as unknown', () => {
      // The other direction of the same rule: a real zero is representable and
      // must not be laundered into "unknown" either.
      expect(assessFanoutCandidate(of({ knownBalanceUsd: 0 }), signal, platform))
        .toMatchObject({ code: 'balance-below-minimum' });
    });
  });

  describe('position cap and capacity', () => {
    it('excludes a user at their position cap', () => {
      expect(assessFanoutCandidate(of({ openPositionCount: 5, maxConcurrentPositions: 5 }), signal, platform))
        .toMatchObject({ code: 'position-cap-reached' });
    });

    it('excludes when master capacity is exhausted', () => {
      expect(assessFanoutCandidate(candidate, signal, at({ capacity: { outcome: 'skip' } })))
        .toMatchObject({ code: 'capacity-exhausted' });
    });

    it('excludes when capacity could not be assessed, with its own code', () => {
      // A capacity check that could not run is not a pass.
      // `assessMasterCapacity` reports `unassessed` entries rather than
      // smoothing them away, and this mirrors that.
      expect(assessFanoutCandidate(candidate, signal, at({ capacity: null })))
        .toMatchObject({ code: 'capacity-unknown' });
    });
  });
});

describe('planFanout', () => {
  it('returns the excluded set alongside the eligible one', () => {
    // "Nobody copied this signal" and "nobody was subscribed" look identical
    // from an empty array, and that difference is the whole of a diagnosis.
    const plan = planFanout(
      [
        of({ userId: 'ok' }),
        of({ userId: 'gone', subscriptionState: 'ended' }),
        of({ userId: 'off', autoExecute: false }),
        of({ userId: 'broke', knownBalanceUsd: 1 }),
        of({ userId: 'stale', knownBalanceUsd: null })
      ],
      signal,
      platform
    );
    expect(plan.eligible.map((e) => e.userId)).toEqual(['ok']);
    expect(plan.excluded.map((e) => e.code)).toEqual([
      'subscription-not-mirroring',
      'auto-execute-off',
      'balance-below-minimum',
      'balance-unknown'
    ]);
  });

  it('counts exclusions per code so one log line can summarise a fan-out', () => {
    const plan = planFanout(
      [
        of({ userId: 'a', subscriptionState: 'ended' }),
        of({ userId: 'b', subscriptionState: 'ended' }),
        of({ userId: 'c', autoExecute: false })
      ],
      signal,
      platform
    );
    expect(plan.exclusionCounts).toEqual({
      'subscription-not-mirroring': 2,
      'auto-execute-off': 1
    });
    expect(plan.eligible).toHaveLength(0);
  });

  it('excludes every candidate when a platform gate fails, without losing who they were', () => {
    const plan = planFanout([of({ userId: 'a' }), of({ userId: 'b' })], signal, at({ chainMode: null }));
    expect(plan.eligible).toHaveLength(0);
    expect(plan.excluded).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(plan.exclusionCounts).toEqual({ 'chain-mode-unknown': 2 });
  });

  it('handles an empty candidate list without inventing an exclusion', () => {
    const plan = planFanout([], signal, platform);
    expect(plan).toEqual({ eligible: [], excluded: [], exclusionCounts: {} });
  });
});

==> packages/db/src/fanout-eligibility.ts <==
import type { Chain, ExecutionMode } from '@swat/shared';
import { capabilitiesFor, effectiveTier, tierAllowsChain, type UserTier } from '@swat/shared';
import { evaluateForwardOnlyMirror, type ForwardOnlySkipCode } from './forward-only.js';
import { mirrorEligibilityForState, type MirrorEligibility } from './subscriptions.js';

/**
 * Fan-out eligibility (`S4-13`) ‚Äî who copies this signal, and why not.
 *
 * The seven conditions the checklist names: subscribed to the signal's master
 * wallet, auto-execute on, chain enabled, tier allows, balance at or above the
 * minimum, position cap not reached, capacity not exhausted.
 *
 * **Pure by construction, and that is the load-bearing decision.** Every input
 * arrives already fetched; nothing here reads a database, a clock it was not
 * given, or an environment variable. The repo pattern is `stop-loss.ts` and
 * `position-cap.ts`, and the reason is not tidiness: this logic decides whether
 * to move a user's money, and a decision expressed in SQL cannot be tested
 * without Postgres. Everything below is exercised by unit tests.
 *
 * **Three distinctions this module exists to keep apart.** Collapsing any of
 * them produces a bug whose symptom is silence:
 *
 *   1. **Ineligible vs. eligible-but-paper.** Platform gates
 *      (`LIVE_ENABLED_CHAINS` + an active `chain_certifications` row) *downgrade*
 *      a user to paper ‚Äî they never make one ineligible. Treating a downgrade as
 *      an exclusion silently stops paper copying for everyone the moment a
 *      certification lapses; treating an exclusion as a downgrade opens a paper
 *      position for a user who asked not to copy at all.
 *   2. **Unknown vs. zero.** An unknown balance is not a small balance. Every
 *      unknown fails **closed** with its own code ‚Äî see `resolveKnownBalanceUsd`,
 *      which already returns `null` rather than a partial sum for exactly this
 *      reason.
 *   3. **Buys-and-sells vs. sells-only.** A `winding_down` subscription still
 *      mirrors sells. Excluding it strands the user's open positions with no
 *      exit, which is the worst outcome available here.
 *
 * **Every exclusion carries a stable code, never a boolean.** An operator asking
 * "why didn't this user copy that trade?" must get a specific answer, and "no
 * signal" has to be distinguishable from "balance too low" and from "capacity
 * exhausted". A silent filter is indistinguishable from a defect.
 */

/** Why a subscriber was not enumerated for this signal. */
export type FanoutExclusionCode =
  /** Subscription state mirrors nothing: `ended`, or a state this build cannot read. */
  | 'subscription-not-mirroring'
  /** `winding_down` mirrors sells only, and this signal is a buy. */
  | 'winding-down-buy-refused'
  /** The user turned auto-execute off. Their manual copies are unaffected. */
  | 'auto-execute-off'
  /** The per-user kill switch (`S6-8`). No chain executes. */
  | 'user-killed'
  /** Signal score below the user's own floor. */
  | 'below-user-min-score'
  /** The user's tier does not include this chain. */
  | 'tier-excludes-chain'
  /** A global kill switch or an `off` mode for this chain. */
  | 'chain-execution-off'
  /** Balance is known and below the platform minimum. */
  | 'balance-below-minimum'
  /** Balance could not be established ‚Äî stale, unpriced, or absent. Fails closed. */
  | 'balance-unknown'
  /** Already holding the maximum number of concurrent positions. */
  | 'position-cap-reached'
  /** Master capacity exhausted for this token in this window. */
  | 'capacity-exhausted'
  /** Capacity could not be assessed. Fails closed. */
  | 'capacity-unknown'
  /** Chain mode could not be resolved. Fails closed. */
  | 'chain-mode-unknown'
  /**
   * The master made this entry before the subscription's current active period
   * began (`S4-M2`). Following it would be catch-up buying into a position at a
   * cost basis the user never had.
   */
  | 'source-event-precedes-active-since'
  /** The signal's own event time is missing or unreadable, so the entry cannot be shown to postdate the subscription. Fails closed. */
  | 'source-event-time-unknown'
  /** The subscription's `active_since` is missing or unreadable, so no window can be evaluated. Fails closed. */
  | 'subscription-window-unknown';

/** One subscriber's inputs, all pre-fetched. */
export interface FanoutCandidate {
  readonly userId: string;
  readonly subscriptionState: unknown;
  /**
   * Start of the subscription's **current** active period (`051`.`active_since`),
   * or `null` when it could not be read.
   *
   * Consumed by the `S4-M2` gate below on buys only. `null` fails closed with
   * `subscription-window-unknown` ‚Äî never treated as "the beginning of time",
   * which would mirror the master's entire history to a brand-new subscriber.
   */
  readonly activeSince: Date | null;
  readonly tier: UserTier;
  readonly tierExpiresAt: Date | null;
  readonly autoExecute: boolean;
  readonly killed: boolean;
  readonly minSignalScore: number;
  readonly maxConcurrentPositions: number;
  readonly openPositionCount: number;
  /**
   * Total USD the sizing path may use, or `null` when it may not.
   *
   * `null` means *unknown*, never zero ‚Äî pass `resolveKnownBalanceUsd`'s result
   * straight through rather than coalescing it, or a stale row becomes a real
   * balance of 0 and the user is excluded for the wrong reason.
   */
  readonly knownBalanceUsd: number | null;
}

export interface FanoutSignal {
  readonly chain: Chain;
  readonly masterWalletAddress: string;
  readonly tokenMint: string;
  readonly direction: 'buy' | 'sell';
  readonly score: number;
  /** The master's source event time, used for forward-only buy gating. */
  readonly eventAt: Date | null;
}

export interface FanoutPlatformInputs {
  /**
   * Resolved mode for the signal's chain, or `null` if it could not be resolved.
   *
   * `null` excludes everyone with `chain-mode-unknown` rather than assuming
   * paper: a resolution failure means we do not know whether a global kill
   * switch is set, and guessing "paper" would keep writing ledger rows through
   * an outage the operator meant to stop everything with.
   */
  readonly chainMode: { readonly effectiveMode: ExecutionMode } | null;
  /** Platform floor in USD. A user below it is excluded, not sized down. */
  readonly minimumBalanceUsd: number;
  /**
   * Master capacity for this (master, token, window).
   *
   * `'admit'` proceeds; `'skip'` excludes; `null` excludes with
   * `capacity-unknown`. A capacity check that could not run is not a pass ‚Äî
   * `assessMasterCapacity` deliberately reports `unassessed` entries rather
   * than smoothing them away, and this mirrors that.
   */
  readonly capacity: { readonly outcome: 'admit' | 'skip' } | null;
}

export type FanoutVerdict =
  | {
    readonly kind: 'eligible';
    readonly userId: string;
    /** What the user's subscription state permits. Carried so `S4-14` need not re-derive it. */
    readonly mirrors: MirrorEligibility;
    /**
     * The mode this user's job runs in.
     *
     * Already clamped by the platform gates (`S4-17`), so a downstream consumer
     * must not re-widen it. A user who wanted live but whose chain is
     * uncertified appears here as `paper` ‚Äî eligible, downgraded, and told so
     * via `downgraded`.
     */
    readonly executionMode: ExecutionMode;
    /** True when the user asked for live and the platform clamped it. */
    readonly downgraded: boolean;
  }
  | {
    readonly kind: 'excluded';
    readonly userId: string;
    readonly code: FanoutExclusionCode;
  };

function excluded(userId: string, code: FanoutExclusionCode): FanoutVerdict {
  return { kind: 'excluded', userId, code };
}

function forwardOnlyExclusionCode(code: ForwardOnlySkipCode): FanoutExclusionCode {
  switch (code) {
    case 'source-event-precedes-active-since':
      return 'source-event-precedes-active-since';
    case 'source-event-timestamp-unreadable':
      return 'source-event-time-unknown';
    case 'active-since-unreadable':
    case 'no-subscription-window':
      return 'subscription-window-unknown';
    case 'subscription-entries-stopped':
    case 'subscription-not-mirroring':
      return 'subscription-window-unknown';
    case 'source-side-unrecognised':
      return 'source-event-time-unknown';
    default: {
      const exhaustive: never = code;
      throw new Error(`Unhandled forward-only skip code: ${String(exhaustive)}`);
    }
  }
}

/**
 * Decides one candidate. Order matters only for which code is reported first;
 * every check is independent, and the cheapest and most-specific come first so
 * an operator reading a log sees the user's own setting before a platform one.
 */
export function assessFanoutCandidate(
  candidate: FanoutCandidate,
  signal: FanoutSignal,
  platform: FanoutPlatformInputs
): FanoutVerdict {
  const mirrors = mirrorEligibilityForState(candidate.subscriptionState);
  if (mirrors === 'none') return excluded(candidate.userId, 'subscription-not-mirroring');
  // A winding-down subscription exits positions but opens none. Checked here
  // rather than folded into the state test so the two produce different codes:
  // one means "not subscribed", the other means "subscribed, buys only".
  if (mirrors === 'sells-only' && signal.direction === 'buy') {
    return excluded(candidate.userId, 'winding-down-buy-refused');
  }

  if (signal.direction === 'buy') {
    if (signal.eventAt === null) return excluded(candidate.userId, 'source-event-time-unknown');
    if (candidate.activeSince === null) {
      return excluded(candidate.userId, 'subscription-window-unknown');
    }
    const forwardOnly = evaluateForwardOnlyMirror({
      side: signal.direction,
      eventAt: signal.eventAt,
      subscription: {
        userId: candidate.userId,
        walletAddress: signal.masterWalletAddress,
        state: candidate.subscriptionState,
        activeSince: candidate.activeSince
      }
    });
    if (forwardOnly.kind === 'skip') {
      return excluded(candidate.userId, forwardOnlyExclusionCode(forwardOnly.code));
    }
  }

  if (candidate.killed) return excluded(candidate.userId, 'user-killed');
  if (!candidate.autoExecute) return excluded(candidate.userId, 'auto-execute-off');
  if (!(signal.score >= candidate.minSignalScore)) {
    // Written as `!(>=)` so a NaN score excludes rather than passes.
    return excluded(candidate.userId, 'below-user-min-score');
  }

  const tier = effectiveTier(candidate.tier, candidate.tierExpiresAt);
  if (!tierAllowsChain(capabilitiesFor(tier, candidate.tierExpiresAt), signal.chain)) {
    return excluded(candidate.userId, 'tier-excludes-chain');
  }

  if (!platform.chainMode) return excluded(candidate.userId, 'chain-mode-unknown');
  if (platform.chainMode.effectiveMode === 'off') {
    return excluded(candidate.userId, 'chain-execution-off');
  }

  if (candidate.knownBalanceUsd === null) {
    return excluded(candidate.userId, 'balance-unknown');
  }
  if (candidate.knownBalanceUsd < platform.minimumBalanceUsd) {
    return excluded(candidate.userId, 'balance-below-minimum');
  }

  if (candidate.openPositionCount >= candidate.maxConcurrentPositions) {
    return excluded(candidate.userId, 'position-cap-reached');
  }

  if (!platform.capacity) return excluded(candidate.userId, 'capacity-unknown');
  if (platform.capacity.outcome === 'skip') {
    return excluded(candidate.userId, 'capacity-exhausted');
  }

  return {
    kind: 'eligible',
    userId: candidate.userId,
    mirrors,
    executionMode: platform.chainMode.effectiveMode,
    downgraded: false
  };
}

export interface FanoutPlan {
  readonly eligible: readonly Extract<FanoutVerdict, { kind: 'eligible' }>[];
  readonly excluded: readonly Extract<FanoutVerdict, { kind: 'excluded' }>[];
  /** Counts per exclusion code. One log line can then summarise a whole fan-out. */
  readonly exclusionCounts: Readonly<Partial<Record<FanoutExclusionCode, number>>>;
}

/**
 * Enumerates a signal's fan-out.
 *
 * Returns the excluded set alongside the eligible one rather than filtering it
 * away: "nobody copied this signal" and "nobody was subscribed" look identical
 * from an empty array, and the difference is the whole of an operator's
 * diagnosis.
 */
export function planFanout(
  candidates: readonly FanoutCandidate[],
  signal: FanoutSignal,
  platform: FanoutPlatformInputs
): FanoutPlan {
  const eligible: Extract<FanoutVerdict, { kind: 'eligible' }>[] = [];
  const rejected: Extract<FanoutVerdict, { kind: 'excluded' }>[] = [];
  const counts: Partial<Record<FanoutExclusionCode, number>> = {};

  for (const candidate of candidates) {
    const verdict = assessFanoutCandidate(candidate, signal, platform);
    if (verdict.kind === 'eligible') eligible.push(verdict);
    else {
      rejected.push(verdict);
      counts[verdict.code] = (counts[verdict.code] ?? 0) + 1;
    }
  }

  return { eligible, excluded: rejected, exclusionCounts: counts };
}

import { describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';

// `forward-only.ts` holds a DB half alongside the pure predicate, so importing it
// pulls in `client.js`, which demands a URL at import time. The pool never
// connects here ‚Äî every case below is pure. Same shim as `stop-loss.test.ts`.
vi.hoisted(() => {
  process.env.DATABASE_URL ??= 'postgres://forward-only-unit-test/unused';
});

import {
  DEFAULT_FORWARD_ONLY_CLOCK_SKEW_TOLERANCE_MS,
  evaluateForwardOnlyMirror,
  type ForwardOnlySubscriptionWindow
} from './forward-only.js';

const ACTIVE_SINCE = new Date('2026-08-20T12:00:00.000Z');

function subscription(
  overrides: Partial<ForwardOnlySubscriptionWindow> = {}
): ForwardOnlySubscriptionWindow {
  return {
    userId: 'user-1',
    walletAddress: 'solana:master-wallet',
    state: 'active',
    activeSince: ACTIVE_SINCE,
    ...overrides
  };
}

/** Offsets from `active_since`, so intent is readable at each call site. */
function at(offsetMs: number): Date {
  return new Date(ACTIVE_SINCE.getTime() + offsetMs);
}

describe('evaluateForwardOnlyMirror ‚Äî the S4-M2 done-when', () => {
  it('refuses a buy the master made BEFORE the subscription went active', () => {
    // The item's done-when: "a test asserts a new subscriber receives no position
    // for a token the master held before subscription." Entering an existing
    // position at an unknown cost basis is how followers become exit liquidity.
    const decision = evaluateForwardOnlyMirror({
      side: 'buy',
      eventAt: at(-60 * 60_000), // an hour before
      subscription: subscription()
    });
    expect(decision).toMatchObject({
      kind: 'skip',
      code: 'source-event-precedes-active-since'
    });
  });

  it('mirrors a buy at or after active_since', () => {
    expect(evaluateForwardOnlyMirror({
      side: 'buy',
      eventAt: at(60_000),
      subscription: subscription()
    })).toMatchObject({ kind: 'mirror', basis: 'event-at-or-after-active-since' });
  });

  it('admits a buy exactly AT active_since', () => {
    // Boundary. Excluding it would drop a legitimate first mirror for a wallet
    // whose event landed in the same millisecond the subscription was written.
    const decision = evaluateForwardOnlyMirror({
      side: 'buy',
      eventAt: ACTIVE_SINCE,
      subscription: subscription()
    });
    expect(decision.kind).toBe('mirror');
    if (decision.kind === 'mirror') expect(decision.eventOffsetMs).toBe(0);
  });

  it('refuses a buy one millisecond before active_since at the default tolerance', () => {
    expect(evaluateForwardOnlyMirror({
      side: 'buy',
      eventAt: at(-1),
      subscription: subscription()
    })).toMatchObject({ kind: 'skip', code: 'source-event-precedes-active-since' });
  });
});

describe('the sell exemption', () => {
  it('never gates a sell, even one long predating the subscription', () => {
    // A sell is the user's exit. If they somehow hold a position, refusing the
    // master's sell strands them ‚Äî strictly worse than a missed entry.
    const decision = evaluateForwardOnlyMirror({
      side: 'sell',
      eventAt: at(-365 * 24 * 60 * 60_000),
      subscription: subscription()
    });
    expect(decision).toMatchObject({ kind: 'mirror', basis: 'exit-never-gated' });
  });

  it('reports no offset for a sell rather than a misleading zero', () => {
    // `0` would claim a comparison that never happened.
    const decision = evaluateForwardOnlyMirror({
      side: 'sell',
      eventAt: at(-1_000),
      subscription: subscription()
    });
    if (decision.kind === 'mirror') expect(decision.eventOffsetMs).toBeNull();
  });

  it('still exempts a sell while the subscription is winding down', () => {
    // Exits-only wind-down (S4-M3): entries have stopped, sells keep mirroring
    // until each open position closes.
    expect(evaluateForwardOnlyMirror({
      side: 'sell',
      eventAt: at(-1_000),
      subscription: subscription({ state: 'winding_down' })
    })).toMatchObject({ kind: 'mirror' });
  });
});

describe('subscription state is delegated, not re-decided', () => {
  it('stops entries while winding down', () => {
    expect(evaluateForwardOnlyMirror({
      side: 'buy',
      eventAt: at(60_000),
      subscription: subscription({ state: 'winding_down' })
    })).toMatchObject({ kind: 'skip', code: 'subscription-entries-stopped' });
  });

  it('mirrors nothing for an ended subscription', () => {
    expect(evaluateForwardOnlyMirror({
      side: 'buy',
      eventAt: at(60_000),
      subscription: subscription({ state: 'ended' })
    })).toMatchObject({ kind: 'skip', code: 'subscription-not-mirroring' });
  });

  it('fails closed on a state this build does not recognise', () => {
    // `state` is a VARCHAR, so an unknown value is reachable. Treating it as
    // mirrorable would let a schema change re-enable entries silently.
    for (const state of ['paused', '', null, undefined, 42]) {
      expect(evaluateForwardOnlyMirror({
        side: 'buy',
        eventAt: at(60_000),
        subscription: subscription({ state })
      })).toMatchObject({ kind: 'skip' });
    }
  });
});

describe('fail-closed branches', () => {
  it('refuses when the user has no subscription at all', () => {
    expect(evaluateForwardOnlyMirror({
      side: 'buy',
      eventAt: at(60_000),
      subscription: null
    })).toMatchObject({ kind: 'skip', code: 'no-subscription-window' });
  });

  it('STILL mirrors a sell when there is no subscription row at all', () => {
    // Counter-intuitive and deliberate: the sell branch is unconditional and sits
    // ahead of every other check, so an exit is gated by nothing ‚Äî not timing, not
    // lifecycle state, not even the existence of a subscription.
    //
    // This is load-bearing rather than theoretical. `unsubscribeFromWallet` still
    // hard-deletes the row today (see S4-M3), so a user can hold an open position
    // with no subscription row, and refusing the master's sell would leave it with
    // no exit path at all. What keeps it safe is downstream: a sell mirror is
    // proportional to the position actually held, and `computeCopySellProportion`
    // throws rather than defaulting to sell-everything when position evidence is
    // missing. So a user holding nothing gets nothing, not a spurious order.
    //
    // If this ever needs to become a skip, the position-orphan case must be closed
    // first, or the change silently strands positions.
    expect(evaluateForwardOnlyMirror({
      side: 'sell',
      eventAt: at(60_000),
      subscription: null
    })).toMatchObject({ kind: 'mirror', basis: 'exit-never-gated' });
  });

  it('mirrors a sell even for an ended subscription, for the same reason', () => {
    // `ended` should mean the wind-down completed and nothing is open ‚Äî but if a
    // position survived, this is its only exit.
    expect(evaluateForwardOnlyMirror({
      side: 'sell',
      eventAt: at(-99_999),
      subscription: subscription({ state: 'ended' })
    })).toMatchObject({ kind: 'mirror', basis: 'exit-never-gated' });
  });

  it('refuses a side that is not provably buy or sell', () => {
    for (const side of ['transfer_in', 'transfer_out', 'BUY', '', 'lp']) {
      expect(evaluateForwardOnlyMirror({
        side,
        eventAt: at(60_000),
        subscription: subscription()
      })).toMatchObject({ kind: 'skip', code: 'source-side-unrecognised' });
    }
  });

  it('refuses an unreadable event timestamp', () => {
    expect(evaluateForwardOnlyMirror({
      side: 'buy',
      eventAt: new Date('not a date'),
      subscription: subscription()
    })).toMatchObject({ kind: 'skip', code: 'source-event-timestamp-unreadable' });
  });

  it('refuses an unreadable active_since', () => {
    expect(evaluateForwardOnlyMirror({
      side: 'buy',
      eventAt: at(60_000),
      subscription: subscription({ activeSince: new Date('not a date') })
    })).toMatchObject({ kind: 'skip', code: 'active-since-unreadable' });
  });
});

describe('clock-skew tolerance', () => {
  it('defaults to zero, so no pre-subscription event is admitted by accident', () => {
    // The failure modes are asymmetric: too low costs one missed entry the user
    // recovers from on the next trade; too high opens a position at a cost basis
    // the user never had, which is unrecoverable and is the harm S4-M2 prevents.
    expect(DEFAULT_FORWARD_ONLY_CLOCK_SKEW_TOLERANCE_MS).toBe(0);
  });

  it('admits an event inside an explicitly widened tolerance, and says so', () => {
    const decision = evaluateForwardOnlyMirror({
      side: 'buy',
      eventAt: at(-5_000),
      subscription: subscription(),
      clockSkewToleranceMs: 10_000
    });
    expect(decision).toMatchObject({
      kind: 'mirror',
      basis: 'event-within-clock-skew-tolerance'
    });
  });

  it('still refuses an event beyond the widened tolerance', () => {
    expect(evaluateForwardOnlyMirror({
      side: 'buy',
      eventAt: at(-15_000),
      subscription: subscription(),
      clockSkewToleranceMs: 10_000
    })).toMatchObject({ kind: 'skip', code: 'source-event-precedes-active-since' });
  });

  it('throws on a misconfigured tolerance rather than coercing it', () => {
    // Coercing to 0 tightens a gate without saying so; coercing upward loosens
    // one. Either way the operator is not told.
    for (const bad of [-1, Number.NaN, Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY]) {
      expect(() => evaluateForwardOnlyMirror({
        side: 'buy',
        eventAt: at(60_000),
        subscription: subscription(),
        clockSkewToleranceMs: bad
      })).toThrow(/non-negative finite/);
    }
  });
});

describe('re-subscribe is the case created_at would get wrong', () => {
  it('measures against the CURRENT active period, not the original signup', () => {
    // The PK is (user_id, wallet_address), so re-subscribe is an ended -> active
    // transition on the same row: `created_at` still reads January for a
    // subscription revived in August. Filtering on it would mirror eight months
    // of history on every re-subscribe ‚Äî catch-up buying in the one case nobody
    // tests. `active_since` is reset on each entry into `active`.
    const revivedAt = new Date('2026-08-20T12:00:00.000Z');
    const duringFirstPeriod = new Date('2026-01-15T00:00:00.000Z');

    expect(evaluateForwardOnlyMirror({
      side: 'buy',
      eventAt: duringFirstPeriod,
      subscription: subscription({ activeSince: revivedAt })
    })).toMatchObject({ kind: 'skip', code: 'source-event-precedes-active-since' });
  });
});

==> packages/db/src/forward-only.ts <==
import type { PoolClient } from 'pg';
import { query } from './client.js';
import { mirrorEligibilityForState } from './subscriptions.js';
import type { UserScope } from './tenancy.js';

/**
 * Forward-only joins (checklist `S4-M2`, ADR-0005 ¬ß3.7).
 *
 * **The failure this prevents.** A user subscribes to a master who is already
 * holding twelve tokens. The master's history is sitting in `source_trades` and
 * the signal path is perfectly willing to mirror any of it. Following those
 * entries means buying into positions whose cost basis the user never had ‚Äî
 * they enter at whatever the price is now, after the move that made the master
 * worth following already happened. That is the mechanism by which a copy
 * cohort becomes the master's exit liquidity, and it is not a rare case: it is
 * what "subscribe" would mean by default for every master worth subscribing to.
 *
 * So the rule is: **a subscription mirrors entries made from the subscription
 * onward, and nothing earlier.** The user's first day may be flat. That is the
 * correct outcome and `S6-31` is the notice that says so at subscribe time.
 *
 * ## Split
 *
 * The decision is **pure** (`evaluateForwardOnlyMirror`) and the read is thin
 * (`readForwardOnlySubscriptionWindow` / `loadForwardOnlySubscriptionWindow`),
 * the same shape `stop-loss.ts` uses between its threshold arithmetic and its
 * DB claim. No clock is read here: `eventAt` and `activeSince` both arrive as
 * arguments, so every boundary case is reachable from a unit test with no
 * infrastructure.
 *
 * ## Why `active_since` and never `created_at`
 *
 * The primary key of `user_wallet_subscriptions` is `(user_id, wallet_address)`
 * (`044`), so a second row for the same pair cannot exist. A re-subscribe is
 * therefore an `ended -> active` transition **on the row that is already
 * there** ‚Äî see `subscribeToWallet` in `subscriptions.ts`, which UPDATEs the
 * existing row rather than inserting. Consequently a subscription created in
 * January, ended in March and revived in August still reads
 * `created_at = January`.
 *
 * A forward-only filter written against `created_at` would let that revived
 * subscriber catch up on eight months of the master's trades ‚Äî precisely the
 * catch-up buying this item exists to forbid, in the one case nobody would
 * think to test. `051_subscription_states.sql` added `active_since` for exactly
 * this, resets it on **every** entry into `active` (`subscribeToWallet` sets
 * `active_since = NOW()` alongside `state = 'active'`), and says so in its
 * `COMMENT ON COLUMN`. This module reads `active_since` and does not read
 * `created_at` at all.
 *
 * ## Why this composes with `mirrorEligibilityForState` instead of restating it
 *
 * `subscriptions.ts` already owns what each lifecycle state permits: `active`
 * is buys and sells, `winding_down` is **sells only**, anything else is
 * nothing. That table is not copied here. The buy branch below *calls*
 * `mirrorEligibilityForState`, so a change to the state machine cannot leave a
 * stale duplicate of it in this file. Forward-only is a strictly narrower
 * question asked only of entries: *given that this subscription may enter at
 * all, is this particular event inside the current active window?*
 */

/**
 * The two columns of `user_wallet_subscriptions` this decision needs, plus the
 * key they were read by.
 *
 * `state` is `unknown` rather than `SubscriptionState` for the same reason
 * `mirrorEligibilityForState` takes `unknown`: the value arrives from a
 * database column that a future migration, a manual UPDATE, or a service on a
 * different release can populate with a state this build has never heard of.
 * A type that cannot be wrong makes the fail-closed branch unreachable and
 * therefore untestable.
 *
 * `walletAddress` is the **chain-prefixed** master address, matching
 * `user_wallet_subscriptions.wallet_address` and `source_trades.wallet_address`
 * (both store `${chain}:${raw}`). Nothing here un-prefixes or re-resolves it;
 * a bare address would simply not match a row, which is why the readers below
 * take the value already prefixed.
 */
export interface ForwardOnlySubscriptionWindow {
  readonly userId: string;
  readonly walletAddress: string;
  readonly state: unknown;
  /** Start of the CURRENT active period. Never `created_at`. */
  readonly activeSince: Date;
}

/**
 * Why an event was admitted, so a caller can tell the ordinary case from the
 * two that deserve a second look.
 */
export type ForwardOnlyMirrorBasis =
  /** The master's entry happened at or after the subscription went active. */
  | 'event-at-or-after-active-since'
  /**
   * The entry reads as *slightly* earlier than `active_since` and was admitted
   * under an operator-configured clock-skew tolerance. Never reached at the
   * default tolerance of zero.
   */
  | 'event-within-clock-skew-tolerance'
  /**
   * The event is a **sell**. This filter never refuses one ‚Äî see
   * {@link evaluateForwardOnlyMirror}.
   */
  | 'exit-never-gated';

export interface ForwardOnlyMirror {
  readonly kind: 'mirror';
  /** Narrowed from the loose input so the caller does not re-derive it. */
  readonly side: 'buy' | 'sell';
  readonly basis: ForwardOnlyMirrorBasis;
  /**
   * Milliseconds from `active_since` to `event_at`; negative when the event
   * reads as earlier. `null` for a sell, where no window was consulted ‚Äî never
   * `0`, which would claim a comparison that did not happen.
   */
  readonly eventOffsetMs: number | null;
}

/**
 * Why an entry was refused. Codes, not prose, because `S4-M24` needs a skip a
 * user can act on and these have genuinely different answers: "this predates
 * your subscription" is expected and permanent, "you unsubscribed" is the
 * user's own doing, and "we cannot read this timestamp" is our bug.
 */
export type ForwardOnlySkipCode =
  /**
   * **The `S4-M2` refusal.** The master made this entry before the current
   * active period began, so following it would be catch-up buying.
   */
  | 'source-event-precedes-active-since'
  /**
   * The subscription is `winding_down`: exits keep mirroring, entries have
   * stopped. Delegated from `mirrorEligibilityForState`, not decided here.
   */
  | 'subscription-entries-stopped'
  /**
   * `mirrorEligibilityForState` says this state mirrors nothing ‚Äî `ended`, or
   * any state this build does not recognise. Fails closed.
   */
  | 'subscription-not-mirroring'
  /**
   * No subscription row for this (user, master) at all, so there is no active
   * window an entry could be inside of. Fails closed.
   */
  | 'no-subscription-window'
  /**
   * Not provably a `buy` or a `sell`. Fails closed ‚Äî see the note in
   * {@link evaluateForwardOnlyMirror} on why the sell exemption forces this.
   */
  | 'source-side-unrecognised'
  /** `source_trades.event_at` is not a usable date. An indexer bug. */
  | 'source-event-timestamp-unreadable'
  /** `active_since` is not a usable date. A subscription-writer bug. */
  | 'active-since-unreadable';

export interface ForwardOnlySkip {
  readonly kind: 'skip';
  readonly code: ForwardOnlySkipCode;
  /** Operator- and user-readable, and specific enough to act on. */
  readonly reason: string;
}

export type ForwardOnlyDecision = ForwardOnlyMirror | ForwardOnlySkip;

export interface ForwardOnlyMirrorInput {
  /**
   * `source_trades.direction`.
   *
   * Typed `string`, not `SourceTradeSide`, following the same reasoning as
   * `evaluateMirrorableActivity`: the column's CHECK admits four values
   * (`028_copy_execution_lifecycle.sql`) and rows are mapped straight through,
   * so a narrow type here would be an assertion about a query rather than a
   * runtime guarantee.
   */
  readonly side: string;
  /** `source_trades.event_at` ‚Äî when the master traded, per the chain. */
  readonly eventAt: Date;
  /** The subscription row, or `null` when the user has none for this master. */
  readonly subscription: ForwardOnlySubscriptionWindow | null;
  /**
   * How far *before* `active_since` an entry may read and still be admitted.
   * Defaults to {@link DEFAULT_FORWARD_ONLY_CLOCK_SKEW_TOLERANCE_MS}. See that
   * constant for why the default is zero.
   */
  readonly clockSkewToleranceMs?: number;
}

/**
 * Zero, and the asymmetry is the whole argument.
 *
 * `event_at` and `active_since` come from **different clocks**: `event_at` is a
 * chain or venue timestamp (a Solana block time is a stake-weighted median of
 * validator clocks; Polymarket's is the venue's own), while `active_since` is
 * this database's `NOW()`. They can disagree in either direction, and the two
 * errors are not equally bad.
 *
 *   * Tolerance too **low** ‚Äî a chain clock running behind ours makes a
 *     genuine first entry read as pre-subscription and it is skipped. The user
 *     misses one entry in the seconds after subscribing and mirrors the next
 *     one. Recoverable, self-limiting, and already what `S6-31` warns about.
 *   * Tolerance too **high** ‚Äî real pre-subscription history reads as
 *     in-window and is mirrored. Unrecoverable: the position is opened at a
 *     cost basis the user never had, which is the precise harm `S4-M2` exists
 *     to prevent.
 *
 * A safety gate whose failure modes are asymmetric defaults to the recoverable
 * one, so an event that reads as earlier than `active_since` is **not**
 * admitted unless an operator deliberately widens the window.
 *
 * There is a second reason not to widen it by default:
 * `listSourceTradeSignalCandidates` already admits `event_at <= now + INTERVAL
 * '30 seconds'`, which is this repo's existing acknowledgement that chain
 * clocks can run up to half a minute **ahead** of ours. Skew in that direction
 * already smuggles a little pre-subscription history past this gate and no
 * filter on these two columns can detect it. Adding backward tolerance on top
 * would widen an already-imperfect boundary in the dangerous direction.
 *
 * The knob exists so an operator who has *measured* a chain's drift can set it
 * with evidence, rather than patching this module.
 */
export const DEFAULT_FORWARD_ONLY_CLOCK_SKEW_TOLERANCE_MS = 0;

/** The only two sides this filter classifies. Anything else fails closed. */
const BUY = 'buy';
const SELL = 'sell';

/**
 * Whether one of the master's events is inside the current active window of
 * one subscription.
 *
 * Pure: no database, no clock, no environment. Both timestamps and the
 * tolerance are arguments.
 *
 * ## A sell is never refused here
 *
 * There is exactly **one** `sell` branch below and it is unconditional: no
 * timestamp is read, no state is consulted, no tolerance applies. The guarantee
 * is meant to be checkable by reading the function rather than by trusting a
 * comment.
 *
 * The reason is an asymmetry in what a refusal costs. Refusing an entry costs a
 * missed opportunity. Refusing an **exit** costs the user their way out: the
 * master's sell mirror is how a copied position was always going to close
 * (ADR-0005 ¬ß3.7 ‚Äî a wind-down keeps honouring sells precisely so nothing is
 * orphaned), and a filter that declined it would leave the user holding a token
 * whose master has already left. Stranded is strictly worse than a missed
 * entry.
 *
 * This is also why the sell exemption is granted to a value that is *provably*
 * `'sell'` and never to "not a buy". If an unclassified side fell through to
 * the exempt branch, then any future or malformed `source_trades.direction`
 * would bypass the window check entirely ‚Äî the exemption would become the hole.
 * Hence `source-side-unrecognised` fails closed even though `S4-M5`
 * (`evaluateMirrorableActivity`) is the gate that properly owns side
 * classification upstream.
 *
 * ## The boundary at `event_at == active_since`
 *
 * The window is **half-open**: `[active_since, infinity)`. An event whose
 * `event_at` is exactly `active_since` is **admitted**.
 *
 * `active_since` names the instant the subscription *became* active, so the
 * subscription is live *at* that instant and not merely after it. An event
 * timestamped there is concurrent with the join, not history ‚Äî "catch-up
 * buying" means a backlog of positions already held, and a single event at the
 * microsecond of subscribing is the first mirror rather than a backlog. It is
 * also the same convention the SQL on this path already uses (`event_at >= now
 * - window` in `listSourceTradeSignalCandidates`), so a future SQL-side
 * implementation of this predicate agrees with the pure one by construction
 * instead of by coincidence.
 *
 * The case is close to unreachable in practice ‚Äî two independent clocks
 * agreeing to the microsecond ‚Äî so it is decided on which error would be
 * worse, and dropping a legitimate first mirror is a real, reachable regression
 * while admitting one concurrent event is not the harm the item names.
 *
 * ## Fails closed
 *
 * Absent evidence is never a pass. No subscription row, an unrecognised state,
 * an unreadable timestamp: all skip, each with its own code, because a missing
 * fact must not read the same as a satisfied check.
 */
export function evaluateForwardOnlyMirror(
  input: ForwardOnlyMirrorInput
): ForwardOnlyDecision {
  const toleranceMs = input.clockSkewToleranceMs ?? DEFAULT_FORWARD_ONLY_CLOCK_SKEW_TOLERANCE_MS;
  if (!Number.isFinite(toleranceMs) || toleranceMs < 0) {
    // Throws rather than degrading, following `resolveMinimumMirrorableNotionalUsd`:
    // silently coercing a bad tolerance to 0 tightens a gate without saying so,
    // and coercing it upward loosens one. A misconfiguration is an operator
    // error and belongs at the boundary, not absorbed into a trade decision.
    throw new Error(
      `clockSkewToleranceMs must be a non-negative finite number, received ${String(
        input.clockSkewToleranceMs
      )}`
    );
  }

  if (input.side !== BUY && input.side !== SELL) {
    return {
      kind: 'skip',
      code: 'source-side-unrecognised',
      reason:
        `the tracked wallet's event has side ${JSON.stringify(input.side)}, which is `
        + 'neither a buy nor a sell, so this build cannot tell whether it is an entry '
        + 'that must respect your subscription start'
    };
  }

  // THE sell branch. Unconditional, deliberately ‚Äî see the doc comment.
  if (input.side === SELL) {
    return { kind: 'mirror', side: SELL, basis: 'exit-never-gated', eventOffsetMs: null };
  }

  const subscription = input.subscription;
  if (!subscription) {
    return {
      kind: 'skip',
      code: 'no-subscription-window',
      reason:
        'no subscription to this wallet was found for you, so there is no '
        + 'subscription start an entry could be after'
    };
  }

  // Delegated, not restated: `subscriptions.ts` is the only definition of what
  // a lifecycle state permits, and it returns 'none' for any state this build
  // does not recognise.
  const eligibility = mirrorEligibilityForState(subscription.state);
  if (eligibility === 'none') {
    return {
      kind: 'skip',
      code: 'subscription-not-mirroring',
      reason:
        `your subscription to this wallet is ${JSON.stringify(subscription.state)}, `
        + 'which mirrors nothing, so no new position will be opened'
    };
  }
  if (eligibility === 'sells-only') {
    return {
      kind: 'skip',
      code: 'subscription-entries-stopped',
      reason:
        'you have unsubscribed from this wallet, so new entries have stopped; '
        + 'the exits for positions you already hold are still being mirrored'
    };
  }

  if (!(subscription.activeSince instanceof Date) || Number.isNaN(subscription.activeSince.getTime())) {
    return {
      kind: 'skip',
      code: 'active-since-unreadable',
      reason:
        'the start of your subscription could not be read, so this entry cannot be '
        + 'shown to have happened after you subscribed'
    };
  }
  if (!(input.eventAt instanceof Date) || Number.isNaN(input.eventAt.getTime())) {
    return {
      kind: 'skip',
      code: 'source-event-timestamp-unreadable',
      reason:
        'the time of the tracked wallet\'s trade could not be read, so this entry '
        + 'cannot be shown to have happened after you subscribed'
    };
  }

  const eventOffsetMs = input.eventAt.getTime() - subscription.activeSince.getTime();
  if (eventOffsetMs >= 0) {
    return {
      kind: 'mirror',
      side: BUY,
      basis: 'event-at-or-after-active-since',
      eventOffsetMs
    };
  }
  if (eventOffsetMs >= -toleranceMs) {
    return {
      kind: 'mirror',
      side: BUY,
      basis: 'event-within-clock-skew-tolerance',
      eventOffsetMs
    };
  }
  return {
    kind: 'skip',
    code: 'source-event-precedes-active-since',
    reason:
      `the tracked wallet bought this token ${Math.abs(eventOffsetMs)}ms before your `
      + 'subscription started, so it is a position it already held; entering it now '
      + 'would mean buying at a cost basis you never had'
  };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The DB half: read the window, decide nothing.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * `active_since` is selected and `created_at` deliberately is not, so this
 * query cannot be edited into the wrong column by autocomplete.
 */
const FORWARD_ONLY_WINDOW_COLUMNS = 'user_id, wallet_address, state, active_since';

interface ForwardOnlyWindowRow {
  user_id: string;
  wallet_address: string;
  state: string;
  active_since: Date;
}

function toWindow(row: ForwardOnlyWindowRow): ForwardOnlySubscriptionWindow {
  return {
    userId: row.user_id,
    walletAddress: row.wallet_address,
    state: row.state,
    activeSince: row.active_since
  };
}

/**
 * Read one subscription's forward-only window **on a caller-supplied client**.
 *
 * This overload exists so the read can happen inside the transaction that is
 * about to create a copy execution. Reading through the pool instead would use
 * a different snapshot, and a subscription that ended between the read and the
 * insert would still get an entry.
 *
 * Every lifecycle state is returned, including `ended`: the decision needs to
 * distinguish "you unsubscribed" from "we have no record of you following this
 * wallet", and a `WHERE state <> 'ended'` here would collapse the two into one
 * skip code.
 *
 * `userId` is a plain string rather than a `UserScope` because on the copy path
 * the tenant has already been established and canonicalised by
 * `normalizeTenantId`; the branded type guards the boundary where a tenant id
 * could come from a request payload, which is what
 * {@link loadForwardOnlySubscriptionWindow} is for.
 */
export async function readForwardOnlySubscriptionWindow(
  client: Pick<PoolClient, 'query'>,
  input: { userId: string; walletAddress: string }
): Promise<ForwardOnlySubscriptionWindow | null> {
  const result = await client.query<ForwardOnlyWindowRow>(
    `SELECT ${FORWARD_ONLY_WINDOW_COLUMNS}
       FROM user_wallet_subscriptions
      WHERE user_id = $1 AND wallet_address = $2`,
    [input.userId, input.walletAddress]
  );
  const row = result.rows[0];
  return row ? toWindow(row) : null;
}

/**
 * Pool-scoped read for callers outside a transaction ‚Äî the fan-out planner and
 * any API surface that wants to explain a skip after the fact.
 *
 * Takes a `UserScope` so the tenant cannot arrive from a request payload.
 * `walletAddress` must be the chain-prefixed master address.
 */
export async function loadForwardOnlySubscriptionWindow(
  scope: UserScope,
  walletAddress: string
): Promise<ForwardOnlySubscriptionWindow | null> {
  const rows = await query<ForwardOnlyWindowRow>(
    `SELECT ${FORWARD_ONLY_WINDOW_COLUMNS}
       FROM user_wallet_subscriptions
      WHERE user_id = $1 AND wallet_address = $2`,
    [scope.userId, walletAddress]
  );
  const row = rows[0];
  return row ? toWindow(row) : null;
}

==> packages/db/src/independence-queries.ts <==
import type { Chain } from '@swat/shared';
import { query } from './client.js';
import type { FunderLabel } from './independence.js';

export interface WalletIndependenceWarning {
  readonly clustered: boolean;
  readonly clusterType: 'funding' | 'behavioral' | null;
  readonly clusterName: string | null;
  readonly warning: string | null;
}

export interface WalletHubStatus {
  readonly isHub: boolean;
  readonly label: FunderLabel | null;
  readonly hubName: string | null;
  readonly reason: string | null;
}

/**
 * Checks whether a candidate wallet belongs to a funding or behavioral cluster (S4-M10).
 *
 * This check is advisory: it produces a descriptive warning to surface to the user,
 * but never blocks a subscription outright (a user may knowingly copy a clustered wallet).
 */
export async function checkWalletClusterIndependence(
  walletAddress: string
): Promise<WalletIndependenceWarning> {
  const rows = await query<{
    cluster_type: string | null;
    name: string | null;
  }>(
    `SELECT c.cluster_type, c.name
       FROM cluster_memberships cm
       JOIN wallet_clusters c ON c.id = cm.cluster_id
      WHERE cm.wallet_address = $1
      LIMIT 1`,
    [walletAddress]
  );

  if (rows.length === 0) {
    return {
      clustered: false,
      clusterType: null,
      clusterName: null,
      warning: null
    };
  }

  const row = rows[0]!;
  const clusterType = (row.cluster_type === 'funding' || row.cluster_type === 'behavioral')
    ? row.cluster_type
    : null;

  const warning = clusterType === 'funding'
    ? `Wallet belongs to funding cluster "${row.name ?? 'unknown'}". Shared funding suggests common control or Sybil coordination.`
    : clusterType === 'behavioral'
      ? `Wallet belongs to behavioral cluster "${row.name ?? 'unknown'}". Co-movement suggests shared strategy or bot ring.`
      : `Wallet belongs to cluster "${row.name ?? 'unknown'}".`;

  return {
    clustered: true,
    clusterType,
    clusterName: row.name ?? null,
    warning
  };
}

/**
 * Checks whether a candidate wallet is an exchange or infrastructure hub (S4-M11).
 *
 * Unlike cluster warnings, hub status blocks subscription: an exchange hot wallet
 * or bridge is infrastructure, not a trading strategy.
 */
export async function checkWalletHubStatus(
  walletAddress: string,
  rawAddress: string,
  _chain: Chain
): Promise<WalletHubStatus> {
  const rows = await query<{ status: string; nickname: string | null }>(
    `SELECT status, nickname FROM wallets WHERE address = $1 OR address = $2 LIMIT 1`,
    [walletAddress, rawAddress]
  );

  if (rows.length > 0 && rows[0]!.status === 'blacklisted') {
    const hubName = rows[0]!.nickname ?? 'Exchange Hub';
    return {
      isHub: true,
      label: 'exchange',
      hubName,
      reason: `This is an exchange wallet (${hubName})`
    };
  }

  return {
    isHub: false,
    label: null,
    hubName: null,
    reason: null
  };
}

// pure -- it is the only part of S4-M11 that can be tested without a database.

const FUNDER = 'solana:FundErAaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa';

    const result = assessFunderIndependence(input({ observedFundedWalletCount: 3 }));
    expect(result.verdict).toBe('independent');
    expect(result.code).toBe('degree-within-cap');

    expect(result.code).toBe('degree-below-minimum');

  });

  it('carries the applied bound on the result so a log line is self-describing', () => {
    const result = assessFunderIndependence(input(), { maxFunderDegree: 9 });
    expect(result.maxFunderDegree).toBe(9);
    expect(result.minFundedWallets).toBe(MIN_FUNDED_WALLETS);

  it('honours an overridden ceiling', () => {
    expect(
      assessFunderIndependence(input({ observedFundedWalletCount: 10 }), {
        maxFunderDegree: 5
      }).code
    ).toBe('degree-exceeds-cap');
  });

    expect(result.code).toBe('degree-unknown');

  it('does not read a missing count as zero', () => {

    // counted. It must not be reachable from an absent count.

  const funders: readonly FunderIndependenceInput[] = [
    { funder: 'solana:small', observedFundedWalletCount: 3, label: null },
    { funder: 'solana:cex', observedFundedWalletCount: 900_000, label: null },
    { funder: 'solana:quietCex', observedFundedWalletCount: 2, label: 'exchange' },
    { funder: 'solana:lonely', observedFundedWalletCount: 1, label: null },
    { funder: 'solana:uncounted', observedFundedWalletCount: null, label: null },
    { funder: 'solana:unlabelled', observedFundedWalletCount: 4 }
  ];

  it('sorts every funder into exactly one bucket', () => {
    const p = partitionFundersByIndependence(funders);
    expect(p.independent.map((a) => a.funder)).toEqual(['solana:small']);
    expect(p.hubs.map((a) => a.funder)).toEqual(['solana:cex', 'solana:quietCex']);
    expect(p.belowMinimum.map((a) => a.funder)).toEqual(['solana:lonely']);
    expect(p.unassessed.map((a) => a.funder)).toEqual([
      'solana:uncounted',
      'solana:unlabelled'
    ]);
    const total =
      p.independent.length + p.hubs.length + p.belowMinimum.length + p.unassessed.length;
    expect(total).toBe(funders.length);
  });

  it('keeps the reason for each unassessed funder rather than one flag', () => {
    const p = partitionFundersByIndependence(funders);
    expect(p.unassessed.map((a) => a.code)).toEqual([
      'degree-unknown',
      'hub-label-unchecked'
    ]);
  });

  it('never puts an unassessed funder in independent', () => {
    const p = partitionFundersByIndependence(funders);
    expect(p.independent.every((a) => a.verdict === 'independent')).toBe(true);
    expect(p.independent.every(admitsFundingCluster)).toBe(true);
  });

  it('returns empty buckets for an empty input rather than throwing', () => {
    const p = partitionFundersByIndependence([]);
    expect(p).toEqual({ independent: [], hubs: [], belowMinimum: [], unassessed: [] });
  });

  it('applies one policy across the batch', () => {
    const p = partitionFundersByIndependence(funders, { maxFunderDegree: 3 });
    expect(p.hubs.map((a) => a.funder)).toEqual([
      'solana:cex',
      'solana:quietCex',
      'solana:unlabelled'
    ]);
  });
