import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import {
  ACCOUNT_EXECUTE,
  ERC20_APPROVE,
  ERC20_TRANSFER,
  decodeEvmCalldata,
  describeUserOperationCall,
  type EvmFunctionDescriptor
} from './evm-calldata.js';

const DESCRIPTORS: readonly EvmFunctionDescriptor[] = [
  ERC20_APPROVE,
  ERC20_TRANSFER,
  ACCOUNT_EXECUTE
];

const TOKEN = '0x1111111111111111111111111111111111111111';
const ACCOUNT = '0x5555555555555555555555555555555555555555';

function addressWord(address: string): string {
  return address.replace(/^0x/, '').toLowerCase().padStart(64, '0');
}

function uintWord(value: bigint): string {
  return value.toString(16).padStart(64, '0');
}

function encodeApprove(spender: string, amount: bigint): string {
  return `${ERC20_APPROVE.selector}${addressWord(spender)}${uintWord(amount)}`;
}

function encodeExecute(dest: string, value: bigint, inner: string): string {
  const body = inner.replace(/^0x/, '');
  const byteLength = body.length / 2;
  const padded = body.padEnd(Math.ceil(byteLength / 32) * 64, '0');
  return `${ACCOUNT_EXECUTE.selector}${addressWord(dest)}${uintWord(value)}${uintWord(96n)}${uintWord(
    BigInt(byteLength)
  )}${padded}`;
}

describe('decodeEvmCalldata (S4-P10)', () => {
  it('decodes a hand-written approve calldata literal', () => {
    // Written out by hand rather than produced by the helper above, so this test
    // is not just asserting that the encoder and decoder are inverses.
    const calldata =
      '0x095ea7b3' +
      '000000000000000000000000' +
      '1111111111111111111111111111111111111111' +
      '00000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000000003e8';

    const decoded = decodeEvmCalldata(calldata, DESCRIPTORS);
    expect(decoded.kind).toBe('decoded');
    if (decoded.kind !== 'decoded') return;
    expect(decoded.functionName).toBe('approve');
    expect(decoded.selector).toBe('0x095ea7b3');
    expect(decoded.args.spender).toBe(TOKEN);
    expect(decoded.args.amount).toBe(1000n);
  });

  it('refuses an unknown selector under its own code rather than guessing', () => {
    const result = decodeEvmCalldata(`0xdeadbeef${uintWord(1n)}`, DESCRIPTORS);
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ kind: 'failed', code: 'authority-action-unknown-selector' });
  });

  it('refuses calldata shorter than its declared head', () => {
    const result = decodeEvmCalldata(`${ERC20_APPROVE.selector}${addressWord(TOKEN)}`, DESCRIPTORS);
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ kind: 'failed', code: 'authority-action-undecodable' });
  });

  it('refuses an address word with dirty high-order bytes instead of masking it', () => {
    const dirty = `ff${'0'.repeat(22)}${TOKEN.slice(2)}`;
    const result = decodeEvmCalldata(
      `${ERC20_APPROVE.selector}${dirty}${uintWord(1n)}`,
      DESCRIPTORS

    expect(result).toMatchObject({ kind: 'failed', code: 'authority-action-undecodable' });
  });

  it('refuses a non-canonical dynamic tail offset', () => {
    const forged = `${ACCOUNT_EXECUTE.selector}${addressWord(TOKEN)}${uintWord(0n)}${uintWord(
      128n
    )}${uintWord(0n)}${uintWord(4n)}`;
    const result = decodeEvmCalldata(forged, DESCRIPTORS);
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ kind: 'failed', code: 'authority-action-undecodable' });
  });

  it('refuses hex that is not whole bytes', () => {
    const result = decodeEvmCalldata('0x095ea7b', DESCRIPTORS);
    expect(result).toMatchObject({ kind: 'failed', code: 'authority-action-undecodable' });
  });
});

==> packages/shared/src/authority/evm-calldata.ts <==
/**
 * Minimal EVM calldata decoding for the permission policy engine (`S4-P10`).
 *
 * **Moves to `packages/authority` with the rest of this directory** (checklist
 * ¬ß7.1).
 *
 * ## Why this exists rather than `viem`
 *
 * `viem@^2.55.1` is a dependency of `apps/api`, `apps/indexer`,
 * `apps/signal-engine` and `apps/trade-executor` ‚Äî but **not** of
 * `packages/shared`, and pnpm's isolated `node_modules` means it is not
 * resolvable from here. Adding it would need a `pnpm install`. So the decoder
 * here is deliberately the *smallest correct* thing rather than a general ABI
 * decoder:
 *
 *   * argument types are `address`, `uint256`, `bool` (one static word each) and
 *     `bytes` (allowed **only** as the final argument, one dynamic tail);
 *   * anything else ‚Äî arrays, structs, multiple dynamic arguments, `executeBatch`
 *     ‚Äî has no descriptor and is refused, not partially decoded.
 *
 * That covers exactly what ¬ß2.1 needs to check: `approve(address,uint256)` on a
 * token, and the 4337 `execute(address,uint256,bytes)` wrapper it arrives inside.
 * Callers that already have `viem` (the trade executor) should decode richer
 * shapes there and hand `evaluateAuthorityAction` an `AuthorityContractCall`
 * directly ‚Äî the engine does not require this module.
 *
 * ## Strictness is the feature
 *
 * Dirty high-order bits in an `address` word and non-0/1 `bool` words are
 * rejected rather than masked. A decoder that silently truncates disagrees with
 * whatever the EVM will actually do, and a policy that checks a value the chain
 * will not use is decoration.
 *
 * ## Selectors are constants, not computed
 *
 * There is no keccak256 in `packages/shared`, so selectors cannot be derived from
 * signatures here ‚Äî they are written out as the published values below. A
 * consumer that has `viem` should assert them at startup with
 * `toFunctionSelector` rather than trust this file; the constants are marked so
 * that assertion is greppable.
 */

import type { AuthorityContractCall, AuthorityFieldValue } from './permission-policy.js';

export type EvmArgType = 'address' | 'uint256' | 'bool' | 'bytes';

export interface EvmArgDescriptor {
  /** The name a policy condition reaches this argument by. */
  readonly name: string;
  readonly type: EvmArgType;
}

export interface EvmFunctionDescriptor {
  readonly name: string;
  /** `0x` + 8 hex. */
  readonly selector: string;
  readonly args: readonly EvmArgDescriptor[];
}

export type EvmDecodeFailureCode =
  /** No descriptor for this 4-byte selector. We cannot say what the call does. */
  | 'authority-action-unknown-selector'
  /** A descriptor matched but the bytes do not decode against it. */
  | 'authority-action-undecodable'
  /** `execute(dest, value, "")`. A definite refusal, not an integration fault. */
  | 'authority-deny-bare-value-transfer';

export interface EvmDecodeFailure {
  readonly kind: 'failed';
  readonly code: EvmDecodeFailureCode;
  readonly reason: string;
}

export interface EvmDecodedCall {
  readonly kind: 'decoded';
  readonly selector: string;
  readonly functionName: string;
  readonly args: Readonly<Record<string, AuthorityFieldValue>>;
}

/**
 * `approve(address,uint256)` ‚Äî published selector. *Not computed here* (no
 * keccak in this package); assert with `viem`'s `toFunctionSelector` in a
 * consumer that has it.
 */
export const ERC20_APPROVE: EvmFunctionDescriptor = {
  name: 'approve',
  selector: '0x095ea7b3',
  args: [
    { name: 'spender', type: 'address' },
    { name: 'amount', type: 'uint256' }
  ]
};

/** `transfer(address,uint256)` ‚Äî published selector, same caveat. */
export const ERC20_TRANSFER: EvmFunctionDescriptor = {
  name: 'transfer',
  selector: '0xa9059cbb',
  args: [
    { name: 'to', type: 'address' },
    { name: 'amount', type: 'uint256' }
  ]
};

/**
 * `execute(address,uint256,bytes)` ‚Äî the ERC-4337 account wrapper a
 * UserOperation's `callData` normally is. Published selector, same caveat.
 */
export const ACCOUNT_EXECUTE: EvmFunctionDescriptor = {
  name: 'execute',
  selector: '0xb61d27f6',
  args: [
    { name: 'dest', type: 'address' },
    { name: 'value', type: 'uint256' },
    { name: 'func', type: 'bytes' }
  ]
};

/**
 * Selectors treated as an account-level execute wrapper, to be unwrapped to the
 * inner call before the policy sees it.
 *
 * Batch wrappers are absent on purpose. They are not listed as unsupported ‚Äî
 * they are simply not decodable here, so they land on
 * `authority-action-unknown-selector`, which is the honest answer: an
 * `executeBatch` is an arbitrary `(target, value, data)` list and we cannot say
 * what it does without array-index paths, which `DG-3` records as unavailable.
 */
export const ACCOUNT_EXECUTE_SELECTORS: readonly string[] = [ACCOUNT_EXECUTE.selector];

const WORD_HEX = 64;

function failed(code: EvmDecodeFailureCode, reason: string): EvmDecodeFailure {
  return { kind: 'failed', code, reason };
}

/** Strips `0x`, lowercases, and rejects anything that is not whole bytes of hex. */
function normalizeHex(value: unknown): string | null {
  if (typeof value !== 'string') return null;
  const body = value.startsWith('0x') || value.startsWith('0X') ? value.slice(2) : value;
  if (body.length % 2 !== 0) return null;
  if (body.length > 0 && !/^[0-9a-fA-F]+$/.test(body)) return null;
  return body.toLowerCase();
}

function readWord(body: string, wordIndex: number): string | null {
  const start = wordIndex * WORD_HEX;
  if (start + WORD_HEX > body.length) return null;
  return body.slice(start, start + WORD_HEX);
}

function validateDescriptor(descriptor: EvmFunctionDescriptor): string | null {
  for (let i = 0; i < descriptor.args.length; i += 1) {
    const arg = descriptor.args[i]!;
    if (arg.type === 'bytes' && i !== descriptor.args.length - 1) {
      return `descriptor ${descriptor.name} declares a bytes argument that is not last; this decoder supports one dynamic tail only`;
    }
  }
  return null;
}

/**
 * Decodes one call against a descriptor table.
 *
 * The descriptor table *is* the allowlist of shapes we are willing to reason
 * about ‚Äî an unlisted selector is refused rather than guessed at, which is the
 * same allowlist discipline the policy itself uses.
 */
export function decodeEvmCalldata(
  calldata: string,
  descriptors: readonly EvmFunctionDescriptor[]
): EvmDecodedCall | EvmDecodeFailure {
  const body = normalizeHex(calldata);
  if (body === null) {
    return failed('authority-action-undecodable', 'calldata is not an even-length hex string');
  }
  if (body.length < 8) {
    return failed(
      'authority-action-undecodable',
      `calldata is ${body.length / 2} bytes, too short to carry a 4-byte selector`
    );
  }

  const selector = `0x${body.slice(0, 8)}`;
  const descriptor = descriptors.find((d) => d.selector.toLowerCase() === selector);
  if (descriptor === undefined) {
    return failed(
      'authority-action-unknown-selector',
      `no descriptor for selector ${selector}; this engine will not authorise a call it cannot decode`
    );
  }

  const descriptorProblem = validateDescriptor(descriptor);
  if (descriptorProblem !== null) {
    return failed('authority-action-undecodable', descriptorProblem);
  }

  const argsBody = body.slice(8);
  const headWords = descriptor.args.length;
  if (argsBody.length < headWords * WORD_HEX) {
    return failed(
      'authority-action-undecodable',
      `call to ${descriptor.name} carries ${argsBody.length / 2} argument bytes, fewer than the ${headWords * 32} its head requires`
    );
  }

  const args: Record<string, AuthorityFieldValue> = {};

  for (let i = 0; i < descriptor.args.length; i += 1) {
    const arg = descriptor.args[i]!;
    const word = readWord(argsBody, i);
    if (word === null) {
      return failed('authority-action-undecodable', `argument ${arg.name} is truncated`);
    }

    if (arg.type === 'address') {
      // Reject dirty high-order bits rather than masking them: masking makes the
      // policy check a value the EVM will not necessarily use.
      if (word.slice(0, 24) !== '0'.repeat(24)) {
        return failed(
          'authority-action-undecodable',
          `argument ${arg.name} is not a clean address word (non-zero high-order bytes)`
        );
      }
      args[arg.name] = `0x${word.slice(24)}`;
      continue;
    }

    if (arg.type === 'uint256') {
      args[arg.name] = BigInt(`0x${word}`);
      continue;
    }

    if (arg.type === 'bool') {
      const asInt = BigInt(`0x${word}`);
      if (asInt !== 0n && asInt !== 1n) {
        return failed(
          'authority-action-undecodable',
          `argument ${arg.name} is not a canonical bool word (${asInt})`
        );
      }
      args[arg.name] = asInt === 1n;
      continue;
    }

    // `bytes`, the single dynamic tail.
    const offset = BigInt(`0x${word}`);
    const expectedOffset = BigInt(headWords * 32);
    if (offset !== expectedOffset) {
      // A non-canonical offset is how the same bytes decode two different ways in
      // two different decoders. Refuse rather than follow it.
      return failed(
        'authority-action-undecodable',
        `argument ${arg.name} has a non-canonical tail offset ${offset}, expected ${expectedOffset}`
      );
    }
    const lengthWord = readWord(argsBody, headWords);
    if (lengthWord === null) {
      return failed('authority-action-undecodable', `argument ${arg.name} has no length word`);
    }
    const byteLength = BigInt(`0x${lengthWord}`);
    if (byteLength > BigInt(argsBody.length)) {
      return failed(
        'authority-action-undecodable',
        `argument ${arg.name} declares ${byteLength} bytes, more than the calldata holds`
      );
    }
    const dataStart = (headWords + 1) * WORD_HEX;
    const dataHexLength = Number(byteLength) * 2;
    if (dataStart + dataHexLength > argsBody.length) {
      return failed(
        'authority-action-undecodable',
        `argument ${arg.name} declares ${byteLength} bytes but only ${(argsBody.length - dataStart) / 2} remain`
      );
    }
    args[arg.name] = `0x${argsBody.slice(dataStart, dataStart + dataHexLength)}`;
  }

  return { kind: 'decoded', selector, functionName: descriptor.name, args };
}

export interface EvmUserOperationCallInput {
  readonly chainId: number;
  /** The smart account. Target of record when `callData` is not an execute wrapper. */
  readonly sender: string;
  /** `UserOperation.callData`, verbatim. */
  readonly callData: string;
}

export type EvmUserOperationDescription =
  | { readonly kind: 'action'; readonly action: AuthorityContractCall }
  | EvmDecodeFailure;

/**
 * Turns a UserOperation's `callData` into the single `AuthorityContractCall` the
 * policy judges.
 *
 * One level of `execute` unwrapping, never recursive. A nested
 * `execute(execute(...))` therefore surfaces as a call to `execute` *on the
 * account itself*, which no sane scope permits, so it lands on
 * `authority-deny-no-matching-rule` ‚Äî obfuscation gets no special case, it gets
 * the default.
 */
export function describeUserOperationCall(
  input: EvmUserOperationCallInput,
  descriptors: readonly EvmFunctionDescriptor[]
): EvmUserOperationDescription {
  const outer = decodeEvmCalldata(input.callData, descriptors);
  if (outer.kind === 'failed') return outer;

  if (!ACCOUNT_EXECUTE_SELECTORS.includes(outer.selector)) {
    // Not a wrapper: the UserOperation calls a function on the account itself.
    return {
      kind: 'action',
      action: {
        kind: 'contract-call',
        chainId: input.chainId,
        target: input.sender,
        selector: outer.selector,
        functionName: outer.functionName,
        value: 0n,
        args: outer.args
      }
    };
  }

  const dest = outer.args.dest;
  const value = outer.args.value;
  const func = outer.args.func;
  if (typeof dest !== 'string' || typeof value !== 'bigint' || typeof func !== 'string') {
    return failed(
      'authority-action-undecodable',
      'execute wrapper did not decode to (address dest, uint256 value, bytes func)'
    );
  }

  const innerBody = normalizeHex(func);
  if (innerBody === null || innerBody.length === 0) {
    return failed(
      'authority-deny-bare-value-transfer',
      `execute(${dest}, ${value}, "") is a bare native transfer; this engine never authorises one`
    );
  }

  const inner = decodeEvmCalldata(func, descriptors);
  if (inner.kind === 'failed') return inner;

  return {
    kind: 'action',
    action: {
      kind: 'contract-call',
      chainId: input.chainId,
      target: dest,
      selector: inner.selector,
      functionName: inner.functionName,
      value,
      args: inner.args
    }
  };
}

import { createCipheriv, createDecipheriv, randomBytes } from 'node:crypto';

/**
 * Context passed to KeyWrapper wrap/unwrap operations (`S4-4`).
 * Both AWS KMS, Vault Transit, and AES-GCM require this context for AAD binding.
 */
export interface WrapContext {
  readonly userId: string;
  readonly chainKind: 'evm' | 'solana';
  readonly keyVersion: number;
}

/**
 * KeyWrapper interface for envelope encryption (`S4-4`, D11).
 *
 * Provides the abstraction seam separating data-key encryption from key-storage
 * backends. Allows transitioning from environment master keys (EnvMasterKeyWrapper)
 * to Vault Transit (VaultTransitWrapper) or AWS KMS with zero business-logic refactoring.
 */
export interface KeyWrapper {
  /** Stable id embedded in every SealedKey this wrapper produces (e.g. 'env:v1', 'null:v1'). */
  readonly id: string;
  wrap(dataKey: Buffer, context: WrapContext): Promise<Buffer>;
  unwrap(wrapped: Buffer, context: WrapContext): Promise<Buffer>;
}

export function buildWrapAad(context: WrapContext): Buffer {
  return Buffer.from(`${context.userId}|${context.chainKind}|${context.keyVersion}`, 'utf8');
}

/**
 * EnvMasterKeyWrapper (`env:v<n>`)
 *
 * Implements envelope encryption using a master key loaded from environment variables
 * (e.g. `CUSTODY_MASTER_KEY`). Data keys are wrapped using AES-256-GCM with a fresh
 * 12-byte IV and AAD bound to the WrapContext.
 */
export class EnvMasterKeyWrapper implements KeyWrapper {
  readonly id: string;
  private readonly masterKey: Buffer;

  constructor(options?: { masterKey?: Buffer | string; version?: number }) {
    const version = options?.version ?? 1;
    this.id = `env:v${version}`;

    let rawKey = options?.masterKey ?? process.env.CUSTODY_MASTER_KEY;
    if (!rawKey) {
      // If neither is provided, check if CUSTODY_MASTER_KEY_HEX or default is set
      rawKey = process.env.CUSTODY_MASTER_KEY_HEX;
    }

    if (!rawKey) {
      throw new Error('[custody] EnvMasterKeyWrapper requires CUSTODY_MASTER_KEY to be configured');
    }

    if (Buffer.isBuffer(rawKey)) {
      this.masterKey = rawKey;
    } else if (rawKey.length === 64 && /^[0-9a-fA-F]+$/.test(rawKey)) {
      this.masterKey = Buffer.from(rawKey, 'hex');
    } else {
      this.masterKey = Buffer.from(rawKey, 'utf8');
    }

    if (this.masterKey.length !== 32) {
      throw new Error(
        `[custody] EnvMasterKeyWrapper master key must be exactly 32 bytes (got ${this.masterKey.length})`
      );
    }
  }

  async wrap(dataKey: Buffer, context: WrapContext): Promise<Buffer> {
    if (dataKey.length !== 32) {
      throw new Error(`[custody] data key to wrap must be 32 bytes, got ${dataKey.length}`);
    }

    const iv = randomBytes(12);
    const cipher = createCipheriv('aes-256-gcm', this.masterKey, iv);
    cipher.setAAD(buildWrapAad(context));

    const ciphertext = Buffer.concat([cipher.update(dataKey), cipher.final()]);
    const tag = cipher.getAuthTag();

    // Packed wire format for wrapped dataKey: IV (12) + Tag (16) + Ciphertext (32) = 60 bytes
    return Buffer.concat([iv, tag, ciphertext]);
  }

  async unwrap(wrapped: Buffer, context: WrapContext): Promise<Buffer> {
    if (wrapped.length !== 60) {
      throw new Error(
        `[custody] invalid wrapped data key length: expected 60 bytes, got ${wrapped.length}`
      );
    }

    const iv = wrapped.subarray(0, 12);
    const tag = wrapped.subarray(12, 28);
    const ciphertext = wrapped.subarray(28);

    const decipher = createDecipheriv('aes-256-gcm', this.masterKey, iv);
    decipher.setAAD(buildWrapAad(context));
    decipher.setAuthTag(tag);

    try {
      const plaintext = Buffer.concat([decipher.update(ciphertext), decipher.final()]);
      return plaintext;
    } catch (error) {
      throw new Error('[custody] failed to unwrap data key: authentication tag mismatch or tampered context');
    }
  }
}

/**
 * NullWrapper (`null:v1`)
 *
 * Refuses wrap and unwrap operations. Used by staging and tests to guarantee that
 * simulated execution environments cannot accidentally access or store real custody secrets.
 */
export class NullWrapper implements KeyWrapper {
  readonly id = 'null:v1';

  async wrap(_dataKey: Buffer, _context: WrapContext): Promise<Buffer> {
    throw new Error('[custody] NullWrapper refuses to wrap secrets');
  }

  async unwrap(_wrapped: Buffer, _context: WrapContext): Promise<Buffer> {
    throw new Error('[custody] NullWrapper refuses to unwrap secrets');
  }
}

const TOKEN = '0x1111111111111111111111111111111111111111';
const ROUTER = '0x2222222222222222222222222222222222222222';
const ATTACKER = '0x3333333333333333333333333333333333333333';
const OWNER = '0x4444444444444444444444444444444444444444';
const ACCOUNT = '0x5555555555555555555555555555555555555555';
const PERMIT2 = '0x6666666666666666666666666666666666666666';

  ERC20_APPROVE,
  ERC20_TRANSFER,
  ACCOUNT_EXECUTE
];

const CONTEXT: AuthorityEvaluationContext = {
  ownerAccount: OWNER,
  nowSeconds: NOW,
  grantExpiresAtSeconds: NOW + 3600
};

function addressWord(address: string): string {
  return address.replace(/^0x/, '').toLowerCase().padStart(64, '0');
}

function uintWord(value: bigint): string {
  return value.toString(16).padStart(64, '0');
}

function encodeApprove(spender: string, amount: bigint): string {
  return `${ERC20_APPROVE.selector}${addressWord(spender)}${uintWord(amount)}`;
}

function encodeExecute(dest: string, value: bigint, inner: string): string {
  const body = inner.replace(/^0x/, '');
  const byteLength = body.length / 2;
  const padded = body.padEnd(Math.ceil(byteLength / 32) * 64, '0');
  return `${ACCOUNT_EXECUTE.selector}${addressWord(dest)}${uintWord(value)}${uintWord(96n)}${uintWord(
    BigInt(byteLength)
  )}${padded}`;
}

/** The approve rule ¬ß2.1 demands: allowlisted spender, bounded amount. */
const APPROVE_RULE = {
  id: 'approve-router',
  effect: 'allow',
  scope: {
    kind: 'contract-call',
    targets: [TOKEN],
    selector: ERC20_APPROVE.selector,
    functionName: 'approve'
  },
  conditions: [
    { field: 'approve.spender', op: 'address_in', addresses: [ROUTER] },
    { field: 'approve.amount', op: 'uint_lte', max: APPROVE_CAP.toString() }
  ]
};

/** The swap rule ¬ß2.1 demands: recipient pinned to the user's own account. */
const SWAP_RULE = {
  id: 'swap-on-router',
  effect: 'allow',
  scope: {
    kind: 'contract-call',
    targets: [ROUTER],
    selector: SWAP_SELECTOR,
    functionName: 'swapTokens'
  },
  conditions: [
    { field: 'swapTokens.recipient', op: 'address_is_owner' },
    { field: 'swapTokens.amountIn', op: 'uint_lte', max: APPROVE_CAP.toString() }
  ]
};

function policy(rules: unknown[] = [APPROVE_RULE, SWAP_RULE]) {
  return compileAuthorityPolicy({ version: 1, chainId: ROBINHOOD_CHAIN_ID, rules });
}

function swapAction(overrides: Partial<AuthorityContractCall> = {}): AuthorityContractCall {
  return {
    kind: 'contract-call',
    chainId: ROBINHOOD_CHAIN_ID,
    target: ROUTER,
    selector: SWAP_SELECTOR,
    functionName: 'swapTokens',
    value: 0n,
    args: { recipient: OWNER, amountIn: 500n },
    ...overrides
  };
}

      policy(),

        chainId: ROBINHOOD_CHAIN_ID,

  it('permits a swap whose recipient is the owner account', () => {
    expect(evaluateAuthorityAction(policy(), swapAction(), CONTEXT)).toMatchObject({

describe('S4-P10 ‚Äî footgun 1: overlapping ALLOW rules let the looser one win (DG-3)', () => {
  it('rejects overlapping ALLOW rules on the same (target, selector) at construction time', () => {
    // Without this, the second rule's wider allowlist unions with the first's and
    // the tight rule is silently defeated ‚Äî the exact DG-3 finding.
    const loose = {
      id: 'approve-anything',
      effect: 'allow',
      scope: {
        kind: 'contract-call',
        targets: [TOKEN],
        selector: ERC20_APPROVE.selector,
        functionName: 'approve'
      },
      conditions: [
        { field: 'approve.spender', op: 'address_in', addresses: [ROUTER, ATTACKER] },
        { field: 'approve.amount', op: 'uint_lte', max: '999999999' }
      ]
    };

    let thrown: unknown;
    try {
      policy([APPROVE_RULE, loose]);
    } catch (error) {
      thrown = error;
    }
    expect(thrown).toBeInstanceOf(AuthorityPolicyError);
    expect(thrown).toMatchObject({ code: 'authority-policy-invalid-overlapping-allow' });
    expect((thrown as Error).message).toContain('approve-router');
    expect((thrown as Error).message).toContain('approve-anything');
  });

  it('rejects overlapping signed-struct ALLOW rules on the same (verifyingContract, primaryType)', () => {
    const permitRule = (id: string, spender: string) => ({
      id,
      effect: 'allow',
      scope: { kind: 'signed-struct', verifyingContracts: [PERMIT2], primaryType: 'PermitSingle' },
      conditions: [
        { field: 'message.spender', op: 'address_in', addresses: [spender] },
        { field: 'message.details.amount', op: 'uint_lte', max: '1000' }
      ]
    });
    expect(() => policy([permitRule('tight', ROUTER), permitRule('loose', ATTACKER)])).toThrow(
      expect.objectContaining({ code: 'authority-policy-invalid-overlapping-allow' })
    );
  });

  it('permits non-overlapping rules that differ only by target', () => {
    const otherToken = '0x7777777777777777777777777777777777777777';
    const compiled = policy([
      APPROVE_RULE,
      {
        ...APPROVE_RULE,
        id: 'approve-router-other-token',
        scope: { ...APPROVE_RULE.scope, targets: [otherToken] }
      }
    ]);
    expect(compiled.rules).toHaveLength(2);
  });

  it('rejects duplicate rule ids, because verdict codes name the rule', () => {
    expect(() =>
      policy([
        APPROVE_RULE,
        { ...SWAP_RULE, id: 'approve-router' }
      ])
    ).toThrow(expect.objectContaining({ code: 'authority-policy-invalid-duplicate-rule-id' }));
  });

  it('reports a hand-built ambiguous policy as unresolved rather than picking a rule', () => {
    // compileAuthorityPolicy cannot produce this. A caller constructing a
    // CompiledAuthorityPolicy by hand can, and must not get union semantics.
    const compiled = policy([SWAP_RULE]);
    const handBuilt = {
      ...compiled,
      rules: [compiled.rules[0]!, { ...compiled.rules[0]!, id: 'shadow' }]
    };
    expect(evaluateAuthorityAction(handBuilt, swapAction(), CONTEXT)).toMatchObject({
      kind: 'unresolved',
      code: 'authority-policy-ambiguous-match'
    });
  });
});

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Footgun 2 ‚Äî a mis-pathed condition fails closed, and says so
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

describe('S4-P10 ‚Äî footgun 2: a mis-pathed condition fails closed (DG-3)', () => {
  it('reports a mis-pathed condition as a distinct unresolved diagnostic, not a denial', () => {
    // `recipent` is a typo for `recipient`. Every request through this rule is
    // refused ‚Äî the right direction ‚Äî but an operator must be told the *path* did
    // not resolve, or they will go and debug a trade that was fine.
    const typoPolicy = policy([
      {
        ...SWAP_RULE,
        conditions: [{ field: 'swapTokens.recipent', op: 'address_is_owner' }]
      }
    ]);

    const verdict = evaluateAuthorityAction(typoPolicy, swapAction(), CONTEXT);

    expect(verdict.kind).toBe('unresolved');
    expect(verdict).toMatchObject({
      kind: 'unresolved',
      code: 'authority-field-path-unresolved',
      ruleId: 'swap-on-router',
      field: 'swapTokens.recipent'
    });
    // It must not present as a generic denial...
    expect(verdict.kind).not.toBe('deny');
    // ...and it must still refuse.
    expect(isPermitted(verdict)).toBe(false);
    if (verdict.kind !== 'unresolved') return;
    // The diagnostic names what was actually available, so the fix is one read.
    expect(verdict.reason).toContain('recipient');
    expect(verdict.reason).toContain('amountIn');
  });

  it('reports a mis-pathed nested struct field with the keys that were available', () => {
    const permitPolicy = policy([
      {
        id: 'permit2-single',
        effect: 'allow',
        scope: { kind: 'signed-struct', verifyingContracts: [PERMIT2], primaryType: 'PermitSingle' },
        conditions: [
          { field: 'message.spender', op: 'address_in', addresses: [ROUTER] },
          { field: 'message.details.amounts', op: 'uint_lte', max: '1000' }
        ]
      }
    ]);
    const verdict = evaluateAuthorityAction(permitPolicy, permitAction(), CONTEXT);
    expect(verdict).toMatchObject({
      kind: 'unresolved',
      code: 'authority-field-path-unresolved',
      field: 'message.details.amounts'
    });
    if (verdict.kind !== 'unresolved') return;
    expect(verdict.reason).toContain('amount');
  });

  it('reports a type-mismatched path distinctly from a mis-pathed one', () => {
    const wrongTypePolicy = policy([
      {
        ...SWAP_RULE,
        conditions: [{ field: 'swapTokens.amountIn', op: 'address_is_owner' }]
      }
    ]);
    expect(evaluateAuthorityAction(wrongTypePolicy, swapAction(), CONTEXT)).toMatchObject({
      kind: 'unresolved',
      code: 'authority-field-type-mismatch',
      field: 'swapTokens.amountIn'
    });
  });

  it('reports a path that lands on a nested struct as a type mismatch, not a value', () => {
    const structPolicy = policy([
      {
        id: 'permit2-single',
        effect: 'allow',
        scope: { kind: 'signed-struct', verifyingContracts: [PERMIT2], primaryType: 'PermitSingle' },
        conditions: [
          { field: 'message.spender', op: 'address_in', addresses: [ROUTER] },
          { field: 'message.details.amount', op: 'uint_lte', max: '1000' },
          { field: 'message.details', op: 'address_in', addresses: [ROUTER] }
        ]
      }
    ]);
    expect(evaluateAuthorityAction(structPolicy, permitAction(), CONTEXT)).toMatchObject({
      kind: 'unresolved',
      code: 'authority-field-type-mismatch',
      field: 'message.details'
    });
  });

  it('catches the commonest mis-path at construction: a root the rule does not permit', () => {
    expect(() =>
      policy([
        {
          ...SWAP_RULE,
          conditions: [{ field: 'transfer.amount', op: 'uint_lte', max: '1' }]
        }
      ])
    ).toThrow(expect.objectContaining({ code: 'authority-policy-invalid-field-path' }));
  });

  it('rejects a call-metadata path that names no real field', () => {
    expect(() =>
      policy([
        {
          ...SWAP_RULE,
          conditions: [{ field: 'call.gasLimit', op: 'uint_lte', max: '1' }]
        }
      ])
    ).toThrow(expect.objectContaining({ code: 'authority-policy-invalid-field-path' }));
  });

  it('reports an owner account that is not an address as a type mismatch, never a pass', () => {
    const verdict = evaluateAuthorityAction(policy(), swapAction(), {
      ...CONTEXT,
      ownerAccount: 'not-an-address'
    });
    expect(verdict).toMatchObject({
      kind: 'unresolved',
      code: 'authority-field-type-mismatch'
    });
  });

  it('refuses a UserOperation whose selector has no descriptor, under its own code', () => {
    const verdict = authorizeUserOperationCall(
      policy(),
      {
        chainId: ROBINHOOD_CHAIN_ID,
        sender: ACCOUNT,
        callData: encodeExecute(TOKEN, 0n, `0xdeadbeef${uintWord(1n)}`)
      },
      DESCRIPTORS,
      CONTEXT
    );
    expect(verdict).toMatchObject({
      kind: 'unresolved',
      code: 'authority-action-unknown-selector'
    });
    expect(isPermitted(verdict)).toBe(false);
  });
});

// Permit2 / signed structs (S4-M13 forward compatibility)

function permitAction(
  overrides: { spender?: string; amount?: bigint; token?: string; deadline?: bigint } = {}
): AuthoritySignedStruct {
  return {
    kind: 'signed-struct',
    chainId: ROBINHOOD_CHAIN_ID,
    primaryType: 'PermitSingle',
    verifyingContract: PERMIT2,
    message: {
      details: {
        token: overrides.token ?? TOKEN,
        amount: overrides.amount ?? 500n,
        expiration: BigInt(NOW + 600),
        nonce: 0n
      },
      spender: overrides.spender ?? ROUTER,
      sigDeadline: overrides.deadline ?? BigInt(NOW + 600)
    }
  };
}

const PERMIT_RULE = {
  id: 'permit2-single',
  effect: 'allow',
  scope: { kind: 'signed-struct', verifyingContracts: [PERMIT2], primaryType: 'PermitSingle' },
  conditions: [
    { field: 'message.details.token', op: 'address_in', addresses: [TOKEN] },
    { field: 'message.spender', op: 'address_in', addresses: [ROUTER] },
    { field: 'message.details.amount', op: 'uint_lte', max: APPROVE_CAP.toString() },
    { field: 'message.sigDeadline', op: 'uint_lte_now_plus', maxSecondsAhead: 1800 }
  ]
};

describe('S4-P10 ‚Äî the same conditions bind a Permit2 permit (S4-M13)', () => {
  it('permits a permit whose token, spender, amount and deadline all hold', () => {
    expect(evaluateAuthorityAction(policy([PERMIT_RULE]), permitAction(), CONTEXT)).toMatchObject({
      kind: 'permit',
      ruleId: 'permit2-single',
      matched: 'PermitSingle'
    });
  });

  it('denies a permit granting allowance to a non-allowlisted spender', () => {
    expect(
      evaluateAuthorityAction(policy([PERMIT_RULE]), permitAction({ spender: ATTACKER }), CONTEXT)
    ).toMatchObject({
      kind: 'deny',
      code: 'authority-deny-condition-failed',
      field: 'message.spender'
    });
  });

  it('denies a permit whose amount exceeds the bound', () => {
    expect(
      evaluateAuthorityAction(
        policy([PERMIT_RULE]),
        permitAction({ amount: APPROVE_CAP + 1n }),
        CONTEXT
      )
    ).toMatchObject({ kind: 'deny', field: 'message.details.amount' });
  });

  it('denies a permit whose deadline is further ahead than the window allows', () => {
    expect(
      evaluateAuthorityAction(
        policy([PERMIT_RULE]),
        permitAction({ deadline: BigInt(NOW + 4000) }),
        CONTEXT
      )
    ).toMatchObject({ kind: 'deny', field: 'message.sigDeadline' });
  });

  it('denies a permit signed against a verifying contract that is not the pinned Permit2', () => {
    expect(
      evaluateAuthorityAction(
        policy([PERMIT_RULE]),
        { ...permitAction(), verifyingContract: ATTACKER },
        CONTEXT
      )
    ).toMatchObject({ kind: 'deny', code: 'authority-deny-no-matching-rule' });
  });

  it('denies a different primary type against the same verifying contract', () => {
    expect(
      evaluateAuthorityAction(
        policy([PERMIT_RULE]),
        { ...permitAction(), primaryType: 'Batch' },
        CONTEXT
      )
    ).toMatchObject({ kind: 'deny', code: 'authority-deny-no-matching-rule' });
  });

  it('refuses at construction a permit rule with no amount bound', () => {
    expect(() =>
      policy([
        {
          ...PERMIT_RULE,
          conditions: [{ field: 'message.spender', op: 'address_in', addresses: [ROUTER] }]
        }
      ])
    ).toThrow(expect.objectContaining({ code: 'authority-policy-invalid-unbounded-approval' }));
  });

  it('refuses at construction a permit rule with no address constraint', () => {
    expect(() =>
      policy([
        {
          ...PERMIT_RULE,
          conditions: [{ field: 'message.details.amount', op: 'uint_lte', max: '1000' }]
        }
      ])
    ).toThrow(expect.objectContaining({ code: 'authority-policy-invalid-unbounded-approval' }));
  });

  it.each([
    'Permit',
    'PermitSingle',
    'PermitBatch',
    'PermitTransferFrom',
    'PermitBatchTransferFrom',
    'PermitWitnessTransferFrom',
    'PermitBatchWitnessTransferFrom'
  ])('applies the structural check to every spending-authority primary type: %s', (primaryType) => {
    // Verified against permit2/src/libraries/PermitHash.sol on 2026-08-25. The
    // two witness variants were missing from the first draft of
    // ALLOWANCE_PRIMARY_TYPES, and a name missing from that list means the
    // structural check is SILENTLY SKIPPED for it -- an unbounded permit rule
    // would compile clean. That is the dangerous direction to be wrong in, so the
    // list is pinned by enumeration rather than by spot-checking one member.
    expect(() =>
      policy([
        {
          ...PERMIT_RULE,
          scope: { kind: 'signed-struct', verifyingContracts: [PERMIT2], primaryType },
          conditions: [{ field: 'message.details.amount', op: 'uint_lte', max: '1000' }]
        }
      ])
    ).toThrow(expect.objectContaining({ code: 'authority-policy-invalid-unbounded-approval' }));
  });

  it('does not apply the structural check to a sub-struct type that can never be a primaryType', () => {
    // PermitDetails and TokenPermissions are referenced BY the permit types, never
    // signed on their own, so a rule scoped to one could not match a real request.
    // Including them would be harmless but misleading; excluding them is the claim
    // being pinned here.
    expect(() =>
      policy([
        {
          ...PERMIT_RULE,
          scope: { kind: 'signed-struct', verifyingContracts: [PERMIT2], primaryType: 'PermitDetails' },
          conditions: [{ field: 'message.amount', op: 'uint_lte', max: '1000' }]
        }
      ])
    ).not.toThrow();
  });
});

    ).toThrow(expect.objectContaining({ code: 'authority-policy-invalid-amount' }));
  });

    expect(rule.scope.targets).toEqual([TOKEN]);

      compileAuthorityPolicy({ chainId: 0, rules: [] });
