};

const of = (over: Partial<PusdMonitorInput> = {}): PusdMonitorInput => ({ ...healthy, ...over });

describe('assessPusdWithdrawalPath (S4-M42)', () => {
  it('reports healthy only when nothing failed AND nothing was unchecked', () => {
    const verdict = assessPusdWithdrawalPath(healthy);
    expect(verdict.outcome).toBe('healthy');
    expect(verdict.unassessed).toEqual([]);
    expect(verdict.failures).toEqual([]);
    expect(pusdWithdrawalsHealthy(verdict)).toBe(true);
  });

  describe('the native side is the exhaustible one', () => {
    it('alarms when native-USDC depth falls below the floor', () => {
      // A withdrawal runs USDC.e -> native USDC, draining the native leg.
      const verdict = assessPusdWithdrawalPath(of({ depth: { nativeUsdcAvailable: 10_000 } }));
      expect(verdict.outcome).toBe('impaired');
      expect(verdict.failures).toContain('pusd-pool-depth-below-floor');
    });

    it('defaults the floor to the venue own large-withdrawal guidance', () => {
      // Polymarket advises splitting withdrawals over $50,000, so below that a
      // single ordinary large withdrawal cannot clear.
      expect(PUSD_LARGE_WITHDRAWAL_USD).toBe(50_000);
      expect(assessPusdWithdrawalPath(of({ depth: { nativeUsdcAvailable: 49_999 } })).outcome)
        .toBe('impaired');
      expect(assessPusdWithdrawalPath(of({ depth: { nativeUsdcAvailable: 50_000 } })).outcome)
        .toBe('healthy');
    });

    it('accepts an explicit floor override', () => {
      expect(assessPusdWithdrawalPath(of({
        depth: { nativeUsdcAvailable: 30_000 },
        depthFloorUsd: 25_000
      })).outcome).toBe('healthy');
    });
  });

  describe('the float-relative alarm ‚Äî the one that matters at our scale', () => {
    it('alarms when depth is above the floor but below our aggregate float', () => {
      // ~195k of measured depth against a ~488M pUSD supply means the POOL, not
      // the supply, bounds our float. This fires at the point where our users
      // collectively cannot exit even though any single withdrawal would clear.
      const verdict = assessPusdWithdrawalPath(of({
        depth: { nativeUsdcAvailable: 195_560 },
        aggregateFloatUsd: 300_000
      }));
      expect(verdict.outcome).toBe('impaired');
      expect(verdict.failures).toContain('pusd-pool-depth-below-float');
      // Deliberately NOT a floor breach: the two alarms are independent.
      expect(verdict.failures).not.toContain('pusd-pool-depth-below-floor');
    });

    it('does not alarm when depth covers the float exactly', () => {
      expect(assessPusdWithdrawalPath(of({
        depth: { nativeUsdcAvailable: 100_000 },
        aggregateFloatUsd: 100_000
      })).outcome).toBe('healthy');
    });

    it('reports both alarms when depth is below the floor AND the float', () => {
      const verdict = assessPusdWithdrawalPath(of({
        depth: { nativeUsdcAvailable: 1_000 },
        aggregateFloatUsd: 500_000
      }));
      expect(verdict.failures).toEqual([
        'pusd-pool-depth-below-floor',
        'pusd-pool-depth-below-float'
      ]);
    });
  });

  describe('pause ‚Äî the most dangerous shape', () => {
    it('alarms on a paused offramp, and outranks thin depth', () => {
      // A pause blocks EVERY withdrawal regardless of liquidity, while thin depth
      // only blocks large ones ‚Äî so it leads the reason code.
      const verdict = assessPusdWithdrawalPath(of({
        collateralPaused: true,
        depth: { nativeUsdcAvailable: 1 }
      }));
      expect(verdict.reasonCode).toBe('pusd-collateral-paused');
      expect(verdict.failures).toContain('pusd-pool-depth-below-floor');
    });

    it('treats an unreadable pause state as unassessed, never as unpaused', () => {
      // The balance looks fine either way, which is what makes guessing here
      // dangerous: collateral can be unwithdrawable while the token reports full.
      const verdict = assessPusdWithdrawalPath(of({ collateralPaused: null }));
      expect(verdict.outcome).toBe('healthy-partial');
      expect(verdict.unassessed).toContain('pause-state-unknown');
      expect(pusdWithdrawalsHealthy(verdict)).toBe(false);
    });
  });

  describe('redeemability', () => {
    it('alarms when a simulated unwrap reverts', () => {
      expect(assessPusdWithdrawalPath(of({ simulatedUnwrap: 'reverted' })).failures)
        .toContain('pusd-unwrap-reverts');
    });

    it('treats an unattempted simulation as unassessed, not as success', () => {
      const verdict = assessPusdWithdrawalPath(of({ simulatedUnwrap: null }));
      expect(verdict.outcome).toBe('healthy-partial');
      expect(verdict.unassessed).toContain('redeemability-untested');
    });
  });

  describe('the 10bp swap bound ‚Äî adopted from the venue, not invented', () => {
    it('uses the documented figure', () => {
      expect(PUSD_SWAP_MAX_OUTPUT_DIFFERENCE_BPS).toBe(10);
    });

    it('alarms above the bound and passes at it', () => {
      expect(assessPusdWithdrawalPath(of({ swapOutputDifferenceBps: 11 })).failures)
        .toContain('pusd-swap-output-outside-bound');
      expect(assessPusdWithdrawalPath(of({ swapOutputDifferenceBps: 10 })).outcome)
        .toBe('healthy');
    });

    it('treats a missing quote as unassessed', () => {
      expect(assessPusdWithdrawalPath(of({ swapOutputDifferenceBps: null })).unassessed)
        .toContain('swap-output-unknown');
    });
  });

  describe('unknown is never a pass (S4-M41 discipline)', () => {
    it('reports unknown depth as its own code rather than passing', () => {
      const verdict = assessPusdWithdrawalPath(of({ depth: { nativeUsdcAvailable: null } }));
      expect(verdict.outcome).toBe('healthy-partial');
      expect(verdict.unassessed).toContain('pool-depth-unknown');
      expect(verdict.failures).toEqual([]);
    });

    it('does not claim a floor breach when depth is merely unknown', () => {
      // Unknown and zero demand opposite responses: one is "go look at the feed",
      // the other is "stop withdrawing".
      expect(assessPusdWithdrawalPath(of({ depth: { nativeUsdcAvailable: null } })).failures)
        .not.toContain('pusd-pool-depth-below-floor');
    });

    it('reports a genuine zero depth as a floor breach, not as unknown', () => {
      // The other direction of the same rule.
      const verdict = assessPusdWithdrawalPath(of({ depth: { nativeUsdcAvailable: 0 } }));
      expect(verdict.failures).toContain('pusd-pool-depth-below-floor');
      expect(verdict.unassessed).not.toContain('pool-depth-unknown');
    });

    it('treats NaN and Infinity as unknown rather than as numbers', () => {
      for (const bad of [Number.NaN, Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY]) {
        expect(assessPusdWithdrawalPath(of({ depth: { nativeUsdcAvailable: bad } })).unassessed)
          .toContain('pool-depth-unknown');
      }
    });

    it('disables the float alarm with its own code when the float is unknown', () => {
      const verdict = assessPusdWithdrawalPath(of({ aggregateFloatUsd: null }));
      expect(verdict.unassessed).toContain('float-unknown');
      expect(verdict.failures).toEqual([]);
    });

    it('keeps a failure visible even when something else was unassessable', () => {
      // An impaired verdict must not be softened to partial just because a
      // different check could not run.
      const verdict = assessPusdWithdrawalPath(of({
        collateralPaused: null,
        simulatedUnwrap: 'reverted'
      }));
      expect(verdict.outcome).toBe('impaired');
      expect(verdict.unassessed).toContain('pause-state-unknown');
    });
  });

  it('pusdWithdrawalsHealthy is the only predicate, so partial cannot be waved through', () => {
    // A caller testing `outcome !== 'impaired'` would admit healthy-partial.
    const partial = assessPusdWithdrawalPath(of({ collateralPaused: null }));
    expect(partial.outcome).not.toBe('impaired');
    expect(pusdWithdrawalsHealthy(partial)).toBe(false);
  });
});

describe('isOnlyUnpausedRevert', () => {
  it('recognises the documented pause selector', () => {
    // Verified two independent ways: viem toFunctionSelector and a raw keccak256
    // of the signature both yield 0x49b8b3ac.
    expect(ONLY_UNPAUSED_SELECTOR).toBe('0x49b8b3ac');
    expect(isOnlyUnpausedRevert('0x49b8b3ac')).toBe(true);
    expect(isOnlyUnpausedRevert('0x49B8B3AC')).toBe(true);
  });

  it('does not mistake another revert for a pause', () => {
    // A generic revert must stay generic: reporting it as a pause would send an
    // operator to check an admin setting that is fine.
    expect(isOnlyUnpausedRevert('0xdeadbeef')).toBe(false);
    expect(isOnlyUnpausedRevert('0x')).toBe(false);
    expect(isOnlyUnpausedRevert(null)).toBe(false);
    expect(isOnlyUnpausedRevert(undefined)).toBe(false);
  });
});

describe('constants', () => {
  it('pins 6 decimals, because 18 is the trap', () => {
    // S4-M41: using the ether helpers on a 6-decimal token understates it by
    // 10^12, which presents as "no funds" rather than as a scaling bug.
    expect(PUSD_DECIMALS).toBe(6);
  });
});

==> packages/shared/src/pusd-liquidity.ts <==
/**
 * pUSD withdrawal-liquidity monitoring (`S4-M42`).
 *
 * **This is not a peg monitor, and the distinction is the whole item.** Per
 * Polymarket's own docs, pUSD is *"a standard ERC-20 token on Polygon, backed by
 * USDC. The smart contract -- which enables the withdrawal functionality --
 * enforces the backing. No algorithmic peg, no fractional reserve."* It is also
 * deliberately **not listed on external exchanges**, so there is **no market
 * price to poll** -- a price feed for pUSD would be measuring nothing.
 *
 * What can actually strand a user's funds is named in the withdraw docs:
 *
 *   *"pUSD is unwrapped to USDC via the Collateral Offramp and swapped through
 *   the Uniswap v3 pool for USDC (native). The UI enforces less than 10bp
 *   difference in output amount. **At times, this pool may be exhausted.**"*
 *
 * So the monitored quantity is **liquidity in one specific pool**, which is
 * public and directly measurable, and the reserve address -- which an earlier
 * attempt was blocked on -- is not needed at all.
 *
 * **Deliberately absent: a reserve-ratio check.** Summing USDC held at the pUSD
 * token, Onramp and Offramp against `totalSupply` yields ~0.000003 on a ~488M
 * supply, and `underlying()`, `asset()`, `totalAssets()`, `reserve()`,
 * `convertToAssets()` and `exchangeRate()` all revert on the proxy. That is
 * **not** evidence pUSD is unbacked -- the docs say the contract enforces
 * backing -- only that the formula is wrong and the reserve lives elsewhere. An
 * alarm on that ratio would fire permanently and be ignored inside a day, which
 * is worse than no alarm. Recorded here so it is not re-attempted.
 *
 * Pure module: no network, no clock, no environment. Every input is an argument,
 * which is what makes it testable with no infrastructure and matches
 * `master-capacity.ts` / `stop-loss.ts` / `position-cap.ts`.
 */

/** Verified on Polygon mainnet, 2026-09-01. */
export const PUSD_CONTRACTS = Object.freeze({
  /** pUSD, 6 decimals. */
  pUsd: '0xC011a7E12a19f7B1f670d46F03B03f3342E82DFB',
  collateralOnramp: '0x93070a847efEf7F70739046A929D47a521F5B8ee',
  collateralOfframp: '0x2957922Eb93258b93368531d39fAcCA3B4dC5854',
  /**
   * The swap pool the withdraw path routes through. `token0` is USDC.e and
   * `token1` is native USDC; fee tier 100 (0.01%).
   */
  withdrawalPool: '0xd36ec33c8bed5a9f7b6630855f1533455b98a418',
  usdcE: '0x2791Bca1f2de4661ED88A30C99A7a9449Aa84174',
  usdcNative: '0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359'
} as const);

/** pUSD and both USDC variants are 6-decimal. Not 18 -- see `S4-M41`. */
export const PUSD_DECIMALS = 6;

/**
 * Selector of `OnlyUnpaused()`, the error `wrap`/`unwrap` revert with when an
 * admin has paused the asset. Verified two ways: viem's `toFunctionSelector`
 * and a raw keccak256 of the signature both give `0x49b8b3ac`.
 *
 * Worth pinning as a constant because the **pause is the most dangerous failure
 * shape here**: collateral cannot be withdrawn while the token still reports a
 * full balance, so nothing about the user's balance looks wrong.
 */
export const ONLY_UNPAUSED_SELECTOR = '0x49b8b3ac';

/**
 * The venue's own output-difference bound on the withdraw swap: *"The UI enforces
 * less than 10bp difference in output amount."*
 *
 * Adopted rather than invented, so the threshold is defensible. A **widening**
 * spread on this pair is early warning before outright exhaustion, which is why
 * it is assessed rather than merely enforced.
 */
export const PUSD_SWAP_MAX_OUTPUT_DIFFERENCE_BPS = 10;

/**
 * Polymarket's own guidance: *"For very large withdrawals (over $50,000),
 * consider breaking the withdrawal into smaller amounts."* Used as the default
 * single-withdrawal notional the depth check is judged against.
 */
export const PUSD_LARGE_WITHDRAWAL_USD = 50_000;

/**
 * Why an assessment could not be completed. **Never a pass**, and never zero.
 *
 * Mirrors `MasterCapacityUnassessedReason`: unknown is a named code, because a
 * missing figure and a figure of zero demand opposite responses -- one is "go
 * look at the feed", the other is "stop withdrawing".
 */
export type PusdUnassessedReason =
  /** No native-USDC depth figure was supplied, or it was not a finite number. */
  | 'pool-depth-unknown'
  /** Our aggregate float is unknown, so the float-relative alarm cannot run. */
  | 'float-unknown'
  /** The pause state could not be read (RPC failure, not a paused result). */
  | 'pause-state-unknown'
  /** The unwrap simulation could not be performed at all. */
  | 'redeemability-untested'
  /** No quoted output, so the 10bp bound cannot be checked. */
  | 'swap-output-unknown';

/** What the monitor concluded. */
export type PusdOutcome =
  /** Everything checked passed, and nothing was left unchecked. */
  | 'healthy'
  /**
   * What was checked passed, but something was unassessable. **Not a clean
   * pass**, and a distinct outcome so a dashboard can never render it as one --
   * the same distinction `master-capacity.ts` draws for an admit under partial
   * information.
   */
  | 'healthy-partial'
  /** A checked condition failed. Withdrawals are impaired or will be. */
  | 'impaired';

export type PusdReasonCode =
  | 'pusd-withdrawal-path-healthy'
  /** Native-USDC depth below the absolute floor. */
  | 'pusd-pool-depth-below-floor'
  /** Depth below our own aggregate float: users collectively cannot exit. */
  | 'pusd-pool-depth-below-float'
  /** An admin has paused wrap/unwrap. */
  | 'pusd-collateral-paused'
  /** A simulated unwrap reverted. */
  | 'pusd-unwrap-reverts'
  /** Swap output difference exceeds the venue's own 10bp bound. */
  | 'pusd-swap-output-outside-bound'
  /** Nothing failed, but not everything could be checked. */
  | 'pusd-partially-assessed';

/**
 * Native-USDC depth, and only native.
 *
 * **The field is named for the side that matters, and the other side is not
 * accepted at all.** A withdrawal runs USDC.e to native USDC, so it *drains* the
 * native leg: an interface taking an undifferentiated "pool balance", or a
 * `{token0, token1}` pair, invites reading the wrong number and would report a
 * healthy pool while the exitable side was empty. `null` means unknown.
 */
export interface PusdPoolDepth {
  readonly nativeUsdcAvailable: number | null;
}

export interface PusdMonitorInput {
  readonly depth: PusdPoolDepth;
  /**
   * Total pUSD our users collectively hold, in USD. `null` is unknown, which
   * disables the float-relative alarm with its own reason rather than passing.
   */
  readonly aggregateFloatUsd: number | null;
  /**
   * Absolute floor for native-USDC depth. Defaults to the venue's own
   * large-withdrawal guidance: below this, a single ordinary large withdrawal
   * cannot clear.
   */
  readonly depthFloorUsd?: number;
  /** `true` = paused, `false` = not paused, `null` = could not read. */
  readonly collateralPaused: boolean | null;
  /**
   * Result of a simulated `unwrap` (`eth_call`, never a send). `'ok'` /
   * `'reverted'` / `null` for not attempted or attempt failed.
   */
  readonly simulatedUnwrap: 'ok' | 'reverted' | null;
  /**
   * Observed output difference on the swap leg, in basis points. `null` when no
   * quote was obtained.
   */
  readonly swapOutputDifferenceBps: number | null;
}

export interface PusdMonitorVerdict {
  readonly outcome: PusdOutcome;
  readonly reasonCode: PusdReasonCode;
  /** Every failing condition, not just the first ‚Äî an operator needs all of them. */
  readonly failures: readonly PusdReasonCode[];
  /**
   * What this verdict says **nothing** about. An empty array is the only thing
   * that means "fully checked", which is why `healthy` requires it.
   */
  readonly unassessed: readonly PusdUnassessedReason[];
  /** Ops-facing detail. Carries figures, so it is never rendered to a user. */
  readonly detail: string;
}

function finite(value: number | null | undefined): value is number {
  return typeof value === 'number' && Number.isFinite(value);
}

/**
 * Assesses the pUSD withdrawal path.
 *
 * Order of precedence in `reasonCode`: a paused offramp outranks thin depth,
 * because a pause blocks every withdrawal regardless of liquidity while thin
 * depth only blocks large ones.
 */
export function assessPusdWithdrawalPath(input: PusdMonitorInput): PusdMonitorVerdict {
  const failures: PusdReasonCode[] = [];
  const unassessed: PusdUnassessedReason[] = [];
  const notes: string[] = [];

  // ---- Pause: checked first because it is unconditional. -------------------
  if (input.collateralPaused === null) {
    unassessed.push('pause-state-unknown');
  } else if (input.collateralPaused) {
    failures.push('pusd-collateral-paused');
    notes.push('collateral wrap/unwrap is paused (OnlyUnpaused)');
  }

  // ---- Redeemability: the end-to-end property we actually depend on. -------
  if (input.simulatedUnwrap === null) {
    unassessed.push('redeemability-untested');
  } else if (input.simulatedUnwrap === 'reverted') {
    failures.push('pusd-unwrap-reverts');
    notes.push('simulated unwrap reverted');
  }

  // ---- Depth, native side only. -------------------------------------------
  const depth = input.depth.nativeUsdcAvailable;
  if (!finite(depth)) {
    unassessed.push('pool-depth-unknown');
    // The float alarm reads the same figure, so it cannot run either. Recorded
    // separately only when the float itself is the missing half.
  } else {
    const floor = finite(input.depthFloorUsd) ? input.depthFloorUsd : PUSD_LARGE_WITHDRAWAL_USD;
    if (depth < floor) {
      failures.push('pusd-pool-depth-below-floor');
      notes.push(`native USDC depth ${depth} below floor ${floor}`);
    }
    if (!finite(input.aggregateFloatUsd)) {
      unassessed.push('float-unknown');
    } else if (depth < input.aggregateFloatUsd) {
      // The alarm that matters at our scale: not "is a withdrawal possible" but
      // "could all of our users exit". ~195k of measured depth against a ~488M
      // pUSD supply means the pool, not the supply, bounds our float.
      failures.push('pusd-pool-depth-below-float');
      notes.push(`native USDC depth ${depth} below aggregate float ${input.aggregateFloatUsd}`);
    }
  }

  // ---- Swap-leg spread: early warning before exhaustion. ------------------
  if (!finite(input.swapOutputDifferenceBps)) {
    unassessed.push('swap-output-unknown');
  } else if (input.swapOutputDifferenceBps > PUSD_SWAP_MAX_OUTPUT_DIFFERENCE_BPS) {
    failures.push('pusd-swap-output-outside-bound');
    notes.push(
      `swap output difference ${input.swapOutputDifferenceBps}bps exceeds `
      + `${PUSD_SWAP_MAX_OUTPUT_DIFFERENCE_BPS}bps`
    );
  }

  if (failures.length > 0) {
    return {
      outcome: 'impaired',
      reasonCode: failures[0]!,
      failures,
      unassessed,
      detail: notes.join('; ')
    };
  }

  if (unassessed.length > 0) {
    return {
      outcome: 'healthy-partial',
      reasonCode: 'pusd-partially-assessed',
      failures,
      unassessed,
      detail: `nothing failed, but unassessed: ${unassessed.join(', ')}`
    };
  }

  return {
    outcome: 'healthy',
    reasonCode: 'pusd-withdrawal-path-healthy',
    failures,
    unassessed,
    detail: 'pause, redeemability, depth, float and swap spread all checked and passing'
  };
}

/**
 * True only for a fully-checked pass.
 *
 * The single predicate callers should use, so `healthy-partial` cannot be waved
 * through by testing `outcome !== 'impaired'` -- the same reason
 * `isPermitted` exists in the authority policy.
 */
export function pusdWithdrawalsHealthy(verdict: PusdMonitorVerdict): boolean {
  return verdict.outcome === 'healthy';
}

/**
 * Recognises a revert as the documented pause rather than a generic failure.
 *
 * Takes the revert data because the caller owns the RPC; keeping this pure means
 * the pause/unknown distinction is testable without a chain.
 */
export function isOnlyUnpausedRevert(revertData: string | null | undefined): boolean {
  return typeof revertData === 'string'
    && revertData.toLowerCase().startsWith(ONLY_UNPAUSED_SELECTOR);
}

import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import { createWalletBackfillJob } from './queues.js';

const EVM_MIXED = '0xAbCdEf0123456789aBCdeF0123456789ABcDef01';
const EVM_LOWER = EVM_MIXED.toLowerCase();

describe('createWalletBackfillJob', () => {
  it('strips a stored prefix and preserves the represented chain', () => {
    expect(createWalletBackfillJob(`robinhood-chain:${EVM_MIXED}`)).toEqual({
      name: 'backfill-wallet',
      data: {
        address: EVM_LOWER,
        chain: 'robinhood-chain'
      },
      options: {
        jobId: `backfill-robinhood-chain-${EVM_LOWER}`,
        removeOnComplete: true,
        removeOnFail: 1000
      }
    });
  });

  it('normalizes a raw EVM address when the chain is explicit', () => {
    expect(createWalletBackfillJob(EVM_MIXED, 'polygon').data).toEqual({
      address: EVM_LOWER,
      chain: 'polygon'
    });
  });

  it('rejects a chain that conflicts with the stored prefix', () => {
    expect(() => createWalletBackfillJob(`polygon:${EVM_LOWER}`, 'solana')).toThrow(
      /does not match/
    );
  });

  it('rejects ambiguous or misclassified raw EVM addresses', () => {
    expect(() => createWalletBackfillJob(EVM_MIXED)).toThrow(/explicit chain/);
    expect(() => createWalletBackfillJob(EVM_MIXED, 'solana')).toThrow(
      /cannot be classified as Solana/
    );
  });
});

==> packages/shared/src/queues.ts <==
import type { Chain } from './types.js';
import { resolveChainAddress } from './address.js';

export const WALLET_BACKFILL_JOB_NAME = 'backfill-wallet';

export type WalletBackfillJobData = {
  address: string;
  chain: Chain;
};

export function createWalletBackfillJob(address: string, chain?: Chain) {
  const resolved = resolveChainAddress(address, chain);

  return {
    name: WALLET_BACKFILL_JOB_NAME,
    data: {
      address: resolved.raw,
      chain: resolved.chain
    } satisfies WalletBackfillJobData,
    options: {
      jobId: `backfill-${resolved.chain}-${resolved.raw}`,
      removeOnComplete: true,
      removeOnFail: 1000
    }
  };
}

import {

      expect(urls[1]).toBe('https://backup1.example');
      expect(urls[2]).toBe('https://backup2.example');
      expect(urls).toContain('https://api.mainnet-beta.solana.com');
    });

    it('resolves polygon URLs correctly', () => {
      const urls = resolveConfiguredRpcUrls('polygon', {
        POLYGON_RPC_URL: 'https://alchemy.polygon.example'
      });
      expect(urls[0]).toBe('https://alchemy.polygon.example');
      expect(urls).toContain('https://polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com');
    });

    it('resolves robinhood URLs correctly with comma-separated fallbacks', () => {
      const urls = resolveConfiguredRpcUrls('robinhood', {
        ROBINHOOD_RPC_URL: 'https://rpc.mainnet.chain.robinhood.com',
        ROBINHOOD_RPC_URLS: 'https://orbit-fallback.robinhood.example'
      });
      expect(urls[0]).toBe('https://rpc.mainnet.chain.robinhood.com');
      expect(urls[1]).toBe('https://orbit-fallback.robinhood.example');
      expect(urls).toContain('https://rpc.mainnet.chain.robinhood.com');
    });
  });

  describe('prioritizeRpcEndpoints & circuit breaker', () => {
    const urls = ['https://rpc-a.example', 'https://rpc-b.example', 'https://rpc-c.example'];

    it('orders by lowest latency among healthy endpoints', () => {
      recordRpcSuccess('https://rpc-a.example', 150);
      recordRpcSuccess('https://rpc-b.example', 50);
      recordRpcSuccess('https://rpc-c.example', 80);

      const prioritized = prioritizeRpcEndpoints(urls);
      expect(prioritized).toEqual([
        'https://rpc-b.example',
        'https://rpc-c.example',
        'https://rpc-a.example'
      ]);
    });

    it('deprioritizes endpoints on failure with active cooldown', () => {
      const now = 100000;
      recordRpcFailure('https://rpc-a.example', new Error('HTTP 429 Too Many Requests'), now);

      const stateA = getOrCreateEndpointState('https://rpc-a.example');
      expect(stateA.consecutiveFailures).toBe(1);
      expect(stateA.cooldownUntil).toBeGreaterThan(now);

      const prioritized = prioritizeRpcEndpoints(urls, now);
      // rpc-a is in cooldown, so healthy rpc-b and rpc-c come first
      expect(prioritized[0]).not.toBe('https://rpc-a.example');
      expect(prioritized[2]).toBe('https://rpc-a.example');
    });

    it('recovers endpoint when cooldown expires', () => {
      const now = 100000;
      recordRpcFailure('https://rpc-a.example', new Error('timeout'), now);

      // Advance time beyond cooldown (15s = 15000ms)
      const future = now + 20000;
      const prioritized = prioritizeRpcEndpoints(urls, future);
      // It has recovered from coolingOff into recovering
      expect(prioritized).toContain('https://rpc-a.example');
    });

    it('clears failures on subsequent success', () => {
      recordRpcFailure('https://rpc-a.example', new Error('failed'));
      expect(getOrCreateEndpointState('https://rpc-a.example').consecutiveFailures).toBe(1);

      recordRpcSuccess('https://rpc-a.example', 45);
      const state = getOrCreateEndpointState('https://rpc-a.example');
      expect(state.consecutiveFailures).toBe(0);
      expect(state.cooldownUntil).toBe(0);
      expect(state.lastLatencyMs).toBe(45);
    });
  });

  describe('executeWithRpcFailover', () => {
    it('succeeds on first attempt if primary works', async () => {
      const env = {
        SOLANA_RPC_URLS: 'https://rpc-1.test,https://rpc-2.test'
      };

      const result = await executeWithRpcFailover({
        chain: 'solana',
        env,
        action: async (url) => {
          if (url === 'https://rpc-1.test') return 'success-from-rpc-1';
          throw new Error('should not reach here');
        }
      });

      expect(result).toBe('success-from-rpc-1');
      expect(getOrCreateEndpointState('https://rpc-1.test').consecutiveFailures).toBe(0);
    });

    it('transparently fails over to secondary when primary fails', async () => {
      const env = {
        SOLANA_RPC_URLS: 'https://failing-rpc.test,https://working-rpc.test'
      };

      const callLog: string[] = [];

      const result = await executeWithRpcFailover({
        chain: 'solana',
        env,
        action: async (url) => {
          callLog.push(url);
          if (url === 'https://failing-rpc.test') {
            throw new Error('503 Service Unavailable');
          }
          return `success-from-${url}`;
        }
      });

      expect(result).toBe('success-from-https://working-rpc.test');
      expect(callLog).toEqual(['https://failing-rpc.test', 'https://working-rpc.test']);
      expect(getOrCreateEndpointState('https://failing-rpc.test').consecutiveFailures).toBe(1);
      expect(getOrCreateEndpointState('https://working-rpc.test').consecutiveFailures).toBe(0);
    });

    it('throws aggregate error if all candidate endpoints fail', async () => {
      const env = {
        SOLANA_RPC_URL: 'https://fail-1.test',
        SOLANA_RPC_URLS: 'https://fail-2.test'
      };

      await expect(
        executeWithRpcFailover({
          chain: 'solana',
          env,
          maxAttempts: 2,
          action: async (url) => {
            throw new Error(`RPC down: ${url}`);
          }
        })
      ).rejects.toThrow(/All 2 RPC endpoint\(s\) failed for solana/);
    });
  });

  describe('getActiveRpcUrl', () => {
    it('returns healthy active endpoint', () => {
      const env = {
        POLYGON_RPC_URLS: 'https://poly-1.test,https://poly-2.test'
      };
      recordRpcFailure('https://poly-1.test', new Error('rate limited'));
      const active = getActiveRpcUrl('polygon', env);
      expect(active).toBe('https://poly-2.test');
    });
  });
});

==> packages/shared/src/rpc-failover.ts <==
/**
/**
 * Resilient Multi-Provider RPC Failover and Health Circuit Breaker.
 *
 * In production multi-tenant trading, single RPC endpoints are common single points
 * of failure (rate-limits, 429s, maintenance windows, networking partitions).
 *
 * This module provides:
 * 1. Multi-provider URL pooling with primary -> secondary fallback cascade.
 * 2. In-memory circuit breaker tracking consecutive failures, latency, and cooldowns.
 * 3. Execution wrapper with automatic failover and retry across healthy providers.
 * 4. Active telemetry probing (getSlot / eth_blockNumber) for system health reports.
 */

import type { Chain } from './types.js';

export interface RpcEndpointState {
  readonly url: string;
  consecutiveFailures: number;
  cooldownUntil: number;
  lastSuccessAt: number | null;
  lastFailureAt: number | null;
  lastLatencyMs: number | null;
  lastError: string | null;
}

export interface RpcEndpointProbe {
  readonly url: string;
  readonly healthy: boolean;
  readonly latencyMs: number;
  readonly blockHeight?: number;
  readonly error?: string;
}

export interface RpcPoolReport {
  readonly chain: string;
  readonly primaryUrl: string;
  readonly activeHealthyUrl: string;
  readonly endpoints: ReadonlyArray<RpcEndpointProbe & { consecutiveFailures: number }>;
}

const DEFAULT_COOLDOWN_BASE_MS = 15_000;
const MAX_COOLDOWN_MS = 120_000;
const DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS = 8_000;

export const DEFAULT_FALLBACK_RPCS: Record<Chain, readonly string[]> = {
  solana: [
    'https://api.mainnet-beta.solana.com'
  ],
  polygon: [
    'https://polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com',
    'https://1rpc.io/matic',
    'https://polygon.drpc.org'
  ],
  'robinhood-chain': [
    'https://rpc.mainnet.chain.robinhood.com'
  ],
  base: [
    'https://mainnet.base.org',
    'https://1rpc.io/base',
    'https://base.drpc.org'
  ],
  ethereum: [
    'https://eth.llamarpc.com',
    'https://1rpc.io/eth',
    'https://ethereum.drpc.org'
  ],
  bsc: [
    'https://binance.llamarpc.com',
    'https://1rpc.io/bnb',
    'https://bsc-dataseed.binance.org'
  ]
};

// Global in-memory registry of endpoint states
const endpointRegistry = new Map<string, RpcEndpointState>();

export function getOrCreateEndpointState(url: string): RpcEndpointState {
  let state = endpointRegistry.get(url);
  if (!state) {
    state = {
      url,
      consecutiveFailures: 0,
      cooldownUntil: 0,
      lastSuccessAt: null,
      lastFailureAt: null,
      lastLatencyMs: null,
      lastError: null
    };
    endpointRegistry.set(url, state);
  }
  return state;
}

export function resetEndpointRegistry(): void {
  endpointRegistry.clear();
}

/**
 * Parses comma-separated URLs or falls back to singular env var and built-in public fallbacks.
 */
export function resolveConfiguredRpcUrls(
  chain: Chain | 'robinhood',
  env: Record<string, string | undefined> = process.env
): string[] {
  const normalizedChain: Chain = chain === 'robinhood' ? 'robinhood-chain' : chain;
  let pluralEnvKey = 'SOLANA_RPC_URLS';
  let singularEnvKey = 'SOLANA_RPC_URL';

  if (normalizedChain === 'polygon') {
    pluralEnvKey = 'POLYGON_RPC_URLS';
    singularEnvKey = 'POLYGON_RPC_URL';
  } else if (normalizedChain === 'robinhood-chain') {
    pluralEnvKey = 'ROBINHOOD_RPC_URLS';
    singularEnvKey = 'ROBINHOOD_RPC_URL';
  }

  const pluralVal = env[pluralEnvKey];
  const singularVal = env[singularEnvKey];

  const gathered: string[] = [];

  if (pluralVal && pluralVal.trim() !== '') {
    for (const raw of pluralVal.split(',')) {
      const trimmed = raw.trim();
      if (trimmed.startsWith('http://') || trimmed.startsWith('https://')) {
        gathered.push(trimmed);
      }
    }
  }

  if (singularVal && singularVal.trim() !== '') {
    const trimmed = singularVal.trim();
    if ((trimmed.startsWith('http://') || trimmed.startsWith('https://')) && !gathered.includes(trimmed)) {
      gathered.unshift(trimmed); // Primary first
    }
  }

  // Append built-in public fallbacks if not already present
  for (const fallback of (DEFAULT_FALLBACK_RPCS[normalizedChain] ?? [])) {
    if (!gathered.includes(fallback)) {
      gathered.push(fallback);
    }
  }

  return gathered;
}

/**
 * Returns endpoints ordered by priority:
 * 1. Healthy endpoints (no active cooldown), sorted by lowest consecutive failures then lastLatencyMs.
 * 2. Cooled-down endpoints where cooldown has elapsed.
 * 3. Currently cooling-off endpoints as a last resort if all endpoints have failed.
 */
export function prioritizeRpcEndpoints(
  urls: readonly string[],
  now: number = Date.now()
): string[] {
  const states = urls.map(getOrCreateEndpointState);

  const healthy: RpcEndpointState[] = [];
  const recovering: RpcEndpointState[] = [];
  const coolingOff: RpcEndpointState[] = [];

  for (const st of states) {
    if (st.consecutiveFailures === 0 && st.cooldownUntil <= now) {
      healthy.push(st);
    } else if (st.cooldownUntil <= now) {
      recovering.push(st);
    } else {
      coolingOff.push(st);
    }
  }

  // Sort healthy by latency if known
  healthy.sort((a, b) => (a.lastLatencyMs ?? 9999) - (b.lastLatencyMs ?? 9999));

  // Sort cooling off by earliest cooldown expiration
  coolingOff.sort((a, b) => a.cooldownUntil - b.cooldownUntil);

  return [...healthy, ...recovering, ...coolingOff].map((s) => s.url);
}

/**
 * Marks an endpoint as failed, applying exponential cooldown.
 */
export function recordRpcFailure(url: string, error: unknown, now: number = Date.now()): void {
  const state = getOrCreateEndpointState(url);
  state.consecutiveFailures += 1;
  state.lastFailureAt = now;
  state.lastError = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);

  const delayMs = Math.min(
    DEFAULT_COOLDOWN_BASE_MS * Math.pow(2, state.consecutiveFailures - 1),
    MAX_COOLDOWN_MS
  );
  state.cooldownUntil = now + delayMs;
}

/**
 * Marks an endpoint as successful, clearing failure counts and recording latency.
 */
export function recordRpcSuccess(url: string, latencyMs: number, now: number = Date.now()): void {
  const state = getOrCreateEndpointState(url);
  state.consecutiveFailures = 0;
  state.cooldownUntil = 0;
  state.lastSuccessAt = now;
  state.lastLatencyMs = latencyMs;
  state.lastError = null;
}

/**
 * Executes an arbitrary asynchronous RPC operation with automatic failover.
 * Tries candidates sequentially across the prioritized pool.
 */
export async function executeWithRpcFailover<T>(options: {
  chain: Chain | 'robinhood';
  action: (rpcUrl: string) => Promise<T>;
  maxAttempts?: number;
  env?: Record<string, string | undefined>;
  now?: () => number;
}): Promise<T> {
  const getNow = options.now ?? Date.now;
  const urls = resolveConfiguredRpcUrls(options.chain, options.env);
  const prioritized = prioritizeRpcEndpoints(urls, getNow());
  const maxAttempts = Math.min(options.maxAttempts ?? prioritized.length, prioritized.length);

  const failureLog: Array<{ url: string; error: string }> = [];

  for (let i = 0; i < maxAttempts; i++) {
    const candidateUrl = prioritized[i];
    const start = getNow();
    try {
      const result = await options.action(candidateUrl);
      recordRpcSuccess(candidateUrl, getNow() - start, getNow());
      return result;
    } catch (err) {
      recordRpcFailure(candidateUrl, err, getNow());
      failureLog.push({
        url: candidateUrl,
        error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)
      });
    }
  }

  const summary = failureLog.map((f) => `[${f.url}]: ${f.error}`).join('; ');
  throw new Error(`All ${maxAttempts} RPC endpoint(s) failed for ${options.chain}: ${summary}`);
}

/**
 * Probes a single RPC URL for liveness and latency.
 */
export async function probeRpcEndpoint(
  url: string,
  chain: Chain | 'robinhood',
  timeoutMs: number = DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS
): Promise<RpcEndpointProbe> {
  const start = Date.now();
  const controller = new AbortController();
  const timer = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), timeoutMs);

  try {
    const body = chain === 'solana'
      ? JSON.stringify({ jsonrpc: '2.0', id: 1, method: 'getSlot' })
      : JSON.stringify({ jsonrpc: '2.0', id: 1, method: 'eth_blockNumber', params: [] });

    const res = await fetch(url, {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
      body,
      signal: controller.signal
    });

    clearTimeout(timer);
    const latencyMs = Date.now() - start;

    if (!res.ok) {
      recordRpcFailure(url, `HTTP ${res.status}: ${res.statusText}`);
      return { url, healthy: false, latencyMs, error: `HTTP ${res.status}` };
    }

    const json = (await res.json()) as { result?: number | string; error?: { message: string } };
    if (json.error) {
      recordRpcFailure(url, json.error.message);
      return { url, healthy: false, latencyMs, error: json.error.message };
    }

    let blockHeight: number | undefined;
    if (typeof json.result === 'number') {
      blockHeight = json.result;
    } else if (typeof json.result === 'string') {
      blockHeight = parseInt(json.result, 16);
    }

    recordRpcSuccess(url, latencyMs);
    return { url, healthy: true, latencyMs, blockHeight };
  } catch (err) {
    clearTimeout(timer);
    const latencyMs = Date.now() - start;
    const msg = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err);
    recordRpcFailure(url, msg);
    return { url, healthy: false, latencyMs, error: msg };
  }
}

/**
 * Probes all endpoints in the pool for a chain and returns a comprehensive report.
 */
export async function probeRpcPool(
  chain: Chain | 'robinhood',
  env: Record<string, string | undefined> = process.env
): Promise<RpcPoolReport> {
  const urls = resolveConfiguredRpcUrls(chain, env);
  const probes = await Promise.all(urls.map((u) => probeRpcEndpoint(u, chain)));

  const endpoints = probes.map((probe) => {
    const state = getOrCreateEndpointState(probe.url);
    return {
      ...probe,
      consecutiveFailures: state.consecutiveFailures
    };
  });

  const prioritized = prioritizeRpcEndpoints(urls);
  const activeHealthyUrl = prioritized[0] ?? urls[0];

  return {
    chain,
    primaryUrl: urls[0],
    activeHealthyUrl,
    endpoints
  };
}

/**
 * Returns the currently most preferred healthy RPC URL for a chain.
 */
export function getActiveRpcUrl(
  chain: Chain | 'robinhood',
  env: Record<string, string | undefined> = process.env
): string {
  const urls = resolveConfiguredRpcUrls(chain, env);
  const prioritized = prioritizeRpcEndpoints(urls);
  return prioritized[0] ?? urls[0];
}

import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import { calculateCompositeScore, scoreToTier } from './scoring.js';

describe('calculateCompositeScore', () => {
  it('returns 0 for an all-zero wallet', () => {
    expect(
      calculateCompositeScore({ winRate: 0, realizedRoi: 0, earlyEntryScore: 0, consistencyScore: 0 })
    ).toBe(0);
  });

  it('returns 100 for a maxed-out wallet', () => {
    // realizedRoi is normalised by /10, so 10 = max
    expect(
      calculateCompositeScore({ winRate: 1, realizedRoi: 10, earlyEntryScore: 1, consistencyScore: 1 })
    ).toBe(100);
  });

  it('clamps inputs above their ceilings', () => {
    const score = calculateCompositeScore({
      winRate: 5,
      realizedRoi: 1000,
      earlyEntryScore: 9,
      consistencyScore: 4
    });
    expect(score).toBe(100);
  });

  it('clamps negative inputs to zero contribution', () => {
    const score = calculateCompositeScore({
      winRate: -1,
      realizedRoi: -50,
      earlyEntryScore: -2,
      consistencyScore: -3
    });
    expect(score).toBe(0);
  });

  it('weights each component per the documented distribution', () => {
    // Only win rate at 100% ‚Üí 25% of 100
    expect(
      calculateCompositeScore({ winRate: 1, realizedRoi: 0, earlyEntryScore: 0, consistencyScore: 0 })
    ).toBeCloseTo(25, 5);
    // Only realized ROI at max ‚Üí 30
    expect(
      calculateCompositeScore({ winRate: 0, realizedRoi: 10, earlyEntryScore: 0, consistencyScore: 0 })
    ).toBeCloseTo(30, 5);
    // Only early entry at max ‚Üí 25
    expect(
      calculateCompositeScore({ winRate: 0, realizedRoi: 0, earlyEntryScore: 1, consistencyScore: 0 })
    ).toBeCloseTo(25, 5);
    // Only consistency at max ‚Üí 20
    expect(
      calculateCompositeScore({ winRate: 0, realizedRoi: 0, earlyEntryScore: 0, consistencyScore: 1 })
    ).toBeCloseTo(20, 5);
  });

  it('normalises realized ROI by a factor of 10', () => {
    // ROI of 5 ‚Üí 0.5 normalised ‚Üí 0.5 * 0.3 * 100 = 15
    expect(
      calculateCompositeScore({ winRate: 0, realizedRoi: 5, earlyEntryScore: 0, consistencyScore: 0 })
    ).toBeCloseTo(15, 5);
  });

import type { Chain, WalletScoreInput, WalletTier } from './types.js';

const WEIGHTS: Record<Chain, { winRate: number; realizedRoi: number; earlyEntryScore: number; consistencyScore: number }> = {
  solana: {
    winRate: 0.25,
    realizedRoi: 0.3,
    earlyEntryScore: 0.25,
    consistencyScore: 0.2
  },
  polygon: { // Polymarket
    winRate: 0.50, // High weight on resolution-derived skill
    realizedRoi: 0.3,
    earlyEntryScore: 0.0,
    consistencyScore: 0.2
  },
  'robinhood-chain': {
    winRate: 0.25,
    realizedRoi: 0.3,
    earlyEntryScore: 0.25,
    consistencyScore: 0.2
  },
  base: {
    winRate: 0.25,
    realizedRoi: 0.3,
    earlyEntryScore: 0.25,
    consistencyScore: 0.2
  },
  ethereum: {
    winRate: 0.25,
    realizedRoi: 0.3,
    earlyEntryScore: 0.25,
    consistencyScore: 0.2
  },
  bsc: {
    winRate: 0.25,
    realizedRoi: 0.3,
    earlyEntryScore: 0.25,
    consistencyScore: 0.2
  }
};

const clamp01 = (value: number): number => Math.max(0, Math.min(1, value));

export function calculateCompositeScore(input: WalletScoreInput): number {
  const normalizedRoi = clamp01(input.realizedRoi / 10);
  const winRate = clamp01(input.winRate);
  const earlyEntryScore = clamp01(input.earlyEntryScore);
  const consistencyScore = clamp01(input.consistencyScore);
  
  const w = WEIGHTS[input.chain] ?? WEIGHTS.solana;

  return Number(
    (
      winRate * w.winRate * 100 +
      normalizedRoi * w.realizedRoi * 100 +
      earlyEntryScore * w.earlyEntryScore * 100 +
      consistencyScore * w.consistencyScore * 100
    ).toFixed(2)
  );
}

export function scoreToTier(score: number): WalletTier {
  if (score >= 90) return 'elite';
  if (score >= 75) return 'pro';
  if (score >= 60) return 'promising';
  return 'speculative';
}

==> packages/shared/src/slippage.test.ts <==
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import {
  DEFAULT_SLIPPAGE_BPS,
  MAX_SLIPPAGE_BPS,
  MIN_SLIPPAGE_BPS,
  isValidSlippageBps,
  resolveSlippageBps
} from './slippage.js';

describe('slippage resolution (S4-P4)', () => {
  it('falls back to the chain default when the user has set nothing', () => {
    // null and undefined are the same case ‚Äî "never expressed a preference".
    expect(resolveSlippageBps('solana', null)).toBe(1500);
    expect(resolveSlippageBps('solana', undefined)).toBe(1500);
    expect(resolveSlippageBps('polygon', null)).toBe(300);
    expect(resolveSlippageBps('robinhood-chain', null)).toBe(300);
  });

  it('preserves the constants it replaces, so nobody who never sets it sees a change', () => {
    // These were the hard-coded values at the venue call sites. If they drift, a
    // user who never touched the setting silently gets different risk.
    expect(DEFAULT_SLIPPAGE_BPS.solana).toBe(1500);
    expect(DEFAULT_SLIPPAGE_BPS['robinhood-chain']).toBe(300);
  });

  it('honours a TIGHTER user value ‚Äî the default is never a floor', () => {
    // The important one. Treating the chain constant as a minimum would widen
    // every cautious user's risk to the platform's own appetite.
    expect(resolveSlippageBps('solana', 50)).toBe(50);
    expect(resolveSlippageBps('robinhood-chain', 10)).toBe(10);
  });

  it('honours a looser user value up to the platform ceiling', () => {
    expect(resolveSlippageBps('robinhood-chain', 900)).toBe(900);
    expect(resolveSlippageBps('solana', 2500)).toBe(2500);
  });

  it('clamps past the platform ceiling rather than obeying it', () => {
    // A user "choosing" 90% is not a risk anyone takes knowingly; the resulting
    // fill reads as a platform failure whatever the setting said.
    expect(resolveSlippageBps('solana', 9000)).toBe(MAX_SLIPPAGE_BPS);
    expect(resolveSlippageBps('solana', Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER)).toBe(MAX_SLIPPAGE_BPS);
  });

  it('clamps zero and negatives to the floor, since zero makes every order unfillable', () => {
    expect(resolveSlippageBps('solana', 0)).toBe(MIN_SLIPPAGE_BPS);
    expect(resolveSlippageBps('solana', -100)).toBe(MIN_SLIPPAGE_BPS);
  });

  it('throws on a fractional value rather than rounding it away', () => {
    // A non-integer is a caller bug. Silently rounding, or falling back to the
    // default, would hide it ‚Äî and the venues take integers regardless.
    expect(() => resolveSlippageBps('solana', 150.5)).toThrow(/integer/);
  });

  it('resolves per chain, so one user can be tight on one venue and loose on another', () => {
    // The reason this lives on (user_id, chain) rather than on the user.
    expect(resolveSlippageBps('solana', 2000)).toBe(2000);
    expect(resolveSlippageBps('polygon', 100)).toBe(100);
  });
});

describe('isValidSlippageBps', () => {
  it('accepts integers within the bounds', () => {
    expect(isValidSlippageBps(1)).toBe(true);
    expect(isValidSlippageBps(300)).toBe(true);
    expect(isValidSlippageBps(5000)).toBe(true);
  });

  it('rejects out-of-range, fractional, and non-numeric input', () => {
    // The API validates before persisting, so an out-of-range value never reaches
    // the column's CHECK and never becomes a confusing 500.
    expect(isValidSlippageBps(0)).toBe(false);
    expect(isValidSlippageBps(5001)).toBe(false);
    expect(isValidSlippageBps(-1)).toBe(false);
    expect(isValidSlippageBps(150.5)).toBe(false);
    expect(isValidSlippageBps('300')).toBe(false);
    expect(isValidSlippageBps(null)).toBe(false);
    expect(isValidSlippageBps(undefined)).toBe(false);
    expect(isValidSlippageBps(Number.NaN)).toBe(false);
  });
});

==> packages/shared/src/slippage.ts <==
import type { Chain } from './types.js';

/**
 * Slippage tolerance resolution (`S4-P4`).
 *
 * Until now slippage was a hard-coded constant at each venue call site ‚Äî 1500 bps
 * on the Solana live paths, 300 on Robinhood. That is survivable with one operator
 * whose appetite is whatever the constant says, and wrong the moment a second user
 * exists: two people with different risk appetites get the same ceiling, so a
 * user's "own stated limit" is not something the system can honour.
 *
 * It matters more than it looks. The `DG-7` decision ‚Äî serve every eligible user
 * rather than capping fan-out ‚Äî relies on each user's own tolerance rejecting a
 * bad fill, so that the platform never has to choose who misses a trade. Without a
 * per-user limit there is nothing bounding the tail of a 500-user fan-out except a
 * 15% constant, and `DG-7` is not safe to ship.
 *
 * **Per chain, not per user.** Tolerable slippage is a property of the venue, not
 * the person: 3% is loose on a Polymarket CLOB book and tight on a thin Solana
 * memecoin. A single global value would force a user to accept the loosest chain's
 * risk everywhere, so the setting lives on `user_chain_execution_settings`
 * (`(user_id, chain)`).
 */

/**
 * Defaults for a user who has not set a tolerance, matching the constants these
 * replace so behaviour is unchanged for anyone who never touches the setting.
 */
export const DEFAULT_SLIPPAGE_BPS: Readonly<Record<Chain, number>> = {
  solana: 1500,
  polygon: 300,
  'robinhood-chain': 300,
  base: 300,
  ethereum: 300,
  bsc: 300
} as const;

/**
 * Platform ceiling. A user may go looser than the chain default but not past this.
 *
 * Without it a user could set 90% and the executor would dutifully fill an order at
 * a tenth of the quoted price ‚Äî technically "their stated limit", but not a risk
 * anyone chooses knowingly, and the kind of fill that reads as a platform failure
 * regardless of what the setting said. Mirrors the `CHECK` on the column.
 */
export const MAX_SLIPPAGE_BPS = 5_000;

/** Floor. Zero would make every order unfillable, which is a footgun, not a policy. */
export const MIN_SLIPPAGE_BPS = 1;

/**
 * Resolves the tolerance for one order.
 *
 * `null` means the user has never set a value and is deliberately distinct from a
 * user-chosen one ‚Äî it is what lets a chain default be retuned later for users who
 * never expressed a preference, without silently overwriting anyone who did.
 *
 * A user value is used **as given**, tighter or looser. The chain default is a
 * default, never a floor: a user who asks for 50 bps on Solana gets 50, not 1500.
 * Treating the constant as a minimum would quietly widen the risk of every
 * cautious user to the platform's own appetite.
 */
export function resolveSlippageBps(
  chain: Chain,
  userValueBps: number | null | undefined
): number {
  if (userValueBps === null || userValueBps === undefined) {
    return DEFAULT_SLIPPAGE_BPS[chain];
  }
  if (!Number.isInteger(userValueBps)) {
    // A fractional bps is a caller bug, not a preference to round. Falling back to
    // the default would hide it; the venues take integers.
    throw new Error(`max_slippage_bps must be an integer, got ${userValueBps}`);
  }
  return Math.min(Math.max(userValueBps, MIN_SLIPPAGE_BPS), MAX_SLIPPAGE_BPS);
}

/** Whether a stored value is acceptable. Used by the API before persisting. */
export function isValidSlippageBps(value: unknown): value is number {
  return (
    typeof value === 'number'
    && Number.isInteger(value)
    && value >= MIN_SLIPPAGE_BPS
    && value <= MAX_SLIPPAGE_BPS
  );
}

import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';
import {

describe('Per-User SOL Reserve Gate (S4-P20)', () => {
  it('passes when user has sufficient SOL at current price', () => {
    // $10 minimum / $200 per SOL = 0.05 SOL required
    const verdict = evaluateSolReserve({
      currentSolBalance: 0.1,
      solPriceUsd: 200
    });

    expect(verdict.status).toBe('funded');
    if (verdict.status === 'funded') {
      expect(verdict.currentSol).toBe(0.1);
      expect(verdict.requiredSol).toBeCloseTo(0.05, 5);
      expect(verdict.solPriceUsd).toBe(200);
    }
  });

  it('fails with actionable message and code when user is underfunded', () => {
    // $10 minimum / $200 per SOL = 0.05 SOL required; user has 0.02
    const verdict = evaluateSolReserve({
      currentSolBalance: 0.02,
      solPriceUsd: 200
    });

    expect(verdict.status).toBe('underfunded');
    if (verdict.status === 'underfunded') {
      expect(verdict.code).toBe('sol-reserve-underfunded');
      expect(verdict.requiredSol).toBeCloseTo(0.05, 5);
      expect(verdict.neededSol).toBeCloseTo(0.03, 5);
      expect(verdict.reason).toContain('Insufficient SOL');
      expect(verdict.reason).toContain('hold at least ~0.0300 more SOL ($10 reserve required)');
    }
  });

  it('handles zero SOL balance accurately', () => {
    const verdict = evaluateSolReserve({
      currentSolBalance: 0,
      solPriceUsd: 150
    });

    expect(verdict.status).toBe('underfunded');
    if (verdict.status === 'underfunded') {
      expect(verdict.currentSol).toBe(0);
      expect(verdict.neededSol).toBeCloseTo(10 / 150, 5);
      expect(verdict.reason).toContain('($10 reserve required)');
    }
  });

  it('dynamically scales required SOL with live SOL price', () => {
    // At $100/SOL, need 0.1 SOL
    const v1 = evaluateSolReserve({ currentSolBalance: 0.06, solPriceUsd: 100 });
    expect(v1.status).toBe('underfunded');

    // At $400/SOL, need 0.025 SOL (0.06 is plenty)
    const v2 = evaluateSolReserve({ currentSolBalance: 0.06, solPriceUsd: 400 });
    expect(v2.status).toBe('funded');
  });

  it('fails closed when SOL price is unavailable, null, or invalid (no 150 fallback)', () => {
    const vNull = evaluateSolReserve({ currentSolBalance: 1.0, solPriceUsd: null });
    expect(vNull.status).toBe('price-unavailable');
    if (vNull.status === 'price-unavailable') {

      expect(vNull.reason).toContain('SOL price feed is currently unavailable');

    const vZero = evaluateSolReserve({ currentSolBalance: 1.0, solPriceUsd: 0 });

    const vNaN = evaluateSolReserve({ currentSolBalance: 1.0, solPriceUsd: Number.NaN });

      targetUsd: 20 // requires 0.1 SOL
    });

    if (verdict.status === 'underfunded') {
      expect(verdict.requiredSol).toBeCloseTo(0.1, 5);
      expect(verdict.reason).toContain('$20 reserve required');
    }
  });
});

==> packages/shared/src/sol-reserve.ts <==
/**
 * Per-user SOL minimum for tips and transaction fees (S4-P20).
 *
 * A user funding only tokens/USDC has zero SOL and cannot execute.
 * The threshold is strictly denominated in USD ($10 equivalent) and converted
 * live via the current SOL price, never fixed at a static SOL floor that drifts
 * with price movement.
 *
 * Fail-closed: an unreadable SOL price must not silently admit an underfunded
 * user or guess a fabricated fallback (e.g. 150). It returns an actionable
 * skip verdict with a specific reason.
 */

export const DEFAULT_SOL_MINIMUM_RESERVE_USD = 10;

export type SolReserveVerdict =
  | {
      readonly status: 'funded';
      readonly currentSol: number;
      readonly requiredSol: number;
      readonly solPriceUsd: number;
    }
  | {
      readonly status: 'underfunded';
      readonly code: 'sol-reserve-underfunded';
      readonly reason: string;
      readonly currentSol: number;
      readonly requiredSol: number;
      readonly neededSol: number;
      readonly solPriceUsd: number;
    }
  | {
      readonly status: 'price-unavailable';
      readonly code: 'sol-price-unavailable';
      readonly reason: string;
      readonly currentSol: number;
    };

export interface EvaluateSolReserveOptions {
  readonly currentSolBalance: number;
  readonly solPriceUsd: number | null | undefined;
  readonly targetUsd?: number;
}

export function evaluateSolReserve(opts: EvaluateSolReserveOptions): SolReserveVerdict {
  const currentSol = opts.currentSolBalance;
  const targetUsd = opts.targetUsd ?? DEFAULT_SOL_MINIMUM_RESERVE_USD;

  if (opts.solPriceUsd == null || Number.isNaN(opts.solPriceUsd) || opts.solPriceUsd <= 0) {
    return {
      status: 'price-unavailable',
      code: 'sol-price-unavailable',
      reason: 'SOL price feed is currently unavailable; refusing trade to protect reserve gate',
      currentSol
    };
  }

  const solPriceUsd = opts.solPriceUsd;
  const requiredSol = targetUsd / solPriceUsd;

  if (currentSol >= requiredSol) {
    return {
      status: 'funded',
      currentSol,
      requiredSol,
      solPriceUsd
    };
  }

  const neededSol = Math.max(0, requiredSol - currentSol);
  return {
    status: 'underfunded',
    code: 'sol-reserve-underfunded',
    reason: `Insufficient SOL for transaction fees: hold at least ~${neededSol.toFixed(4)} more SOL ($${targetUsd} reserve required)`,
    currentSol,
    requiredSol,
    neededSol,
    solPriceUsd
  };
}

==> packages/shared/src/starter-pack.ts <==
export type SignatureRecord = {
  signature: string;
};

export type SignaturePageRequest = {
  before?: string;
  limit: number;
};

export type PaginatedSignatures<T extends SignatureRecord> = {
  signatures: T[];
  reachedOldest: boolean;
  capped: boolean;
};

export function clampInteger(
  value: unknown,
  fallback: number,
  minimum: number,
  maximum: number
): number {
  const parsed = typeof value === 'number' ? value : Number(value);
  if (!Number.isFinite(parsed)) return fallback;
  return Math.min(maximum, Math.max(minimum, Math.trunc(parsed)));
}

export async function collectSignaturesToOldest<T extends SignatureRecord>(
  fetchPage: (request: SignaturePageRequest) => Promise<T[]>,
  options: {
    maxTotal: number;
    pageSize?: number;
  }
): Promise<PaginatedSignatures<T>> {
  const maxTotal = clampInteger(options.maxTotal, 1000, 1, 100_000);
  const pageSize = clampInteger(options.pageSize, 1000, 1, 1000);
  const signatures: T[] = [];
  const seen = new Set<string>();
  let before: string | undefined;
  let reachedOldest = false;

  while (signatures.length < maxTotal) {
    const limit = Math.min(pageSize, maxTotal - signatures.length);
    const page = await fetchPage({ before, limit });
    if (page.length === 0) {
      reachedOldest = true;
      break;
    }

    for (const record of page) {
      if (!seen.has(record.signature)) {
        seen.add(record.signature);
        signatures.push(record);
      }
    }

    if (page.length < limit) {
      reachedOldest = true;
      break;
    }

    const nextBefore = page[page.length - 1]?.signature;
    if (!nextBefore || nextBefore === before) {
      break;
    }
    before = nextBefore;
  }

  // A full final page does not prove that the final record is the account
  // origin. Probe once beyond the cap without retaining more history.
  if (!reachedOldest && signatures.length >= maxTotal && before) {
    const probe = await fetchPage({ before, limit: 1 });
    reachedOldest = probe.length === 0;
  }

  return {
    signatures,
    reachedOldest,
    capped: !reachedOldest && signatures.length >= maxTotal
  };
}

export type StarterPackWalletScore = {
  address: string;
  patterns: string[];
  successfulTrades: number;
  totalTrades: number;
  winRate: number | null;
  score: number;
};

type MutableWalletScore = {
  address: string;
  patterns: Set<string>;
  patternMatches: Set<string>;
  tradeOutcomes: Map<string, boolean>;
};

export function createStarterPackScoreTracker() {
  const wallets = new Map<string, MutableWalletScore>();

  function getWallet(address: string) {
    const existing = wallets.get(address);
    if (existing) return existing;

    const created: MutableWalletScore = {
      address,
      patterns: new Set(),
      patternMatches: new Set(),
      tradeOutcomes: new Map()
    };
    wallets.set(address, created);
    return created;
  }

  function recordPattern(address: string, pattern: string, context: string) {
    const wallet = getWallet(address);
    wallet.patterns.add(pattern);
    wallet.patternMatches.add(`${pattern}:${context}`);
  }

  function recordTradeOutcome(address: string, tradeKey: string, isWin: boolean) {
    const wallet = getWallet(address);
    if (!wallet.tradeOutcomes.has(tradeKey)) {
      wallet.tradeOutcomes.set(tradeKey, isWin);
    }
  }

  function results(): StarterPackWalletScore[] {
    return [...wallets.values()]
      .filter((wallet) => wallet.patternMatches.size > 0)
      .map((wallet) => {
        const outcomes = [...wallet.tradeOutcomes.values()];
        const successfulTrades = outcomes.filter(Boolean).length;
        const totalTrades = outcomes.length;

        return {
          address: wallet.address,
          patterns: [...wallet.patterns],
          successfulTrades,
          totalTrades,
          winRate: totalTrades > 0
            ? Math.round((successfulTrades / totalTrades) * 100)
            : null,
          score: wallet.patternMatches.size
        };
      });
  }

  return {
    recordPattern,
    recordTradeOutcome,
    results
  };
}

==> packages/shared/src/tiers.test.ts <==
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import {
  capabilitiesFor,
  effectiveTier,
  quotaExceeded,
  tierAllowsChain,
  tierAtLeast,
  TIER_CAPABILITIES
} from './tiers.js';

const NOW = new Date('2026-08-05T00:00:00.000Z');
const PAST = new Date('2026-08-01T00:00:00.000Z');
const FUTURE = new Date('2026-09-01T00:00:00.000Z');

describe('tier matrix', () => {
  describe('effectiveTier', () => {
    it('keeps a tier whose expiry is in the future', () => {
      expect(effectiveTier('operator', FUTURE, NOW)).toBe('operator');
      expect(effectiveTier('ultra', FUTURE, NOW)).toBe('ultra');
    });

    it('degrades an expired paid tier to free', () => {
      expect(effectiveTier('operator', PAST, NOW)).toBe('free');
      expect(effectiveTier('ultra', PAST, NOW)).toBe('free');
    });

    it('treats a null expiry as LIFETIME, never as expired', () => {
      // This is the USDC lifetime tier. Inverting this check would silently
      // downgrade every lifetime customer to free.
      expect(effectiveTier('ultra', null, NOW)).toBe('ultra');
      expect(effectiveTier('operator', null, NOW)).toBe('operator');
    });

    it('leaves free alone regardless of expiry', () => {
      expect(effectiveTier('free', PAST, NOW)).toBe('free');
      expect(effectiveTier('free', null, NOW)).toBe('free');
    });
  });

  describe('capabilitiesFor', () => {
    it('returns the expired tier‚Äôs capabilities, not the nominal one', () => {
      const expired = capabilitiesFor('ultra', PAST, NOW);
      expect(expired.tier).toBe('free');
      expect(expired.trackedWallets).toBe(3);
      expect(expired.liveExecution).toBe(false);
    });

    it('returns full capabilities for a lifetime ultra', () => {
      const lifetime = capabilitiesFor('ultra', null, NOW);
      expect(lifetime.tier).toBe('ultra');
      expect(lifetime.trackedWallets).toBe(null);
      expect(lifetime.liveExecution).toBe(true);
    });
  });

  describe('quotaExceeded', () => {
    it('treats null as unlimited', () => {
      expect(quotaExceeded(null, 0)).toBe(false);
      expect(quotaExceeded(null, 1_000_000)).toBe(false);
    });

    it('blocks at the limit, not past it', () => {
      // A free user with 3 of 3 wallets must be blocked from adding a 4th, so
      // the boundary is `used >= quota`, not `used > quota`.
      expect(quotaExceeded(3, 2)).toBe(false);
      expect(quotaExceeded(3, 3)).toBe(true);
      expect(quotaExceeded(3, 4)).toBe(true);
    });

    it('blocks everything at a zero quota', () => {
      // Free tier gets 0 API keys; this must not read as unlimited.
      expect(quotaExceeded(0, 0)).toBe(true);
      expect(TIER_CAPABILITIES.free.apiKeys).toBe(0);
    });
  });

  describe('tierAtLeast', () => {
    it('orders free < operator < ultra', () => {
      expect(tierAtLeast('ultra', 'operator')).toBe(true);
      expect(tierAtLeast('operator', 'operator')).toBe(true);
      expect(tierAtLeast('free', 'operator')).toBe(false);
      expect(tierAtLeast('operator', 'ultra')).toBe(false);
    });
  });

  describe('tierAllowsChain', () => {
    it('allows free all registered chains so backfills are available across tiers', () => {
      const free = TIER_CAPABILITIES.free;
      expect(tierAllowsChain(free, 'solana')).toBe(true);
      expect(tierAllowsChain(free, 'polygon')).toBe(true);
      expect(tierAllowsChain(free, 'robinhood-chain')).toBe(true);
    });

    it('allows operator every built-in chain', () => {
      const operator = TIER_CAPABILITIES.operator;
      expect(tierAllowsChain(operator, 'solana')).toBe(true);
      expect(tierAllowsChain(operator, 'polygon')).toBe(true);
      expect(tierAllowsChain(operator, 'robinhood-chain')).toBe(true);
    });

    it('treats ultra‚Äôs and unlimited‚Äôs null chain list as every chain', () => {
      // Ultra adds custom chains in Stage 7, so its list cannot be enumerated.
      const ultra = TIER_CAPABILITIES.ultra;
      const unlimited = TIER_CAPABILITIES.unlimited;
      expect(ultra.chains).toBe(null);
      expect(unlimited.chains).toBe(null);

      expect(tierAllowsChain(ultra, 'polygon')).toBe(true);
      expect(tierAllowsChain(unlimited, 'solana')).toBe(true);
      expect(tierAllowsChain(unlimited, 'polygon')).toBe(true);
    });
  });

  describe('matrix invariants', () => {
    it('never lets a higher tier have a smaller quota', () => {
      const { free, operator, ultra, unlimited } = TIER_CAPABILITIES;
      const atLeast = (higher: number | null, lower: number | null) =>
        higher === null || (lower !== null && higher >= lower);
      expect(atLeast(operator.trackedWallets, free.trackedWallets)).toBe(true);
      expect(atLeast(ultra.trackedWallets, operator.trackedWallets)).toBe(true);
      expect(atLeast(unlimited.trackedWallets, operator.trackedWallets)).toBe(true);
      expect(atLeast(operator.tokenBackfillsPerDay, free.tokenBackfillsPerDay)).toBe(true);
      expect(atLeast(ultra.tokenBackfillsPerDay, operator.tokenBackfillsPerDay)).toBe(true);
      expect(atLeast(unlimited.tokenBackfillsPerDay, operator.tokenBackfillsPerDay)).toBe(true);
      expect(operator.backfillDepthDays).toBeGreaterThan(free.backfillDepthDays);
      expect(ultra.backfillDepthDays).toBeGreaterThan(operator.backfillDepthDays);
      expect(unlimited.backfillDepthDays).toBeGreaterThan(operator.backfillDepthDays);
    });

    it('ensures unlimited and ultra have the exact same amount of everything', () => {
      const { ultra, unlimited } = TIER_CAPABILITIES;
      expect(unlimited.trackedWallets).toBe(ultra.trackedWallets);
      expect(unlimited.tokenBackfillsPerDay).toBe(ultra.tokenBackfillsPerDay);
      expect(unlimited.backfillDepthDays).toBe(ultra.backfillDepthDays);
      expect(unlimited.chains).toBe(ultra.chains);
      expect(unlimited.signalDelaySeconds).toBe(ultra.signalDelaySeconds);
      expect(unlimited.liveExecution).toBe(ultra.liveExecution);
      expect(unlimited.apiKeys).toBe(ultra.apiKeys);
      expect(unlimited.backfillPriority).toBe(ultra.backfillPriority);
    });

    it('gives higher tiers a lower (sooner) backfill priority number', () => {
      // BullMQ runs LOWER priority numbers first ‚Äî the inversion is easy to get
      // backwards and would silently starve paying users behind free ones.
      const { free, operator, ultra, unlimited } = TIER_CAPABILITIES;
      expect(operator.backfillPriority).toBeLessThan(free.backfillPriority);
      expect(ultra.backfillPriority).toBeLessThan(operator.backfillPriority);
      expect(unlimited.backfillPriority).toBe(ultra.backfillPriority);
    });

    it('delays only the free tier‚Äôs signal feed', () => {
      expect(TIER_CAPABILITIES.free.signalDelaySeconds).toBeGreaterThan(0);
      expect(TIER_CAPABILITIES.operator.signalDelaySeconds).toBe(0);
      expect(TIER_CAPABILITIES.ultra.signalDelaySeconds).toBe(0);
      expect(TIER_CAPABILITIES.unlimited.signalDelaySeconds).toBe(0);
    });

    it('gates live execution to paid tiers', () => {
      expect(TIER_CAPABILITIES.free.liveExecution).toBe(false);
      expect(TIER_CAPABILITIES.operator.liveExecution).toBe(true);
      expect(TIER_CAPABILITIES.ultra.liveExecution).toBe(true);
      expect(TIER_CAPABILITIES.unlimited.liveExecution).toBe(true);
    });
  });

==> packages/shared/src/tiers.ts <==
import type { Chain } from './types.js';

/**
 * Tier capability matrix ‚Äî the single source of truth for quotas, features, and
 * chain access, consumed by both API guards and frontend gating (SaaS Phase 2).
 *
 * **Capability only, never price.** Stage 5 owns billing, so a price change never
 * has to touch quota logic and a quota change never has to touch a payment path.
 */

export type UserTier = 'free' | 'operator' | 'ultra' | 'unlimited';

export const USER_TIERS: readonly UserTier[] = ['free', 'operator', 'ultra', 'unlimited'] as const;

/**
 * `null` means unlimited ‚Äî deliberately not `Infinity`.
 *
 * `Infinity` does not survive `JSON.stringify` (it becomes `null` anyway) or a
 * numeric database column, and it invites `if (!limit)` checks that treat it the
 * same as `0`. `null` forces an explicit branch at every call site.
 */
export type Quota = number | null;

export interface TierCapabilities {
  readonly tier: UserTier;
  /** Concurrent tracked-wallet subscriptions. */
  readonly trackedWallets: Quota;
  /** Token-contract backfills startable per rolling 24h. */
  readonly tokenBackfillsPerDay: Quota;
  /** How far back a backfill may reach. */
  readonly backfillDepthDays: number;
  /** Chains this tier may track. `null` = every registered chain (Stage 7). */
  readonly chains: readonly Chain[] | null;
  /**
   * Signal feed delay in seconds. The free tier is delayed on purpose; this is a
   * product decision recorded here because the feed query must implement it, and
   * retrofitting it into a hot path later is worse.
   */
  readonly signalDelaySeconds: number;
  /** Whether live execution may be enabled at all (Stage 4; platform gates still apply). */
  readonly liveExecution: boolean;
  readonly apiKeys: Quota;
  /** BullMQ job priority for backfills ‚Äî LOWER runs sooner (D9). */
  readonly backfillPriority: number;
}

const FREE: TierCapabilities = {
  tier: 'free',
  trackedWallets: 3,
  tokenBackfillsPerDay: 5,
  backfillDepthDays: 30,
  chains: ['solana', 'polygon', 'robinhood-chain'],
  signalDelaySeconds: 900,
  liveExecution: false,
  apiKeys: 0,
  backfillPriority: 10
};

const OPERATOR: TierCapabilities = {
  tier: 'operator',
  trackedWallets: 25,
  tokenBackfillsPerDay: 25,
  backfillDepthDays: 180,
  chains: ['solana', 'polygon', 'robinhood-chain', 'base', 'ethereum', 'bsc'],
  signalDelaySeconds: 0,
  liveExecution: true,
  apiKeys: 3,
  backfillPriority: 5
};

const ULTRA: TierCapabilities = {
  tier: 'ultra',
  trackedWallets: null,
  tokenBackfillsPerDay: 100,
  backfillDepthDays: 730,
  // null = every registered chain, including Ultra's custom ones (Stage 7).
  chains: null,
  signalDelaySeconds: 0,
  liveExecution: true,
  apiKeys: 10,
  backfillPriority: 1
};

const UNLIMITED: TierCapabilities = {
  ...ULTRA,
  tier: 'unlimited'
};

export const TIER_CAPABILITIES: Readonly<Record<UserTier, TierCapabilities>> = {
  free: FREE,
  operator: OPERATOR,
  ultra: ULTRA,
  unlimited: UNLIMITED
};

/** Ordering for "at least this tier" comparisons. */
const TIER_RANK: Readonly<Record<UserTier, number>> = {
  free: 0,
  operator: 1,
  ultra: 2,
  unlimited: 2
};

/**
 * Resolves the tier a user is *actually* entitled to right now.
 *
 * An expired paid tier degrades to `free`. `expiresAt === null` means **lifetime**
 * (the USDC lifetime tier) and must never be read as expired ‚Äî inverting that
 * check would silently downgrade every lifetime customer.
 */
export function effectiveTier(tier: UserTier | string, expiresAt: Date | null, now = new Date()): UserTier {
  const normalized: UserTier =
    tier === 'unlimited' || tier === 'lifetime' ? 'unlimited' :
    tier === 'operator' ? 'operator' :
    tier === 'ultra' ? 'ultra' :
    tier === 'free' ? 'free' : 'free';

  if (expiresAt === null) return normalized;
  return expiresAt.getTime() < now.getTime() ? 'free' : normalized;
}

export function capabilitiesFor(tier: UserTier | string, expiresAt: Date | null = null, now = new Date()): TierCapabilities {
  return TIER_CAPABILITIES[effectiveTier(tier, expiresAt, now)] ?? TIER_CAPABILITIES.free;
}

export function tierAtLeast(tier: UserTier, minimum: UserTier): boolean {
  return TIER_RANK[tier] >= TIER_RANK[minimum];
}

/** True when `used` is already at or over the limit. `null` quota is never exceeded. */
export function quotaExceeded(quota: Quota, used: number): boolean {
  return quota !== null && used >= quota;
}

export function tierAllowsChain(capabilities: TierCapabilities, chain: Chain): boolean {
  return capabilities.chains === null || capabilities.chains.includes(chain);
}

==> packages/shared/src/trade-queues.test.ts <==
import { describe, it, expect } from 'vitest';
import {
  QUEUES,
  TRADE_QUEUES_BY_CHAIN,
  chainFromTokenMint,
  tradeQueueForChain,
  tradeQueueForTokenMint
} from './constants.js';

describe('trade queue naming (D6 / S3-25)', () => {
  it('routes each chain to its own queue', () => {
    expect(tradeQueueForChain('solana')).toBe('swat-trades-solana');
    expect(tradeQueueForChain('polygon')).toBe('swat-trades-polygon');
    expect(tradeQueueForChain('robinhood-chain')).toBe('swat-trades-robinhood');
  });

  it('gives every chain a distinct queue', () => {
    const names = Object.values(TRADE_QUEUES_BY_CHAIN);
    expect(new Set(names).size).toBe(names.length);
  });

  it('covers exactly the supported chains', () => {
    expect(Object.keys(TRADE_QUEUES_BY_CHAIN).sort()).toEqual([
      'base',
      'bsc',
      'ethereum',
      'polygon',
      'robinhood-chain',
      'solana'
    ]);
  });

  it('no longer routes any chain to the pre-split queue', () => {
    // The drain worker in `tradeWorkerSpecs` is the only remaining reader of
    // `swat-trades`. If a producer started resolving to it again, jobs would
    // land in a queue scheduled for deletion.
    for (const chain of Object.keys(TRADE_QUEUES_BY_CHAIN) as Array<
      keyof typeof TRADE_QUEUES_BY_CHAIN
    >) {
      expect(tradeQueueForChain(chain)).not.toBe(QUEUES.trades);
    }
  });

  it('keeps the pre-split queue name pinned for the drain worker', () => {
    // Not a producer target any more, but the executor still reads it to drain
    // jobs enqueued before the cutover. If this drifts, those jobs are orphaned.
    expect(QUEUES.trades).toBe('swat-trades');
  });
});

describe('chainFromTokenMint (S3-25 routing agreement)', () => {
  it('reads the chain from a prefixed mint', () => {
    expect(chainFromTokenMint('solana:So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112')).toBe('solana');
    expect(chainFromTokenMint('polygon:0xabc')).toBe('polygon');
    expect(chainFromTokenMint('robinhood-chain:0xabc')).toBe('robinhood-chain');
  });

  it('reads an unprefixed mint as Solana', () => {
    // Every historical Solana mint in this codebase is stored unprefixed in
    // older rows, and the executor has always read them this way.
    expect(chainFromTokenMint('So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112')).toBe('solana');
  });

  it('throws on an unsupported prefix rather than defaulting to Solana', () => {
    // Defaulting would route a job to the Solana queue, whose worker would then
    // refuse it ‚Äî a trade lost at the far end of the pipeline instead of a loud
    // failure at the near end.
    expect(() => chainFromTokenMint('avalanche:0xabc')).toThrow(/Unsupported trade chain: avalanche/);
    expect(() => chainFromTokenMint('arbitrum:0xabc')).toThrow(/Unsupported trade chain: arbitrum/);
  });

  it('throws on an empty prefix', () => {
    expect(() => chainFromTokenMint(':0xabc')).toThrow(/Unsupported trade chain/);
  });

  it('does not mistake a mint containing a later colon for a prefix', () => {
    // Only the first segment is a prefix; anything after is part of the mint.
    expect(chainFromTokenMint('polygon:0xabc:1')).toBe('polygon');
  });
});

describe('tradeQueueForTokenMint (S3-25 producer routing)', () => {
  it('routes a job to the queue its own chain owns', () => {
    expect(tradeQueueForTokenMint('solana:So111')).toBe('swat-trades-solana');
    expect(tradeQueueForTokenMint('polygon:0xabc')).toBe('swat-trades-polygon');
    expect(tradeQueueForTokenMint('robinhood-chain:0xabc')).toBe('swat-trades-robinhood');
    expect(tradeQueueForTokenMint('base:0xabc')).toBe('swat-trades-base');
    expect(tradeQueueForTokenMint('ethereum:0xabc')).toBe('swat-trades-ethereum');
    expect(tradeQueueForTokenMint('bsc:0xabc')).toBe('swat-trades-bsc');
  });

  it('refuses to pick a queue for an unsupported chain', () => {
    expect(() => tradeQueueForTokenMint('avalanche:0xabc')).toThrow(/Unsupported trade chain/);
  });
});

==> packages/shared/src/validation.ts <==
import { PublicKey, Keypair } from '@solana/web3.js';
import { z } from 'zod';

export { PublicKey, Keypair };

export const chainSchema = z.enum(['solana', 'polygon', 'robinhood-chain', 'base', 'ethereum', 'bsc']);

export const walletAddressSchema = z
  .string()
  .min(32)
  .max(44)
  .refine((value) => {
    try {
      new PublicKey(value);
      return true;
    } catch {
      return false;
    }
  }, 'Invalid Solana wallet address');

export const evmAddressSchema = z
  .string()
  .regex(/^0x[a-fA-F0-9]{40}$/, 'Invalid EVM wallet address');

export function isValidAddressForChain(address: string, chain: z.infer<typeof chainSchema>): boolean {
  if (chain === 'solana') return walletAddressSchema.safeParse(address).success;
  return evmAddressSchema.safeParse(address).success;
}

export const walletInputSchema = z.object({
  address: z.string(),
  chain: chainSchema.default('solana'),
  source: z.enum(['shiller', 'manual', 'discovered']).default('manual'),
  nickname: z.string().max(100).optional()
}).superRefine((value, ctx) => {
  if (!isValidAddressForChain(value.address, value.chain)) {
    ctx.addIssue({
      code: z.ZodIssueCode.custom,
      path: ['address'],
      message: value.chain === 'solana' ? 'Invalid Solana wallet address' : 'Invalid EVM wallet address'
    });
  }
});

export type WalletInput = z.infer<typeof walletInputSchema>;

export function isValidSolanaAddress(address: string): boolean {
  return walletAddressSchema.safeParse(address).success;
}
